As beautiful as this vista is, most of today's visitors to Park City are there to spend the day inside. Sundance Film Festival, the nation's biggest celebration of independent cinema, opens today and runs through January 29. The careers of Hollywood directors such as Quentin Tarantino and Steven Soderbergh were launched here, and every year a new crop of greenhorns arrives in this mountain enclave with the dream that they'll leave with a distribution deal.

It's a common misconception that the festival was founded by Robert Redford. It was actually started as the Utah Film Festival in Salt Lake City in 1978 by Sterling Van Wagenen, who then brought on Redford as chairman. Redford has remained involved with the festival ever since, presiding over its move to Park City and transformation into the largest festival of its kind in the United States. In the past decade, Sundance London and Sundance Hong Kong have expanded the mission of the Sundance Institute.

bing-41583.jpg.title: King penguins in the Falkland Islands
bing-41583.jpg.headline: 'Come on, guys, this way!'. Penguin Awareness Day
bing-41583.jpg.description: We're celebrating Penguin Awareness Day in the Falkland Islands, taking a stroll with some king penguins. Kings are the second-largest penguin species, only outranked in stature by their emperor penguin cousins. And while the kings' tuxedo coloring gives them a dash of the debonair, it also provides an important and more practical purpose: camouflage. When the birds dive deep into the ocean looking for food, their black feathers disguise the birds from predators above, while their white undersides do the reverse. Kings are legendary for their diving prowess—in their quest for tasty squid and lanternfish, they can dive to depths of 300 feet, and some have even been spotted nearly 1,000 feet beneath the surface. Underwater, these flightless birds are the epitome of grace. On land, however, they are not so graceful, and waddle or 'toboggan' on their bellies to get around.

bing-41589.jpg.title: Waschbär (Procyon Lotor) zwei Babys klettern auf den Baum
bing-41589.jpg.headline: Wenn nur eine Umarmung genügt. Knuddeltag
bing-41589.jpg.description:
Egal, ob es sich um Knuddeln oder Umarmen handelt, die Kraft der Berührung hat etwas an sich, das alle Säugetiere nachvollziehen können. Dieses Waschbärenpaar zum Beispiel braucht keine Worte, um zu vermitteln, was auf diesem Bild passiert. Diese niedlichen Tierchen lassen uns nicht nur die Haare zu Berge stehen, sie sind auch das perfekte Bild für den Nationalen Knuddeltag, den wir heute feiern.

Dieser warme Anlass wurde 1986 von einem Mann namens Kevin Zaborney ins Leben gerufen, der den 21. Januar auswählte, weil er nach den Neujahrsfeiertagen und damit mitten im Winter liegt, wenn die Stimmung eher schlecht ist. Für uns macht das absolut Sinn. Schließlich ist das Umarmen seit Jahrtausenden ein wesentlicher Bestandteil der menschlichen Erfahrung. Und Studien haben gezeigt, dass es auch Stress abbaut. Suchen Sie sich also einen Partner, der bereit ist, Sie zu umarmen. Wir versprechen, dass Sie sich besser fühlen werden.

bing-41598.jpg.title: 春节的桃花和红灯笼
bing-41598.jpg.headline: 春节快乐，兔年大吉！
bing-41598.jpg.description: 兔年快乐！今天是农历新年的开始，我们迎来了兔年。兔子十二生肖中的第四种动物。中国的新年也称为春节，也是家庭团聚的传统日子。春节的起源蕴含着深邃的文化内涵，在传承发展中承载了丰厚的历史文化底蕴。在春节期间，全国各地均有举行各种庆贺新春活动，带有浓郁的各地地方特色。而从年初一开始便进入迎禧接福、拜祭神祖、祈求丰年主题。元日子时交年时刻，鞭炮齐响、烟花照天、辞旧岁、迎新年等各种庆贺新春活动达于高潮。年初一，人们都早早起来，穿上最漂亮的衣服，打扮得整整齐齐出门，恭祝新年大吉大利。

bing-41607.jpg.title: Mountain hare in Derbyshire, England
bing-41607.jpg.headline: Hop into Lunar New Year. Mountain hare hopping into Lunar New Year
bing-41607.jpg.description: Today is the start of the Lunar New Year, which ushers in the Year of the Rabbit. Those born under the sign of the rabbit are believed to be ingenious, sweet, happy, quiet, and persistent. Famous rabbits include Albert Einstein, Frank Sinatra, Lionel Messi, and Ingrid Bergman. The Lunar New Year celebration starts with the first new moon in January and goes for the next 15 days, until the year's first full moon lights up the night sky. Historically it has been an occasion for feasting and honoring deities as well as ancestors. We're doing our part by sharing this lovely winter image of a mountain hare in Derbyshire, England.

bing-41619.jpg.title: Moai statues on Easter Island, Chile
bing-41619.jpg.headline: Stony sentinels. Moai statues on Easter Island, Chile
bing-41619.jpg.description: Today we're looking at something you may have heard about before—the famous Moai statues on Chile's remote Easter Island. These big-headed statues were carved out of solidified volcanic ash by the Rapa Nui people between 1250 and 1500, and there are nearly 1,000 of them on the island. Archaeologists believe they were meant to honor Rapa Nui ancestors and were revered as symbols of power and authority. All but seven of the statues face away from the surrounding Pacific Ocean, and instead look inward toward the villages, as if positioned to watch protectively over the Rapa Nui.

bing-41631.jpg.title: Colle Santa Lucia in the Dolomites, Italy
bing-41631.jpg.headline: The envy of postcards and snow globes. Colle Santa Lucia, Dolomites, Italy
bing-41631.jpg.description: This tiny hamlet on the slopes of the Dolomite Mountains is so picturesque, we'd understand if you mistook it for a movie set. But Colle Santa Lucia is a real village in Italy with about 400 residents. Despite its location in Italy's northern reaches, the village is more culturally Austrian than Italian, and is only a stone's throw from the Austrian border state of Tyrol. And like its Austrian neighbors, Colle Santa Lucia is known for its peaks and ski resorts. It has more in common with wintry Innsbruck than sunny Venice, which is less than 100 miles away to the south.

bing-41641.jpg.title: Ponte Estaiada na cidade de São Paulo
bing-41641.jpg.headline: Aniversário da cidade de São Paulo
bing-41641.jpg.description:
A Ponte Octávio Frias de Oliveira está localizada na cidade de São Paulo. Inaugurada em 10 de maio de 2008, após três anos de construção, ela é hoje um dos cartões postais mais famosos da cidade.

Ela é composta por duas pistas estaiadas em curvas independentes de 60º que cruzam o Rio Pinheiros, no bairro do Brooklyn, sendo a única ponte estaiada do mundo com duas pistas curvas conectadas ao mesmo mastro.

Escolhemos essa imagem para celebrar o aniversário da cidade de São Paulo, comemorado em 25 de janeiro. Parabéns pelos seus 469 anos!

bing-41643.jpg.title: Statue of Robert Burns in the Birks of Aberfeldy, Perth and Kinross, Scotland
bing-41643.jpg.headline: Celebrating the Scottish Bard. Burns Night
bing-41643.jpg.description:
Today we're wishing a very happy birthday to the man regarded as Scotland's national poet and a pioneer of the Romantic movement, Robert Burns. Perhaps you can celebrate by visiting his statue at the Birks of Aberfeldy in Perth and Kinross, as seen in today's photo. The birch trees here ('birks' in the Scots language) and a local waterfall inspired him to write a song lyric, 'The Birks of Aberfeldy,' in 1787.

You might also take part in Burns Night, a worldwide celebration that involves a lavish, multicourse dinner, a recital of Burns' 'Address to a Haggis,' and a serving of that poem's titular dish. After much discussion and several poetry readings, the night traditionally ends with guests singing the New Year's standard, 'Auld Lang Syne,' with words written by Burns himself in 1788.

bing-41647.jpg.title: Indian Army soldiers march through the ceremonial Rajpath in New Delhi
bing-41647.jpg.headline: Republic Day
bing-41647.jpg.description:
Republic Day is one of three Indian national holidays and it commemorates the enactment of the constitution of India, which occurred on January 26, 1950. India had achieved independence from Britain on August 15, 1947 (which is celebrated as a separate national holiday), but for its first three years the country remained governed largely by the colonial Government of India Act of 1935.

The main event for the holiday is a massive parade held in the capital of New Delhi, which includes cultural, historical, and military displays. The parade is preceded by the prime minister laying a wreath at the Amar Jawan Jyoti — an arched war memorial — and taking a moment of silence to commemorate fallen soldiers.

bing-41652.jpg.title: Silbury Hill in the winter snow at sunrise, Avebury, Wiltshire
bing-41652.jpg.headline: The glowing winter. Silbury Hill, Wiltshire
bing-41652.jpg.description:
Silbury Hill is a prehistoric artificial chalk mound near Avebury in the English county of Wiltshire. It is the tallest prehistoric man-made mound in Europe and one of the largest in the world similar in volume to contemporary Egyptian pyramids. It is part of the Stonehenge, Avebury and Associated Sites UNESCO World Heritage Site.

Around Avebury, it is part of the complex of Neolithic monuments which includes the Avebury Ring and West Kennet Long Barrow. Several other important Neolithic monuments in Wiltshire in the care of English Heritage, including the large henges at Marden and Stonehenge, may be culturally or functionally related to Avebury and Silbury.

bing-41655.jpg.title: Heaven's Gate Cave in Tianmen Mountain National Park, China
bing-41655.jpg.headline: A heavenly view. Heaven's Gate Cave, Tianmen Mountain National Park, China
bing-41655.jpg.description: The rock arch formation you're looking at today is Heaven's Gate Cave, a popular landmark in Hunan province, China. This busy tourist destination is located on Tianmen (Heaven's Gate) Mountain in Tianmen Mountain National Park. To reach the arch, you must either ride a cable car or take a bus up a twisty, winding road with 99 turns. (The number 9 represents eternity in Chinese numerology.) Once off the bus, you'll need to walk 999 steps up a 45-degree incline—a stairway to the heavens. It's no easy feat, but this is no ordinary cave. At an elevation of 4,100 feet, the arch is 440 feet high and 180 feet wide.

bing-41667.jpg.title: Red mangrove tree seedlings in Guanahacabibes National Park, Cuba
bing-41667.jpg.headline: All hail the mighty mangrove!. Guanahacabibes National Park, Cuba
bing-41667.jpg.description:
Today we're admiring red mangrove seedlings at Guanahacabibes National Park in Cuba. Mangrove forests not only protect coastlines but are a crucial component of tropical coastal ecosystems and are uniquely suited to thrive in brackish or salty water. These hardy trees can withstand the force of tremendous waves and ferocious winds, fending off the damaging effects of storms and erosion.

Below the surface, they work just as hard: Their complex root systems filter out salt and provide shelter and protection for marine life, encouraging biodiversity. Here in Guanahacabibes, that marine life includes several species of turtles as well as red swamp crayfish and a slew of reptiles and amphibians.

Another reason to tip our hats to the mighty mangroves? They capture up to 10 times more carbon dioxide from the atmosphere than tropical forests do. They're also incredible carbon sinks, storing much more carbon in their roots than their terrestrial counterparts.

bing-41679.jpg.title: Blue-green waters around the Bahamas as seen from the International Space Station
bing-41679.jpg.headline: When life imitates art. The Bahamas as seen from the ISS
bing-41679.jpg.description: The islands of the Bahamas are an easy photo op for astronauts aboard the International Space Station. The massive hills under the water's surface make for striking images when seen from the ISS's vantage point high above Earth. These undersea hills, which appear dark blue in this ocean image, indicate depths that can reach 13,000 feet.

bing-41691.jpg.title: Blackbird in Essex, England
bing-41691.jpg.headline: Days of the blackbird. Blackbird in Essex, England
bing-41691.jpg.description: The end of January in the Northern Hemisphere can be quite cold, as it is near the midpoint of winter. According to Italian folklore, the last three days of January are the coldest of the year and are referred to as the 'days of the blackbird.' One local legend gives a fun take on how blackbirds got their dark feathers: To protect her young chicks from the cold Northern Italian winter, a mother bird with white feathers built her nest in a chimney. After her white chicks emerged from their eggs, their feathers turned black from the chimney's soot, and from that day on, all such birds were born as 'blackbirds.'

bing-41703.jpg.title: Ice and Snow Sailing European Championships on Lake Balaton in Hungary
bing-41703.jpg.headline: Wind-powered ice racing. Ice and Snow Sailing World Championships
bing-41703.jpg.description: Today is the opening day of the WISSA Ice and Snow Sailing World Championships, which take place this year in Lithuania. Iceboating, also known as ice sailing, began in 17th-century Europe. Travelers used vessels on blades to traverse the frozen Gulf of Riga in the Baltic Sea and the iced-over canals of the Netherlands. These days, the sport is enjoyed as a recreational and competitive activity using a variety of boats, boards, skates, and kites. The world championships, which fall under the broader umbrella of windsurfing competitions, have been held since 1980. Good luck to all those out there competing for fame and glory on the windswept ice!

bing-41704.jpg.title: Nagarhole National Park, Karnataka, India
bing-41704.jpg.headline: Nagarhole National Park, Karnataka, India
bing-41704.jpg.description:
Nagarahole Tiger Reserve previously known as Rajiv Gandhi (Nagarahole) National Park, was named after the river ‘Nagarahole’ which literally means ‘Serpent River’ (Nagara=Serpent; Hole=River) in the Kannada language. Nagarahole is an important Tiger Reserve in Karnataka and is a major hub of conservation under Project Tiger and Project Elephant. The protected area supports large gathering of carnivores and herbivores: tiger, leopard, Asiatic wild dog and sloth bear, Asiatic elephant, gaur, sambar, chital, muntjac, Four-horned antelope, wild pig, mouse deer, and South-western langur.

The park comprises of some amazing landscapes and marvelous streams that deviate around like a snake, leaving wildlife enthusiasts and visitors astonished by its natural beauty. It is also considered a World Heritage Site by UNESCO.

bing-41715.jpg.title: Burchell's zebras, Rietvlei Nature Reserve, South Africa
bing-41715.jpg.headline: A dazzling sight. Burchell's zebras for International Zebra Day
bing-41715.jpg.description:
It's International Zebra Day, and we're giving a shout-out to the flashiest animal on the African savanna. It's a day to raise awareness of these distinctive creatures and encourage measures to protect them and their habitat. This group of Burchell's zebras is hanging out at Rietvlei Nature Reserve in South Africa.

The most attention-grabbing feature of a zebra is, of course, those unique stripes. In recent years, researchers have found that the high-contrast patterns of zebra stripes seem to confuse horseflies as they approach, causing them to veer away or bounce off. Horseflies in Africa carry diseases that can be lethal to zebras, so the stripes do a lot more than just make them look fancy.

bing-41720.jpg.title: Olivos centenarios en Deyá, Islas Baleares, España
bing-41720.jpg.headline: Un sitio para dejar volar la imaginación. Deyá, Islas Baleares, España
bing-41720.jpg.description: El poeta y escritor Robert Graves (1895-1985) vivió en Deià, Mallorca. La casa de Graves fue reacondicionada tras su muerte para ser visitada. En la casa de Graves destacan olivos centenarios llenos de historia. Los olivos pueden alcanzar hasta 15 mentros de altura y se han llegado a encontrar olivos con la edad de más de 2000 años. España se considera como uno de los países con más olivos del mundo y con alrededor de un 45 por ciento de producción a nivel mundial de aceite de oliva.

bing-41727.jpg.title: 'Testament: The Little Rock Nine Monument,' Little Rock, Arkansas
bing-41727.jpg.headline: Courage and conviction. Black History Month
bing-41727.jpg.description: They were just high school kids, named Ernest, Elizabeth, Jefferson, Terrence, Carlotta, Minnijean, Gloria, Thelma, and Melba, who made history in 1957 when they became the first Black pupils at their school, in the face of fierce opposition. We start Black History Month here in Little Rock, the state capital of Arkansas, at the Little Rock Nine Monument, named for that group of kids who played an important role in desegregating public schools. Their contributions to the civil rights movement are a moving reminder of how far we've come as a nation, and of how very different life was for Black Americans not so long ago.

bing-41728.jpg.title: Château de Pierrefonds, France
bing-41728.jpg.headline: Château de Pierrefonds
bing-41728.jpg.description: The Château de Pierrefonds is situated in the scenic city of Pierrefonds. It was built in the late fourteenth century by Duke Louis d'Orléans. The original château was in ruins for over two centuries, but today's castle was built in the 19th century when Emperor Napoleon III decided to reconstruct it and use it as his imperial residence. The château features eight towers decorated with sculptures of eight dignified knights and kings, all heroes of the ancient and Middle Ages. The courtyard is composed of various architectural styles, mostly medieval and Renaissance. The château has frequently been used as a location for filming and television series such as Wizards of Waverly Palace. The castle is without a doubt one of the most beautiful castles in the vicinity of Paris.

bing-41739.jpg.title: Alpine marmots in Hohe Tauern National Park, Austria
bing-41739.jpg.headline: Signs of spring?. Groundhog Day
bing-41739.jpg.description: Groundhog Day is a North American tradition with roots in the February 2 Candlemas observance practiced by German immigrants. The most well-known Groundhog Day celebration, in Punxsutawney, Pennsylvania, was first promoted by a local newspaper editor in 1886. Thousands of people gather in Punxsutawney each year to witness the groundhog emerge from its burrow, and more importantly, to see if the critter spots its shadow. If it does, winter will go on for six weeks, according to tradition. If it does not, spring-like conditions are said to be coming. Studies have yet to prove any link between the two events, but that hasn’t cast a shadow over this unusual tradition, which remains as popular as ever in the 21st century.

bing-41751.jpg.title: Château Frontenac, Quebec City, Canada
bing-41751.jpg.headline: Warmly embracing winter. Quebec City for Winter Carnival
bing-41751.jpg.description: Among all the pre-Lenten celebrations that take place around the world in February, the most famous are associated with warm-weather cities like Rio and New Orleans, where revelers party in elaborate costumes during the run-up to Ash Wednesday. It's a different affair in Quebec City, Canada, pictured here, where participants in the Quebec Winter Carnival enjoy all things winter, from snow sculptures to sleigh races. This former frontier outpost, and little sister to Montreal, is known for its spirited embrace of the coldest, darkest season. So, it's no surprise that its winter festival is the biggest in the Western Hemisphere. Our homepage image shows the grandiose Château Frontenac hotel, which opened in 1893, towering over the city's historic Old Quebec neighborhood, a UNESCO World Heritage Site.

bing-41756.jpg.title: Perdices Rojas en la Sierra de Andujar, España
bing-41756.jpg.headline: Perdíz Roja aportando color a la naturaleza. Sierra de Andujar, España
bing-41756.jpg.description: El parque natural de la Sierra de Andújar es un precioso espacio natural protegido situado al noroeste de la provincia de Jaén. Dentro de la flora podemos encontrar el bosque más grande de la Sierra Morena. Dentro de su fauna podemos hallar perdices rojas rondando por estos enormes montes y su espesura. La perdíz roja, a pesar de ser la más común se encuentra en cautividad y puede llegar a los 10 años de vida.

bing-41760.jpg.title: Feldberg Tower in the Black Forest, Baden-Württemberg, Germany
bing-41760.jpg.headline: Best views tower. Feldberg Tower in the Black Forest, Baden-Württemberg, Germany
bing-41760.jpg.description: The Feldberg is called the highest mountain top in the Black Forest. Without a doubt it is the highest peak with its 1493 meters. It offers one of the most extensive panoramic views in Germany, especially in winter when there is a temperature inversion. On its top, there is a 21-meter-high tower with a radar station called the Feldberg tower. It can be comfortably reached in a few minutes with the Feldberg cable car or in around 40 minutes by foot.

bing-41763.jpg.title: Rosa Parks sits in the front of a bus in Montgomery, Alabama, Dec 21, 1956
bing-41763.jpg.headline: Remembering Rosa Parks. Rosa Parks Day
bing-41763.jpg.description:
On Dec 1, 1955, Alabama native Rosa Parks took a stand when she refused to stand. Parks rejected bus driver James F. Blake's order to vacate a seat on a Mongomery bus in favor of a white passenger and was arrested and fined for this act of civil disobedience. Parks then helped lead a boycott of Montgomery buses that lasted for over a year. The year-long protest finally ended when the US Supreme Court ruled that Alabama’s laws enforcing segregation on city buses and other modes of transportation were unconstitutional.

We're remembering Parks on the anniversary of her birth on Feb 4, 1913. Her act of defiance was a pivotal moment in the civil rights struggle. Though some tried to paint the seamstress as an accidental martyr, Parks was already involved in the movement at the time of her arrest. She later said of the incident, 'People always say that I didn't give up my seat because I was tired, but that isn't true. I was not tired physically, or no more tired than I usually was at the end of a working day. I was not old, although some people have an image of me as being old then. I was forty-two. No, the only tired I was, was tired of giving in.'

bing-41775.jpg.title: Monarch butterflies at Pismo Beach, California
bing-41775.jpg.headline: Migration of the monarchs. Monarch butterflies, Pismo Beach, California
bing-41775.jpg.description:
Today we're in Pismo Beach, California, to celebrate one of the best-known species of butterflies—the monarch. Western Monarch Day marks their seasonal migration to California's Central Coast from cold northern locations west of the Rocky Mountains.

A grove of eucalyptus trees at Pismo State Beach creates an optimal microclimate for the butterflies. Thousands arrive in the fall and roost through the winter until March, when they begin to fly north. After traveling a relatively short distance inland, the monarchs stop to mate and lay eggs on milkweed plants. The eggs will hatch after just a few days, eventually transforming into the next generation of adult butterflies to continue the trek. The annual cycle takes four or five generations of monarchs to complete, so the butterflies are following in the path most recently traveled by their great-grandparents (or so).

In recent years, Western monarch butterfly populations have suffered significant declines, due to climate change and loss of overwintering habitats. We can help protect and restore monarch butterflies by planting native milkweed (their primary food source) and other pollinator-friendly plants in our gardens and yards.

bing-41795.jpg.title: Ski hors-piste, Courchevel, France
bing-41795.jpg.headline: Championnats du monde FIS de ski alpin Courchevel Méribel 2023
bing-41795.jpg.description: Le championnat du monde de ski 2023 a débuté hier à Courchevel et à Méribel. Ce championnat est le plus grand événement dans le monde du ski après les Jeux Olympiques. Il a lieu tous les deux ans, les années impaires. Il réunit les meilleurs skieurs alpins féminins et masculins, toutes disciplines confondues. C’est la troisième fois qu’il est organisé en France après Chamonix en 1937 et Val d’Isère en 2009.

bing-41799.jpg.title: Village of Labro, Rieti Province, Italy
bing-41799.jpg.headline: History on the hill. Village of Labro, Italy
bing-41799.jpg.description:
Join us for a journey to a tiny Italian village about 40 miles northeast of Rome. Labro, which covers about 4.4 square miles, was founded sometime between the 9th and 10th centuries and was assigned to a powerful aristocratic family by Emperor Otto the Great. Perched atop a wooded hill, the Nobili-Vitelleschi castle originally served to secure the border and control communication routes in the valley below.

With its panoramic views and historic buildings, Labro is now a popular tourist destination, having been restored for the purpose shortly after World War II, when its existence was threatened by a mass exodus of the population.

bing-41811.jpg.title: Ureddplassen, a rest area on the Helgelandskysten scenic route, Norway
bing-41811.jpg.headline: A place to pause. Uredd Rest Area, Norway
bing-41811.jpg.description:
With sweeping views of fjords, mountains, and the sea, this is possibly one of the most beautiful places in the world to rest when you are on the road. Ureddplassen, also known as Uredd Rest Area, provides a place for respite to travelers on a section of the Helgelandskysten national scenic route in Norway. It also serves as a WWII memorial, sharing its name with a Norwegian submarine which was lost when it hit a German mine in February 1943.

With its minimalist architecture and breath-taking scenery, Ureddplassen offers a visual experience like no other. It has marble benches and steps leading out to the open sea, and a wave-shaped public restroom with frosted glass that lights up beautifully in the dark.

Since its unveiling, the rest area has quickly become a popular tourist destination. Here, visitors and locals can witness the midnight sun in summer and feast their eyes on the northern lights in winter.

bing-41823.jpg.title: Lower Antelope Canyon near Page, Arizona
bing-41823.jpg.headline: Waves of stone. Lower Antelope Canyon, Arizona
bing-41823.jpg.description:
Today we're peering up from the depths of Lower Antelope Canyon, located in Lake Powell Navajo Tribal Park near Page, Arizona. This tall, narrow channel is an entry point into Antelope Canyon, a slot canyon that was created over millions of years by flash floods carving away at the soft Navajo sandstone.

The Navajo name for Lower Antelope Canyon is Hazdistazí (spiral rock arches), but hikers have nicknamed it the Corkscrew for its twists and turns. Visitors shimmy through tight passages and climb up and down ladders to reach the bottom of the chamber. There they find themselves in an almost otherworldly environment, where sunbeams break through to the canyon floor, making the stone walls glow.

Tour guides, managed by the Navajo Nation, are mandatory for visitors to the canyon.

bing-41830.jpg.title: Il castello di Cigognola immerso nella neve, Pavia
bing-41830.jpg.headline: Un castello sulle bianche colline
bing-41830.jpg.description: Il castello di Cigognola sorge in provincia di Pavia, ed è situato nell'Oltrepò Pavese su una collina a 309 metri di altezza. L'edificazione risale all'inizio del XIII secolo, durante il periodo medievale e fu coinvolto in diversi attacchi che miravano ad ottenerne il possesso. La storia racconta che nel 1372, Giovanni Acuto, condottiero e capitano di ventura inglese, ne prese il controllo, acquisendo in tal modo una posizione strategica data l'ottima visuale sulla pianura Padana. Nei decenni successivi, al suo interno si alternarono diverse famiglie aristocratiche dell'epoca come i Sannazzaro, i Beccaria, gli Aicardi e i Visconti fino ai giorni nostri in cui viene utilizzato privatamente da una azienda vitivinicola.

bing-41831.jpg.title: Théâtre antique d'Épidaure, Argolis, Grèce
bing-41831.jpg.headline: Le génie de la Grèce Antique. Théâtre antique d'Épidaure, Argolis, Grèce
bing-41831.jpg.description:
Le théâtre antique d'Épidaure se trouve caché dans les collines d'Épidaure à environ 160 km d'Athènes. Il est dédié au dieu de la médecine de la Grèce antique, Asclépios.

Les 3 principales caractéristiques des théâtres grecques antiques sont :  l’orchestra ou l’autel qui servait de scène principale en forme de cercle, le skene ou scene, utilisé pour les décors et enfin les gradins en demi-cercle appelés cavea ou auditorium

Le théâtre d’Epidaure incarne le génie antique appliqué aux arts du spectacle. C’est une véritable une prouesse d'ingénierie construite à flanc de colline avec une telle précision que le théâtre possède à la fois une acoustique parfaite et une structure pensée pour une vision optimale du spectacle. Depuis 1954, le théâtre accueille des représentations théâtrales et musicales avec des acteurs grecs ou internationaux célèbres, il peut accueillir plus de 14.000 spectateurs.

bing-41843.jpg.title: Temple chinois Fête du Citron de 2015, Menton, Cote d'Azur, France
bing-41843.jpg.headline: Un festival unique au monde !. Fête du Citron, Menton, Côte d’azur, France
bing-41843.jpg.description:
La ville de Menton accueille chaque année le Festival du Citron. Cette fête, appelée aussi Carnaval de Menton, est unique au monde. Tous les chars et sculptures présentés sont créés à partir de citrons et d'oranges pour célébrer la production de l’année.

C’est un hôtelier qui a eu l’idée en 1929 d’organiser une exposition de fleurs et d’agrumes dans les jardins de l’Hôtel Riviera. Le succès est immense et la fête est reprise dans la rue de la ville pour attirer les touristes. La première fête du Citron a eu lieu en 1934. Le carnaval est depuis reconnu et inscrit par le ministère de la Culture à l'inventaire du patrimoine culturel immatériel français en 2019.

L’édition 2023 débute aujourd’hui jusqu’au 26 février sur le thème « Rock et de l’Opéra », courez-y !

bing-41879.jpg.title: Igloo décoré pour le festival du chemin de neige et de lumière d’Otaru, Hokkaido, Japon
bing-41879.jpg.headline: C’est l’amour à la neige !. C’est la Saint Valentin !
bing-41879.jpg.description:
Aujourd’hui, nous célébrons l'amour ! La Saint-Valentin est l'une des fêtes les plus populaires au monde. Bien que son origine exacte ne soit pas connue, elle a souvent été associée à diverses festivités anciennes comme les Lupercales en Italie ou la fête du Saint du même nom, Valentin.

Et pourquoi ne pas le célébrer dans cet endroit merveilleux que nous avons choisi : le festival du chemin de neige et de lumière d’Otaru au Japon. Chaque année, la petite ville s’éclaire à la lueur des bougies et des lanternes disposées sur le chemin du canal de la ville. Près de 500 000 visiteurs y participent chaque année.

bing-41891.jpg.title: Une maman hippopotame et son bébé, parc national de Chobe, Botswana
bing-41891.jpg.headline: Journée mondiale de l’hippopotame
bing-41891.jpg.description:
Nous célébrons aujourd’hui la journée mondiale de l’hippopotame, l’un des animaux les plus impressionnants de la planète. Il nous donne l’image d’un animal statique, voire pataud, et c’est pourtant tout le contraire ! Saviez-vous qu’il peut atteindre 30 km/h en cas de danger ?

On le reconnaît entre mille avec sa silhouette arrondie et ses pattes un peu trop courtes. L’hippopotame peut peser plus de 3 tonnes, mesurer de 1,5 mètre de hauteur et 5 mètres de long. C’est un herbivore et il vit la plupart du temps dans l’eau. Enfin, il peut vivre jusqu’à 40 ans à l’état sauvage.

Malheureusement, l’hippopotame est une espèce vulnérable. La perte de leur habitat naturel, le braconnage et l’activité humaine grandissante les menace.

bing-41900.jpg.title: Encinas y amapolas en la dehesa, La Serena, Badajoz, España
bing-41900.jpg.headline: Los colores brotan en la dehesa. Dehesa en La Serena, Badajoz, España
bing-41900.jpg.description:
Extremadura cuenta con casi un millón de hectáreas de dehesa, zonas que componen un espectáculo ecológico repleto de flora y fauna. Las dehesas son conocidas por albergar encinas que producen las famosas bellotas para alimentar los cerdos ibéricos. Además, la madera de las encinas es bastante fuerte, por lo que es utilizada para utensilios que deban soportar una gran resistencia.

Estas praderas tan cuidadas son idóneas para la aparición de flores como amapolas o caléndulas que a menudo dejan bonitas estampas en primavera. No obstante, en invierno son cubiertas por un manto blanco de nieve, ofreciendo una bonita fotografía invernal.

bing-41901.jpg.title: Industriekletterer besteigen den Berlinale-Bären im Kino Zoo-Palast, Berlin
bing-41901.jpg.headline: Ein Fest für den Film. Berlinale
bing-41901.jpg.description:
Die 73. Ausgabe der internationalen Filmfestspiele in Berlin, auch bekannt als Berlinale, findet dieses Jahr vom 16. bis 26. Februar statt. Es gilt neben Venedig (1932) und Cannes (1946) als eines der "großen drei" Filmfestivals. In diesem Jahr wird auch ein Preis für die beste Fernsehserie vergeben.

Kirsten Stewart wird den Vorsitz der Jury übernehmen und das Festival wird mit dem Drama "She came to me" von Rebecca Miller eröffnet. Steven Spielberg wird auf dem Festival mit einer besonderen Hommage geehrt, indem ihm der Goldene Ehrenbär für sein Lebenswerk verliehen wird und seine Filme in der Sektion Hommage gezeigt werden.

bing-41912.jpg.title: Carroza de carnaval con un pavo real dorado. Santa Cruz de Tenerife, España
bing-41912.jpg.headline: Celebrando el carnaval de la mano del arte. Carroza de carnaval en Santa Cruz de Tenerife, España
bing-41912.jpg.description:
En febrero, las calles de España se tiñen del color de los disfraces, las carrozas y las comparsas de algunos de los carnavales más icónicos del mundo y que han sido declarados Fiesta de Interés Turístico Internacional. Podemos destacar los de Santa Cruz de Tenerife, Cádiz o Águilas como algunas de las ciudades que albergan los más famosos a nivel nacional.

Si te encuentras por el centro de Santa Cruz de Tenerife no podrás evitar fijarte en las enormes y coloridas carrozas que, después de ser trabajadas durante todo el año, son exhibidas en este espectacular evento. Por otro lado, si te decantas por visitar Cádiz, en la comunidad de Andalucía, podrás disfrutar de sus ingeniosas chirigotas, canciones típicas de carnaval con temáticas satíricas. Si lo que quieres es disfrutar de máscaras, disfraces y personajes mitológicos, Águilas, en Murcia, es tu elección.

bing-41914.jpg.title: Parco Nazionale del Gran Sasso, chiesa Madonna della Pietà, L'Aquila
bing-41914.jpg.headline: La chiesa sul Gran Sasso
bing-41914.jpg.description: La chiesa della Madonna della Pietà sorge sulla sommità del colle del Gran Sasso in Abruzzo, nella piazza del vecchio centro abitato. Ha un impianto ottagonale preceduto da un colonnato e risulta rialzata rispetto al piano della piazza. Si stima che la prima costruzione risalga al secolo XII ‐ XIII e successivamente nel XVIII ‐ XVIII fu effettuato un rifacimento della facciata inserendo delle rielaborazioni in sintonia con quello che era lo stile dell'epoca. Il terremoto del 2009 ne ha compromesso la stabilità, rendendo di fatto la struttura inagibile.

bing-41915.jpg.title: Les toits de Paris sous la neige
bing-41915.jpg.headline: Connaissez-vous les toits de Paris ?. Connaissez-vous l'histoire des toits de Paris ?
bing-41915.jpg.description:
Le Baron Haussmann, architecte de Napoléon III, entreprit au 19e siècle un chantier titanesque pour repenser la ville de Paris. Il dessine de grandes avenues, des immeubles dont le style porte aujourd’hui son nom, et il installe, entre autres, les égouts. Pour les toitures, il choisit un matériau plus économique, le zinc.

Les artisans couvreurs sont de nos jours en charge de leur restauration, ils ont un savoir-faire unique. D’autre part, pour préserver cet héritage exceptionnel, une candidature a été déposée pour faire entrer les toits de Paris au Patrimoine Mondial de l'UNESCO.

bing-41927.jpg.title: Eben grotte de glace, Michigan, USA
bing-41927.jpg.headline: Un spectacle à couper le souffle. Eben, grotte de glace dans l'état américain du Michigan
bing-41927.jpg.description:
Les grottes de glace d'Eben sont visibles uniquement pendant la période hivernale. Le reste de l’année, on y trouve des falaises de grès et des cèdres. Les grottes se forment avec la baisse des températures glaciales, l’eau coule sur les falaises du canyon et se transforme en glace de couleur jaune.

Les visiteurs peuvent marcher dans l’espace créé entre les falaises et les murs de glace qui s’étendent sur 15 mètres. Pour y accéder, assurez-vous de porter des crampons ou de bonnes chaussures de randonnée, et surtout, prenez garde aux animaux sauvages ! En effet, seul 3 % de la population vit dans cette partie du Michigan. La région a une faune très riche avec, entre autres, des ours, des élans et des loups.

bing-41951.jpg.title: Voie lactée au-dessus de Zabriskie Point, Vallée de la Mort, Californie
bing-41951.jpg.headline: Un ciel plein d'étoiles. Voie lactée au-dessus de Zabriskie Point
bing-41951.jpg.description:
Les photographes et les touristes du monde entier affluent pour admirer la vue emblématique de Zabriskie Point. Le temps et l'eau ont sculpté ces paysages pendant des siècles. La roche sombre sur les crêtes a été formée par de la lave d'une ancienne éruption volcanique, lui donnant ainsi cet aspect lunaire unique.

Niché dans le parc national de la Vallée de la Mort, Zabriskie Point a servi de décor à d'innombrables films comme "Spartacus" ou encore "Stars Wars". Il figure aussi en couverture de l'album mythique du groupe de rock irlandais U2, "The Joshua Tree".

En ce moment, et jusqu'au 26 février, le parc accueille comme tous les ans, le « Death Valley Dark Skies Festival ». Les visiteurs viennent y explorer le ciel nocturne pour résoudre, qui sait, les grands mystères de l’Univers.

bing-41956.jpg.title: Itaimbezinho canyon
bing-41956.jpg.headline: Itaimbezinho canyon, Brazil
bing-41956.jpg.description: The Itaimbezinho canyon is a beautiful landscape located in Brazil. The canyon is now a part of Aparados da Serra National Park, a national park which was established to protect the canyon itself. The Itaimbezhino canyon is almost 170 kilometres from Porto Alegre, the capital city of Rio Grande do Sul, the largest city in the state of Brazil. The canyon is surrounded by rich flora and fauna and is a treat for nature lovers. It has many spots where one can enjoy the views, such as Morro dos Cabritos.

bing-41976.jpg.title: Royal Albert Hall at night, South Kensington, London.
bing-41976.jpg.headline: Last night of the Proms
bing-41976.jpg.description:
London’s Royal Albert Hall will reverberate with music later as it hosts the Last Night of the Proms, bringing the curtain down on eight weeks of daily classical music concerts, a summer tradition since 1895. Expect flags, glitzy dresses, tuxedos and Union Flag hats as a medley of British singalongs from Rule Britannia to Jerusalem are belted out by “Prommers”. The flag-waving might not be everyone’s cup of tea but its fans describe it as the world’s greatest classical music festival, bringing the classics to the widest possible audience.

Most of the Proms concerts are hosted here at the Grade I listed Royal Albert Hall, one of the UK’s most recognisable buildings. Opened in 1871 by Queen Victoria, who named it after her late husband, Prince Albert, its design was inspired by the amphitheatres of Ancient Rome. The civil engineers who designed it succeeded in creating a structurally sound and visually striking building but from the start, its main auditorium was plagued by an echo that became infamous.

Various fixes were attempted but it wasn’t until the 1960s when acoustic diffusing discs, nicknamed mushrooms, were installed on the ceiling that things really improved. They’ve been upgraded since but were so successful they were also used at the Sydney Opera House. The Royal Albert Hall has retained its place as the nation’s home of live performances be they rock concerts, boxing matches or the annual Festival of Remembrance.

bing-41980.jpg.title: Peace bell on the summit of Fichtelberg, Saxony, Germany
bing-41980.jpg.headline: Peace bell on the summit of Fichtelberg, Germany
bing-41980.jpg.description: The Fichtelberg is a mountain located in Saxony, Germany, in the Ore Mountain range. It is the highest mountain in Saxony, standing almost 1215 metres above sea level. This mountain is frequented by skiers going downhill and cyclists going up to the top while enjoying the surrounding scenic beauty. The Fichtelberg is home to many rare species of mountain plants such as the small white orchid and alpine clubmoss. A beautiful peace bell is located at the summit of this mountain, a perfect location to ring out over the valleys below.

bing-41987.jpg.title: Paris, France
bing-41987.jpg.headline: Paris ville lumière. Paris, France
bing-41987.jpg.description:
Au crépuscule, la ville de Paris s'illumine. Les rues et les bâtiments sont baignés de lumière, tout comme les grands monuments comme la tour Eiffel.  Sous son règne, le roi Louis XIV a demandé que des réverbères soient installés dans toute la ville afin que la police puisse attraper facilement les bandits dans les ruelles sombres. Les habitants ont également été invités à installer des lanternes, des lampes à huile et des bougies à leurs fenêtres.

Aujourd'hui, la Ville Lumière est une destination de rêve pour les voyageurs à la recherche de musées, de cuisine et d'un cadre romantique. La ville a beaucoup d'histoire à offrir avec ses jardins splendides, ses monuments, ses catacombes et plus encore, avec des quantités de choses à apprendre sur la riche culture française et parisienne.

bing-42023.jpg.title: Reproductions fresques de la Grotte de Chauvet, Ardèche, France
bing-42023.jpg.headline: Voyage au cœur du paléolithique. Fresques de la Grotte de Chauvet en Ardèche
bing-42023.jpg.description:
Découverte le 18 décembre 1994, la grotte s'est imposée comme l'un des plus grands chefs-d'œuvre de l'art paléolithique. Elle date de l'Aurignacien, soir environ – 35.000 ans avant JC. Cette grotte est très fragile et inaccessible au public. Pour la préserver, des ingénieurs et des artistes ont reconstitué les parois de cette grotte à l’identique, elle est appelée « Chauvet 2 Ardèche ».

La visite de cette grotte est extraordinaire. Dans un jeu d’ombres et de lumière, les œuvres se révèlent peints à l’ocre rouge, gravés au silex, tracés au doigt ou au fusain. Des centaines d’animaux, de quinze espèces différentes apparaissent : 27 panneaux, des centaines d’animaux, de quinze espèces différentes apparaissent, la grande fresque des lions de 12 mètres de long ponctue la visite.

Depuis sa découverte, la grotte de Chauvet est l’une des trois plus importantes au monde avec Altamira et Lascaux.

bing-42044.jpg.title: Figura de bronce de un abuelo y su nieto cuidando de las plantas y las flores, Córdoba, España
bing-42044.jpg.headline: Día de Andalucía. Patio cordobés, Córdoba, España
bing-42044.jpg.description:
Cada 28 de febrero se celebra el día de Andalucía. Una fecha conmemorativa que celebra el aniversario del referéndum que dio a Andalucía plena autonomía y que es considerado como día festivo en dicha comunidad.

Más allá de los diferentes actos institucionales que se celebran este día en Andalucía, muchas ciudades festejan este día con concursos de patios andaluces, toda una tradición de la comunidad que llena de color, felicidad y alegría cada rincón de sus ciudades.

bing-42056.jpg.title: Vista aérea de barcos, yates de lujo y mar transparente en un día soleado en Mallorca, España
bing-42056.jpg.headline: Día de las Islas Baleares. Calas en Mallorca, España
bing-42056.jpg.description: Cada año, el día 1 de marzo se celebra el día de las Islas Baleares, conmemorando así la inclusión en el BOE, allá por 1983, del Estatuto de Autonomía de Baleares. A partir de ese día, el archipiélago balear pasó a ser una Comunidad Autónoma más. Este día, festivo local, es una ocasión perfecta para poder disfrutar de las playas y calas paradisíacas que ofrecen las cinco islas que conforman las Islas Baleares.

bing-42108.jpg.title: Le jardin de Monet à Giverny, France
bing-42108.jpg.headline: Bonne fête à nos grands-mères !. Jardin de Monet à Giverny en Normandie
bing-42108.jpg.description:
La fête des grands-mères a été créée en 1987 par la marque de café « Grand'Mère ». Même si cette journée n’était pas au début une fête officielle du calendrier, sinon commerciale, elle a été finalement adoptée par les Français. Alors pourquoi ne pas emmener votre grand-mère découvrir ce merveilleux jardin de Claude Monet pour célébrer sa journée ?

Très célèbre pour son étang, ses nymphéas et son pont japonais, le jardin de Claude Monet est une explosion de couleurs à visiter en toute saison. Le peintre et jardinier y a vécu pendant plus de quarante ans jusqu'à sa mort en 1926.

bing-42112.jpg.title: Cherry trees in full bloom near the Imperial Palace with Tokyo Tower in the background, Tokyo, Japan
bing-42112.jpg.headline: Spring blossoms in Tokyo. Cherry blossom season in Tokyo
bing-42112.jpg.description:
Each spring, folks across Japan observe 'hanami,' a treasured tradition of viewing nature's breathtaking display of cherry blossoms. Japanese cherry trees, known as 'sakura,' reach full bloom in March in the south of the country. Our homepage picture shows cherry blossoms cascading over the moats which surround the Imperial Palace in Tokyo.

Blooms progress northward throughout March and April, with the final flowerings gracing the slow-to-thaw Hokkaido prefecture as the season ends. To help people seek out the best displays, the Japanese Meteorological Agency carefully tracks the 'cherry blossom front' across the island nation. This year, the earliest blooms are expected to start flowering in Tokyo on or around March 16.

bing-42130.jpg.title: Parktheater im Kurhaus Göggingen, Architekt Jean Keller, Bayern
bing-42130.jpg.headline: Kurhaus Göggingen. Parktheater im Kurhaus Göggingen
bing-42130.jpg.description:
Das Kurhaus Göggingen wurde vom deutschen Architekten Jean Keller zwischen 1885 und 1886 gebaut. Dieses architektonische Wunderwerk ist das einzige Multifunktionstheater aus der Gründerzeit, welches erhalten blieb.

Nach der Fertigstellung des Baus konnte sich das Gögginger Kurhaus rühmen, sowohl einen Wintergarten als auch ein Theater mit Orchestergraben zu besitzen. Zu dieser Zeit hatten nur Paris, Leipzig und Blackpool so etwas zu bieten. Heute ist es in seiner Art einzigartig.

Nach dem Zweiten Weltkrieg verfiel der Kurort. Im Oktober 1972 geriet das Kurhaus in Brand. Es war zwar ein tragisches Ereignis, aber es führte zur Wiedergeburt dieses Ortes. Obwohl es mehr als zwanzig Jahre dauerte, wurde das Kurhaus Göggingen 1998 wieder instand gesetzt und dient heute als Veranstaltungsort für Theateraufführungen, Konzerte, Tagungen, Bälle, Konferenzen und Hochzeitsfeiern. Heute kann man unter der Woche von 9 bis 18 Uhr das Kurhaus kostenlos besichtigen. Sie können sich auch in das gemütliche Restaurant setzen und entspannen. Wenn Sie das Kurhaus in den Wintermonaten besuchen sollten, dürfen Sie auf keinen Fall den klassischen Weihnachtsmarkt verpassen.

bing-42135.jpg.title: Cabins in Valley Forge National Historic Site, Pennsylvania
bing-42135.jpg.headline: Winter at Valley Forge. Winter at Valley Forge, Pennsylvania
bing-42135.jpg.description: Valley Forge, famous for its role in the U.S. Revolutionary War as a winter refuge in 1777-78, became the first state park in Pennsylvania in 1893 and later gifted as a national historical park on July 4, 1976 during the U.S. Bicentennial celebration. It was chosen by General George Washington for its proximity to British-held Philadelphia and various supply points, and the fact that it’s situated on a plateau which could be more easily defended than other locations in the area. If it were a city, it would have been the fourth largest by the time it was fully populated in 1778. Today, the U.S. National Historic Landmark includes Washington’s headquarters, log cabins remade with materials that would have been used during that fateful winter, memorial chapel, arch, observation tower, and walking tours. If history isn’t your thing, you can also hike, bike, canoe, kayak, and ride horses for an invigorating visit to this iconic refuge.

bing-42167.jpg.title: Veduta aerea di Castel del Monte, Andria
bing-42167.jpg.headline: La fortezza di Federico II
bing-42167.jpg.description: La fortezza di Castel del Monte fu fatta costruire da Federico II di Svevia nel XIII secolo sulla sommità di una collina la cui altezza è 540 m. Nel 1996 è stato inserito nell’elenco dei Patrimoni dell’umanità UNESCO. Secondo le varie testimonianze che ci sono pervenute, la fortezza sembra essere stata edificata nei pressi di una precedente chiesa di Santa Maria del Monte che non esiste più e sulle rovine di precedenti fortificazioni di età diverse attribuibili ai longobardi e ai normanni. Durante il corso della sua lunga esistenza, questo complesso ha anche ospitato un carcere. I materiali con cui è stato costruito sono essenzialmente tre: la pietra calcarea, con cui sono state realizzate le strutture architettoniche, il marmo bianco usato per le decorazioni e la breccia corallina che dona colore alla struttura.

bing-42190.jpg.title: Nahaufnahme von Gerste und Kornblumen, Nordhausen
bing-42190.jpg.headline: Ein Feld voller Blumen. Pflanz-eine-Blume-Tag
bing-42190.jpg.description: Mit der Ankunft des lang ersehnten Frühlings widmen wir diesen Tag den Blumen und insbesondere dem Pflanzen einer Blume. Eine Blume zu pflanzen ist gut für die Gesundheit, den Geist, die Seele und den Körper. Und es ist auch gut für unseren geliebten Planeten Erde. Nach den langen Wintermonaten, inmitten von Kälte, Dunkelheit und Melancholie, gibt es keine bessere Art und Weise, eine der schönsten Jahreszeiten des Jahres zu beginnen!

bing-42203.jpg.title: Quartieri Spagnoli, Napoli, Italia
bing-42203.jpg.headline: Il quartiere ha un che di esotico
bing-42203.jpg.description: Un famoso detto recita:” Vedi Napoli e poi muori”. Prima di passare a miglior vita, i Quartieri Spagnoli di Napoli sono una tappa obbligata. Facenti parte del centro storico più grande d’Europa, vennero eretti come accampamento temporaneo per la truppe iberiche durante la dominazione spagnola. Appaiono oggi come uno spettacolare dedalo di vicoli e viuzze, ove chiese e palazzi si sovrappongono a vicenda come nel più bello dei quadri. Le botteghe degli artigiani e ristoratori donano ulteriore linfa vitale ai quartieri, con il loro viavai di turisti ansiosi di provare i prodotti locali.

bing-42215.jpg.title: Las Fallas, Día de San José, Denia, Alicante, Comunidad Valenciana, España
bing-42215.jpg.headline: Fiesta de Las Fallas en Valencia. Las Fallas, Día de San José, Denia, Alicante, Comunidad Valenciana, España
bing-42215.jpg.description:
Las Fallas son una celebración que se festeja en la provincia de Valencia, y comienza el último domingo de febrero en honor a San José, patrón de los carpinteros. Este evento es considerado fiesta de Interés Turístico Internacional y la Unesco la inscribió en su Lista Representativa del Patrimonio Cultural Inmaterial de la Humanidad.

El origen de Las Fallas nace en una tradición que comenzaron los carpinteros la noche del 19 de marzo, para dar comienzo a la primavera. La tradición consistía en quemar fuera de sus talleres una pieza que sostenía los candiles que los habían acompañado durante todo el invierno. Esta tradición fue cobrando mayor importancia al evolucionar dichas piezas a figuras gigantes con grandes presupuestos, conocidas hoy por el nombre valenciano de “Ninot”.

Dentro de la indumentaria tradicional valenciana nos encontramos con los trajes de falleras, que representan la vestimenta típica para las mujeres en esta festividad, tal y como vemos en nuestra imagen. Estos preciosos trajes bordados, coloridos y majestuosos son un icono de la moda valenciana, que son un reflejo de estos días tan emotivos para la provincia.

bing-42264.jpg.title: Mur peint des écrivains, Lyon, France
bing-42264.jpg.headline: Semaine de la Francophonie. Semaine de la langue française et de la francophonie 2023
bing-42264.jpg.description:
La semaine de la langue française et de la francophonie célèbre la langue française à travers de nombreuses animations organisées partout en France et à l'étranger.  L’Organisation internationale de la Francophonie (OIF) représente un ensemble unique qui, à partir du lien de la langue commune, développe une coopération politique, éducative, économique et culturelle entre ses pays membres, au service des populations.

Saviez-vous que, sans être la langue la plus parlée, le français est la langue la plus enseignée après l'anglais ? D’après l'Observatoire de la langue française, c’est la 5e langue la plus parlée après l'anglais, le chinois, l’indi et l'espagnol. Elle compte 321 millions de locuteurs sur les cinq continents.

bing-42273.jpg.title: Pingüinos emperadores, Bahía Atka, Antártida
bing-42273.jpg.headline: Día del padre. Pingüinos emperadores en la Bahía Atka, Antártida
bing-42273.jpg.description:
El día del padre es una celebración en honor a todos los padres y reconocida en todo el mundo, sin embargo, en la religión católica europea, se celebra el día de San José, padre de Jesús.

Algunas de las tradiciones de este día se caracterizan por organizar comidas familiares, realizar alguna excursión en familia o incluso los más pequeños preparan regalos hechos a mano. De esta forma tan bella se les agradecen todas sus labores y responsabilidades como progenitor.

En la imagen de hoy, tenemos un par de pingüinos emperadores machos cuidando de una cría y un huevo a punto de eclosionar. Los pingüinos macho son los responsables de incubar y proteger a los huevos mientras la hembra sale a cazar. Una vez el huevo eclosiona, las obligaciones y cuidados se reparten hasta que la cría es independiente.

bing-42274.jpg.title: Erlebnisholzkugel, Steinberg am See, Bayern
bing-42274.jpg.headline: Die Welt in einer Kugel. Erlebnisholzkugel, Steinberg am See, Bayern
bing-42274.jpg.description:
Lieben Sie die freie Natur und sind Sie ein Abenteuerfan? Haben Sie schon einmal von der Erlebnisholzkugel am Steinberg am See etwas gehört? Wenn nicht, müssen Sie diese unbedingt besuchen. Abgesehen von der spektakulären Natur, die die Erlebnisholzkugel umgibt, ist dieser Ort perfekt, um ein paar Tage oder auch nur ein paar Stunden mit Familie und Freunden zu verbringen. Wenn Sie Kinder haben, werden diese am meisten Spaß haben. Frischen Luft, sie können klettern gehen und am See schwimmen.

Natürlich gibt es auch für Sie die Möglichkeit, sich zu erholen und kurz zu verschnaufen. Wenn Sie nicht unbedingt gerne Klettern oder Schwimmen, können Sie sich ja ein Bier bestellen, zurücklehnen und die frische Luft im Herzen Bayerns genießen.

bing-42280.jpg.title: Barn owl, England
bing-42280.jpg.headline: Whooo's the wisest of them all?. Barn owl, England
bing-42280.jpg.description: Barn owls, distinguished by their white heart-shaped faces, are one of the world's most widespread birds, found on every continent except Antarctica. They live in woodlands, farms, and on cliffs, but barn owls also enjoy roosting in places like bell towers and barns—hence the name. They are nighttime predators that fly over open lands to hunt rats and mice. During heavy rain, they are unable to hunt because their feathers aren't waterproof, leaving them vulnerable to starvation during long periods of wet weather. Although some see them as a symbol of wisdom and fortune, their haunting cries and ghostly appearance mean they have often been seen as bad omens in rural areas.

bing-42329.jpg.title: Gorges du Fier, Haute-Savoie, France
bing-42329.jpg.headline: Gorges du Fier, France
bing-42329.jpg.description:
Today, we are leaving for one of the most unmissable sites in Haute-Savoie: the Gorges du Fier which, in our image, are immobilized by the striking winter. Resulting from the millennial erosion of water on the rock, the Fier runs through a narrow passage between two steep walls almost 50 metres high. It took no less than 20,000 years to achieve the result we know today. The places, listed since 1943, attract many nature lovers and hikers. The visit to the gorges remains relatively easy because half of it takes place on secure footbridges located about 25 meters from the bed of the torrent.

In addition to the view, the humid atmosphere, the play of light and backlighting on the mossy stones and the sound of the torrent below, this visit is also an opportunity for visitors to admire the rocks sculpted by Mother Nature. Incredible potholes and other geological features line the route and remind us of the power of water.

bing-42335.jpg.title: Teatro La Fenice, Venezia
bing-42335.jpg.headline: Dalle ceneri...al prossimo spettacolo!
bing-42335.jpg.description:
“Come una fenice risorgerò dalle mie ceneri” recita una famosa citazione. È questo il caso del Teatro della Fenice di Venezia, uno dei più rinomati del globo. Inaugurato nel 1792 per poi venir distrutto e riedificato per ben due volte, è stato loco delle prime di famosissimi artisti del calibro di Giuseppe Verdi, Vincenzo Bellini e Gioachino Rossini.  L'interno è contraddistinto da una vasta scalinata che precede la facciata edificata in stile neoclassico, con quattro colonne corinzie, alla cui sommità è ubicata una balaustra. Nelle nicchie sono presenti magnifiche sculture raffigiranti la Danza e la Musica,  sovrastate da rilievi con maschere. Nel fregio, in posizione centrale, troviamo infine la Fenice.   La due sale, note come Apollinea e del Teatro, ospitano ogni anno il tradizionale Concerto di Capodanno di Venezia. Manifestazione tenutasi, a porte chiuse e unicamente in diretta televisiva, anche nel 2021 durante la pandemia.

Se la cultura è immortale, questa struttura ne è la prova assoluta.

bing-42347.jpg.title: Basilica di San Francesco d’Assisi
bing-42347.jpg.headline: Le luci della sera sulla Basilica
bing-42347.jpg.description:
L’imponente Basilica di San Francesco sorge su una collina della cittadina umbra e deve il suo nome al santo Francesco a cui è dedicata. Sembra che sia stato lo stesso Francesco ad indicare il luogo in cui avrebbe voluto fossero poste le sue spoglie mortali, ovvero la collina inferiore in cui per tradizione venivano seppelliti gli uomini che vivevano al di fuori della legge e i condannati. L’inizio dei lavori avvenne il 15 luglio del 1228, su volontà di Papa Gregorio IX, che insieme a frate Elia da Cortona, uno dei primi seguaci di Francesco, posero la prima pietra. La Basilica, quindi, svolge un duplice ruolo, ovvero accoglie la tomba del Santo e allo stesso tempo ospita la chiesa madre dell'Ordine fondato dal poverello di Assisi, come viene popolarmente definito.

La Basilica è formata da due chiese sovrapposte, costruite con stili architettonici differenti: in quella inferiore è custodito il sarcofago di Francesco, mentre in quella superiore si trovano superlativi affreschi realizzati da artisti del calibro di Cimabue e Giotto, che furono danneggiati dal terremoto del 1997 e successivamente quasi totalmente ricostruiti. Questi tesori artistici sono ogni anno meta di centinaia di migliaia di devoti pellegrini o semplici turisti e visitatori.

bing-42377.jpg.title: New York City skyline in fog
bing-42377.jpg.headline: Cloud City. New York City skyline
bing-42377.jpg.description:
New York City's skyline is instantly recognizable, even when half-covered in fog. Eight of the United States' 10 tallest buildings reside there, all in the borough of Manhattan. One of New York City's most famous landmarks, the Empire State Building, was the world's tallest building for 41 years.

When it was completed in 1931, it towered over New York City's skyline, the first building in the world to be more than 100 stories tall. But in the decades since, it has been joined by scores of other skyscrapers and is now the Big Apple's seventh-tallest building. While it may have been overtaken by some of its younger neighbors, the Empire State Building remains one of the most iconic features of New York's skyline, if you can see it through the fog.

bing-42475.jpg.title: 杭州西湖水墨意境般的风景，浙江省，中国
bing-42475.jpg.headline: 水墨西湖
bing-42475.jpg.description:
清明节，又称踏青节、行清节、三月节、祭祖节等，节期在仲春与暮春之交。清明节，兼具自然与人文两大内涵，既是“二十四节气”之一，也是传统祭祖节日。清明这一节气，万物皆洁齐、生气旺盛、吐故纳新、气温升高，大地呈现春和景明之象，正是郊外踏青春游与行清墓祭的好时节。

今天，我们图片中为大家带来的是闻名天下的杭州西湖美景。西湖及周边分布着100多处公园景点，历代有“西湖十景”“新西湖十景”“三评西湖十景”之说，西湖十景系列景观涉及了春夏秋冬、晨晌昏夜、晴雾风雪、花鸟虫鱼等关于季节、时节、气象、动植物的景观特色，以及堤、岛、桥、亭、台、楼、阁、园林、宅院、寺塔等较为丰富的景观元素，并各有侧重地表现出或生动、或静谧、或隐逸、闲逸、冷寂、禅境等审美意境。反映了中国古代文化艺术中诗、画、景在审美和哲学层面上的有机结合。

bing-42508.jpg.title: Baby Eurasian beavers, Finland
bing-42508.jpg.headline: Saluting beavers. International Beaver Day
bing-42508.jpg.description:
Behold the mighty beaver, nature's engineer. They fell trees with their massive orange incisors, using the wood to build two main structures, the dam, which creates a pond in which they can build their living quarters—the lodge. A beaver uses a lodge to hide from predators, store food, rest, and protect their offspring.

The lodge usually has an underwater entrance—an extra element of protection from predators like wolves and coyotes. This underwater entry is no problem for beavers, which can hold their breath for up to 15 minutes. Their paddle-shaped tails help them swim, and to slap the water's surface or the ground to warn other beavers of danger. Let's salute these marvelous mammals today on International Beaver Day.

bing-42515.jpg.title: Il Pantheon di Roma, Lazio, Italia
bing-42515.jpg.headline: L’occhio degli dei
bing-42515.jpg.description:
Il Pantheon di Roma è un edificio antico costruito in epoca romana. Si trova nel centro di Roma, nel Rione Pigna, a pochi passi da Piazza Navona. Fu eretto il 27 a. C. da Marco Agrippa, come anche inciso nel fregio del monumento. Fu costruito come tempio per le divinità pagane dell’Antica Roma. Venne poi, in epoca successiva convertito in una chiesa cattolica e in mausoleo. Vi si possono trovare le tombe di Umberto I. e Vittorio Emanuele II.

Uno degli aspetti più affascinanti di questo edificio è la sua cupola aperta, chiamata oculo, che permette la circolazione dell’aria all’interno dell’edificio. La cupola aperta è dovuta a motivi tecnici, visto che crollerebbe a causa del peso eccessivo. Ha anche un valore simbolico però, perché avrebbe permesso ai fedeli di poter comunicare direttamente con gli dei.  Tornando all’oculo, questo, quando piove, scaturisce una sorta di “effetto camino”. Una corrente d’aria interna fa si che le gocce della pioggia non entrino, o perlomeno si frantumino. C’è anche un altro motivo però. I fori di drenaggio all’interno del Pantheon impediscono la formazione di pozzanghere.

bing-42517.jpg.title: House of Parliament on the Thames, London, UK
bing-42517.jpg.headline: History in the making. House of Parliament, London, UK
bing-42517.jpg.description:
The Houses of Parliament, famous as The Palace of Westminster, is an important symbol of the United Kingdom’s democratic system, and it has played a crucial role in shaping the country’s history. The building has survived numerous wars and disasters, including a major fire in 1834, and remains a significant landmark in London and a popular destination for visitors from around the world.

It’s famous for its iconic clock tower, known as Big Ben, which is one of the most recognisable landmarks in London. Visitors can take guided tours of the building, including the historic Westminster Hall, the House of Commons, the House of Lords chambers, and the Queen's Robing Room.

bing-42520.jpg.title: The Giant's Causeway, County Antrim, Northern Ireland
bing-42520.jpg.headline: In the footsteps of giants. The Giant's Causeway, Northern Ireland
bing-42520.jpg.description:
Throughout history, humans have crafted legends to explain natural phenomena that defy our understanding. A prime example is the Giant's Causeway in Northern Ireland where some 40,000 basalt columns spring from the ground at the shore. Scientists tell us these columns developed 50 to 60 million years ago, when lava erupted from volcanic fissures, then cooled and contracted, cracking into hexagonal structures.

But Gaelic legend tells a different tale. It says the giant Fionn mac Cumhaill, anglicized as Finn McCool, built a bridge across the sea to fight his Scottish giant counterpart, Benandonner. The remains of his bridge are said to be found in the Giant's Causeway on one side, and Fingal's Cave on the Scottish island of Staffa, also formed by basalt columns. Though we understand the geology of the Giant's Causeway now, some may prefer to picture giants striding across the sea.

bing-42532.jpg.title: Lithuanian Easter eggs
bing-42532.jpg.headline: Happy Easter!
bing-42532.jpg.description:
Humans have been decorating eggs for Easter for centuries, but decorated ostrich eggs have been found from as far back as 60,000 years ago, long before the Christian festival began. The Easter egg has long been a symbol of fertility and rebirth, but exactly why people started decorating them is unclear. One theory is that, because animal products were not eaten during the religious Lenten season, people would hard-boil the eggs and decorate them with dye and wax, until they could be eaten at Easter. A more opulent type of decorated egg, Fabergé eggs, were famously created as bejeweled Easter gifts to the Russian imperial family. Our homepage image shows eggs from Lithuania, where people use traditional methods to paint patterns with wax using sharp objects or etch patterns into dyed eggs.

What creative ideas do you have to decorate eggs this Easter?

bing-42537.jpg.title: Observatorio y Vía Láctea, Santa Cruz De La Palma, España
bing-42537.jpg.headline: Bajo la luz de las estrellas. Observatorio, Santa Cruz De La Palma, España
bing-42537.jpg.description:
Esta espectacular imagen tomada desde el Observatorio del Roque de los Muchachos situado a 2396 metros, en La Palma, nos enseña la inmensidad del universo sobre nuestros ojos. El Observatorio fue inaugurado en 1985, pertenece al Instituto de Astrofísica de Canarias (IAC) y dispone del conjunto de telescopios más completo del mundo, entre ellos, el mayor telescopio óptico e infrarrojo existente. Gracias a las labores de investigación realizadas en el observatorio se han podido llevar a cabo multitud de estudios reveladores y conseguir captar galaxias más lejanas.

Si estás dispuesto a adentrarte en la infinidad del universo y deseas realizar una visita particular, puedes llevarla a cabo siempre que las condiciones meteorológicas lo permitan y reservando tu entrada en la Fundación Starlight.

bing-42540.jpg.title: Colibri d'Allen perché sur la plante patte de kangourou rouge
bing-42540.jpg.headline: Les oiseaux sont de retour !. La migration des oiseaux au Printemps
bing-42540.jpg.description:
Le printemps marque le retour des oiseaux migrateurs. Les colibris d’Allen que nous observons aujourd’hui, se trouvent dans le sud et le centre du Mexique. Il se nourrit principalement du nectar des fleurs qu’il happe avec sa longue langue. Il consomme deux fois son poids corporel en nectar par jour.

Des nuées d’oiseaux migrateurs survolent la France à l’arrivée du printemps et l’hirondelle est, sans nul doute, la plus attendue, car elle annonce symboliquement la belle saison. Saviez-vous qu’elles parcourent jusqu’à 10 000 km, survolent des montagnes, des mers et le désert ? Malheureusement, leur population est en baisse chaque année à cause de la population, des pesticides et de la destruction de leur habitat. Toutes les espèces d’hirondelles sont protégées et il est interdit de détruire leurs nids, même s’il est inoccupé.

bing-42546.jpg.title: コロンビア川峡谷, 米国 オレゴン州
bing-42546.jpg.headline: 苔むした岩に囲まれた滝
bing-42546.jpg.description:
この苔むした岩に囲まれた、高さ約 6m の小さな滝は、米国オレゴン州のコロンビア川渓谷にあります。コロンビア川渓谷は滝が多く、オレゴン州だけで約 90 の滝があります。この小さい滝は 2006 年に発見され、著名な写真家たちが撮影したことで、近年人気が高まっています…

この小さい滝と対照的なのは、ベネズエラにあるエンジェルフォールです。エンジェルフォールは落差が 979m もあり、世界一の落差を誇る滝です。その迫力と壮麗な絶景で、ベネズエラで最も人気のある観光スポットのひとつとなっています。

bing-42550.jpg.title: Tatzelwurm Holzbrücke, Essing,
bing-42550.jpg.headline: Halb Brücke - Halb Tatzelwurm. Tatzelbrücke, Essing, Bayern
bing-42550.jpg.description:
Bei der Holzbrücke bei Essing handelt es sich um eine Spannbandbrücke, die sowohl für Fußgänger als auch für Fahrräder bestimmt ist. Diese Brücke, die 189,91 Meter lang ist, war mehrere Jahre lang die längste Holzbrücke Europas und ist über den Main-Donau-Kanal errichtet worden. Den Rekord brach dann im Jahre 2006 die Drachenschwanzbrücke in Ronneburg. Ein sehr interessanter Aspekt ist für uns der Name der Brücke. Der Tatzelwurm ist eine mythologische Figur aus dem Alpenbogen. Charakteristisch für diese Kreatur ist, dass sie ein Wurm ist, aber Beine hat. Diese ist ein Äquivalent zu der viel bekannteren Figur des Drachens. Wenn wir das Wort selbst analysieren, kann das Wort Tatze, Pfote, Bein oder Klaue bedeuten. Der deutsche Dichter Josef Victor von Scheffel hat ihm sogar ein Gedicht gewidmet.

Verlassen wir für einen Moment dieses mythologische Ungeheuer und kehren wir zu dieser Brücke zurück, die so schön und mitten in der Natur liegt. Wir empfehlen Ihnen, diesen Ort zu besuchen und auch die umliegenden Sehenswürdigkeiten wie die Burg Randeck und den Blautopf, ein faszinierendes geologisches Phänomen, zu entdecken.

bing-42555.jpg.title: Canada Continental Divide, Yoho National Park, Canada
bing-42555.jpg.headline: A glimpse of Yoho National Park. Canada Continental Divide, Yoho National Park, Canada
bing-42555.jpg.description:
In the province of British Colombia, within Yoho National Park, you can find this glimpse of the Great Divide. Continental divides are elevated natural boundaries that separate a continent’s river systems, and this one, also known as the Continental Divide of the Americas, is the largest and longest in the world.

The Great Divide follows the ridge of the Rocky Mountains and is a remarkable natural landmark that boosts the beauty and diversity of Canada's geography. However, the Canadian portion makes up only a fraction of it. The divide spans almost the whole length of North and South America.

bing-42556.jpg.title: Mossy Grotto Falls, Columbia River Gorge, Oregon
bing-42556.jpg.headline: Where is this hidden waterfall?. Mossy Grotto Falls, Oregon
bing-42556.jpg.description: Mossy Grotto Falls is a tiny 20-foot waterfall in Oregon's Columbia River Gorge, home to around 90 waterfalls. This winsome waterfall became popular in recent years after several renowned photographers snapped it following its discovery in 2006. Waterfalls around the world draw our attention and inspire emotions (and even themes for pop songs). In contrast to the serene, burbling Mossy Grotto Falls, Angel Falls in Venezuela is the tallest in the world, where water plunges 2,648 feet before reaching the ground. This roaring wonder is awe-inspiring and one of the top tourist-draws in the country. If you need a moment of reflection, we recommend searching for the nearest waterfall and taking a trip to connect with nature.

bing-42569.jpg.title: Earth seen from the International Space Station
bing-42569.jpg.headline: A view that's out of this world. Earth seen from the International Space Station
bing-42569.jpg.description: On April 12, 1961, Russian cosmonaut Yuri Gagarin astounded the world by becoming the first person to travel to outer space. In less than two hours, Gagarin completed a full orbit of the Earth in the Vostok 3KA spacecraft. Less than a month later, Mercury astronaut Alan Shepard became the first American in space. The spectacle of looking back at Earth from space has not lost its charm, as you can see in today's picture taken from the International Space Station. Also known as the 'World Space Party,' Yuri's Night is a global celebration of astronomy and a reflection on how space exploration can unite people in a divided world.

bing-42575.jpg.title: Parque Hitsujiyama, Prefectura de Saitama, Japón
bing-42575.jpg.headline: ¡La vida en rosa!. Parque Hitsujiyama, Prefectura de Saitama, Japón
bing-42575.jpg.description:
El "Phlox subulata" recibe muchos nombres. Algunos lo llaman musgo rosa, otros phlox rastrero, musgo floreciente o phlox de montaña. Sea cual sea el nombre por el que la conozcas, no podrás negar la belleza y el encanto de estas diminutas flores perennes. Florecen en primavera y añaden toques luminosos de color allí donde crecen.

Las pequeñas flores de esta planta y su patrón de crecimiento en forma de alfombra dan la apariencia de musgo; de ahí su nombre. El parque japonés de Hitsujiyama, en Chichibu, es conocido por la “shibazakura”, como se conoce en japonés. Cuando estas flores están en plena floración, cubren las onduladas colinas del parque y ofrecen una impresionante vista hortícola.

bing-42581.jpg.title: Moss pink displays at Hitsujiyama Park, Saitama Prefecture, Japan
bing-42581.jpg.headline: Pretty in pink. Hitsujiyama Park, Saitama Prefecture, Japan
bing-42581.jpg.description:
Phlox subulata is known by many names. While some call it moss pink, others call it creeping phlox, flowering moss, or mountain phlox. No matter what name you know it by, you cannot deny the beauty and charm of these tiny perennial flowers. They bloom in spring and add bright splashes of color wherever they grow.

This plant's small flowers and carpet-like growth pattern give the appearance of moss; hence, the name. Japan's Hitsujiyama Park in Chichibu is known for shibazakura, as it's known in Japanese. When these flowers are in full bloom, they cover the rolling hills in the park and offer a breathtaking horticultural view.

bing-42589.jpg.title: Étoile de mer rouge, Mer Méditerranée
bing-42589.jpg.headline: Animal ou végétal?. Étoiles de mer rouges
bing-42589.jpg.description:
Les étoiles de mer sont l’une des créatures les plus fascinantes de nos océans. Ce ne sont ni des plantes, ni des poissons – elles appartiennent à un groupe d’invertébrés marins appelés échinodermes. Les étoiles de mer sont caractérisées par la symétrie radiale de leur corps, qui comporte généralement plusieurs « bras » partant du disque central.

Saviez-vous que les étoiles de mer peuvent régénérer leurs bras ? Cela signifie que si elles sont attaquées par un prédateur, elles peuvent éventuellement se remettre en forme (littéralement). En fait, certaines espèces peuvent même régénérer une étoile de mer entièrement neuve à partir du bras, à condition qu’elle ait encore un peu du disque central qui y est attaché.

bing-42593.jpg.title: Mediterranean red sea stars, Mediterranean Sea
bing-42593.jpg.headline: Stars in daylight. Mediterranean red sea stars
bing-42593.jpg.description:
Sea stars—often called starfish—are some of the most fascinating creatures to live in our oceans. For starters, despite their name, they aren't fish—they belong to a group of marine invertebrates called echinoderms. Like all echinoderms, sea stars are characterized by the radial symmetry of their bodies, which usually have multiple arms extending from the central disc.

Did you know that sea stars can regenerate their arms? This means if they are attacked by a predator, they can get back into shape eventually (and quite literally). In fact, some species can also regenerate an entirely new sea star from just the arm, provided it still has a bit of the central disc attached to it.

bing-42604.jpg.title: Japanese cherry blossom trees in High Park, Toronto
bing-42604.jpg.headline: A street filled with sakura trees. Vancouver Cherry Blossom Festival
bing-42604.jpg.description:
It’s cherry blossom season once again, and that means it’s time for the Sakura Days Japan Fair in Vancouver. It’s held on the 15th and 16th of April, so get ready to experience the beauty of spring this weekend. The trees in today's image are located in Toronto and are a beautiful example of cherry blossoms in full bloom.

Cherry blossoms are called sakura in Japanese, and they play a vital role in the country's cultural heritage.  When the flowers bloom every year, it’s time for Hanami, which means “flower viewing” in English. Cherry blossoms fall from their trees just two weeks after they appear, so be sure to experience their beauty while you can.

bing-42605.jpg.title: 'Together' sculpture by Lorenzo Quinn, Great Pyramids of Giza, Cairo, Egypt
bing-42605.jpg.headline: When art imitates life. World Art Day
bing-42605.jpg.description: 'Life imitates art far more than art imitates life.' There is perhaps no better day to ponder these iconic words by Oscar Wilde than World Art Day. Celebrated each April 15, it marks the birthday of Renaissance luminary Leonardo da Vinci. The celebration, which started in 2012, continues to be a beautiful reminder of the power of art and its ability to heal, strengthen, and inspire society. The sculpture in today's image, Italian artist Lorenzo Quinn's 'Together,' displayed near the Great Pyramids of Giza, serves as a fitting commentary on this inimitable power of art and also a symbol of the unbreakable human connection.

bing-42606.jpg.title: Aerial view of Jaipur from Nahargarh Fort in Rajasthan, India
bing-42606.jpg.headline: Nahargarh Fort in Rajasthan, India
bing-42606.jpg.description: The Nahargarh Fort is a medieval fort located in Jaipur, India's Pink City. It was first known as Sudarshangarh Fort and was constructed in the 18th century by Maharaja Sawai Jai Singh II. The place was eventually given the name Nahargarh, which translates to "abode of tigers," since it was thought to be haunted by the ghost of a royal by the name of Nahar Singh. The fort is a well-liked tourist destination and provides breathtaking panoramic views of the city.

bing-42617.jpg.title: Adelaide International Kite Festival, Australia
bing-42617.jpg.headline: Go fly a kite!. Go Fly a Kite Day
bing-42617.jpg.description: Is there a simpler joy than flying a kite on a windy day? The date of this magical invention is unknown, but the first written documentation of kite flying comes from China in 200 BCE. There they were initially used to measure distance, but over the years they have been tapped for fishing, sport, science, celebration, communication, and recreation. Kites can take many shapes and be made of various materials, but all of them have a wing surface, a tether, and a bridle that keeps the surface at an angle to the wind. In fact, you can easily make your own, and there's no better time than today: Go Fly a Kite Day.

bing-42629.jpg.title: 'One Thousand Springs' haiku art installation by Chiharu Shiota, Kew Royal Botanic Gardens, London, England
bing-42629.jpg.headline: Poetry in suspense. International Haiku Poetry Day
bing-42629.jpg.description:
Get out your pen and paper—it's International Haiku Poetry Day! Haikus originated in Japan as the opening segment of a larger poem called a renga. Eventually they became individual poems of their own. A traditional haiku consists of 17 phonetic units—similar to a syllable—in a 5, 7, 5 formation. Though simple, a great haiku creates a sense of beauty and a connection to nature. That connection was captured in the artwork seen here, 'One Thousand Springs,' an installation of 5,000 haikus suspended within a web of red threads by artist Chiharu Shiota. It was part of the 2021 Japan Festival at Kew Royal Botanic Gardens in London. Here's some inspiration for you to write a haiku yourself:

poetry blooms bright / scattered by the vernal winds / may it take strong root

bing-42632.jpg.title: 马丘比丘，秘鲁
bing-42632.jpg.headline: 山顶上的文化奇观
