bing-42632.jpg.description: 高悬于安第斯山脉之上，秘鲁的马丘比丘被认为曾属于古印加皇帝帕查库蒂。今天是联合国教科文组织国际古迹遗址日，推荐这座“印加的失落之城”实在是恰逢其时，它是代表一整个民族记忆的文化符号。国际古迹遗址日由国际古迹遗址理事会首次提出，并于1983年正式设立。它给了我们一个回望过去的机会，让我们得以一睹前人的文化，同时为后人保留这些久远的记忆。

bing-42641.jpg.title: Machu Picchu, Peru
bing-42641.jpg.headline: A mountaintop marvel. International Day for Monuments and Sites
bing-42641.jpg.description: Located high in the Andes Mountains, Peru's Machu Picchu is believed to have been an estate for the Inca emperor Pachacuti, who ruled in the mid-15th century. This 'Lost City of the Incas' is one of the world's most famous archaeological sites, an engineering marvel, built without mortar, metal tools, or the wheel. As an icon of Inca civilization, it is a perfect fit for UNESCO's International Day for Monuments and Sites, which has been celebrating important cultural heritage sites for 40 years. Landmarks such as the Pueblo Indian dwellings of Mesa Verde, the Taj Mahal, the Great Pyramid of Giza, and the Parthenon give us the opportunity to look back at the cultures that came before us and preserve their memory for future generations.

bing-42648.jpg.title: Torri medievali a San Gimignano, Siena
bing-42648.jpg.headline: Maestose torri medievali
bing-42648.jpg.description: Immerso tra le verdi colline del paesaggio toscano, e precisamente in provincia di Siena, sorge il piccolo comune di San Gimignano. Il borgo può vantare un grande passato testimoniato dal ricco patrimonio architettonico e culturale che gli hanno consentito di essere dichiarato patrimonio dell’umanità dell’UNESCO nel 1990. Grazie alla sua posizione strategica e ai suoi 324 metri di altezza, il piccolo borgo domina la Val d’Elsa, e già dall’età etrusca, di cui si hanno numerose testimonianze, questa sua caratteristica gli conferì una relativa importanza, rientrando ad esempio nel percorso della via Francigena. Una delle sue caratteristiche più ammirate ed apprezzate risiede nelle torri e case-torri medievali che svettano come grattacieli nel centro storico. Se ne contavano ben 75, ma ad oggi ne rimangono solo 14; la più antica rimane la Torre Rognosa o sede del Podestà, che è stata edificata in Piazza del Duomo intorno al 1200. San Gimignano ospita al suo interno numerose chiese come ad

bing-42649.jpg.title: Hugh Coltman sur la scène du Printemps de Bourges
bing-42649.jpg.headline: La musique adoucit les cœurs. Printemps de Bourges
bing-42649.jpg.description:
Le Printemps de Bourges est né en 1977 avec comme leitmotiv la création et l’expression de la chanson dans tous ses aspects. Depuis, le festival a accueilli plus de 3200 artistes du monde entier, de tous les horizons et pour tous les publics.

Se rendre à ce festival est aussi l’occasion de découvrir la ville de Bourges, avec son centre historique et ses maisons à pans de bois, ses remparts et sa cathédrale Saint-Étienne de Bourges, construite entre la fin du XIIe et la fin du XIIIe siècle. C’est l'un des grands chefs-d'œuvre de l'art gothique, patrimoine de l’UNESCO. Enfin, n’oubliez pas de faire une petite une balade nature dans les surprenants Marais de Bourges, en plein cœur de la ville.

bing-42653.jpg.title: Taiwan yuhina pair, Alishan National Scenic Area, Taiwan
bing-42653.jpg.headline: Two's company. Taiwan yuhinas in Alishan National Scenic Area
bing-42653.jpg.description: The Taiwan yuhina is a chirpy little bird with an eye-catching crest. Found only on the island of Taiwan, they constantly chatter while feeding and sometimes hang upside-down on cherry trees like bats. Birdwatchers can glimpse the small songbirds at Taiwan’s Alishan National Scenic Area, which features postcard-worthy forest trails and picturesque sunrises.

bing-42665.jpg.title: Juniper Springs in Ocala National Forest, Florida
bing-42665.jpg.headline: A subtropical soak. Juniper Springs, Florida
bing-42665.jpg.description:
Yes, the water here is as inviting as it looks: clear as glass, the shade of a precious gem, and a perfect 73 degrees every day of the year. Set within a subtropical forest, Juniper Springs is one of Florida's oldest and best-known recreation areas, established in the 1930s as a place to camp, hike, and swim. Long before Disney arrived, natural springs like this one were the big draw in the Sunshine State.

Florida is home to the largest concentration of freshwater springs in the world, with more than 1,000 popping up where the massive Floridan aquifer breaks through the surface. This underground reservoir hides beneath the entire state, providing Florida with almost all of its drinking water.

Overextraction and pollution from fertilizers and septic systems have put some springs in peril but in Juniper Springs, these jewel-toned waters are protected by the Ocala National Forest, so it's likely to look like this for a long time.

bing-42666.jpg.title: Anjuna Beach, Goa, India
bing-42666.jpg.headline: Anjuna Beach, Goa, India
bing-42666.jpg.description: We are at Anjuna Beach in Goa – a tiny state on the southwestern coast of India known for its beautiful landscapes and scenic beaches. Located about 21 kilometres from Panaji, the capital of Goa, Anjuna Beach is among the most popular beaches in this area. A hippie paradise of sorts, it is characterised by its rocky outcrops. From family outings to adrenaline-filled adventures, Anjuna Beach is famed for its golden coastline, nightclubs, beach shacks, watersports, full-moon parties and flea markets.

bing-42673.jpg.title: Saugues et de sa sculpture en bois de la bête du Gevaudan, Haute-Loire
bing-42673.jpg.headline: La bête veille sur la vallée. Sculpture de la bête du Gévaudan
bing-42673.jpg.description:
Saugues est situé dans le département de la Haute-Loire et dans la région d'Auvergne-Rhône-Alpes.  Le village de 1697 habitants est une célèbre ville étape du chemin de Saint Jacques de Compostelle. Plus de 20 000 personnes empruntent chaque année les chemins du Gévaudan-Lozère. La région est également connue dans le monde entier pour le mythe qu’elle abrite au creux de ses terres…

La Bête du Gévaudan a sévi dans les campagnes françaises entre 1764 et 1767, elle a tué une centaine de personnes. Les rescapés des attaques diront qu’il ne s’agissait pas d’un simple loup, mais d’un autre animal qu’ils nommeront « La Bête ».  Malgré de nombreuses tentatives, l’animal en question n’a jamais pu être identifié et plus de 250 ans plus tard, le mystère reste entier.

bing-42674.jpg.title: Meldon Hill, Dartmoor National Park, Devon
bing-42674.jpg.headline: Rugged rocks and ancient history. Dartmoor National Park
bing-42674.jpg.description:
You can find this beautiful, sunlit landscape within Dartmoor National Park, a reserved area located in the southwest of England. Despite its beauty, Meldon Hill isn’t particularly well-known, although the park itself is a popular visitor destination. It is famous for its rugged landscape, ancient history and wildlife. The park features granite tors, which are large rocky outcrops that dot the landscape. Since ancient times, the region has been inhabited and is rich in archaeological sites. This includes prehistoric stone circles and cairns, Bronze Age settlements and medieval ruins.

Additionally, this park is home to ponies, birds of prey and rare butterflies along with numerous outdoor activities, including hiking, cycling, horseback riding and fishing. You’ll also find museums in the park, which provide information on the history, culture and ecology of the area.

bing-42689.jpg.title: Island fox in Channel Islands National Park, California
bing-42689.jpg.headline: Back from the brink. Earth Day and National Park Week
bing-42689.jpg.description: This tiny island fox is a great cheerleader for Earth Day, which celebrates the achievements of the environmental movement. Island foxes exist only on the Channel Islands of Southern California. You can find them on six of the eight islands, and each island's fox is considered a unique subspecies. While numbers have never been huge, they declined catastrophically in the 1990s. Thanks to a recovery program, their population is growing steadily, and these tiny foxes have bounced back from the brink of extinction. If you want to visit Channel Islands National Park to see this success story, today is a good day to go. Admission fees at all national parks will be waived today to mark the start of National Park Week.

bing-42693.jpg.title: Early morning shafts of light through deciduous forest, Bandhavgarh National Park, India
bing-42693.jpg.headline: In the spotlight. Bandhavgarh National Park, India
bing-42693.jpg.description: This forest with a sunlit spotlight is located in the Umaria district of Madhya Pradesh, India, in Bandhavgarh National Park. The park is well-known for having a large biodiversity, with a large population of Bengal tigers, as well as other animals like leopards, deer and other bird species. In fact, it has one of the highest densities of tigers known in the world. The Vindhya Mountain range encircles the park, which has a surface area of about 105 square kilometers. Bandhavgarh has a long history, with indications of human habitation going back to the Paleolithic era. It is now a well-liked vacation spot for those who enjoy the outdoors and wildlife.

bing-42694.jpg.title: Casa Batlló de Gaudí, Barcelona, España
bing-42694.jpg.headline: Lectura con aroma a rosas. Día de Sant Jordi, Casa Batlló de Gaudí, Barcelona, España
bing-42694.jpg.description:
La Casa Batlló de Gaudí es el mayor símbolo de expresión en torno a la leyenda del día de Sant Jordi. Esta relata una historia donde un atroz dragón que atemorizaba la ciudad era alimentado diariamente con un miembro de la población escogido de manera aleatoria, hasta que un día, de forma totalmente fortuita, le tocó el turno a la princesa del reino. En ese momento, cuando la princesa se dirigía a ser devorada por el feroz dragón apareció un valiente caballero, Sant Jordi, quien desfundó su espada y atravesó al dragón. Cuando este sacó su espada, la sangre del dragón se convirtió en hermosos rosales, como en nuestra imagen de hoy.

En el día de Sant Jordi miles de personas se reúnen en torno a La Rambla de Barcelona para comprar rosas y libros, que son escaparate para numerosos visitantes y turistas. Si estás por Barcelona en este día tan esperado no dudes en hacerte el mejor regalo de la vida, ¡despertar tu curiosidad con rosas y libros!

bing-42698.jpg.title: Monastery, St. George, Prague
bing-42698.jpg.headline: The beauty of intricate carvings. Czech Republic, Prague
bing-42698.jpg.description:
St. George’s Basilica is a magnificent church in Prague and the oldest surviving church in the city. It was consecrated in 921 A.D. by Vrastislaus I, the Duke of Bohemia. The interior is made of sandstone and is elaborately decorated with sculptures and reliefs. The sculptures depict various biblical scenes, such as Adam and Eve in the Garden of Eden and the crucifixion of Jesus Christ. There are also several reliefs depicting saints and apostles.

The portal is one of the best examples of Romanesque sculpture in central Europe and is a popular tourist attraction in Prague. It is also significant in the history of Czech art, as it represents the first known use of the 'Prague style' of sculpture, which later became a dominant form of art in the region.

bing-42701.jpg.title: Stuttgart Public Library, Germany
bing-42701.jpg.headline: A book lover's paradise. World Book Day
bing-42701.jpg.description:
'There is no friend as loyal as a book,' Ernest Hemingway once wrote. On World Book Day, we are honoring these loyal friends in the German city of Stuttgart, where a huge monolithic cube is both a modern landmark and home to the city library. Opened in 2011, this striking building was designed by architect Eun Young Yi to be a calming, meditative space in a bustling city. Its interior is white, with splashes of color provided by the books that line its walls.

World Book Day was set up by UNESCO in 1995 to celebrate recreational reading. It also marks the start of National Library Week here in the US, so there's no better time to head to your local library to find your next great 'friend' to take you on new adventures.

bing-42719.jpg.title: Baumwipfelpfad Naturerbezentrum Rügen bei Prora, Rügen
bing-42719.jpg.headline: Wo steht dieser imposante Baum?. Tag des Baumes
bing-42719.jpg.description:
Die Insel Rügen an der Ostsee ist für ihre beeindruckende Natur, ihre weißen Sandstrände und ihre historischen Sehenswürdigkeiten bekannt. Diese hat auch eine lange Tradition als Ort der Inspiration für Künstler und Schriftsteller. Einer der wahrscheinlich bekanntesten Künstler, der diese besucht hat, ist Caspar David Friedrich. Der Maler der Romantik verbrachte mehrere Sommer dort und malte einige seiner berühmtesten Werke, darunter das Gemälde „Kreidefelsen auf Rügen”. Der Expressionist Max Pechstein besuchte ebenfalls mehrere Male Rügen. Die Schönheit der Natur und die idyllische Landschaft faszinierte ihn ebenfalls sehr.

Der Schriftsteller Gerhart Hauptman, der den Nobelpreis für Literatur 1912 gewann, lebte zeitweise auf der Insel. Dort schrieb er mehrere Werke, unter anderem das Buch „Die Ratten”. Rügen war auch für andere Schriftsteller wie z. B. für Christa Wolf ein magischer Ort der Inspiration.

Heute gibt es auf Rügen mehrere Museen und Ausstellungen, die sich der Kultur, der Geschichte und der Kunst der Insel widmen. Im heutigen Foto können Sie den Baumwipfelpfad bewundern. Wenn Sie nach Rügen reisen sollten, empfehlen wir Ihnen, den Baumwipfelpfad ebenfalls zu besuchen. Eine tolle Sicht erwartet Sie von dort oben.

bing-42720.jpg.title: Festa della Liberazione
bing-42720.jpg.headline: Una bandiera nel cielo?
bing-42720.jpg.description: Tirate fuori le bandiere, alzate lo sguardo verso il cielo e ammirate le nostre “Frecce”, la Festa della Liberazione è finalmente giunta. Essa venne istituita per festeggiare il termine di un capitolo oscuro della nostra storia con la liberazione dell’Italia dall'occupazione nazi-fascista avvenuta nel 1945. Dopo anni di cruente battaglie sui fronti più svariati, città in rovina e perdite spaventose tra militari e civili, l’Italia divenne finalmente libera. La decisione di scegliere il 25 aprile venne presa nel 1946 dal governo provvisorio di Alcide De Gasperi, mediante un decreto firmato dal re Umberto II. La celebrazione si svolge con manifestazioni pubbliche in tutte le città italiane e con uno show aereo acrobatico delle note Frecce Tricolori. Per tradizione, il Presidente  deposita personalmente una corona di alloro al monumento del Milite Ignoto all’Altare della Patria, al fine di onorare i caduti in guerra.

bing-42725.jpg.title: Adélie penguins in Antarctica
bing-42725.jpg.headline: Chilling out on World Penguin Day. World Penguin Day
bing-42725.jpg.description:
Penguins are pretty amazing. From their social personalities to their impressive talent for swimming and diving, they're a bird worth celebrating. Today, World Penguin Day, is the perfect time to learn more about these flightless birds, noted for their swimming prowess.

Native to the land and surrounding waters of Antarctica, Adélie penguins migrate an average of 8,000 miles annually, as they follow the sun from their breeding colonies to winter foraging grounds and back again. The species is easy to recognize by the white rings around their eyes. Oh, and if you think you were chilly this winter, these birds thrive in temperatures as low as -20 degrees Fahrenheit.

bing-42730.jpg.title: Feria de Abril, Sevilla, España
bing-42730.jpg.headline: Luces de colores e ilusión. Feria de Abril, Sevilla, España
bing-42730.jpg.description:
Sevilla cuenta con la población más grande de Andalucía y cuarta de España. Está catalogada como la ciudad con más monumentos de Europa y presenta un gran patrimonio histórico y monumental.

La Feria de Abril, celebrada en Sevilla, es una de las más famosas del país. Tuvo su comienzo en el año 1846, tras la necesidad de celebrar una feria agrícola y ganadera, derivando en lo que hoy en día conocemos como la cumbre de las fiestas y tradiciones reunidas en un recinto, el Real de la Feria.

En esta semana de fiesta se lucen colores, trajes de flamenca y tus mejores galas para disfrutar del mejor ambiente, con música en vivo y comida típica en las casetas del recinto ferial. Si estás por Sevilla y quieres vivir el verdadero clima andaluz, ¡baila con nosotros en este maravilloso alumbrado!

bing-42734.jpg.title: Great horned owl fledglings
bing-42734.jpg.headline: Just a couple of 'know-it-owls'. Great horned owl fledglings
bing-42734.jpg.description: You're looking at the great horned owl, a common raptor coloured for camouflage and ready to hunt. They're fierce predators and can easily capture prey larger than themselves. As voracious carnivores, they hunt whatever they can find—typically small animals like rabbits, squirrels, mice and even scorpions. They spend their days roosting and their nights hunting alone.  Great horned owls don't migrate but often move from one territory to another. These distinctive birds can be found almost anywhere, from the Arctic regions to the tropics. You might even find them in your own backyard!

bing-42736.jpg.title: Cave and Basin National Historic Site, Sulphur Mountain, Banff National Park, Alberta
bing-42736.jpg.headline: The origin of Canada's national parks. Cave and Basin National Historic Site
bing-42736.jpg.description: Cave and Basin National Historic Site is a protected area in Banff National Park that houses geothermally heated hot springs. The uncovering of the caves, first recorded in 1859, led to the foundation of not only this park but Canada’s entire national parks system in 1885. Briefly, water from the springs was sold as a cure-all, until they were turned into a bathing site in 1914. The pool was closed for swimming in 1994, but guests can still enjoy the natural beauty of the springs and the cave. If you're still in need of a soak, worry not, the Banff Upper Hot Springs are located a mere five kilometres away.

bing-42737.jpg.title: Great horned owl fledglings
bing-42737.jpg.headline: Destined for greatness. Great horned owl fledglings
bing-42737.jpg.description:
These little furballs will grow up to be great horned owls, fierce predators with camouflage coloring. For now, they sport a layer of fluffy light-colored down and have yet to grow their full 'horns'—tufts of feathers known as plumicorns. But they will become voracious carnivores capable of hunting down prey larger than themselves, including other owls. Typical meals will consist of small animals like rabbits, squirrels, mice, and even scorpions.

They spend their days roosting and their nights hunting alone. Great horned owls don't migrate but often move from one territory to another. These distinctive birds can be found almost anywhere in the Americas, from sub-Arctic regions to the tropics. You might even find them in your own backyard!

bing-42744.jpg.title: Alpe di Siusi, Dolomiti, Italia
bing-42744.jpg.headline: La meraviglia fatta natura!
bing-42744.jpg.description: Situato nel Trentino, nella parte occidentale delle Dolomiti e ad una quota compresa tra i 1680 e i 2350 m s.l.m., l’Alpe di Siusi è il più esteso altipiano d’Europa ed offre tra i più spettacolari panorami sul pianeta. Con le sue innumerevoli attività ricreative e specialità culinarie, rappresenta una meta ideale per sportivi, famiglie ed amanti della cucina. Gli impianti sciistici ivi presenti lo rendono un attrazione spettacolare per gli appassionati dello sci e snowboarding nei mesi di inverno. Inoltre, grazie anche al suo vero è proprio tesoro di biodiversità vegetale, con oltre 780 diverse specie di piante presenti, è anche il paradiso degli escursionisti, studiosi ed amanti della natura anche nei mesi primaverili ed estivi.

bing-42749.jpg.title: South Padre Island, Texas
bing-42749.jpg.headline: An endless stretch of sky. South Padre Island, Texas
bing-42749.jpg.description:
Located a few miles offshore on the Texas Gulf Coast, Padre Island is the largest of the state's string of barrier islands. At 113 miles in length, it is also the longest barrier island in the world. Barrier islands usually run parallel to the coast and, as the name suggests, serve as the mainland's first line of defense against storms.

Since the Port Mansfield Channel was built in the early 1960s, Padre Island has been split into two parts, South Padre Island, pictured here, and North Padre Island. Connected by a bridge to the shore, the resort town of South Padre Island draws in thousands of visitors every year for swimming, boating, fishing, or simply lounging on the beach. Others come for the trail of elaborate sandcastles scattered across the island, created by professional artists.

bing-42751.jpg.title: ヨセミテ国立公園にあるマリポサグローブ, 米国 カリフォルニア州
bing-42751.jpg.headline: 今日は米国の植樹祭
bing-42751.jpg.description:
ここは米国のヨセミテ国立公園にあるマリポサグローブ、巨大なセコイアが林立しており、中には樹齢 3500 年と推定されるものもあるのだとか。米国国立公園局によると、地質学的な証拠からセコイアは地球上で最も古い植物のひとつです…

そして今日は、毎年 4 月の最終金曜日に行われている、米国の植樹祭。農務長官であるジュリアス・スターリング・モートンの提唱によって制定されました。植樹祭は米国以外にも多数の国で実施されており、日本においては、1950 年から毎年春に全国植樹祭が開催されています。

bing-42758.jpg.title: Mariposa Grove in Yosemite National Park, California
bing-42758.jpg.headline: Warm light through an ancient forest. Arbor Day
bing-42758.jpg.description:
On this last Friday of April, we're celebrating the importance of planting and preserving trees. The history of this day—Arbor Day—can be traced back to Nebraska in the early 1870s when a journalist, Julius Sterling Morton, editor of the Nebraska City News, used his public platform to highlight the ecological importance of trees. In 1872, he proposed a day for Nebraskans to plant trees, and thus, Arbor Day came into existence.

The giant sequoia, seen here, is an embodiment of the significance of trees. According to the US National Park Service, geological evidence shows that sequoias have one of the oldest lineages of any living thing on earth. Mariposa Grove in Yosemite National Park, pictured here, has hundreds of sequoias that can be as ancient as 3,500 years old.

bing-42761.jpg.title: Mariposa Grove of Giant Sequoias in Yosemite National Park, California
bing-42761.jpg.headline: The giants of Yosemite. Arbor Day
bing-42761.jpg.description:
We're celebrating Arbor Day with some of Yosemite's most famous residents, the giant sequoia trees of Mariposa Grove. The day champions the planting and preservation of trees and can trace its roots back more than 150 years. In 1872, Nebraska City News editor Julius Sterling Morton proposed a day for locals to plant trees, and the idea grew and grew. Today all 50 states celebrate Arbor Day, most commonly on the last Friday in April, although different states might observe it on the best dates for tree planting in their area.

Giant sequoias, like the ones on our homepage, have been around for a very long time. Geological evidence suggests that they are the third-longest-lived tree species in the world. There are hundreds of them in Yosemite's Mariposa Grove, including the famous Grizzly Giant, which is estimated to be about 3,000 years old. Let's hope it is around for thousands of Arbor Days to come.

bing-42777.jpg.title: Interior of Hawa Mahal or Palace of Winds, India
bing-42777.jpg.headline: A feel of an era bygone. Hawa Mahal, Jaipur
bing-42777.jpg.description: Rajasthan's capital Jaipur is home to the stunning Hawa Mahal, popularly referred to as the Palace of Winds. Maharaja Sawai Pratap Singh commissioned the construction of the palace in 1799 with the intention of enabling the women of the royal family to observe street life and festivities from behind its ornately carved windows without being seen themselves. The five-storey pink sandstone palace includes 953 tiny windows, called jharokhas, that let air flow through the structure and maintain the building's coolness even during the hottest months. The Hawa Mahal, a well-liked tourist destination, showcases the Rajput era's architectural skill.

bing-42785.jpg.title: Preservation Hall, New Orleans, Louisiana
bing-42785.jpg.headline: A day of swing and celebration. International Jazz Day
bing-42785.jpg.description: Born in the Black communities of New Orleans, jazz music quickly caught on outside the Big Easy and became an international sensation. Due to its improvisational nature, jazz never stays the same, fusing with other cultures and genres to create styles such as Afro-Cuban, Latin, and Indo Jazz. UNESCO Goodwill Ambassador and jazz pianist Herbie Hancock created International Jazz Day to celebrate the global genre, first held in 2012 with events in New York, Paris, and New Orleans. We hope you celebrate by putting on your favorite jazz record, or if you can swing it, visit New Orleans' legendary jazz venue, Preservation Hall, seen in our photo here.

bing-42786.jpg.title: Temple E at Selinunte, Sicily, Italy
bing-42786.jpg.headline: Temple E at Selinunte, Sicily
bing-42786.jpg.description: This picture-perfect temple was built toward the middle of the 6th century, and it’s the best conserved of the temples of Selinunte. How is it so intact? Temple E, also known as the Temple of Hera, was reconstructed in 1959 and is a Greek temple in Sicily in the east of the city’s acropolis. This style contains a peristyle with six columns on the front, and fifteen on the long sides. However, the architecture marks a transition between two styles, from the archaic to the classical period. Selinunte is an ancient city on the south-western coast of the island, featuring five temples centered on an acropolis, which is a settlement the Greeks used as religious places of worship.

bing-42791.jpg.title: Biene im Sonnenblumenfeld bei Fresdorf
bing-42791.jpg.headline: Arbeiten Bienen am 1. Mai?. Tag der Arbeit
bing-42791.jpg.description:
Der 1. Mai wird weltweit als Tag der Arbeit oder auch als Tag der Arbeiterbewegung gefeiert. Er ehrt und erinnert an den historischen Kampf der Arbeiterinnen und Arbeiter für ihre Rechte und den Acht-Stunden-Arbeitstag. Heute wird der Tag oft dazu genutzt, um auf die aktuellen Herausforderungen und Ungerechtigkeiten in der Arbeitswelt aufmerksam zu machen und für bessere Arbeitsbedingungen und soziale Gerechtigkeit zu demonstrieren. In Deutschland wurde der 1. Mai erstmals 1890 gefeiert.

Dieser Tag wird fast weltweit gefeiert. Viele Städte organisieren Kundgebungen, Konzerte und Volksfeste, die oft eine lange Tradition haben. Und Sie, haben Sie Pläne? Mit Freunden sich treffen, in den Park gehen, aufs Land fahren, Konzerte oder Feste besuchen, oder möchten Sie sich doch nur von der Arbeit erholen und zu Hause entspannen?

Auf diesem Foto von heute können wir eine Biene bei ihrer Arbeit bewundern. Was denken Sie, wird sich die Biene auch ausruhen? Wohl kaum, denn Bienen sind erstaunliche Insekten, die in einer perfekt organisierten Gesellschaft arbeiten. Sollten wir vielleicht etwas von ihnen lernen?

bing-42793.jpg.title: Muguet de mai en fleurs
bing-42793.jpg.headline: Un petit brin de bonheur !. Fête du muguet
bing-42793.jpg.description:
Le muguet est une plante vivace originaire d'Europe, qui pousse à l'état sauvage dans les sous-bois et les prairies. On le reconnait à première vue pour ses petites fleurs blanches en forme de clochettes très parfumées.

Le muguet est associé à la fête du 1er mai, qui est célébrée dans de nombreux pays européens comme le jour du travail. Traditionnellement, les gens offrent des brins de muguet à leurs proches pour leur souhaiter bonheur et prospérité pour l'année à venir.

bing-42794.jpg.title: Quebec Bridge across the lower Saint Lawrence River, Canada
bing-42794.jpg.headline: Spanning the soft sunlight. Quebec Bridge, Canada
bing-42794.jpg.description:
The Quebec Bridge holds great significance in the history of Canadian civil engineering. This architectural marvel has a centre span of 549 metres, making it the longest cantilevered bridge in the world. At more than 20 metres wide, it can accommodate two sets of railway tracks, two sets of streetcars, and two roadways.

The bridge has a rich history, plagued with difficulties and challenges with construction. It took over thirty years to complete, with design flaws causing two major collapses in 1907 and 1916. However, The Quebec Bridge as we see it today opened in 1919 and remains a national historic site.

bing-42797.jpg.title: Korean Bell of Friendship, Los Angeles
bing-42797.jpg.headline: Asian American and Pacific Islander Heritage Month
bing-42797.jpg.description:
This stunning structure is the stone pavilion housing the massive Korean Bell of Friendship in Los Angeles, a city with a large Korean American population. It's ringing in Asian American and Pacific Islander (AAPI) Heritage Month, which starts today. The month was chosen in recognition of the first documented arrival of Japanese immigrants, on May 7, 1843, and the completion of the transcontinental railroad by more than 20,000 Asian immigrants on May 10, 1869.

Back to that intricately decorated bronze bell. It was a gift to the city from South Korea to mark the US bicentennial in 1976 and is modeled on the largest bell cast in Korean history, the Divine Bell of King Seongdeok, made in 771. Both versions are among the largest bells in the world.

bing-42821.jpg.title: Wildebeests in the Maasai Mara National Reserve, Kenya
bing-42821.jpg.headline: The animal kingdom's great migration. Wildebeests in Maasai Mara, Kenya
bing-42821.jpg.description:
Welcome to Kenya's Maasai Mara National Reserve, where some of its most iconic inhabitants are out for an evening stroll. Wildebeests, also known as gnus, are social animals which often form large herds. There are two types: black wildebeests and blue wildebeests and it is the latter which take part in the famous Great Migration, one of the world's greatest wildlife spectacles.

This typically starts in January or February and sees more than a million wildebeests, along with large herds of zebras and other species, migrate from the Serengeti in neighboring Tanzania to the Maasai Mara in search of water and greener pastures. They arrive in Kenya from late July and stay until November when they start moving south again, a round trip of some 500 miles. Tourists flock to the Maasai Mara to witness this incredible natural spectacle.

bing-42833.jpg.title: Mayan ruins in Tikal, Guatemala
bing-42833.jpg.headline: May the Fourth be with you. Star Wars Day
bing-42833.jpg.description:
May the Fourth be with you! The 'Star Wars' universe has captured the imagination of fans for decades and its impact, like the 'Force,' is all around us. The original 1977 film introduced us to a galaxy far, far away, a cast of unforgettable characters, and a gripping battle between good and evil. Its reach has since extended to television, books, comics, theme parks, thousands of products, and a day of its own to celebrate the much-loved sci-fi franchise.

Fans might recognize today's image of the Mayan ruins in Tikal, Guatemala, as the rebel base on Yavin 4 from 'Star Wars: A New Hope.' These real-life temples served as a key setting in the cinematic Battle of Yavin, a fight so pivotal in the 'Star Wars' storyline that calendar years in the universe are called ABY or BBY: After the Battle of Yavin or Before the Battle of Yavin.

bing-42845.jpg.title: Church of Nuestra Señora de los Remedios and Popocatépetl, Puebla, Mexico
bing-42845.jpg.headline: Celebrating Cinco de Mayo. Cinco de Mayo
bing-42845.jpg.description:
Contrary to what many people believe, Cinco de Mayo is not Mexico's Independence Day, which is celebrated on September 16. Instead, May 5 marks Mexico's victory over better-equipped French forces at the Battle of Puebla on May 5, 1862. Although the French Empire would counterattack and take the city a year later, the unexpected victory was a morale boost which still has symbolic significance. While in the US, Cinco de Mayo is a popular festival celebrating Mexican American culture, celebrations in Mexico are relatively quiet and focused mostly on Puebla.

In Mexico, the celebration became known as Battle of Puebla Day after President Benito Juárez declared it a national holiday in 1862. Today, the people of Puebla celebrate with parades, speeches, and battle reenactments. The Church of Nuestra Señora de los Remedios in Puebla, pictured here, was already nearly 300 years old when the 1862 battle was fought. And human history is just the blink of an eye to ancient Popocatépetl, the smoking volcano which towers over Puebla in the background of our homepage image.

bing-42846.jpg.title: Sasso Caveoso, Basilicata, Matera, Italy
bing-42846.jpg.headline: Sasso Caveoso, Matera, Italy
bing-42846.jpg.description: Sasso Caveoso, a district in Matera, Basilicata, Italy, is well-known for its ancient cave dwellings. These buildings were carved from stone more than 9,000 years ago, and today serve as churches, museums and even homes. Sasso Caveoso, along with the Sasso Barisano district, are thought to be among the first human settlements in Italy.  Since 1993, these districts have been classified as a UNESCO World Heritage site, which helped them grow their tourism. Visitors can explore the district's winding lanes and tiny streets as well as take tours of the many ancient caves. Sasso Caveoso offers a fascinating look into Matera's past and is a must-visit location for those who enjoy history and architecture.

bing-42851.jpg.title: Feuerwerk in Speyer Rheinland-Pfalz
bing-42851.jpg.headline: Speyer-Feier. Rhein in Flammen
bing-42851.jpg.description:
Rheinland-Pfalz ist für seine spektakulären Feuerwerke, die jedes Jahr zu verschiedenen Anlässen stattfinden, bekannt. Besonders beliebt sind die Feuerwerke zum Rheinland-Pfalz-Tag, der alle zwei Jahre in einer anderen Stadt des Bundeslandes gefeiert wird. Auch zu Sylvester und anderen Festen zelebrieren die Rheinland-Pfälzer gerne und sorgen immer für aufsehenerregende Feuerwerke am Himmel. Die Feuerwerke sind oft aufwendig inszeniert und beeindrucken mit ihrer Farbenvielfalt und den imposanten Lichteffekten. Wer sich dafür begeistert, sollte unbedingt einmal bei einem der vielen Feuerwerk-Spektakeln in Rheinland-Pfalz teilnehmen und sich von diesen atemberaubenden Shows hinreißen lassen. Dieses Jahr wird der Rheinland-Pfalz-Tag in Speyer gefeiert. Am Abend des letzten Festtags wird das grandiose Feuerwerk am Rheinufer gezündet, das Besucher aus aller Welt anzieht.

Die Stadt Speyer ist vor allem für ihren Dom bekannt, der zum UNESCO-Weltkulturerbe gehört. Der Speyerer Dom gehört zu den größten romanischen Kirchen der Welt und beeindruckt Besucher mit seinen imposanten Dimensionen und seiner prächtigen Innenausstattung.

In Sachen Folklore hat Speyer einiges zu bieten. Jährlich findet am 23. Juni das Johannismarkt-Spektakel statt, bei dem man sich in vergangene Zeiten zurückversetzt fühlt. Die historischen Gassen der Altstadt werden mit Fackeln beleuchtet und es gibt zahlreiche Marktstände, Handwerksvorführungen sowie mittelalterliche Musik und Tänze.

bing-42854.jpg.title: Westminster Abbey Church, England, UK
bing-42854.jpg.headline: An architectural masterpiece fit for a king. Westminster Abbey Church, UK
bing-42854.jpg.description:
Today we will witness a historic moment—King Charles III's coronation at Westminster Abbey.  The former prince will be crowned the 62nd monarch of England, in a ceremony steeped in ancient traditions and pageantry. After the coronation, the royal family will appear at the balcony of Buckingham Palace to celebrate the grand occasion and share their happiness with the British people.

Westminster Abbey, formally titled the Collegiate Church of Saint Peter, was built in the 10th century and is a truly remarkable landmark.  It's a masterpiece of Gothic architecture with beautiful stained-glass windows, intricate wood carvings and other ornate decorations. The site has hosted significant events in British history, including past coronations, royal weddings and funerals of monarchs and other notable figures. The tomb of Queen Elizabeth I, for example, features an effigy of the queen surrounded by a series of carved figures representing the virtues she embodied.

bing-42857.jpg.title: Royal azaleas in bloom on Hwangmaesan Mountain, South Korea
bing-42857.jpg.headline: The purple peaks of Hwangmaesan. Azaleas blooming on Hwangmaesan Mountain, South Korea
bing-42857.jpg.description:
Vast colonies of royal azaleas paint the sides of South Korea’s Hwangmaesan Mountain a vibrant purple as summer approaches. Sightseers flock to see this striking pink and purple carpet of flowers which was created gradually as dairy cows and sheep ate the grass and plants, but left behind the poisonous azaleas which spread across the mountain.

For those who want to climb it, Hwangmaesan also features massive rock formations, stunning views, and a legend that anyone who prays at the summit will have their wish granted. It reaches an altitude of around 3,650 feet and offers a peaceful escape from city life for hikers and campers. Those who want to walk among the azaleas should head there in May, when they come into bloom. But dress appropriately, it still gets chilly up at the summit.

bing-42858.jpg.title: Barley and cornflowers, Nordhausen, Germany
bing-42858.jpg.headline: Barley and cornflowers, Germany
bing-42858.jpg.description:
Known for their distinctive qualities and purposes, barley and cornflowers are two famous agricultural crops of Germany. Gerste, the German name for barley, is a grain that may be used to make bread, brew beer and feed livestock. In many parts of Germany, especially in Bavaria and Franconia, it is an important crop.

Cornflowers, the bright blue blossoms you see in today’s photo, are a type of wildflower that bloom in the summer and are used as a decorative plant in gardens or as natural textile dyes. They are endemic to Europe and have come to represent the fauna and flora of Germany. During the harvest, the combination of these two crops is a sight to behold in the German countryside.

bing-42869.jpg.title: Gray seal pup, Lundy Island, England
bing-42869.jpg.headline: Happy World Laughter Day!. World Laughter Day
bing-42869.jpg.description:
Everyone loves a good giggle, but did you know that laughter is also good for you? Today is World Laughter Day, which highlights the healing benefits of laughing, both physically and emotionally. Some studies have shown that laughing can boost the immune system, elevate mood, and reduce pain. It turns out the old adage is true—laughter really is the best medicine.

Whether the gray seal pup in our homepage image has heard something funny, or is just yawning in the waters off England's southwest coast is debatable. But we think you'll agree, it makes a good mascot for World Laughter Day.

bing-42877.jpg.title: Port Vieux-Bassin de Honfleur, Calvados, Normandie
bing-42877.jpg.headline: Un port historique. Port Vieux-Bassin de Honfleur, Calvados
bing-42877.jpg.description:
Honfleur est une ville célèbre pour son charmant Vieux-Bassin, entouré de maisons en bois datant du XVIIe siècle et de restaurants de fruits de mer délicieux. Ce site a été représenté par de nombreux artistes, dont le célèbre Claude Monet.

La ville et la région normande ont également été le théâtre d'événements historiques majeurs, notamment pendant la Seconde Guerre mondiale, dont nous célébrons aujourd'hui l'armistice. Ce port était l'un des rares en Normandie qui pouvait accueillir des navires de taille moyenne pour faciliter l'approvisionnement des troupes.

bing-42881.jpg.title: Delicate Arch, Arches National Park, Utah
bing-42881.jpg.headline: Delicate but enduring. Arches National Park, Utah
bing-42881.jpg.description: This stunning structure is Delicate Arch, the most famous of 2,000 stone arches scattered around Arches National Park in Utah. It is made up of Entrada Sandstone, the grains of which once formed a massive desert. They were cemented together by minerals, forming sandstone riddled with tiny holes. Over millennia, the rain seeped in and slowly dissolved the rock from the inside, forming these eye-catching sculptures. Most of the arches in the national park are formed from Entrada Sandstone and were once buried by other rock layers. They won't last forever, but over time, new shapes will emerge from the layers of rock below to replace them. Every year, close to 1.4 million people visit the park to see Delicate Arch and this slowly shifting landscape for themselves.

bing-42885.jpg.title: Backlight sunrays at Jim Corbett National Park
bing-42885.jpg.headline: A natural spotlight. Jim Corbett National Park, India
bing-42885.jpg.description: India's Uttarakhand state is home to the well-known wildlife refuge known as Jim Corbett National Park. The park, which bears legendary British conservationist Jim Corbett's name, is home to a wide variety of flora and animals, including tigers, elephants, leopards, and more than 500 different species of birds. Visitors can enjoy the spectacular natural splendour of the Himalayan foothills while exploring the park on foot, by elephant, or on a jeep safari. For lovers of the natural world and wildlife looking for an immersive and memorable experience, the park is a must-visit location.

bing-42889.jpg.title: The Yorkshire Dales, UK
bing-42889.jpg.headline: Rolling hills and charming villages. Yorkshire Dales National Park, England
bing-42889.jpg.description:
England's Yorkshire Dales are known for rolling hills, craggy outcrops and charming villages. It supports a diverse variety of vegetation and fauna, notably wildflowers, birds of prey and rare butterflies. The stunning Malham Cove cliff that overlooks the community of Malham and Aysgarth Falls are two of the Yorkshire Dales' most well-known attractions.

The Yorkshire Dales are also known for their excellent local produce, including cheeses, meats and beers. Visitors can sample these at the many pubs and restaurants in the area. Overall, the Yorkshire Dales are a beautiful and tranquil part of the UK and a must-visit destination for anyone who loves the great outdoors.

bing-42890.jpg.title: Rovine di Pompei, Campania
bing-42890.jpg.headline: Che è successo a questa città?
bing-42890.jpg.description:
Ammirate l’antica Pompei! Una tra le più famose città dell’Impero romano nota soprattutto, ahinoi, per il suo triste destino. Oggi, la città è letteralmente rinata grazie ai lavori di restauro e all'ingente afflusso di turisti che riscoprono quella che era una delle città più fiorenti dell'Urbe. Il benessere economico della città fu sin dall'inizio dovuto alla sua posizione strategica e le sue estese rotte commerciali, rendendola il porto dell'entroterra campano. Precedentemente sotto il dominio prima greco e poi sannitico, nel II secolo a.C. entrò a far parte dell'orbita romana, durante la quale la città conobbe un periodo di grande espansione economica, dovuta soprattutto alla produzione ed esportazione di beni quali vino e olio.

Tale opulenza, permise lo sviluppo dell'edilizia pubblica e privata. Esempio di ciò sono il Tempio di Giove, la Basilica nell'area del Foro e le dimore signorili come la Casa del Fauno. Furono inoltre eretti nuovi maestosi edifici pubblici, come l'Anfiteatro e l'Odeon. Nel 79 d.C., con l'eruzione del Vesuvio, Pompei venne letteralmente seppellita dalla cenere.  Il ricordo di quel tragico evento è giunto ai nostri giorni non solo tramite le Epistole di Plinio il Giovane, ma anche dalle espressioni terrorizzate dei calchi delle vittime investite dal flusso piroclastico.

bing-42892.jpg.title: Muttart Conservatory, Alberta, Canada
bing-42892.jpg.headline: Mesmerising glass pyramids. Muttart Conservatory, Alberta, Canada
bing-42892.jpg.description:
If you’re a nature lover, Edmonton, Alberta’s Muttart Conservatory is the perfect place to unwind and de-stress.  This botanical collection houses four iconic glass pyramids, each playing an essential role in the lifecycle of its plants. In total, the structures have 2,140 square meters of space for the featured flora.

Three of the pyramids showcase more than 700 species of plants from various parts of the world, including the arid, temperate, and tropical regions. The fourth will vary depending on when you visit—the plants change with the seasons and feature unique displays and celebrations.

bing-42893.jpg.title: Poenari Castle on Mount Cetatea, Făgăraș Mountains, Romania
bing-42893.jpg.headline: A castle fit for a count
bing-42893.jpg.description:
Peeking out above the trees in the Făgăraș Mountains of Romania is Poenari Castle, a fortress steeped in history and legend. In the 15th century, this castle was occupied by the notorious ruler Vlad III, aka Vlad the Impaler, aka Vlad Dracula.

Vlad wasn't a vampire, but he had a reputation for cruelty towards his enemies. His bloody resistance to Ottoman encroachment made him a national hero and the subject of much folklore—some of it gruesome. These tales are likely what inspired author Bram Stoker to name his fictional vampire Count Dracula.

Poenari Castle was abandoned decades after Vlad's death in 1476. Over the centuries, it fell into ruin as earthquakes and landslides sent parts of the building down the cliff and into the Argeș River below. Visiting the ruins today requires a bit of stamina. It's a 1,480-step climb to the citadel walls, unless you can change into a bat and fly to the top.

bing-42894.jpg.title: Kauehi atoll, Tuamotu Archipelago, French Polynesia
bing-42894.jpg.headline: Kauehi atoll, French Polynesia
bing-42894.jpg.description: French Polynesia's Tuamotu Archipelago is home to the breathtaking Kauehi atoll. Due to its pristine lagoon, white sand beaches and an abundance of marine life, it is a favourite vacation spot for tourists and divers. A limited number of Polynesians reside on the atoll and rely on fishing and pearl cultivation for a living. Local customs and beliefs have been passed down through the years, and they are strongly anchored to the sea and the surrounding environment. Visitors to Kauehi atoll can participate in a variety of activities like snorkeling, scuba diving and beachcombing while learning about the rich culture and stunning natural surroundings of Polynesia.

bing-42905.jpg.title: Cordouan Lighthouse, Royan, Charente, France
bing-42905.jpg.headline: King of lighthouses. Cordouan Lighthouse, France
bing-42905.jpg.description:
Built between 1584 and 1611, the Cordouan Lighthouse is France's oldest working lighthouse and the only one in the country that is still inhabited by keepers. For centuries, this maritime marvel has watched over the Gironde Estuary, on France's Atlantic coast, a treacherous area where shipwrecks were once common.

Designed by engineer Louis de Foix and remodeled in the 18th century, this stunning lighthouse with its stained-glass windows and Renaissance architecture is sometimes known as the Versailles of the Seas, after the famous French palace. Others call it the King of Lighthouses.

A visit to this historic landmark will take you on a journey to a bygone era, concluding with a climb up more than 300 steps to the lighthouse's pinnacle, where you can enjoy a commanding view of the coast and Atlantic Ocean.

bing-42912.jpg.title: Uliveto con vista sulla valle, Bevagna
bing-42912.jpg.headline: Ulivi nelle verdi colline umbre
bing-42912.jpg.description: Immersa tra il verde delle colline umbre e dei rigogliosi ulivi, sorge Bevagna, una piccola cittadina situata nella provincia di Perugia. Grazie alla sua lunga storia, visto che si hanno tracce di insediamenti umani nella zona già dall’età del ferro, e la sua bellezza architettonica, Bevagna è stata inserita tra i “Borghi più belli d’Italia” e tra le “Bandiere arancioni” per le sue eccellenti doti di accoglienza. Nel corso dei secoli, la cittadina umbra ha visto l’alternarsi alla sua guida vari Papi, oltre che famiglie nobiliari sia della città di Foligno che di quella di Perugia, tra cui spicca quella dei Baglioni; rimase sotto le influenze del papato fino al 1860, anno in cui passò, come il resto del Paese, sotto il Regno d’Italia. Bevagna ospita una ricostruzione storica che ha come riferimento il periodo medievale conosciuta con il nome di “Mercato delle Gaite”.

bing-42917.jpg.title: Henningsvær Stadion, Norway
bing-42917.jpg.headline: Pitch perfect. Henningsvær Stadion, Norway
bing-42917.jpg.description:
If you want to take in a soccer game and the grandiose beauty of the Norwegian Sea at the same time, this place is pitch perfect. Squeezed into a small Norwegian fishing village, it's fair to say that Henningsvær Stadion's grounds will probably never host a UEFA Champions League. But, while it lacks stands for spectators, there's still plenty of atmosphere to soak up in this striking location. Those who play here do so surrounded by the sound of waves, seabirds, and the smells of salt air and cod, drying on the racks surrounding the pitch.

Cod fishing is central to the economy here in Henningsvær, in the Lofoten Islands–but partly due to drone photography, this scenic pitch has become an important tourist attraction. Resting on a rugged island, surrounded by bare rocks and deep blue waters, watching a game here can make for a surreal and unforgettable experience.

bing-42928.jpg.title: Tulip festival Ottawa Canada
bing-42928.jpg.headline: A butterfly’s best friend. Tulip festival Ottawa
bing-42928.jpg.description:
The Canadian Tulip Festival begins today and will welcome visitors through May 22nd. This highly anticipated event will take place in Commissioner Park, Ottawa and marks the arrival of spring. People come in huge numbers to witness the stunning display of colourful tulip blooms. This mega festival carries along a lot of history—it began in 1953 and has since then been an epitome of the friendship between Netherlands and Canada.

This cherished tradition dates back to World War II, when the members of the Dutch royal family took refuge in Ottawa. To show their gratitude toward the hospitality of Canadians, the family sent back thousands of tulip buds. Malak Karsh, the renowned photographer, suggested the idea of this festival. This festival celebrates not only the beauty of tulips but also the multiculturism and diversity that Canada possesses.

bing-42929.jpg.title: Wild lupines in bloom
bing-42929.jpg.headline: A butterfly's best friend. Wild lupines
bing-42929.jpg.description: These stunning wild lupines bring shades of blue, pink, and purple to meadows and roadsides from early spring. They are not just a stunning addition to the landscape—they are crucial for the survival of the rare Karner blue butterfly. The larvae of the short-lived species will only feed on wild blue lupines, crawling up their stems to eat new leaves when they hatch. Once widespread across much of eastern North America, wild lupines have been in decline since the Industrial Revolution and human development has reduced their range. This has had a knock-on effect on the butterflies, which are now an endangered species. Conservation efforts have focused on replanting areas of wild blue lupines to boost butterfly numbers.

bing-42941.jpg.title: Pelicans at Sonny Bono Salton Sea National Wildlife Refuge, California
bing-42941.jpg.headline: 'Tis the season for travel. World Migratory Bird Day
bing-42941.jpg.description: The migration of birds, such as the pelicans seen here over California's Salton Sea, is part of the pulse of our planet's ecosystem. Around 40% of bird species migrate, typically in the fall and spring, some traveling incredible distances. Tiny hummingbirds can migrate 500 miles across the Gulf of Mexico overnight. Arctic terns fly between the Arctic and Antarctic each year, potentially racking up more than 1.5 million miles over a lifetime. The bar-tailed godwit can travel 7,000 miles in eight days, without stopping. On World Migratory Bird Day, we can help our feathered friends by protecting their habitats and taking simple steps like leaving less lights on at night, leaving out birdseed, and making windows more visible to avoid collisions.

bing-42942.jpg.title: Mannheim Water Tower, Germany
bing-42942.jpg.headline: Mannheim Water Tower, Germany
bing-42942.jpg.description: The Mannheim Water Tower is a historic landmark and popular tourist attraction located in Mannheim, Germany. The tower, which was constructed in 1889 and is more than 60 metres tall, was initially used to bring water to the city. It now functions as a cultural hub and observation platform with breathtaking views over Mannheim and the region. The tower is well-known for its unique architecture, which combines Gothic and Art Nouveau design elements. It is a well-liked location for photography as well as occasions like concerts and exhibitions. Anyone interested in history, architecture or simply admiring stunning views must visit the Mannheim Water Tower.

bing-42945.jpg.title: Waterfall in Meghalaya, India
bing-42945.jpg.headline: Beautiful falling waters. Waterfall in Meghalaya, India
bing-42945.jpg.description: Meghalaya, meaning 'abode of clouds' in Sanskrit, is a state in northeastern India. Also known as 'the Scotland of the East,' the state is known as one of the richest botanical habitats in Asia. Due to its heavy rainfall, Meghalaya also features some of the most breathtaking waterfalls on earth, including the one you see in today's photo.  Some of its most well-known waterfalls are Nohkalikai Falls, Seven Sisters Falls and Dainthlen Falls, but there are sixteen main waterfalls that are all worth seeing for yourself. For nature enthusiasts and adventure seekers visiting Meghalaya, experiencing these waterfalls is a must.

bing-42946.jpg.title: Fiesta de los patios cordobeses, Córdoba, Andalucía, España
bing-42946.jpg.headline: Sinfonía de fragancias y colores. Córdoba, Andalucía, España
bing-42946.jpg.description:
El Festival de los Patios Cordobeses es una Fiesta de Interés Turístico Nacional y Patrimonio Cultural Inmaterial de la Humanidad que se celebra anualmente y muestra la belleza de los patios tradicionales de Córdoba. Durante el festival, los patios se adornan con una variedad de plantas, flores y decoración de muebles antiguos, entre otros detalles, creando una explosión de colores y aromas que envuelve a los visitantes. Además de ser una muestra de la rica cultura andaluza, la feria es una oportunidad para conocer la vida cotidiana de los cordobeses y su amor por la naturaleza. Sin duda, una experiencia inolvidable para cualquier amante de la historia, la arquitectura y la jardinería.

Un dato curioso sobre los patios cordobeses es que algunos de los más antiguos de la ciudad datan de la época romana y fueron construidos como una forma de recoger y almacenar agua de lluvia. A lo largo de los siglos, estos patios se convirtieron en espacios de reunión social y hoy en día son considerados un importante patrimonio cultural de la región que no puedes perderte si te encuentras por esta maravillosa ciudad.

bing-42953.jpg.title: White-tailed deer doe and newborn fawn, Montana
bing-42953.jpg.headline: Happy Mother's Day!
bing-42953.jpg.description: Is this newborn white-tailed deer wishing its mom a Happy Mother's Day? We hope so—it won't be long before it loses those spots and strikes out on its own. But for the first year or so of its life, it will rely on mom to feed it and keep it safe from predators. We honor mothers and maternal figures everywhere on the second Sunday in May. It was first celebrated in the US in 1908 and was made a national holiday six years later in 1914, thanks to campaign efforts by social activist Anna Jarvis. While Jarvis became known as the founder of Mother's Day in the US, she later complained that it had become too commercial and began to vocally oppose it. You don't need to spend a fortune to let mom know you love her. Like our homepage fawn, you can simply spend some quality time with her today, to show how much you appreciate your nearest and 'deer'-est.

bing-42958.jpg.title: Colegiata de San Isidro desde la Plaza Mayor de Madrid, España
bing-42958.jpg.headline: ¿Dónde está este sitio tan peculiar?. Plaza Mayor, Madrid, España
bing-42958.jpg.description:
La Feria de San Isidro, que reúne grandes toreros y las ganaderías más punteras, es una de las celebraciones más populares de Madrid. Durante una semana, la ciudad se llena de música, baile y toros, siendo un evento repleto de tradición. Los amantes de los toros pueden asistir a corridas y novilladas en la Plaza de Toros de Las Ventas, mientras que los aficionados a la música pueden disfrutar de conciertos en vivo y bailes en las casetas. La Feria de San Isidro es un reflejo de la pasión y el espíritu festivo de Madrid, así como una experiencia única para los visitantes.

En la imagen de hoy podemos ver desde un arco de la Plaza Mayor la Colegiata de San Isidro, es allí donde se encuentran los restos mortales de San Isidro, patrón de Madrid, y de su cónyugue, Santa María de la Cabeza.

bing-42965.jpg.title: Morro Jable and Playa del Matorral, Fuerteventura, Canary Islands, Spain
bing-42965.jpg.headline: Aglow in the Atlantic. The Canary Islands, Spain
bing-42965.jpg.description: Welcome to Fuerteventura, one of Spain's Canary Islands, found nearly 70 miles off the northwestern coast of Africa. For thousands of years, the volcanic islands have served as an international crossroads, attracting the interest of the Romans, Arab traders, and European navigators. Agriculture has long been important here, with bananas, tomatoes, and potatoes among the main crops. But while the first voyagers came in search of trade, today's visitors come to explore the many beautiful national parks and relax on beaches like the Playa del Matorral on Fuerteventura, seen here during a spectacular sunset.

bing-42973.jpg.title: Îles de Lerins, Cannes, Côtes d’Azur
bing-42973.jpg.headline: Qui remportera la palme d’or tant convoitée cette année ?. Îles de Lerins, Cannes
bing-42973.jpg.description:
Le Festival de Cannes est l'un des événements les plus prestigieux du monde du cinéma. Fondé en 1946, il a pour objectif de promouvoir le cinéma international. Pendant la durée du festival, de nombreux films en compétition sont projetés dans différentes catégories, telles que la Palme d'Or, le Grand Prix et le Prix du Jury.

Les îles de Lérins, que nous admirons aujourd’hui, sont un archipel situé au large de la ville de Cannes, composé de deux îles principales : Sainte-Marguerite et Saint-Honorat. Sainte-Marguerite, la plus grande des deux, est surtout connue pour sa prison, où le célèbre prisonnier "L'Homme au Masque de Fer" a été détenu pendant 11 ans au XVIIe siècle. Le site est devenu depuis un musée où les visiteurs peuvent explorer les cellules et découvrir l'histoire fascinante de ce personnage légendaire.

bing-42977.jpg.title: Canoeing in Okefenokee National Wildlife Refuge, Georgia
bing-42977.jpg.headline: Serene waters on a 'trembling earth'. American Wetlands Month
bing-42977.jpg.description:
It's American Wetlands Month, a time to celebrate swamps, marshes, bogs, and other types of these important ecosystems. Wetlands play a vital role in storing carbon, improving water quality, and serving as habitat for many endangered plants and animals, including American crocodiles and whooping cranes. And yet, wetlands are threatened. Over the centuries, they have been drained to provide land for farming, industry, and housing. Pollution and invasive plants pose further threats. Since the late 1700s, more than half of the 221 million acres of wetlands that once existed in the 48 contiguous states have disappeared.

Georgia's Okefenokee Swamp, seen here, is a thriving wetland that is home to dozens of bird species, American alligators. and other critters. It is also the largest blackwater swamp in North America—the water appears almost black due to tannins from decaying vegetation. All looks calm in our homepage image, but the swamp gets its name from a Native American word that is often translated as 'trembling earth' or 'bubbling water.'

bing-42989.jpg.title: Natural Bridges State Beach in Santa Cruz, California
bing-42989.jpg.headline: Getting a bird's-eye view. Natural Bridges State Beach in Santa Cruz, California
bing-42989.jpg.description:
California brown pelicans, cormorants, and gulls enjoy jostling for position on top of this stunning rock formation in Natural Bridges State Beach in Santa Cruz. It is the sole surviving natural 'bridge' in this state park. Once three bridges stood side-by-side here, carved by waves into cliffs that jutted out into the Pacific. This one stood in the middle, but the outermost bridge collapsed in 1905 and the innermost one disappeared in 1980.

The erosion of the waves is relentless, so eventually the final arch will collapse, and the birds will have to find another favorite perch. But there are plenty of other views on offer. The park is also a seasonal home to migratory monarch butterflies, which flutter through the air or cluster together in its eucalyptus grove. And if you're lucky, you might spot a migrating whale or see seals and otters playing offshore.

bing-42995.jpg.title: Wiedehopf füttert seine Jungen nach der Exkursion, Biosphärenreservat Mittelelbe, Sachsen-Anhalt
bing-42995.jpg.headline: Vater und Sohn. Vatertag
bing-42995.jpg.description:
In Deutschland wird der Vatertag jedes Jahr am Christi Himmelfahrtstag gefeiert, der immer 40 Tage nach Ostern stattfindet. Die Geschichte des Vatertags in Deutschland geht auf das 19. Jahrhundert zurück. Es handelte sich in der damaligen Zeit vor allem um einen Männertag. Diese trafen sich und waren unter sich, tranken oft dazu Alkohol und genossen ihre exklusive Gesellschaft. Es waren andere Zeiten und andere Sitten.

Heute ist der Vatertag nicht mehr, so wie er es früher einmal war. Die meisten deutschen Männer haben, einer Umfrage nach gemeint, dass sie den Tag gar nicht richtig feiern oder wahrnehmen. In anderen europäischen Ländern wird dieser an anderen Tagen gefeiert. In Italien und in Spanien z. B. findet dieser immer am 19. März statt. Der 19. März ist der Josefstag. In solchen Ländern ist es üblich, dass Kinder Geschenke für den Vater basteln oder Lieder und Gedichte, vor allem in der Schule oder im Kindergarten, vorbereiten.

Der Vatertag ist ein Tag, an dem die Männer im Mittelpunkt stehen und an dem man ihnen für ihre harte Arbeit und ihr Engagement dankt. Obwohl der Tag traditionell von Männern gefeiert wird, wird er zunehmend von der gesamten Familie als Gelegenheit genutzt, um gemeinsam Zeit zu verbringen und zu feiern.

bing-43001.jpg.title: Museo Soumaya, Plaza Carso, Mexico City, Mexico
bing-43001.jpg.headline: International Museum Day
bing-43001.jpg.description: For International Museum Day, we’re featuring the towering aluminum-clad Plaza Carso building, part of the Museo Soumaya in Mexico City. It was built to house Mexican billionaire Carlos Slim’s vast art collection, which includes the largest collection of sculptures by Auguste Rodin outside France. The building, designed by Fernando Romero, is a sculpture in itself. Covered in 16,000 hexagonal aluminum plates, the windowless facade looks stunning and helps protect the artwork inside from intense sunlight. It is one of many eye-catching museum buildings worldwide which attract interest both for their collections and for their creative design.

bing-43002.jpg.title: La Manga, Murcia, Spain
bing-43002.jpg.headline: La Manga, Murcia, Spain
bing-43002.jpg.description: Southeast Spain's La Manga is a coastal region between the Mar Menor lagoon and the Mediterranean Sea. It is a popular beach getaway for both visitors and residents due to its beautiful beaches and crystal-clear water. La Manga, which means 'the sandbar' in English, is Europe’s largest saltwater lagoon. Its shallow, protected waters make it an international destination for water activities including sailing, windsurfing, canoeing and scuba diving. It is the perfect destination to visit all year round due to its pleasant climate and bright days.

bing-43013.jpg.title: Sumatran rhinoceros female eating leaves, Way Kambas National Park, Sumatra, Indonesia
bing-43013.jpg.headline: On the edge of extinction. Endangered Species Day
bing-43013.jpg.description:
Sumatran rhinos like this one were once plentiful across the forests and swamps of Southeast Asia. But there are thought to be fewer than 80 alive today, surviving only on the Indonesian islands of Sumatra and Borneo. Logging and hunting have led to their inclusion on the ‘red list’ of more than 42,100 critically endangered species. This one is pictured in Way Kambas National Park, Sumatra, where a rhino sanctuary is home to a tiny population and is the center of a breeding and research program.

Endangered Species Day highlights the thousands of animals and plants under threat of extinction, as well as conservation success stories. Humpback whales, gray wolves, tigers, and bald eagles have all seen population increases, thanks to conservation efforts. It’s now 50 years since the US passed the Endangered Species Act, a powerful wildlife conservation law. But while it is said to have saved 99 percent of species it protects, the challenges remain — habitat loss, invasive species, and climate change are among ongoing threats. The work continues to bring more animals and plants back from the brink.

bing-43025.jpg.title: European honeybees in Sheffield, England
bing-43025.jpg.headline: The buzz about World Bee Day. World Bee Day
bing-43025.jpg.description: As flowers start to bloom, you'll hear the soft hum of bees buzzing between them, drinking nectar, and gathering pollen to take back to their hives. Some pollen grains on their bodies get carried between flowering plants, helping them to reproduce, yield better crops, and support other species. The UN proclaimed May 20 as World Bee Day to highlight the importance of these pollinators and the threats they face, including habitat loss, climate change, and pesticide use. Busy bees attend to over 90% of the world’s top 107 crops and are vital to our food supply, but populations worldwide have declined. So today, let's support our industrious friends to help them go about their important work in peace.

bing-43030.jpg.title: Temps de Flors, Girona, Cataluña, España
bing-43030.jpg.headline: Recorre las calles repletas de colores y aromas. Temps de Flors, Girona, Cataluña, España
bing-43030.jpg.description:
El festival Temps de Flors comenzó en 1954 como una iniciativa del Girona Garden Club, un grupo de aficionados a la jardinería y la horticultura. El objetivo del festival era embellecer la ciudad y fomentar el amor por las flores y las plantas entre los ciudadanos. A lo largo de los años, el festival ha ido creciendo y evolucionando, expandiéndose por toda la ciudad y convirtiéndose en un evento importante en el calendario cultural de Cataluña. Entre los lugares más destacados, se encuentran la Catedral de Girona, el Monasterio de Sant Pere de Galligants, la Basílica de Sant Feliu, la Plaza de la Independencia y el Jardín de la Infancia. Además, muchas tiendas, restaurantes y edificios privados abren sus puertas al público durante el festival, permitiendo a los visitantes explorar rincones secretos y escondidos de la ciudad.

El festival ofrecer una serie de eventos culturales y actividades para el disfrute de los visitantes como música en vivo, oportunidad para probar la gastronomía local, arte y exposiciones, así como visita a monumentos y edificios históricos.

Un dato curioso es que cada año se utilizan más de 100.000 plantas y flores para crear las exhibiciones, además, los organizadores del evento trabajan con floristas y paisajistas locales para utilizar plantas y flores cultivadas de forma sostenible y ecológica. Otra curiosidad que te sorprenderá saber es que ha sido fuente de inspiración para artistas como Woody Allen. Desde luego, este evento único te hará amar la jardinería y sus rincones.

bing-43031.jpg.title: Universum Bremen, Science Center
bing-43031.jpg.headline: Die Zukunft ist heute. Museumstag
bing-43031.jpg.description:
Das Universum Bremen ist ein interaktives Wissenschaftsmuseum, das am 9. September im Jahre 2000 eröffnet wurde. Dieses umfasst eine Fläche von 4.000 Quadratmetern. Es bietet eine Vielzahl von interaktiven Exponaten und anschaulichen Experimenten, die die Welt der Wissenschaft und Technologie für Besucher jeden Alters zugänglich machen.

Das Wissenschaftsmuseum besteht aus vier verschiedenen Themenbereichen, die auf drei Ebenen verteilt sind: „Mensch und Gesundheit“, „Technik und Innovation“, „Mensch und Natur“ und „Kinder-Universum“. Dieser letzte Themenbereich ist speziell für Kinder bis zu zwölf Jahren konzipiert. Das Universum Bremen bietet nicht nur eine interaktive Ausstellung, sondern auch regelmäßig wechselnde Sonderausstellungen zu verschiedenen Themen an. Darüber hinaus werden auch Workshops und Veranstaltungen für Schulen und Kindergärten sowie Ferienprogramme für Kinder angeboten.

Insgesamt ist das Universum Bremen ein einzigartiges Museumserlebnis, das sich perfekt für den heutigen Tag eignet. Besucher jeden Alters können hier auf eine spannende Art und Weise lernen wie die Welt um uns herum funktioniert.

bing-43037.jpg.title: Pont d’Arcole on the Seine river, Paris, France
bing-43037.jpg.headline: Spanning the Seine. Pont d'Arcole over the Seine river, Paris, France
bing-43037.jpg.description:
Welcome to Paris, France’s ancient capital city, through which flows one of the country’s longest rivers, the Seine. Human habitation here dates back to at least the 3rd century BCE, when a Gallic tribe called the Parisii settled on an island in the middle of the river. Today, that island is known as the Île de la Cité, seen on the left of our photo, and is home to Notre-Dame cathedral, as well as other striking buildings such as the medieval Conciergerie, pictured here.

It is linked to the Place de l'Hôtel-de-Ville by the Pont d’Arcole, one of 37 bridges connecting the city’s left and right banks. The Pont d’Arcole was built in the 1850s and holds a special place in Parisiennes’ hearts. In 1944, it supported General Jacques-Philippe Leclerc's tanks on their way to liberate Paris.

bing-43048.jpg.title: Ottawa Parliament Buildings Sunset View, Canada
bing-43048.jpg.headline: Celebrating Canada and England's common bond. Victoria Day
bing-43048.jpg.description: Today's holiday honours Queen Victoria’s birth and was created to strengthen the bond between England and what was formerly known as the Province of Canada. While the holiday—permanently moved to the Monday before May 25 in 1952—is a federal holiday, it is celebrated differently across the country.  One notable celebration is Ottawa's day-long event at Parliament Hill. It starts with a flag-raising ceremony followed by a parade that starts at the Canadian War Museum and concludes at Parliament. The festivities end with a display of fireworks in the night sky for spectators watching from the banks of the Ottawa River. However you're celebrating, we hope you have a fun and festive Victoria Day!

bing-43049.jpg.title: Arenal Volcano seen from Monteverde, Costa Rica
bing-43049.jpg.headline: Life in the clouds. International Day for Biodiversity
bing-43049.jpg.description:
It’s International Day for Biological Diversity, a day to celebrate the variety of life on Earth in all its forms, from bacteria, plants, and animals to entire ecosystems like coral reefs and rainforests. All living things within each ecosystem are interconnected, and we rely on healthy ecosystems for our water, food, medicines, clothes, energy, and shelter. But many species are threatened with extinction and ecosystems are being destroyed, which mean Earth’s rich biodiversity is in decline.

Our homepage image shows Costa Rica’s Monteverde Cloud Forest, home to about half of all species in the country, including more than 2,500 types of plants and 400 bird species. Here you’ll find jaguars and pumas living alongside sloths, howler monkeys, and the endangered resplendent quetzal. This forest alone represents about 2.5% of the world’s biodiversity, the perfect ambassador for today’s event, which calls on us to rethink our relationship with nature and work to be better stewards of the Earth.

bing-43053.jpg.title: Coffee plantations, Kerala, India
bing-43053.jpg.headline: Nature's boost fruit. Coffee plantations, Kerala, India
bing-43053.jpg.description: Kerala, located in the southwestern region of India, is a major producer of coffee. The state's coffee plantations are primarily located in the districts of Wayanad and Idukki. The coffee produced in Kerala is mainly of Robusta and Arabica varieties and is known for its strong and distinctive flavour. The state's coffee plantations are often interspersed with other crops like pepper, cardamom and jackfruit, creating a diverse agricultural landscape. Kerala's coffee plantations attract tourists who come to experience the scenic beauty of the lush green hillsides and learn about the history and culture of coffee cultivation in the region.

bing-43061.jpg.title: Western box turtle
bing-43061.jpg.headline: Turtle power!. World Turtle Day
bing-43061.jpg.description:
With distinctive markings on their shells, western box turtles, such as the one seen here, are among the most widely recognized turtle species and one of two box turtle species in the US. Box turtles are named after their dome-shaped shells which are hinged at the bottom, allowing the shell to close like a box if it needs to hide from predators. They generally live for around 25 years but can survive for more than 50, and there have been reports of some living for 100 years.

Some turtles may have existed more than 100 million years ago but while they outlived the dinosaurs, more than half of all turtle and tortoise species are now on the verge of extinction. Today is World Turtle Day, an event set up to celebrate these incredible creatures and highlight their disappearing habitats.

bing-43073.jpg.title: The Old Fortress of Corfu, Greece
bing-43073.jpg.headline: Standing firm. Old Fortress, Corfu, Greece
bing-43073.jpg.description: This imposing structure is the Old Fortress on the Greek island of Corfu, off the western coasts of Greece and Albania. Situated in a strategic location between the Ionian and Adriatic seas, Corfu became one of the most fortified places in Europe amid successive sieges by the Ottoman Empire. The island was ruled by the Republic of Venice for 400 years until the late 18th century, which built forts in Corfu's Old Town to defend its maritime trading interests. They held off three Ottoman sieges in 1537, 1571, and 1716 but have been repaired, rebuilt, and added to over the centuries. The Old Fortress has witnessed the rise and fall of mighty empires for hundreds of years, from the tip of a rocky peninsula jutting into the sea. These days, however, it is home to the public library and Corfu's archives.

bing-43080.jpg.title: Pozzo del Papa scala e finestra a doppia elica, Orvieto
bing-43080.jpg.headline: Le scale a doppia elica del pozzo
bing-43080.jpg.description: Tra le numerose meraviglie architettoniche e naturalistiche che è possibile ammirare nella verde Umbria, merita sicuramente una visita il pozzo di San Patrizio a Orvieto. La struttura fu edificata per volere del Papa Clemente VII per tutelare l’approvvigionamento d’acqua della città in caso di assedio o di calamità naturali. Il pozzo deve la sua forma particolare ad un capolavoro di ingegneria elaborato da Antonio da Sangallo il Giovane che fu in grado di realizzare due rampe elicoidali che non si incrociano mai per facilitare così il lavoro di trasporto dell’acqua dal fondo. Il pozzo è tuttora visitabile e sul suo fondo, alla profondità di 54 metri, vi è ancora presente l’acqua che proviene da una sorgente naturale.

bing-43082.jpg.title: Hay Festival, UK
bing-43082.jpg.headline: Portable portals into our imagination. Hay Festival
bing-43082.jpg.description: The Hay Festival is an annual weeklong literature and arts festival that takes place in Hay-on-Wye, a small town in Wales, UK. The spring festival was founded in 1988 by Peter Florence and his parents and has since become a very prestigious literary events with sister festivals taking place internationally in countries such as India, Kenya, Spain and Colombia. The festival features a diverse range of talks, workshops, and performances from renowned writers, poets, artists, musicians, and other cultural figures from around the globe. Avid readers spend their time devouring literary content in tents and fields. To top it off, sculptures made up of books are placed around the grounds to make visitors feel embraced by their love of literature.

bing-43085.jpg.title: Saksun, Faroe Islands, Denmark
bing-43085.jpg.headline: Where the grass is greener. Saksun, Faroe Islands, Denmark
bing-43085.jpg.description:
Nestled in a picturesque valley next to a lagoon flanked by mountains, Saksun is a small, remote village famous for its stunning vistas. It is situated on the coast of Streymoy in the remote Faroe Islands, which sit about halfway between Iceland and Scotland in the North Atlantic. Home to these iconic houses with turf roofs and a tiny population—estimates vary between 8 and 30—it is said that there are more waterfalls in Saksun, than houses.

There's something to be said about the beauty of Saksun and its power to hypnotize visitors with its peaceful atmosphere. It is a far cry from the relatively bustling streets of Tórshavn, the capital of the islands. With greenery as far as the eye can see, Saksun provides an almost otherworldly sense of solitude.

bing-43097.jpg.title: Wat Sri Sawai in Sukhothai Historical Park, Thailand
bing-43097.jpg.headline: The splendors of Sukhothai. Wat Sri Sawai in Sukhothai Historical Park, Thailand
bing-43097.jpg.description: Welcome to Sukhothai Historical Park, one of Thailand's most spectacular UNESCO World Heritage sites. The park is dotted with ancient temples, the remains of a palace, and towering Buddha statues—within its boundaries is the historic town of Sukhothai, an important metropolitan hub in the 13th and 14th centuries. The name translates as 'the dawn of happiness' and you can spend many happy hours here, strolling among the beautiful lawns, trees, and lakes. The temple on our homepage is Wat Si Sawai, one of the oldest on the site, founded in the late 12th or early 13th century. Sukhothai was the capital of the first Kingdom of Siam more than 700 years ago and this historic site continues to offer a window onto what is sometimes seen as a golden age of Thai civilization.

bing-43109.jpg.title: Quiver trees in Namibia
bing-43109.jpg.headline: Stretching to the sky. Quiver trees in Namibia
bing-43109.jpg.description: The quiver trees pictured on our homepage are uniquely suited to Namibia's hot, dry climate. They are not trees at all, but an endangered species of aloe plant. These succulents can grow up to 30 feet tall and live for 200 years. The name comes from the Indigenous San people who made quivers out of the plant's tube-shaped branches to hold their arrows while hunting. You can see scattered quiver trees across southern Namibia, but for sheer numbers, head to the Quiver Tree Forest, where more than 200 of these distinctive plants grow among dolerite rock formations outside the city of Keetmanshoop. In June and July, during Namibia's winter, you can see the plant's flowers in bright, yellow bloom.

bing-43114.jpg.title: Romería de El Rocío, Huelva, Andalucía, España
bing-43114.jpg.headline: ¿Dónde van estos peregrinos?. Romería de El Rocío, Huelva, Andalucía, España
bing-43114.jpg.description:
