Esta semana, Pamplona se convierte en una de las ciudades más festivas de España donde podrás disfrutar de una experiencia única llena de tradición, diversión y emoción.

bing-43589.jpg.title: Southern rockhopper penguins, Falkland Islands
bing-43589.jpg.headline: A peck between penguins. International Kissing Day
bing-43589.jpg.description: This photograph captures a heartwarming moment between two southern rockhopper penguins, the perfect image for International Kissing Day. Why do we kiss? Well, dozens of cultures don't kiss on the lips at all. For those that do, theories range widely, from the chemical reactions in the brain, to ancient ancestral parents chewing food for their children, to simply smelling each other. Of course, no scientific explanation can capture the magic of a shared kiss. Perhaps that's why artists including Prince, Faith Hill, and Hall & Oates have all had chart-toppers about lip-locking; they have found a way to put an indescribable feeling into words.

bing-43590.jpg.title: Southern rockhopper penguins, Falkland Islands
bing-43590.jpg.headline: Penguins in Falkland Islands
bing-43590.jpg.description: The Falkland Islands are home to the charming Southern Rockhopper Penguins. These small penguins are known for their distinctive yellow eyebrows, spiky yellow crests and red eyes. They have a unique hopping behaviour, navigating the rocky cliffs and jumping from one ledge to another. Southern Rockhoppers form large colonies during the breeding season, with thousands of pairs gathering in one place. They feed on krill and small fish, and their playful antics and vibrant appearance make them a popular attraction for wildlife enthusiasts visiting the Falkland Islands.

bing-43601.jpg.title: Cocoa pods from Ambanja, Madagascar
bing-43601.jpg.headline: A chocolate lover's favorite fruit. World Chocolate Day
bing-43601.jpg.description:
Happy World Chocolate Day! Hidden inside these colorful pods are cocoa seeds, or beans, which will be fermented, roasted, and ground on their way to being turned into chocolate, a sweet treat with a worldwide fanbase.

Chocolate has a fascinating history. Its origins can be traced back to the Indigenous Olmec people of Mesoamerica, who dried and fermented the seeds of the cacao tree to create an unsweetened alcoholic beverage. The solid chocolate bars we love today came much later, in the 19th century, when J.S. Fry and Sons put them into production. The company created its first solid bar in 1847, closely followed in 1849 by rival firm Cadbury. Things snowballed from there and today, we are spoiled for choice. So, whether you prefer the creamy sweetness of milk chocolate, or the bitterness of super dark chocolate, today is the perfect time to indulge yourself in this delicious confection.

bing-43608.jpg.title: Sirmione, Lago di Garda
bing-43608.jpg.headline: Sirmione la bella
bing-43608.jpg.description:
Sirmione è un affascinante borgo situato sulle sponde del Lago di Garda. Il castello che potete osservare sulla foto di oggi si chiama Castello Scaligero di Sirmione. Fu costruito durante il XIII secolo su ordine di Leonardino della Scala. Nel 1405 il castello diventò di dominio della Repubblica di Venezia. Fu proprio in quell’epoca che fu realizzata la darsena che possiamo ammirare ancora oggi. Sirmione è rinomata per le sue sorgenti termali benefiche, che attirano visitatori da ogni parte del mondo. Inoltre, la maestosa rocca che si erge nel borgo offre una prospettiva panoramica mozzafiato sulla pittoresca area circostante. La bellezza incontaminata di Sirmione è esaltata dalla splendida natura che la circonda: le dolci colline adornate da vigneti, gli oliveti secolari e l’acqua azzurra del lago di Garda rendono questo luogo qualcosa di magico.

Come avevamo accennato in precedenza Sirmione è ricca di storia. Non è situato nel comune di Sirmione, bensì a Gardone Riviera, a pochi km di distanza. Lì si trova il Vittoriale degli Italiani, la celeberrima casa del poeta-soldato Gabriele D’Annunzio. Una residenza straordinaria, nella quale si racchiude l’eclettismo del poeta italiano. Potrete visitare la sua reggia e spaziare dalla sua biblioteca personale, che contiene più di diecimila volumi, ad un teatro all’aperto se non che ammirare la nave militare Puglia incastonata nel giardino. E questo è solo l’inizio...

bing-43609.jpg.title: Les célèbres parasols multicolores de la plage de Deauville, Normandie
bing-43609.jpg.headline: Vive les vacances d’été !. Vacances d’été
bing-43609.jpg.description:
Les parasols de Deauville sont un véritable mythe, ils illuminent le ciel de Normandie et les yeux des promeneurs admiratifs, créant ainsi une ambiance empreinte d’un charme unique. Implantés en 1875, leurs couleurs et leurs formes ont évolué au fil des années. C’est dans les années 60 qu’ils ont adopté définitivement ces tons vifs, ce diamètre unique, les franges, les embouts en bois et cette façon si particulière de nouer les jupes lorsque le parasol est replié et se plante dans le sable.

Cette photo illustre avec bonheur cette première journée de vacances scolaires. Adieu tableau, cartable, horaires et interros… et vive l’été ! Un repos bien mérité vous attend pour recharger les batteries et créer des souvenirs inoubliables. Alors, bonnes vacances à toutes et à tous !

bing-43613.jpg.title: Mildred B. Cooper Memorial Chapel, Bella Vista, Arkansas
bing-43613.jpg.headline: Sanctuary among the trees. Mildred B. Cooper Memorial Chapel in Arkansas
bing-43613.jpg.description: The Mildred B. Cooper Memorial Chapel in Bella Vista, Arkansas, is one of the most charming buildings in the country. Constructed in 1988 and named for a beloved community member whose husband commissioned it, this chapel was designed by E. Fay Jones, an architect known for his wooden creations. Its unique design seamlessly blends modernist principles with nature's splendor, resulting in a harmonious space which blends with its natural setting. Surrounded by lush trees, with sunlight filtering in through the huge glass windows, the chapel serves as a perfect sanctuary for contemplation and prayer. It also stands as a powerful testament to the ability of architecture to inspire and uplift the human spirit.

bing-43625.jpg.title: Moselle River loop, Kröv, Germany
bing-43625.jpg.headline: In the loop. Moselle River loop near Kröv, Germany
bing-43625.jpg.description: The Moselle River, a tributary of the powerful Rhine, meanders through the landscapes of France, Luxembourg, and Germany. Along the way, it carves out valleys of breathtaking natural beauty, dotted with towns and historic landmarks. Lush, sun-drenched vineyards cling to the steep slopes overlooking the river, producing some of the finest wines in the world, including riesling, pinot blanc, and pinot gris, to name a few. The river's gentle flow and sparkling waters invite visitors to embark on leisurely cruises or peaceful walks along its shores. The Moselle creates a haven for nature lovers, wine enthusiasts, and history buffs alike.

bing-43637.jpg.title: Field of lavender, Somerset, England
bing-43637.jpg.headline: A scented sea of purple. A field of English lavender
bing-43637.jpg.description: Delighting the senses with its vibrant hues and fragrant blooms, lavender is thought to have arrived in England with the Romans, around 2,000 years ago. While it’s nice to look at, the Romans likely brought it with them for its many practical uses, including cooking, repelling insects, and as an antiseptic. Many perfumes, modern and historical, have featured lavender, and Queen Elizabeth I is purported to have used lavender scent. You’ll find lavender fields scattered across the country. This one is a typical example, a quintessential summer sight here in the picturesque county of Somerset, in southwest England.

bing-43638.jpg.title: Field of lavender, Somerset, England
bing-43638.jpg.headline: A field of English lavender
bing-43638.jpg.description: The picturesque county of Somerset, in south-west England is renowned for its lovely lavender fields. Delighting the senses with their vibrant hues and fragrant blooms, they offer a captivating sight. Lavender came to England with the Romans around 2,000 years ago. While lavender is nice to look at, the Romans likely brought it with them for its many practical uses including cooking, repelling insects and as an antiseptic. Many perfumes, modern and historical, have featured lavender, and Queen Elizabeth I is purported to have used it. Lavender fields are still common in England today, and these ones in Somerset are a true delight, enchanting all who encounter their natural beauty.

bing-43649.jpg.title: Hong Kong SAR
bing-43649.jpg.headline: A sea of humanity. World Population Day
bing-43649.jpg.description:
On July 11, 1987, the world is thought to have welcomed its 5-billionth person. Thirty-six years later, our population has reached 8 billion and is still rising. World Population Day, established by the UN, is a day to reflect on how much life Earth can sustain, and how our lives impact our environment.

Pictured here is Hong Kong, a city recognized as one of the world's most densely populated areas, with approximately 17,582 people per square mile. Though Hong Kong has a low birth rate, the density remains high as people live longer thanks to improvements in healthcare, a contributing factor to population increases worldwide. While this colorful night scene might appear glamorous, it is also an example of light pollution, which can disrupt ecosystems and affect our health—one of humanity's many impacts on the world around us.

bing-43654.jpg.title: Lagos de Covadonga, Asturias, España
bing-43654.jpg.headline: Prepárate para hidratarte con estas vistas. Lagos de Covadonga, Asturias, España
bing-43654.jpg.description:
El Parque Nacional de los Picos de Europa alberga un conjunto de lagos, montañas escarpadas y vegetación exuberante. Los Lagos de Covadonga, situados en esta zona, son un conjunto de tres lagos, el Ercina, Bricial y Enol que vemos en nuestra imagen de hoy. Estos impresionantes lagos forman parte de la belleza natural y valor histórico de Asturias, famosa por sus paisajes, tradiciones y gastronomía.

Además, tal día como hoy, a pocos kilómetros de este maravilloso lago, podrás disfrutar de la gastronomía y sidra típica de esta región, ya que se celebra el Festival de la Sidra Natural de Asturias y Nava, donde tendrás el placer de deleitarte con degustaciones, concursos, exhibiciones y espectáculos.

Este festival ofrece eventos musicales, danzas tradicionales y actividades culturales que permiten a los visitantes sumergirse en la rica tradición asturiana; pero si te consideras una persona más aventurera, te recomendamos llevarte un buen plato típico a la montaña y disfrutar de estas maravillosas vistas.

bing-43661.jpg.title: Sand bar in Nakupenda Beach Nature Reserve, Zanzibar, Tanzania
bing-43661.jpg.headline: The world's most exclusive beach?. Nakupenda Beach Nature Reserve, Zanzibar, Tanzania
bing-43661.jpg.description: Off the west coast of Zanzibar, the Nakupenda Beach Nature Reserve sits on a small, sandy island. Surrounded by the Indian Ocean, this sand bar is a popular destination with tourists looking to soak up the sun's rays on its white sands. Plentiful marine life here creates a vibrant underwater world that is perfect for snorkeling. The islands of Tanzania are home to an array of wildlife like the Pemba scops owl and the African fish eagle. To the north of Nakupenda, there is a giant tortoise sanctuary on Changuu Island, while their sea turtle cousins swim in the surrounding waters.

bing-43662.jpg.title: Capo Caccia, Sardinia, Italy
bing-43662.jpg.headline: Capo Caccia, Sardinia, Italy
bing-43662.jpg.description: In the northern part of Sardinia, in the province of Alghero, there is an imposing promontory formed by limestone rocks which has been given the name of Capo Caccia. Its name derives from the pigeon hunting activity to which the notables of the 19th century were dedicated. The promontory housed large colonies of monk seals that took refuge inside the numerous natural caves, which today have completely disappeared. On the other hand, you can admire numerous types of birds such as the peregrine falcon, the swift or Bonelli's eagle. The seabed surrounding this part of Sardinia is characterised by the presence of red coral, which is still used to create jewellery by local artisans.

bing-43673.jpg.title: Zhangye Danxia National Geopark, Gansu province, China
bing-43673.jpg.headline: Walking a rocky rainbow. International Rock Day
bing-43673.jpg.description:
International Rock Day, on July 13, celebrates these hardy heroes, which have played a big part in human history since at least the Stone Age. They served as humanity's first tools and as nature's journals, protecting ancient fossils and documenting changes caused by geological processes.

Our homepage image shows Zhangye National Geopark's Rainbow Mountains in China, an incredible landscape created over millions of years. Those colorful layers are formed of sedimentary sandstone rock. Iron oxide gave the rock its predominately rusty hue, while other oxides tinted the various layers brown, yellow, and green. Sandstone and minerals that were once layered on top of each other were lifted and distorted by tectonic movement, revealing those colorful stripes. And that is not the end of this geological tale. This unique landscape continues to change, as wind and water erosion sculpts new pillars and ravines. No matter what your favorite category of rock is—metamorphic, sedimentary, or igneous—rocks of every kind helped build the world we live in today.

bing-43679.jpg.title: Botanische Nacht im Botanischen Garten, Berlin
bing-43679.jpg.headline: Botanischer Palast. Botanische Nacht in Berlin
bing-43679.jpg.description:
Heute ist der 14. Juli, und heute findet zum 14. Mal das Event „Botania“ in Berlin statt. Sie werden in eine unglaubliche, fast surreale Welt der Pflanzen eintauchen. Ausstellungen und Installationen werden Ihnen die Vielfalt der Natur auf eine Art und Weise vorstellen, wie Sie sie noch nie zuvor erlebt haben.

Lichtinszenierungen, Kunst, Tanz, Musik und vieles mehr bietet die Wohltat Entertainment GmbH bei diesem Event den Gästen an. Es gibt zehn magische Welten zu erleben und zu entdecken. Idyll der Illusion, Funkeltal, Hain der Hoffnung und viele mehr warten nur darauf erkundet zu werden. Es werden aber auch interaktive Technologien eingesetzt, die Ihnen die Möglichkeit geben, aktiv mit der Natur zu interagieren.

Diese Veranstaltung bietet Ihnen vieles. Hier können Sie nicht nur Spaß haben, sondern auch Ideen austauschen und über Themen wie Technik, Natur und die biologische Welt sprechen. Experten auf diesem Gebiet werden Vorträge halten, um Ihr Wissen zu erweitern und die Verbindung zwischen dem Menschen und der Pflanzenwelt zu vertiefen.

bing-43681.jpg.title: Feu d'artifice du 14 juillet à Carcassonne, Occitanie
bing-43681.jpg.headline: Allons enfants !. 14 juillet, Fête nationale française
bing-43681.jpg.description:
Le 14 juillet, fête nationale en France, commémore la Révolution française de 1789. Cette journée est marquée par des défilés militaires, des feux d'artifice et des festivités populaires à travers tout le pays. Elle symbolise les valeurs fondamentales de la République française : liberté, égalité et fraternité.

Carcassonne, la cité médiévale fortifiée qui illustre cette journée, est située dans le département de l'Aude en Occitanie. C’est un véritable trésor architectural inscrit au patrimoine mondial de l'UNESCO. Elle se distingue par ses remparts imposants, ses tours, ses ruelles pavées et ses maisons à colombages.

Carcassonne combine parfaitement son héritage historique avec une multitude d'événements culturels qui nous submergent dans l'époque médiévale. De surcroît, depuis ses remparts, vous pouvez profiter d'une vue magnifique sur la ville moderne en contrebas, créant ainsi un contraste captivant entre le passé et le présent.

bing-43685.jpg.title: Blacktip reef sharks, Maldives
bing-43685.jpg.headline: A shiver of sharks on the hunt. Shark Awareness Day
bing-43685.jpg.description: Today, on Shark Awareness Day, let's dive into the ocean's depths to meet our finned friends. It's believed that sharks have been cruising the oceans for at least 420 million years. Today’s homepage shows blacktip reef sharks, hunting in a group in the waters around the Maldives, one of more than 500 species of shark, each uniquely adapted to its habitat. From the graceful hammerhead with its panoramic vision to the fastest species, the sleek mako, shark species are diverse, but a third face extinction. Among threats are unregulated fishing and abandoned nets as well as demand for shark fins. They have a fearsome reputation but are the victims of myths and misconceptions that paint them as mindless killing machines. Today, let's celebrate these magnificent creatures, a key part of healthy marine ecosystems, by advocating for their conservation.

bing-43694.jpg.title: Le pont d’Avignon et le palais des Papes, Provence Alpes Côte d’Azur
bing-43694.jpg.headline: Sous le pont d’Avignon…. Le pont d’Avignon et le palais des Papes
bing-43694.jpg.description:
Le festival d'Avignon, qui a débuté le 5 juillet, est l'un des plus grands festivals de théâtre de rue au monde. Fondé en 1947 par Jean Vilar, il attire chaque année des artistes, des compagnies théâtrales et des spectateurs du monde entier. Pendant le festival, Avignon se transforme en un lieu unique où se déroulent des représentations théâtrales de tout genre, des spectacles de danse, des concerts, des expositions et des débats artistiques.

La ville Avignon, située dans la région Provence-Alpes-Côte d'Azur, a une histoire riche et fascinante. Au XIVe siècle, la ville devient le siège de la papauté, après que le pape Clément V décide de s'établir à Avignon au lieu de Rome. Pendant près d'un siècle, de 1309 à 1377, Avignon devient le centre de l'Église catholique romaine et accueille les papes successifs, qui résident dans le magnifique Palais des Papes.

Aussi, le pont d’Avignon est le monument emblématique de la ville. Construit au XIIe siècle, il enjambait autrefois le Rhône avant d'être partiellement détruit. Aujourd'hui, il ne reste que 4 arches sur les 22 du pont d'origine. Il est également célèbre dans le monde entier grâce à une chanson traditionnelle intitulée "Sur le Pont d'Avignon". Cette chanson populaire évoque la danse qui se déroulait autrefois sur le pont lors des fêtes et des rassemblements.

bing-43698.jpg.title: Castelmezzano, Italy
bing-43698.jpg.headline: A postcard-perfect landscape. Castelmezzano, Italy
bing-43698.jpg.description: Embraced by the rugged peaks of the Lucanian Dolomites, the ancient village of Castelmezzano in southern Italy glows with charm. Its narrow alleys and cobblestone streets pass buildings that cling to the mountainside. This picturesque destination is brimming with history; from its rule by feudal lords to battles long forgotten. It's believed that the Normans settled here around the 11th century AD and constructed a castle, from which the village gets its name. Castelmezzano isn't just a sleepy portrait of the past, it also offers adventure activities for the brave, including a high-altitude zip line between mountains on the Volo dell'Angelo (Flight of the Angel). Yet the finest pleasure the small village offers might just be grabbing a cup of coffee and watching the sun rise behind the majestic mountain peaks, illuminating those huddled houses as the streetlamps go out.

bing-43710.jpg.title: Bear Hole Brook, Catskill Mountains, New York
bing-43710.jpg.headline: Babbling on and on. Bear Hole Brook, Catskill Mountains, New York
bing-43710.jpg.description: Stretched over 4,000 square miles in upstate New York, the Catskill Mountains captivate visitors with their breathtaking beauty. Towering peaks cloaked in forests surround valleys filled with meandering streams like Bear Hole Brook, seen in today's image. The region boasts hiking trails that wind through enchanting woodlands, past waterfalls and lakes while motorists can enjoy scenic drives and spot the region's covered bridges, dating from the 1800s. The Catskills also hold a place in cultural history, attracting artists and dreamers and as the fictional setting for the movie 'Dirty Dancing'—which was actually filmed in Pembroke, Virginia. With other attractions including ski resorts and picturesque small towns and hamlets, visitors continue to flock to the Catskills, a huge wilderness within driving distance of more than 20 million Americans.

bing-43722.jpg.title: Cloughoughter Castle in Lough Oughter, County Cavan, Ireland
bing-43722.jpg.headline: No moat required. Cloughoughter Castle, County Cavan, Ireland
bing-43722.jpg.description: Cloughoughter Castle sits on a small island in the middle of Lough Oughter, a huge complex of lakes and waterways in County Cavan in Ireland. Its first stones are thought to have been laid in the early 13th century by the Anglo-Norman de Lacy family, but the O'Reilly clan took possession of the area in 1233 and completed the castle's construction. They retained control of Cloughoughter Castle for centuries, but by 1653, it had been bombed and abandoned. Since then, it has been in ruins, resplendent in a sort of tattered grandeur. It can only be visited by boat but, as a symbol of Ireland's medieval heritage, it is a must-see for history and castle enthusiasts alike.

bing-43728.jpg.title: Hintersee, Ramsau, Bayern
bing-43728.jpg.headline: Die magische Kunst der Natur. Hintersee bei Ramsau, Bayern
bing-43728.jpg.description:
Der Sommer ist endlich da und mit ihm die lang ersehnten Ferien! Entfliehen Sie dem Alltag und genießen Sie die Schönheit der Natur. Verreisen Sie lieber alleine oder unternehmen Sie gern eine Rundfahrt mit Familie und Freunden? Hier am Hintersee ist jede Wahl eine gute Wahl. Falls Sie alleine verreisen sollten, keine Angst, die Natur wird Sie aufnehmen, Ihnen zuhören, und Ihnen Gesellschaft leisten. Hier können Sie sich erholen und den Alltagsstress vergessen.

Wenn Sie gern baden und Sonne tanken, können Sie dies am Seeufer tun. Sollte es Ihnen zu warm werden, bietet der kühle, frische und klare Hintersee die Erfrischung, die Sie brauchen. Genießen Sie das sanfte Plätschern des Wassers und lauschen Sie dem Rauschen am Strand. Das Paradies gibt es tatsächlich und es ist gar nicht allzu weit entfernt!

In den Bergen hingegen wird sich Ihnen eine majestätische Kulisse eröffnen. Wollen Sie die Giganten der Natur herausfordern und sich beim Klettern selbst übertreffen? Oder wollen Sie einfach nur gemütlich durch die Berge spazieren und die spektakuläre Aussicht genießen, die Sie umgibt? Dieser Ort hat schon viele Menschen inspiriert und zur Genesung beigetragen. Wollen Sie es auch mal versuchen?

bing-43734.jpg.title: Great hornbill, Khao Yai National Park, Thailand
bing-43734.jpg.headline: This bird is peak beak. Great hornbill, Thailand
bing-43734.jpg.description: The great hornbill is a remarkable bird found in the tropical forests of Southeast Asia. Despite weighing as much as 9 pounds and growing up to 4 feet long, it is an agile flyer capable of maneuvering through dense forests. Alongside its striking black and yellow plumage, the great hornbill has a unique helmet-like casque on its bill, which amplifies its calls. The bird primarily feeds on fruit but also eats small mammals, reptiles, and insects. While incubating her eggs, the female great hornbill seals herself inside a tree cavity, leaving a small opening through which the male inserts food. This magnificent bird holds cultural and spiritual significance in many Southeast Asian cultures as a sacred animal and the subject of festivals.

bing-43741.jpg.title: Duomo di San Pietro, Modica, Italia
bing-43741.jpg.headline: Che cattedrale stupenda!
bing-43741.jpg.description:
Nella stupenda città barocca di Modica, in provincia di Ragusa, si erge impetuosa la Chiesa di San Pietro. Questa cattedrale è nota come il duomo della città bassa, condividendo questo primato alla pari con il Duomo di San Giorgio. Ad accrescerne ulteriormente l'imporatnza è stato il suo inserimento nella lista dei Patrimoni dell’Umanità Unesco.

Danneggiato dai sismi che lo colpirono e ristrutturato più volte nel corso dei secoli, l'edificio è costituito da un'elegante scalinata affiancata da statue raffiguranti i dodici Apostoli, meglio noti come “Santoni”. Suddiviso al suo interno in tre navate, lo stabile poggia ancora sulle stesse fondamenta della chiesa del Seicento, della quale rimane la Cappella dell’Immacolata, oggi  sacrestia, ove è ancora possibile leggere la scritta "1620". I capitelli in stile corinzio e i numerosi decori che lo abbeliscono, come la pavimentazione del 1864 in marmo e i superbi affreschi, rendono questa struttura una meta obbligata per gli amanti della storia dell'arte e i curiosi in cerca di un tuffo nel passato. In caso stiate organizzando una vacanza in Sicilia, considerate l'inclusione di Modica nel vostro itinerario.

bing-43746.jpg.title: Crescent Lake near Dunhuang, Gansu province, China
bing-43746.jpg.headline: This oasis is no mirage. Crescent Lake near Dunhuang, China
bing-43746.jpg.description: Crescent Lake is a captivating natural wonder hidden in the vast Gobi Desert near the Chinese city of Dunhuang in Gansu province. This oasis, named for its unusual shape, has been a vital water source here for centuries. The lake is thought to have formed in a valley carved by wind and been fed by an underground spring. It sits amid Dunhuang's 'singing' sand dunes, which make a noise when the wind blows. The sand dunes also help stop the lake from being swallowed by sand and conservation efforts have ensured that it doesn't dry out. Visitors enjoy boating on the lake, camel rides through the surrounding dunes, and seeing ancient Buddhist art and murals in the nearby Mogao Caves.

bing-43758.jpg.title: The moon seen from the Orion spacecraft of NASA's Artemis mission
bing-43758.jpg.headline: Celebrating our lunar neighbor. International Moon Day
bing-43758.jpg.description: International Moon Day is celebrated on July 20, the day humans first set foot on the moon during the Apollo 11 mission in 1969. It recognizes our lunar achievements and highlights scientific and technological advancements, like NASA's Orion spacecraft, seen here. Designed for deep space exploration, Orion completed a test flight to the moon without astronauts in 2022 and will carry out a crewed orbit in 2024. The plan is to return astronauts to the moon's surface in 2025. NASA hopes that these flights, along with events like International Moon Day, will encourage public engagement and education about the moon and its influence on Earth, as well as the potential for future space exploration and colonization.

bing-43763.jpg.title: Playa de La Concha vista desde el Monte Igueldo, San Sebastián, España
bing-43763.jpg.headline: Muévete al ritmo de las olas. Playa de La Concha vista desde el Monte Igueldo, San Sebastián, España
bing-43763.jpg.description:
San Sebastián, conocida también por Donostia en euskera, es una pintoresca ciudad situada en el País Vasco, norte de España. Esta preciosa ciudad cuenta con una gran bahía y extensas playas famosas en toda Europa, como la que vemos hoy en nuestra imagen, donde poder practicar surf, dar paseos o incluso deleitarse con festivales como el Jazzaldia (festival de jazz) que da hoy su comienzo y cuenta con una gran reputación internacional.

El País Vasco destaca por su belleza natural, enormes acantilados y vistas dignas de ser enmarcadas, tal y como lo hicieron en Juego de Tronos, donde rodaron varias escenas en estos impresionantes paisajes.

Si en estos días de verano recorres esta impresionante ciudad, no olvides moverte al ritmo de las olas y el jazz mientras te deleitas con sus sabrosos “pintxos”, famosos gastronómicamente en toda España.

bing-43770.jpg.title: Storseisundet Bridge, Atlantic Ocean Road, Norway
bing-43770.jpg.headline: Connecting the dots. Storseisundet Bridge, Norway
bing-43770.jpg.description: Norway's picturesque Atlantic Ocean Road crosses eight bridges as it makes its way across islands, islets, and reefs to link the island of Averøya with the Romsdal Peninsula on the mainland. The longest of them, pictured here, is the Storseisundet Bridge. This bridge, surrounded by ample natural beauty, was tough to build. It took six years, and during construction workers were pelted by the region's unpredictable weather, including 12 hurricanes. It opened in 1989 and remains a popular visitor attraction. With its dramatic curve and sudden incline, Storseisundet Bridge creates the illusion of suddenly disappearing into the ocean, making drivers skip a heartbeat. Its construction showcases the brilliance of Norwegian engineering, blending seamlessly with the landscape.

bing-43777.jpg.title: Polignano a Mare, Puglia
bing-43777.jpg.headline: Una perla nell'azzurro mare
bing-43777.jpg.description:
Chi non vorrebbe vivere un'estate fatta di colori mediterranei, profumi e sapori della cucina tipica del terriorio pugliese? Polignano a Mare è una splendida cittadina situata sulla costa adriatica, a circa 60 chilometri da Bari. Ha una storia molto antica, che risale al periodo romano, quando era un importante centro di scambio commerciale tra Brindisi e Roma. Successivamente, fu dominata dai Normanni, dai Veneziani e dagli Aragonesi, che lasciarono le loro tracce nell’architettura e nella cultura del luogo.

Famosa per le sue bellezze naturali, come le scogliere a strapiombo sul mare, le grotte marine e le spiagge di sabbia e ciottoli, Polignano ha anche un affascinante centro storico, che si raggiunge attraversando l’Arco Marchesale, l’antica porta della città. Qui si possono visitare la Chiesa Matrice, dedicata a Santa Maria Assunta e risalente al XIII secolo, la Chiesa del Purgatorio, del XVIII secolo e decorata con teschi e ossa, il Museo Pino Pascali, dedicato all’artista polignanese scomparso prematuramente nel 1968, e il balcone di Domenico Modugno, da dove si può godere di una vista mozzafiato sul mare e sulla statua del celebre cantante di “Volare”.

È anche un ottimo punto di partenza per esplorare i dintorni, ricchi di attrazioni e luoghi d’interesse. Tra questi ci sono l’Abbazia di San Vito, un antico complesso monastico sul mare, Alberobello, la città dei trulli dichiarata patrimonio dell’umanità dall’UNESCO, Monopoli, una pittoresca cittadina marinara con il suo castello e il suo porto, e Castellana Grotte, dove si possono visitare le spettacolari grotte carsiche.

bing-43782.jpg.title: Hammock camping in a bald cypress tree, Florida
bing-43782.jpg.headline: Want to hang out?. National Hammock Day
bing-43782.jpg.description: It’s National Hammock Day! A day to slowly unwind while rocking gently from side to side. These days, hammocks are associated with summer relaxation, but they were originally developed by Central Americans to protect them from dangerous insects and animals. Today the hammock is a traveler's best buddy, made from a variety of materials like fabric, netting, or rope. But where best to hang it? Florida boasts some beautiful hammock hang-out spots, like the bald cypress tree pictured on our homepage. Have hammock, will travel and relax. It's just that simple.

bing-43793.jpg.title: The Calgary Central Library, also known as the Calgary New Central Library
bing-43793.jpg.headline: Books are man's best friend. Calgary Central Library, Alberta
bing-43793.jpg.description: In the heart of Calgary resides the Calgary Central Library. The magnificent structure stands tall like a literary sentinel, giving access to seekers of knowledge and welcoming curious visitors. In this sanctum of literature, one is surrounded by a collection of 450,000 books. Creativity blooms in every nook and cranny of this futuristic library, which offers more than 30 meeting rooms, a modern yet elegant café, outdoor plaza, recording studios, and a lot more. The Calgary Central Library was designed by an architectural firm named Snøhetta and opened its doors in 2018. Information is accessible via books, digital media, and interactive technology. One can easily end up spending hours exploring its modern and unique architecture. The Calgary Central Library is a sanctuary where imagination and exploration intertwine.

bing-43794.jpg.title: Edinburgh Tea Estate, Nuwara Eliya, Sri Lanka
bing-43794.jpg.headline: Hello, is it 'tea' you’re looking for?. Nuwara Eliya, Sri Lanka
bing-43794.jpg.description: Legend has it that tea was first brewed accidentally around 2737 BC in China thanks to a strong wind and some loose leaves. If you find that hard to swallow, there are other origin stories to choose from. However, one thing is certain—the feeling it stirs in tea drinkers worldwide. From gongfu tea practice in China to darye in Korea, there are plenty of fascinating tea cultures to savor. Tea tourism has gained popularity, with visitors to tea plantations and estates learning all about their history. Our homepage image shows one such place, Nuwara Eliya's Edinburgh Estate in the central highlands of Sri Lanka. Nuwara Eliya's colonial-era buildings and mist-shrouded tea gardens have earned it the name 'Little England.' The area is known for producing some of the world's finest orange pekoe tea. So, for your next trip, are you willing to 'chai' something new?

bing-43806.jpg.title: Zebras in Tarangire National Park, Tanzania
bing-43806.jpg.headline: A day for cousins of every stripe. Cousins Day
bing-43806.jpg.description: When it comes to honoring family members, parents and siblings get most of the attention—but today, let us sing the praises of our cousins on Cousins Day! These extended family members hold a special place in our hearts. They're not quite siblings, but more than mere friends. When we're young, they're the buddies we go adventuring with, while the adults stay behind to make small talk. Maybe you've fallen out of touch with your cousins, or maybe you're still close—either way, today's a great day to reach out, say hello, and reminisce. That's what it looks like these zebras are doing; there's likely a set of cousins or two in this group that's horsing around on the savannah in Tanzania.

bing-43811.jpg.title: Piscina natural en Santa Cruz de Tenerife, España
bing-43811.jpg.headline: Fusión entre naturaleza y glamur. Piscina natural en Santa Cruz de Tenerife, España
bing-43811.jpg.description:
La isla de Tenerife, en las Islas Canarias, es internacionalmente conocida por sus playas idílicas y su volcán Teide. No obstante, también es digna de resaltar su celebración de la Recreación de la Gesta, durante la cual los tinerfeños conmemoran que tal día como hoy en 1797 repelieron el asedio británico capitaneado por el entonces contraalmirante Horatio Nelson.

Los habitantes de Santa Cruz se visten de época y recrean cómo sus antepasados libraron aquellas batallas a finales del s.XVIII, en las cuales el propio Horatio Nelson resultó herido por el conocido como ‘Cañón Tigre’, obligando a su evacuación y dando por finalizado el conflicto.

En medio de tanta agitación, las piscinas naturales de Tenerife ofrecen un refugio de serenidad. Estos tesoros escondidos, alimentados por las aguas del océano Atlántico, son verdaderos oasis naturales donde los visitantes pueden sumergirse en sus aguas cristalinas y disfrutar de las propiedades terapéuticas de las algas marinas. Una combinación perfecta que no te debes perder si vas por allí.

bing-43818.jpg.title: Laguna de Torrevieja, Alicante, Spain
bing-43818.jpg.headline: Pretty in pink. Laguna de Torrevieja, Spain
bing-43818.jpg.description: When we encounter bodies of water in nature, we might expect hues of blue, from the pale cyan shade of lagoons to the navy blue of deep lakes. But pink water—where on Earth could that be found? At (deep breath) El Parque Natural de Las Lagunas de La Mata y Torrevieja in Alicante, Spain. Here, there are two lakes: one green and one pink, and it is the latter that you see on our homepage. The highly saline water, dotted with clusters of salt crystals, is the perfect environment for microscopic algae, which are rich in carotenes. This results in the rosy tinge that protects the algae from solar radiation. And the pink is just getting started, as the algae are eaten by tiny crustaceans, which turn pink and are then eaten by flamingos, which acquire the rosy hue as well.

bing-43827.jpg.title: ondon Aquatics Centre at the Queen Elizabeth Olympic Park in Stratford
bing-43827.jpg.headline: Go with the flow. Queen Elizabeth Olympic Park, Stratford, London
bing-43827.jpg.description: Built to stage the 2012 Summer Olympics and Paralympics, the London Aquatics Centre is a 560-acre complex, containing 6.5 kilometres of waterways and 10.5 hectares of woods, and holds a place among the most recognised green spaces in the UK. Award-winning architect Zaha Hadid designed the 160 metre-long and 80 metre-wide wave-like roof of the main building to mirror the surrounding riverside landscapes. Interestingly, when studying the east London site before construction, archaeologists came across many prized finds: four Iron Age skeletons, Roman coins, a 4,000-year-old Neolithic flint axe, and a 19th century boat.

bing-43830.jpg.title: Jubail Mangrove Park in Abu Dhabi, United Arab Emirates
bing-43830.jpg.headline: Say hello to these halophytes!. International Day of Mangrove Conservation
bing-43830.jpg.description: Natural vegetation is sparse in the United Arab Emirates, due to its hot and dry desert climate. But along its coast, mangroves have taken root. These hardy trees and shrubs are halophytes, salt-tolerant plants that can filter 90% of the salt from the seawater they live in. Despite their resilience, mangroves are threatened globally, largely due to human activity. Mangrove coverage is thought to have halved over the past 40 years, and they are dwindling much faster than forests overall. The UN has established the International Day of Mangrove Conservation, scientific funding, Global Geoparks, and World Heritage sites to try to reverse these trends. These efforts are vital; mangroves help prevent erosion and protect against storm surges, as well as providing a home for fish, crustaceans, and other wildlife.

bing-43842.jpg.title: Arc de Triomphe du Carrousel and Louvre Pyramid, Paris, France
bing-43842.jpg.headline: Another Arc de Triomphe?. Arc de Triomphe du Carrousel and the Louvre Pyramid
bing-43842.jpg.description: Paris features an impressive stretch of parks, gardens, and monuments called the Axe historique, or historical axis, that starts at the Louvre Museum, in the city center, and extends west, ending at La Grande Arche. Today's image shows the Arc de Triomphe du Carrousel at the eastern end of the route, with the embodiment of Peace riding a chariot atop it. It shouldn't be confused with the better-known and much larger Arc de Triomphe de l'Étoile, which stands 2 miles away, halfway along the Axe historique. It's a lovely walk from one to the other, through the Jardin Des Tuileries and along the famous Avenue des Champs-Élysées. If the statue on the left side of the photo caught your eye, wave hello to King Louis XIV on horseback.

bing-43847.jpg.title: Parque de la Naturaleza de Cabárceno, Cantabria, España
bing-43847.jpg.headline: Un día para relajarse. Parque de la Naturaleza de Cabárceno, Cantabria, España
bing-43847.jpg.description:
El Día de Cantabria fue proclamado oficialmente el 28 de julio de 1985 mediante la Ley de Cantabria 5/1985, aprobada por el Parlamento de Cántabro. La elección de esta fecha se basa en la tradición y devoción hacia la Virgen de la Bien Aparecida, patrona de Cantabria. Este día es una ocasión especial para que los cántabros se unan en una celebración que destaca la belleza y la riqueza cultural de su tierra, como el Parque de la Naturaleza de Cabárceno que vemos hoy en nuestra imagen.

Este parque, inaugurado en 1990, es uno de los principales atractivos turísticos de la región y se extiende sobre una antigua explotación minera a cielo abierto, lo que le confiere un paisaje único y espectacular.

Los animales viven en amplios recintos que imitan su hábitat natural, proporcionando condiciones óptimas para su bienestar. Entre las especies que se pueden encontrar en el parque se incluyen elefantes, leones, tigres, jirafas, osos, rinocerontes, aves rapaces y lobos, entre otros. En total, se estima que alberga más de 120 especies de animales que podrás avistar si visitas este maravilloso parque.

bing-43854.jpg.title: San Blas Islands, Panama
bing-43854.jpg.headline: A blue-tiful island. San Blas Islands, Panama
bing-43854.jpg.description: Nestled off the northern coast of Panama, the San Blas Islands are an archipelago of more than 360 islands in the Caribbean Sea. Known for their clean, calm waters, they are the perfect place for adventure sports such as snorkeling, surfing, and diving. Staghorn and pillar coral are among the species found in coral reefs surrounding the islands, which teem with marine life. The islands are inhabited primarily by Gunas—people indigenous to Guna Yala—who preserve their way of living with vibrant, traditional clothing, thatched-roof huts known as 'bohíos,' and intricate, handcrafted mola textiles.

bing-43866.jpg.title: Bengal tiger, Ranthambore National Park, India
bing-43866.jpg.headline: Eyes of the tiger. International Tiger Day
bing-43866.jpg.description: It's International Tiger Day! A day to celebrate these magnificent animals and consider how best they can be protected. The largest wild cats in the world, all tiger species are endangered, facing challenges including habitat loss, the illegal wildlife trade, and poaching. The Bengal tiger, an iconic subspecies primarily found in India, is the star of today's image. As apex predators, Bengal tigers play a vital role in maintaining ecological balance by controlling populations of deer, wild boar, and bison. With an estimated population in the wild of between 2,500 and 3,000, tiger conservation is crucial to secure the future of this majestic species.

bing-43871.jpg.title: Allariz, Orense, Galicia, España
bing-43871.jpg.headline: Fiestas de Santiago Apóstol de Compostela. Allariz, Orense, Galicia, España
bing-43871.jpg.description:
Durante esta semana Galicia se envuelve en fiestas, en concreto en un evento religioso y cultural en honor a Santiago Apóstol, patrono de España y especialmente de la ciudad de Santiago de Compostela, en Galicia.

Durante las Fiestas de Santiago Apóstol, la ciudad se llena de música, danzas, desfiles, conciertos y eventos religiosos. Uno de los momentos más destacados es la tradicional "Ofrenda del Botafumeiro", en la que este enorme incensario es balanceado en la catedral de Santiago por un grupo de “tiraboleiros”. Este ritual es uno de los atractivos más impresionantes de las celebraciones y atrae a grandes devotos y visitantes a la ciudad.

Además de las celebraciones religiosas, las Fiestas de Santiago Apóstol incluyen numerosas actividades culturales, como conciertos de música tradicional gallega, exhibiciones de danzas folclóricas, ferias artesanales y muestras gastronómicas. Los visitantes tienen la oportunidad de disfrutar de la exquisita cultura gallega y degustar platos típicos como el pulpo a la gallega o las empanadas.

bing-43872.jpg.title: Zwei Jungfüchse spielen auf einer Wiese, Deutschland
bing-43872.jpg.headline: Lebenskraft durch Freundschaft und Leidenschaft. Tag der Freundschaft
bing-43872.jpg.description:
Heute ist es wieder so weit: Heute feiern wir den „Internationalen Tag der Freundschaft“. Wir feiern diesen Tag auf der ganzen Welt, um die Bedeutung von Freundschaften in unserem Leben zu würdigen. Doch was ist Freundschaft? Meinen wir alle dasselbe, wenn wir von Freundschaft sprechen?

Unserer Meinung nach ist Freundschaft eine besondere Bindung zwischen Menschen, die auf Vertrauen, Unterstützung und gegenseitiger Wertschätzung beruht. Freundschaft spielt in unserem sozialen Leben eine sehr wichtige Rolle. Mit einem Freund oder eine Freundin durchs Leben zu gehen ist ein wichtiger Teil unseres Daseins, das uns bereichert und im Leben unterstützt.

Jeder lebt und erlebt Freundschaft auf seine eigene Art und Weise. Es gibt keine Anleitung dafür, ein guter Freund zu sein. Vielleicht schon. Wie wäre es mit Ehrlichkeit, Einfühlsamkeit, Respekt und Vertrauen? Haben Sie sich für diesen besonderen Tag etwas vorgenommen? Vielleicht alte Freunde treffen und auf die guten alten Zeiten anstoßen?

bing-43878.jpg.title: Farmland in the Palouse, Washington
bing-43878.jpg.headline: Perfect, pastoral Palouse. Palouse farmland, Washington state
bing-43878.jpg.description: The Palouse region in the Pacific Northwest is known for its picturesque landscapes, agricultural heritage, and unique geological features. Those stunning hills in our homepage image were formed over tens of thousands of years, from dust and silt blown by the wind, known as loess. The Palouse's fertile soil and climate make it ideal for farming and it is known for its wheat, barley, lentils, and other crops. With its beautiful rolling hills covered in patchworks of green and golden fields, it is often compared to Italy's Tuscany region or the French countryside.

bing-43890.jpg.title: Rock House, Hocking Hills State Park, Ohio
bing-43890.jpg.headline: Home of stone. Rock House in Hocking Hills State Park, Ohio
bing-43890.jpg.description: Ancient and beautiful, Rock House is the only true cave in Ohio's Hocking Hills State Park. This corridor, halfway up a 150-foot cliff, was carved by erosion and has offered shelter to various dwellers over different periods. Long before European settlers arrived, the area's Native American people are believed to have used Rock House as a refuge. Small recesses in the rock walls are thought to have been used as baking ovens, while troughs gouged in the cave's floor helped them to collect water. The walls of Rock House have seven window-like openings, allowing sunlight to filter through, casting beautiful patterns inside the cave and offering cliffside views over the trees for generations of Rock House dwellers.

bing-43898.jpg.title: Plage de Rondinara et sa réserve naturelle, Bonifacio, Corse
bing-43898.jpg.headline: Le paradis Corse. Plage de Rondinara et sa réserve naturelle, Bonifacio
bing-43898.jpg.description:
Bienvenue à la plage de Rondinara, l’une des plus belles plages d’Europe ! Préparez-vous à vivre une expérience inoubliable dans un cadre enchanteur où la beauté de la nature se marient harmonieusement.

Imaginez-vous marcher pieds nus sur le sable doux et doré de la plage, sentir la brise marine caresser votre visage et entendre le doux murmure des vagues. La plage de Rondinara est un paradis caché, niché dans une baie en forme de coquillage, offrant une vue à couper le souffle sur les collines verdoyantes qui l'entourent.

Mais ce n'est pas tout ! La plage de Rondinara est également adossée à une réserve naturelle préservée où vous pourrez explorer les sentiers sinueux et observez la diversité de la faune et de la flore qui y résident. Vous pourrez apercevoir des espèces végétales et animales rares, dont certaines sont endémiques à la région. C'est un véritable havre de paix pour les amoureux de la nature.

bing-43901.jpg.title: Confederation Bridge, Prince Edward Island, Canada
bing-43901.jpg.headline: The only road to P.E.I.. Confederation Bridge, Prince Edward Island
bing-43901.jpg.description:
Spanning across the azure waters of the Northumberland Strait, the Confederation Bridge stands as a triumphant engineering marvel in Prince Edward Island, Canada. The prodigious structure measures nearly 13kilometres in length and connects the island to the mainland, forever transforming accessibility to this picturesque province. Constructed with meticulous precision and completed in 1997, the bridge symbolizes the unity and strength of the Canadian Confederation. Its sleek design and towering presence gracefully blend with the surrounding natural beauty.

Today, the bridge serves as a vital lifeline, accommodating vehicular traffic and fostering economic growth. As travellers cross its expanse, they are embraced by panoramic views, pretty sunsets and the unmistakable sense of embarking on a journey to charming Prince Edward Island.

bing-43902.jpg.title: Climber on Denali, Denali National Park, Alaska
bing-43902.jpg.headline: There's no denying the power of Denali. National Mountain Climbing Day
bing-43902.jpg.description: Today is National Mountain Climbing Day, dedicated to celebrating the sport while highlighting its many risks and rewards. In a bid to scale the tallest peaks and conquer difficult terrain around the world, mountain climbers embark on physically strenuous journeys that demand exceptional training and experience. But the panoramic views and sense of achievement after reaching the summit makes the effort worthwhile. Our image today is that of Denali, North America's highest peak at 20,310 feet, in south-central Alaska. The name 'Denali' means 'the high one' in the native Athabascan language. Four climbers, Walter Harper, Harry Karstens, Robert Tatum, and Hudson Stuck, were the first to set foot on the top of the mountain in 1913.

bing-43914.jpg.title: Sandstone butte in Capitol Reef National Park, Utah
bing-43914.jpg.headline: Sandstone butte-iful. Capitol Reef National Park, Utah
bing-43914.jpg.description: Behold the rugged grandeur of Utah's red rock country. This hidden gem of the American Southwest is Capitol Reef National Park, a tapestry of towering cliffs, twisting canyons, colorful sandstone buttes, and sweeping desert landscapes. Less popular than Zion and Bryce Canyon, the park offers a pleasantly uncrowded experience for visitors keen to enjoy this spectacular landscape. It is also home to a wide variety of plants and animals, including the elusive desert bighorn sheep and more than 230 bird species. But its crown jewel is the nearly 100-mile long Waterpocket Fold, a 7,000-foot-high step in the rock layers, officially known as a monocline. This massive wrinkle on the surface of the planet was formed around 50 to 70 million years ago.

bing-43926.jpg.title: Zelenci Nature Reserve, Slovenia
bing-43926.jpg.headline: A lake that never freezes. Zelenci Nature Reserve, Slovenia
bing-43926.jpg.description: Experience nature's palette at its colorful best at Zelenci Springs, where Italy, Austria, and Slovenia meet, and multiple springs combine to form this aquamarine lake. Here in Slovenia’s Triglav National Park, these crystal-clear waters are the source of the Sava Dolinka, which runs into the country’s longest river, the Sava. Peer closely at the lakebed and you will see tiny springs bubbling up beneath the water's surface. These spring waters never freeze as underground water temperatures stay around 41 degrees Fahrenheit, enough to keep flowing through harsh winters in this alpine region.

bing-43938.jpg.title: Tintern Abbey, Wales
bing-43938.jpg.headline: A window on the past. Tintern Abbey, Wales
bing-43938.jpg.description: Set deep in a gorge of the UK's River Wye, Tintern Abbey has an enduring presence. Originally built in wood, this Gothic masterpiece in Monmouthshire, Wales, was rebuilt in stone in 1269. It was in use for centuries until the dissolution of the monasteries in the 1530s, when Henry VIII broke with the Catholic Church. The building fell into ruin but, as the centuries passed, word of its intricate stones and romantic, pastoral setting spread. From painter J. M. W. Turner to poet William Wordsworth, many artists were drawn to the abbey over the years. This majestic ruin is now a national icon on the Welsh bank of the River Wye, on the border between Wales and England. There's another abbey in County Wexford, Ireland, of the same name. Back in olden days, the one in Wales was often known as 'Tintern Major,' while the Ireland one was called 'Tintern de Voto' (Tintern of the Vow).

bing-43944.jpg.title: Rakotzbrücke in Kromlau, Landkreis Görlitz, Sachsen
bing-43944.jpg.headline: Der See und seine Brücke uns entzücke!. Rakotzbrücke in Kromlau, Landkreis Görlitz, Sachsen
bing-43944.jpg.description:
Dieses Bild könnte ein Foto eines Werkes des französischen Künstlers Claude Monet sein, finden Sie nicht auch? Brücken und Seen waren Leitmotive vieler seiner Gemälde. Der Rakotzsee ist ein künstlicher See. Das genaue Datum seiner Entstehung ist unbekannt, doch es wird geschätzt, dass er zwischen 1842 und 1875 im Auftrag von Rittergutsbesitzer Hermann Friedrich Roetschke angelegt wurde. Wir befinden uns im Azalee- und Rhododendronpark in Kromlau, im Landkreis Görlitz im Osten Deutschlands.

Heute ist dies ein idealer Ort, um der Realität zu entfliehen, in den Armen der Natur Geborgenheit zu suchen, sich zu erholen und im Wasser zu plantschen. Alle sprechen vom Sommer, wir auch! Doch Sie können diese wundervolle Gegend auch im Winter besuchen, dies bleibt Ihnen überlassen. Die Rakotzbrücke und der See sind zu jeder Jahreszeit ein Postkartenidyll, daher empfehlen wir Ihnen diese märchenhafte Gegend zu erkunden.

Wussten Sie, dass die Rakotzbrücke auch in einigen Filmen zu sehen ist? In „Der Zauberlehrling“ von Frank Stoye, der von Goethes gleichnamigen Ballade inspiriert wurde, ist sie zu bewundern. Doch sind dieser See und seine Brücke so bezaubernd und verlockend, dass sogar die Regisseure von Matrix diesen Schauplatz für „Matrix Resurrections“ als Filmkulisse benutzt haben.

bing-43950.jpg.title: Atlantic puffin, Iceland
bing-43950.jpg.headline: It's puffling season!. Atlantic puffin, Iceland
bing-43950.jpg.description: Meet the Atlantic puffin! Known as 'sea parrots' or 'clowns of the sea,' about 60% of all Atlantic puffins nest on the coasts of Iceland. If you visit between June and September, you might see baby puffins being flung off a cliff. Do not be alarmed! It's part of puffling season, a yearly tradition on Iceland's Westman Islands, home of the largest puffin colony in the world. Residents search with a flashlight for lost or wayward pufflings—baby puffins—around cliffs, harbors, and the seaside area. They pick them up with gloved hands, take them to a cliff before sundown, and toss them over the edge. Why? Well, the lights of the town can confuse pufflings, who use the light of the moon and stars to guide them to the ocean, where they live for much of the year. Residents are simply doing their part to ensure they find their way to their natural habitat.

bing-43962.jpg.title: Kagami-ike (Mirror Pond), Nagano, Japan
bing-43962.jpg.headline: A peaceful place for self-reflection. Kagami-ike, Nagano, Japan
bing-43962.jpg.description: This serene Japanese landscape is reflected in the still waters of an artificial reservoir known as Kagami-ike, meaning ‘mirror pond.' Surrounded by lush greenery and the Togakushi Mountain Range in Nagano Prefecture, Kagami-ike emerges from the morning mists to create an enchanting spectacle. During the cherry blossom season, visitors walk among sakura petals that float along the breeze while, in autumn, they can enjoy its surrounding orange and yellow foliage. This secluded spot is a wonderfully peaceful place for mindful meditation and self-reflection.

bing-43974.jpg.title: Bodie Island Lighthouse, Nags Head, North Carolina
bing-43974.jpg.headline: Sentinels of the sea. National Lighthouse Day
bing-43974.jpg.description: Happy National Lighthouse Day! A beacon, a warning, and a symbol of hope and home, lighthouses have existed for thousands of years. The earliest known was the Pharos of Alexandria, which stood an estimated 330 feet tall. Built by the ancient Egyptians in the 3rd century BCE, an open fire was lit at its highest part to guide ships into port. Illumination technology advanced over the centuries, culminating in today's electric versions beaming light that can be seen from over 20 miles away. North Carolina's Bodie Island Lighthouse, pictured here, was built in 1872 and overlooks a section of ocean once known as the Graveyard of the Atlantic. Since then, it's been doing its best to outshine the stars above, as it guides sailors home to safe harbor.

bing-43977.jpg.title: 五花海，阿坝九寨沟旅游景区，四川省，中国
bing-43977.jpg.headline: 恍若童话世界，胜似人间仙境
bing-43977.jpg.description:
在立秋的这一天，我们带您来欣赏一下九寨沟五花海绝美景色。中国的秋季景色堪称四季之最，树木层林尽染，叠翠流金。虽然酷热与凉爽的分水岭并不在立秋这一天，但是人们在经历了一个夏季的高温季节后，开始期待秋日的凉爽温度，也开始期待出门欣赏秋季的美景。

九寨沟五花海之美在于能够在同一水域中呈现出鹅黄、墨绿、深蓝、藏青等色，色彩缤纷，是九寨沟各个景点中最为精彩的景点之一。进入秋季的九寨沟恍若童话世界，胜似人间仙境！翠海、叠瀑、彩林、雪峰，演绎着赤、橙、黄、绿、青、蓝、紫的梦幻组合，令人几乎不敢相信眼前的现实！

bing-43982.jpg.title: Champ de lavande sur le plateau de Valensole au lever du jour, Alpes-de-Haute-Provence
bing-43982.jpg.headline: Un petit coin de paradis provençal. Champ de lavande sur le plateau de Valensole, Alpes-de-Haute-Provence
bing-43982.jpg.description:
Valensole est un petit coin de paradis en plein cœur de la Provence. Situé dans le département des Alpes-de-Haute-Provence, ce charmant village est réputé pour ses vastes champs de lavande qui s'étendent à perte de vue. Dès que l'on pénètre dans cette région, une douce odeur de lavande nous envahit. Les couleurs vives des fleurs violettes contrastent magnifiquement avec le bleu intense du ciel provençal.

Valensole, qui vient de vallis et solis, "La Vallée du Soleil", a su conserver le caractère et le charme authentiques des villages de Haute Provence. Avec plus de 300 jours de soleil par an, le site est également très apprécié pour la qualité et la pureté de son air.

La lavande, emblème de Valensole, est cultivée ici depuis des siècles. Les champs s'étendent sur des kilomètres, formant des vagues pourpres qui se déplacent doucement au gré du vent. En été, lorsque les fleurs sont en pleine floraison, c'est un véritable enchantement pour les sens.

bing-43983.jpg.title: View of St Michael's Mount in Cornwall at sunset, Penzance, Cornwall, United Kingdom
bing-43983.jpg.headline: Cheerful colours of a Cornwall classic. St Michael's Mount in Cornwall
bing-43983.jpg.description:
Take a journey through steep, uneven paths on this ancient and picturesque island. Located in Mount's Bay, Cornwall, and connected to the town of Marazion by a causeway of granite block, St Michael's Mount is capped with a mediaeval church, an ancient castle and a terraced garden.

Spiritual seekers believe the island holds a unique energy owing to its age-old ley lines that intersect at the heart of the Mount and run under the sea. The island is rich in history, with the oldest building dating back to the 12th century. The St Aubyn family works to preserve the rich heritage here along with the National Trust.

bing-43986.jpg.title: Highways in Taipei, Taiwan
bing-43986.jpg.headline: To the infinite and back. Infinity Day
bing-43986.jpg.description:
This looping highway in Taipei bears a resemblance to the symbol of infinity—the concept of something without ends or limits that is celebrated today. Infinity Day is held on the eighth day of the eighth month, a nod to the symbol's likeness to a sideways figure-of-eight. Established in 1987 by a New York-based philosopher, Jean-Pierre Ady Fenyo, the day celebrates freedom of thinking in its various forms, from philosophy through the arts and sciences. The symbol itself has a much longer history. English mathematician John Wallis is credited with introducing it as a mathematical symbol in 1655. The philosophical concept of infinity dates back at least as far as ancient Greece.

Taipei, the capital of Taiwan, was founded in the 18th century. The city might seem remote due to its location at the northern tip of the island, but Taipei's industrial activity encouraged the construction of impressive highways and public transport systems. Its green areas and nature preserves are equally remarkable, creating an extraordinary aerial view of the parks and roads in surprising shapes.

bing-43998.jpg.title: Indigenous artwork, Ngaruwanajirri Art Centre, Wurrumiyanga, Bathurst Island, Australia
bing-43998.jpg.headline: Celebrating Indigenous peoples. International Day of the World's Indigenous Peoples
bing-43998.jpg.description: Earth is home to an estimated 476 million Indigenous people, a term meaning 'sprung from the land' or native, which refers to the descendants of an area's first-known inhabitants. They represent about 6% of the global population but speak more than half of the world's estimated 7,000 languages. Our homepage today showcases the art of the Tiwi people of Australia, who speak a unique language unlinked to another other known language, in their community of only 2,000 people. Colonization has long impacted Indigenous people, contributing to high rates of poverty and loss of language and traditional lands. The UN first held the International Day of the World's Indigenous Peoples in 1994, and every August 9 they bring attention to the fight to preserve the rights, dignity, and existence of the world's oldest cultures.

bing-43999.jpg.title: Pan di Zucchero sea stack in Masua, Sardinia, Italy
bing-43999.jpg.headline: Pan di Zucchero sea stack in Masua, Sardinia, Italy
bing-43999.jpg.description: Masua is a small town in the Italian comune of Iglesias that is encircled by Mediterranean flora and flanked by towering limestone cliffs. Anyone who enjoys fishing, snorkeling, or scuba diving will adore this location because of the crystal-clear seas and excellent visibility. However, the stunning Pan di Zucchero—a huge sea stack that emerges from the water directly in front of the beach—might be the bay's main draw. It gets its name, meaning 'sugarloaf', from a rock formation in Rio de Janeiro, Brazil, that visitors thought it looked similar to. Despite being only 30 square metres in area, Pan di Zucchero is remarkably tall, rising 133 metres above the ocean's surface. Natural arches and tunnels may be found on the islet's northwest and southeast sides, respectively, where erosive forces have carved away at the stone. One of the tunnels can be traversed by a small boat if you're feeling brave.

bing-44005.jpg.title: Notte di San Lorenzo
bing-44005.jpg.headline: Chi vedrà più stelle cadenti?
bing-44005.jpg.description:
Alza lo sguardo all'insù ed esprimi un desiderio. Chissà che non si realizzi! La notte La notte di San Lorenzo è una delle più magiche dell’anno. Si dice che in questa notte, il 10 agosto, si possano guardare le stelle cadenti che solcano il cielo. Le stelle cadenti non sono altro che frammenti di meteoriti che entrano nell’atmosfera terrestre e si incendiano per l’attrito con l’aria. Il fenomeno è chiamato pioggia di meteoriti delle Perseidi, perché sembra che esse provengano dalla costellazione di Perseo. La notte di San Lorenzo è anche un’occasione per celebrare l’amore, la poesia e la bellezza della natura. Molti innamorati si scambiano promesse sotto il cielo stellato, mentre altri si raccontano storie e leggende sulle costellazioni.

La notte del 10 agosto ha una storia antica. La leggenda narra che nel 258 d.C. fu martirizzato a Roma il diacono Lorenzo, che fu arrostito su una graticola. Prima di morire, egli disse al suo carnefice: “Sei sazio di carne? Volgimi dall’altra parte e mangia”. Per questo motivo, San Lorenzo è il patrono dei cuochi e dei fornai. La tradizione popolare vuole che le stelle cadenti siano le lacrime o le scintille del santo.

bing-44010.jpg.title: A lion in Maasai Mara, Kenya
bing-44010.jpg.headline: 'King of the jungle'?. World Lion Day
bing-44010.jpg.description: Lions are known as 'the king of the jungle,' but on World Lion Day, let's set the record straight: Lions don't live in the jungle. Lions lounge in lordly leisure and hunt with ferocious focus on grasslands and plains. When they're not hunting, these majestic creatures nap, wrestle, and groom each other. But in an instant, they're chasing down a hapless gazelle or a hippopotamus that's wandered too far from the safety of its river. Like the opening song of 'The Lion King' movie says, it's the circle of life. World Lion Day is our opportunity to (ahem) lionize these regal beasts and raise awareness of threats to their well-being like poaching, habitat destruction, and other human-lion conflicts.

bing-44021.jpg.title: Gwaii Haanas National Park Reserve and Haida Heritage Site, British Columbia, Canada
bing-44021.jpg.headline: Among the cedar and spruce. Gwaii Haanas National Park Reserve and Haida Heritage Site
bing-44021.jpg.description: Gwaii Haanas National Park is a pristine and unique protected area situated in the southern part of the Haida Gwaii archipelago, off the coast of British Columbia. The park was established in 1993 as part of an innovative and collaborative effort between the Government of Canada and the Haida Nation. This was the first region in Canada to be mutually managed by Indigenous and federal authorities. This national park is a rich tapestry of diverse ecosystems, from ancient temperate rainforests to rugged coastlines and lush marine environments. The temperate rainforests within the park feature towering western red cedar and Sitka spruce trees that have stood for centuries. The Haida people have lived here for thousands of years, and their culture, traditions, and beliefs are deeply intertwined with the natural environment.

bing-44022.jpg.title: 'Gateway Pool' art installation at Jupiter Artland sculpture park, Edinburgh, Scotland
bing-44022.jpg.headline: A splash of color. Edinburgh Art Festival
bing-44022.jpg.description:
It might look futuristic, but this stunning pool was created a few years ago at the Jupiter Artland sculpture garden near Edinburgh, for the Scottish city's annual art festival. Nearly 30 feet wide, 'Gateway' is both a landscape sculpture and a functioning swimming pool. It was made by the artist Joana Vasconcelos from over 11,000 hand-painted tiles, produced in a traditional ceramic workshop in Portugal.

Today is the first day of this year's Edinburgh Art Festival, which runs for two weeks and features events and exhibitions by both established artists and emerging talents. August is festival season in Scotland's capital city, which is also hosting its international festival, the famous Edinburgh Festival Fringe, the Royal Edinburgh Military Tattoo, and the city's international book and film festivals.

bing-44023.jpg.title: Helmcken Falls, Wells Gray Provincial Park, British Columbia, Canada
bing-44023.jpg.headline: Helmcken Falls, Wells Gray Provincial Park, Canada
bing-44023.jpg.description: Nestled in the breathtaking Wells Gray Provincial Park, Canada, are the Helmcken Falls, an awe-inspiring natural wonder. Can you believe that in 1939, the provincial park was created with the sole motive of protecting this graceful waterfall? Robert Henry Lee, a land surveyor working for the government, discovered this natural gem. Cascading down a sheer volcanic rock cliff, this majestic waterfall is the fifth-highest in Canada. Plummeting from a height of 141 metres, the falls unleash an ethereal mist that dances in the sunlight, creating rainbows in the pristine landscape. The Wells Gray Provincial Park itself is a sanctuary of untamed wilderness, adorned with lush alpine meadows, ancient forests and vibrant wildflowers. Adventure seekers are rewarded with scenic hiking trails and nature's music.

bing-44034.jpg.title: Elephant family in Amboseli National Park, Kenya
bing-44034.jpg.headline: Protecting the gentle giants. World Elephant Day
bing-44034.jpg.description: These giants are the largest land animals on Earth, African bush elephants, which can reach 13 feet in shoulder height and weigh as much as 11 tons. They are one of three living species of elephant, alongside their smaller relatives, the African forest elephant and the Asian elephant. Their immense size is not the only incredible thing about them. Studies suggest that elephants can recognize themselves in the mirror and that these mammals display emotions such as grief when they lose family members. World Elephant Day—held on August 12—was set up to admire them but also to highlight the difficulties they face. Amboseli National Park in Kenya—where this photograph was taken—is one of the few remaining habitats where African elephant herds can still be found in large numbers.

bing-44039.jpg.title: Panorámica nocturna de la Vía Láctea, Chulilla, España
bing-44039.jpg.headline: Lluvia de estrellas. Vía Láctea, Chulilla, España
bing-44039.jpg.description:
El cometa Swift-Tuttle tiene una órbita elíptica alrededor del Sol y es responsable de la famosa lluvia de estrellas que ocurre cada año entre julio y agosto. Las partículas de polvo y rocas que deja el cometa al paso por su órbita cruzan la órbita de la Tierra y dan lugar a las tan esperadas Perseidas.

Si miramos el cielo nocturno, las estrellas fugaces de las Perseidas parecen provenir de la constelación de Perseo, dando origen a su nombre. Esta constelación se encuentra en el hemisferio norte y es fácilmente visible desde latitudes boreales durante gran parte del año.

Para este año tendremos la máxima actividad prevista para el día 12 y 13 de agosto, y podremos disfrutarlas en un maravilloso cielo nocturno durante estos días, ya que la luna nueva tendrá lugar el 16 de agosto. ¡Así que no te olvides hoy de mirar hacia arriba y dejarte deslumbrar!

bing-44046.jpg.title: Perseid meteor shower, Cottonwood Canyon State Park, Oregon
bing-44046.jpg.headline: Look up, incoming…. Perseid meteor shower over Oregon
bing-44046.jpg.description: What must our ancestors have thought when they saw meteors light up the night sky? Was it terrifying or an event of wonder? Thankfully, we now know that this celestial cascade is a harmless annual event. The Perseid meteor shower thrills stargazers from mid-July to late August and is due to peak today. The Perseids are caused by Earth passing through debris left behind by the Comet Swift-Tuttle. When the cosmic debris hits our atmosphere, it disintegrates in a colorful, fiery light display. It's a good night to catch the Perseids if you can—the moon is projected to only be 10% illuminated, so the meteors should really stand out against the dark sky.

bing-44058.jpg.title: Tiny gecko on a leaf
bing-44058.jpg.headline: Peek-a-boo, I see you!. World Lizard Day
bing-44058.jpg.description:
When trying to draw attention to World Lizard Day, you don't want to lead off with a scary Gila monster or monitor lizard. Nope, what you want front and center is a cute little gecko like the one we see here. Geckos come in varying sizes across 1,500 species and are unique among lizards for their vocalizations for mating, distress, and social interactions.

World Lizard Day might not be a big event for most of us, but it is important: These reptiles are threatened worldwide, and as both predators and prey, they are a critical part of ecosystems. So today let's think about our scaled friends, and if you're thinking about getting a pet, why not a lizard? Leopard geckos and bearded dragons are among the most beginner-friendly lizards to own.

bing-44062.jpg.title: Indian flags selling on Independence Day
bing-44062.jpg.headline: 76 glorious years of independence. Independence Day
bing-44062.jpg.description: On August 15th, 1947, the Prime Minister of India, Jawaharlal Nehru, hoisted the Indian flag for the first time and marked the end of British rule with his speech, 'Tryst with Destiny.' As a result, India and Pakistan were formed during the tenure of India's last viceroy, Lord Mountbatten. The Independence Movement was led by Mohandas K. Gandhi, who adopted a peaceful and nonviolent approach to end the rule. Today, India celebrates its 76th Independence Day.

bing-44063.jpg.title: Feria de Málaga, Andalucía, España
bing-44063.jpg.headline: Una semana de arte, tradición y buen pescado. Feria de Málaga, Andalucía, España
bing-44063.jpg.description:
Esta semana, Málaga se ha llenado de luces, colores, música y mucho arte. La famosa Feria de Málaga se remonta a 1487 cuando Los Reyes Católicos entraron a la ciudad el 19 de agosto. Desde entonces, ha tenido lugar esta conmemoración de la toma de la ciudad, traduciéndose en una gran feria que suele durar unos 10 días.

Esta espectacular fiesta se celebra en dos puntos de la ciudad, dividiéndose entre la Feria de Día que se celebra en las calles del centro de la ciudad y en el Cortijo de Torres, y, por otro lado, la Feria de Noche se lleva a cabo únicamente en el Real de la Feria (Cortijo de Torres).

Además de la música y el baile, hay actividades para todas las edades, como atracciones de feria, casetas con gastronomía típica, espectáculos de fuegos artificiales y desfiles de caballos, ¡una tradición andaluza muy arraigada y que te recomendamos encarecidamente este verano!

bing-44065.jpg.title: La Maddalena, Cala Coticcio, Sardegna, Italia
bing-44065.jpg.headline: Un pezzetto di paradiso
bing-44065.jpg.description:
Indossate il costume e prendete la borsa da spiaggia: è arrivato Ferragosto. In questo momento, milioni di Italiani si  stanno godendo il meritato riposo nelle loro località balneari predilette. Tra queste, vi è l'arcipelago di La Maddalena, un vero e proprio paradiso terrestre situato al largo della costa nord-orientale della Sardegna. Composto da sette isole principali e numerose isolette, tutte caratterizzate da acque cristalline e spiagge bianchissime.

Sullo sfondo di oggi, possiamo ammirare Cala Coticcio, conosciuta anche come la "Tahiti" sarda, una splendida baia situata nell'isola di Caprera. Raggiungibile a piedi dopo una piccola scarpinata, questo piccolo Eden è attorniato da acque argentine e sabbia bianca, che si fondono in un'atmosfera tropicale. La baia è circondata da scogliere e vegetazione lussureggianti, offrendo un ambiente naturale incantevole. Cala Coticcio è un luogo ideale per rilassarsi, fare snorkeling e godersi il sole. Nonostante la sua bellezza, è ancora relativamente poco conosciuta, rendendola una destinazione perfetta per coloro che cercano un'esperienza rara e tranquilla.

bing-44070.jpg.title: Piazza IX Aprile, Taormina, Sicily, Italy
bing-44070.jpg.headline: The Pearl of the Ionian Sea. Piazza IX Aprile, Taormina, Sicily, Italy
bing-44070.jpg.description:
Welcome to Taormina, an historic Italian resort built into a hillside high above the Ionian Sea on the coast of Sicily. From here you can take in panoramic views of the coast of Calabria, on the Italian mainland, the city of Syracuse, and Mount Etna, roughly 20 miles away.

Our homepage image shows the town's main square, the Piazza IX Aprile, with a Baroque church and bell tower, the Chiesa di San Giuseppe, and an historic clock tower. The square is seen as an elegant 'public living room' with many outdoor bars and artists waiting to paint your portrait.

bing-44082.jpg.title: Overseas Highway in the Florida Keys
bing-44082.jpg.headline: On the open ocean road. Overseas Highway, Florida Keys
bing-44082.jpg.description:
Once upon a time, there lived a wealthy industrialist, Henry Flagler, who embarked on the herculean task of creating an overseas railway connecting mainland Florida to Key West. When it opened in 1912, it was dubbed the Eighth Wonder of the World. However, the triumph was short-lived. It was hit by a hurricane on Labor Day, 1935 and the railroad discontinued operations. The railway was sold to the US government and rebuilt as an automobile highway, opening in 1938.

These days, the Overseas Highway still stretches about 113 miles through the Florida Keys over 42 bridges, which jump from island to island over the Atlantic Ocean, Florida Bay, and the Gulf of Mexico. Many of the original bridges were replaced in 1982, including the longest, the Seven Mile Bridge pictured in the distance in our homepage image. Drivers crossing the Overseas Highway can still see remnants of some of the old bridges running alongside their replacements, including the Old Seven Mile Bridge, a section of which was renovated for cyclists and pedestrians. An engineering marvel, the ‘highway that goes to sea' has also featured in blockbusters like 'License to Kill' and 'True Lies.'

bing-44094.jpg.title: Giant sequoia trees in Sequoia and Kings Canyon National Parks, California
bing-44094.jpg.headline: Things are looking up
bing-44094.jpg.description: We're looking at sequoia trees in Sequoia and Kings Canyon National Parks, California—the two parks border each other in the Sierra Nevada range in Central California. These giant sequoias can grow nearly 300 feet tall and some specimens have lived more than 3,000 years. Their longevity—even in areas prone to wildfires—is helped by thick bark that's full of fire-resistant tannins.

bing-44095.jpg.title: Rothenburg ob der Tauber, Bavaria, Germany
bing-44095.jpg.headline: Rothenburg ob der Tauber, Bavaria, Germany
bing-44095.jpg.description:
Rothenburg ob der Tauber, a charming town in Bavaria, is one of the most beautiful medieval cities in Europe. The well-preserved half-timbered houses, narrow streets, churches and city walls will give you the feeling of having stepped into a time machine.

The history of Rothenburg dates back to the 13th century when it was a thriving trading centre. Today, the city is known worldwide for its vibrant Christmas market, but one of the most interesting features of this city is 'The Master's Potion'. It is a historical spectacle that celebrates the legend of Mayor Georg Nusch, who saved Rothenburg from destruction in 1631. Johann Tserclaes of Tilly, who had besieged the city, decided, after the citizens begged for mercy, that if someone could drink an entire wine barrel in one go, he would free the city. Mayor Georg Nusch accepted the challenge and became a hero! To this day, this event, which takes place on the Pentecost weekend, is a popular cultural festival.

bing-44100.jpg.title: Altstadt und die Trave, Lübeck, Schleswig-Holstein
bing-44100.jpg.headline: Die Stadt eines Nobelpreisträgers. Lübeck, Schleswig-Holstein
bing-44100.jpg.description:
Lübeck, eine faszinierende Stadt im Norden Deutschlands, ist reich an Geschichte und beeindruckenden Merkmalen. Als einstiges Mitglied der Hanse, einer mächtigen Handelsvereinigung im Mittelalter, war Lübeck ein Zentrum von Wohlstand und Kultur. Ihre mittelalterliche Altstadt, von der UNESCO als Weltkulturerbe anerkannt, beherbergt majestätische Backsteinbauten und enge Gassen, die in vergangene Zeiten entführen.

Die Trave, der malerische Fluss, der durch Lübeck fließt, ist eine lebendige Ader, die das Herz der Stadt mit Leben erfüllt und entscheidend in der Entwicklung dieser war und ist. Entlang des Flusses erstrecken sich Promenaden, die zum Spazieren und Entspannen einladen. Das klare Wasser reflektiert die prächtige Silhouette der Stadt und gibt ihr so diesen idyllischen Hauch, den sie besitzt.

Heute ist Lübeck eine moderne Stadt, die ihre Traditionen mit einer pulsierenden Kulturszene verbindet. Sie wurde oft auch als Filmkulisse für verschiedene Bildstreifen benutzt. Erwähnenswert sind unserer Meinung nach „Nosferatu“ von Friedrich Wilhelm Murnau, die „Buddenbrooks“, die Verfilmung des Gesellschaftsromans von Thomas Mann und die deutsche Krimiserie „Morden im Norden“.

bing-44105.jpg.title: The Canadian International Air Show in Marilyn Bell Park
bing-44105.jpg.headline: Up and away!. Canadian National Exhibition
bing-44105.jpg.description: The grand and festive Canadian National Exhibition dates back almost 150 years. It is held in Toronto annually and goes on for 18 days; this year from August 18 until September 4. The exhibition grounds allow you to immerse yourself in various pavilions featuring indigenous art, mouth-watering delicacies, exciting rides, parades and multicultural performances.
