A highlight of the exhibition is the Canadian International Air show, which takes place in the festival's closing weekend. Overhead you can see Canadian and US military aircraft, stunt performers and civilian planes. Keep an eye out for the Snowbirds, the aerobatic flight team of the Royal Canadian Air Force, as they perform jaw-dropping acts of daring and teamwork.

bing-44106.jpg.title: 'Avatar Mountains,' Zhangjiajie National Forest Park, China
bing-44106.jpg.headline: Inspiring spires of stone. 'Avatar Mountains,' Zhangjiajie National Forest Park, China
bing-44106.jpg.description:
These stunning stone spires, rising from the forest in China's Hunan province, are said to have inspired the floating mountains of the movie 'Avatar.' There are more than 3,000 of these quartz-sandstone pillars in Zhangjiajie National Forest Park, often swathed in mist, part of a spectacular landscape that has inspired generations of painters. These days, they are popularly known as the 'Avatar Mountains' and one, the 3,544-foot-high Southern Sky Pillar, was officially renamed as 'Avatar Hallelujah Mountain' in 2010, the year after the blockbuster movie was released.

The spires sit within the wider Wulingyuan Scenic and Historic Interest Area, a UNESCO World Heritage Site, and attract millions of tourists each year who come to marvel at their otherworldly beauty. The park is dotted with numerous hiking trails and glass-bottomed skywalks, allowing visitors to enjoy panoramic views of this natural wonder.

bing-44114.jpg.title: Alignements de Carnac, Golfe du Morbihan, France
bing-44114.jpg.headline: Des menhirs à perte de vue. Journée mondiale de la Photographie
bing-44114.jpg.description:
Le 19 août célèbre la journée mondiale de la photographie. Cette date coïncide avec l’invention « officielle » de la photographie le 19 août 1839 par le français Louis Daguerre. Pour illustrer cette journée, nous avons décidé de vous emmener faire un petit tour en Bretagne, à la découverte des menhirs de Carnac.

Si Astérix, ça vous semble "vieux" ? C'est parce que vous ne vous êtes jamais arrêté sur l'âge des mégalithes bretons ! Les alignements de menhirs de Carnac dans le Morbihan datent au moins du 5e millénaire avant J.C. : ces 2 733 menhirs d'environ 300 tonnes chacun n'ont donc pas été alignés par le plus costaud des irréductibles gaulois, mais bien par de vrais humains, sans potion magique (à notre connaissance). Mais comment faisaient-ils pour déplacer ces colosses de pierre, en plein néolithique (voire avant), alors que même la roue n'existait pas ? C'est l'un des grands mystères de l'Humanité...

Distribués sur trois sites principaux, le long de la baie de Quiberon, les alignements de Carnac représentent l'un des monuments mégalithiques les plus impressionnants de Bretagne. Mais la région abrite d'autres sites intéressants, comme Locmariaquer, avec le plus grand menhir d’Europe. En effet, le grand menhir brisé d'Er Grah, s'il a un jour été dressé (il est aujourd'hui à terre, brisé en 4 morceaux), a pu atteindre les 20 mètres de hauteur, pour environ 330 tonnes. Que le menhir ne vous tombe pas sur la tête !

bing-44118.jpg.title: Squirrel looking into the lens of a camera
bing-44118.jpg.headline: Ready for my close-up. World Photography Day
bing-44118.jpg.description:
On August 19, 1839, French artist and photographer Louis-Jacques-Mandé Daguerre made public his invention that created an image using a silver-plated copper sheet and mercury vapor. The daguerreotype process became the first publicly available photographic process and was used throughout the 1840s and 1850s.

Today, August 19 is World Photography Day, promoting the art as a means of storytelling, creative expression, and cultural preservation. The world of photography is vast and captures many subjects and styles on camera, from abstract and fashion photography to landscapes and wildlife, like this cheeky squirrel here. Some seek to keep the charm and artistry of old-fashioned photography alive, though digital cameras and smartphones give everyone the opportunity to capture great photos, sometimes in unexpected places.

bing-44130.jpg.title: Start Point Lighthouse, South Devon, England
bing-44130.jpg.headline: Celebrating lighthouses. International Lighthouse Weekend
bing-44130.jpg.description: To mark International Lighthouse Weekend, we're on England's southwest coast, where Start Point Lighthouse looks out over the turbulent waters of the English Channel. The lighthouse is perched upon a rugged cliff on one of the country's most exposed peninsulas, which stretches nearly a mile into the sea in the county of Devon. Built in 1836, the elegant lighthouse was designed by civil engineer James Walker in the Gothic style, as seen in its castle-like parapet. It has undergone many changes since then and more accommodation was added in the 1870s, but no lighthouse keepers live there now—it has been automated since 1993.

bing-44139.jpg.title: Cotswolds village of Snowshill, Gloucestershire, England, United Kingdom, Europe
bing-44139.jpg.headline: 'Cot' in this town's charms. Cotswolds village of Snowshill, Gloucestershire, England
bing-44139.jpg.description:
Honey-coloured buildings surrounded by lush greenery—this landscape has a rustic elegance to it. Nestled in central-southwest England, the Cotswolds are home to picturesque villages and towns like the one pictured here, Snowshill. The region, covering 787 square miles, is the largest Area of Outstanding Natural Beauty. From Beatrix Potter to Edward Thomas, many writers and poets have immortalised its pastoral setting over the centuries.

When dinosaurs roamed the Earth, this region was under a warm sea and now, it is known for the oolitic limestone that formed during the Jurassic period. Cotswold stones are rich in fossils and their colour varies in the shade of brown according to where it was quarried.

bing-44142.jpg.title: Emerald Lake, South Klondike Highway, Yukon, Canada
bing-44142.jpg.headline: Glowing from within. Discovery Day in Yukon, Canada
bing-44142.jpg.description:
It's Discovery Day in Yukon, Canada, a day to commemorate the 1896 discovery of gold at Bonanza Creek. The event set off the Klondike Gold Rush, which attracted thousands of prospectors to the region in search of gold, leading to significant economic and social changes. The population increase led to Yukon separating from the Northwest Territories and the formation of Yukon Territory in 1898.

Discovery Day celebrates Yukon's rich heritage, history, and natural resources—like Emerald Lake, seen in today's image, known for its deep green hues. You'll find it on the Klondike Highway, which roughly follows the route used by the prospectors more than a century ago. It is also a day to honor the spirit of adventure exhibited during the gold rush. Government offices, schools, and many businesses close to allow people to participate in the festivities, including parades, historical reenactments, gold panning competitions, and concerts.

bing-44154.jpg.title: Amphitheatre of El Jem, Tunisia
bing-44154.jpg.headline: A 'standing ovation' to Roman architecture. Amphitheatre of El Jem, Tunisia
bing-44154.jpg.description:
This impressive structure is the Amphitheatre of El Jem, in the Tunisian town of the same name. Made entirely from stone blocks, it was built in the 3rd century CE, when this area was Thysdrus, a city of ancient Rome. Once capable of seating up to 35,000 spectators, it is the largest colosseum in North Africa and one of the largest in the world. A UNESCO World Heritage Site since 1979, it is one of the best-preserved Roman amphitheatres, almost equal in grandeur to the Colosseum in Rome.

Beneath the arena, there is an extensive underground network of tunnels and chambers, which are open to visitors. Despite its age, the arena floor is still preserved, and visitors can walk on it, following in the footsteps of gladiators and others who stepped out before huge crowds, nearly 2,000 years ago.

bing-44158.jpg.title: Full Moon set at dawn, behind Cenotaphs, Orchha, Madhya Pradesh, India
bing-44158.jpg.headline: Reaching beyond Earth's boundaries. Cenotaphs, Orchha, Madhya Pradesh
bing-44158.jpg.description: India is set to join the ranks of the United States, China and the former Soviet Union as the fourth country to successfully land a spacecraft on the Moon. Leading this mission is the Indian Space Research Organisation (ISRO), with their Chandrayaan-3 project marking India's third landing endeavor. Chandrayaan-2 was the first, and it faced disappointment in 2019 when its lander crashed during its descent. The primary goal of this mission is to explore water ice in craters at the lunar south pole and study the region's cold traps that hold a record of our early Solar System. The outcome of the Chandrayaan-3 moon lander mission by the ISRO will play a critical role in establishing India's involvement in lunar exploration and governance.

bing-44166.jpg.title: Skógafoss waterfall, Iceland
bing-44166.jpg.headline: Making a splash. Skógafoss waterfall, Iceland
bing-44166.jpg.description:
Behold Skógafoss, one of Iceland’s largest waterfalls. This powerful cascade measures 82 feet across and drops 200 feet over what were once the sea cliffs of the country’s southern coast. The coastline receded seaward, but the cliffs remained, leaving behind this natural wonder, powered by water from two glaciers. Skógafoss, which translates as 'forest waterfall,' is frequently graced with single or double rainbows, formed by the refraction of sunlight through the mist. Legend has it that a treasure chest is hidden behind Skógafoss, left there by a Viking settler named Prasi Porolfsson.

The waterfall has appeared on the big screen, in 'Thor: The Dark World' and the Bollywood movie 'Dilwale,' as well as on TV in the final season of 'Game of Thrones.' The Skógar Museum, which offers insights into Iceland's cultural heritage, sits near the waterfall in Skógar village.

bing-44178.jpg.title: Shark Fin Cove, Davenport, California
bing-44178.jpg.headline: What a fin-tastic view!. Shark Fin Cove, California
bing-44178.jpg.description: Shark Fin Cove, also known as Shark Tooth Beach, is nestled in a cove in the tiny town of Davenport on California's Central Coast. The cove is a coastal gem known for its stunning sea stack—a vertical rock formation that resembles a shark's fin. The fin used to be connected to the mudstone cliff that surrounds the beach. Over time, the relentless crashing waves and strong winds slowly eroded the rock formation. Shark Fin Cove is visible from Highway 1, where travelers can stop and look at the expansive Pacific Ocean views.

bing-44183.jpg.title: Fiesta de la Batalla de las flores, Laredo, Cantabria, España
bing-44183.jpg.headline: Una fiesta aromática. Fiesta de la Batalla de las flores, Laredo, Cantabria, España
bing-44183.jpg.description:
Laredo es una pequeña localidad cántabra situada al norte de España y con una preciosa tradición llevada a cabo el último viernes de agosto, donde se celebra la famosa Batalla de Flores.

En esta batalla de colores y aromas florales se lucen enormes carrozas adornadas con miles de flores y plantas naturales formando motivos alegóricos para participar en una gran ceremonia centenaria declarada Fiesta de Interés Turístico Nacional desde 1965.

Si te encuentras por esta zona, será un paseo obligado de diversión, arte y espectáculo en el que poder perderte entre la multitud de chirigotas, mercadillos callejeros y fuegos artificiales que adornarán este viernes festivo.

bing-44190.jpg.title: Lower Yellowstone Falls, Yellowstone National Park, Wyoming
bing-44190.jpg.headline: This land is your land. National Park Service anniversary
bing-44190.jpg.description: Though summer is winding down, it's not too late to pack some gear and head into the great outdoors. Unsure where to go? Look no further than our 63 national parks, which exist thanks to the National Park Service, created on this day in 1916 by President Woodrow Wilson. He ordered the service to preserve the landscape, wildlife, and history of the parks 'in such manner and by such means as will leave them unimpaired for the enjoyment of future generations.' In other words, the park service was established for all of us! Just make sure that whether you're visiting the islands of American Samoa, the glaciers of the North Cascades, the waterways of the Everglades, or the 308-foot Lower Falls of Yellowstone in today's image, that you explore them with care and appreciation so that they can be preserved for centuries to come.

bing-44202.jpg.title: Berlin Cathedral and Museum Island, Berlin, Germany
bing-44202.jpg.headline: A night at the museums. Museum Night in Berlin
bing-44202.jpg.description: As the summer is fading away, we find ourselves reminiscing about vacations and long hours of lively evenings. But let's not bury the picnic days just yet! There is plenty to look forward to, especially if you are in Berlin. The Long Night of Museums only happens once a year—on the last Saturday of August since 1997—but it shakes up Museum Island and the rest of the German capital. The event series is more than a peaceful appreciation of artifacts—quite the opposite—you can expect music, talks, workshops, cocktails, dance, and more from 6 PM into the small hours of the morning. Featured in today's image, Museum Island—embraced by the Spree River—is listed as a UNESCO World Heritage Site, and it is home to a museum quintet: Altes, Bode, Pergamon, and Neues Museums, and Alte Nationalgalerie.

bing-44209.jpg.title: Veduta della città di Ragusa Ibla, città patrimonio dell'UNESCO
bing-44209.jpg.headline: Tutta la bellezza della Sicilia
bing-44209.jpg.description:
Per tutti gli amanti dei caldi colori mediterranei e per i viaggiatori curiosi di scoprire la bellezza incontaminata della Trinacria, esiste un posto che mette tutti d’accordo e vi farà innamorare a prima vista: Ragusa Ibla. Ibla è il quartiere più antico e suggestivo di Ragusa ed è famoso per il suo patrimonio artistico e architettonico, che riflette lo stile barocco del XVIII secolo. Tra le attrazioni principali ci sono oltre cinquanta chiese, palazzi nobiliari e giardini panoramici. Il quartiere cittadino è stato dichiarato Patrimonio dell’Umanità dall’UNESCO nel 2002 e si trova nella parte bassa della città, rispetto alla parte superiore, chiamata tradizionalmente nel dialetto locale “Iusu”.

Dopo il terremoto del 1693, la città antica fu ricostruita con uno stile barocco tardivo. Nella parte orientale della città, si trova il Giardino Ibleo e i resti di una antica città che forse corrisponde all’Hybla Heraia. Nel 1866, questo quartiere si separò da Ragusa e divenne un comune indipendente chiamato Ragusa Inferiore, poi rinominato Ragusa Ibla nel 1922. Nel 1927, si riunì nuovamente a Ragusa che era diventata nel frattempo sede della provincia.

bing-44211.jpg.title: Colourful houses in Notting Hill, UK
bing-44211.jpg.headline: 'Notting' but fun here. Notting Hill Carnival
bing-44211.jpg.description: When a parade of masquerade dancers and smoky barbecue stalls take over the streets, and performers rustle their proudest feathers to Calypso music, it means one thing: Notting Hill Carnival in West London is back to paint the neighbourhood colourful! The carnival's origin stems from reactions to the shameful era of slave trades and the Notting Hill race riots of the late 1950s. It was in 1966 that the festival first took over the streets of the Kensington area of London as a celebration of British Caribbean culture. Fast-forward to 2023, and now the two-day bonanza is one of the world's largest street events. This year, the iconic street party will mark the 75th anniversary of the docking of HMT Empire Windrush which brought hundreds of Caribbean immigrants to England. Are you ready to party?

bing-44214.jpg.title: Seongsan Ilchulbong, a tuff cone on Jeju Island, South Korea
bing-44214.jpg.headline: A 'tuff'-tastic crater. Jeju Island, South Korea
bing-44214.jpg.description: The South Korean island of Jeju is full of wonders. If you don't have a chance to visit its volcanic landscape, ancient stone statues, waterfalls, and rocky coastline, you can dive into the island's fascinating chronicles from the comfort of your computer. The star of today's image, Seongsan Ilchulbong (Sunrise Peak), is the island's rare tuff cone formation, created by an underwater volcanic eruption about 5,000 years ago. Tuff cones are also called ash cones, referring to the accumulated ash settling in a cone formation after the lava's forceful explosion. Seongsan Ilchulbong was added to the UNESCO World Natural Heritage List in 2007.

bing-44226.jpg.title: Fort Lovrijenac, West Harbor, Dubrovnik, Croatia
bing-44226.jpg.headline: Watch out for dragons!. Dubrovnik, Croatia
bing-44226.jpg.description: Though you might instinctively watch out for invading fleets or dragons overhead, you're more likely to encounter a tourist than a Lannister in the Croatian city of Dubrovnik. As you may know, 'Game of Thrones' filmed here frequently throughout the run of the show, and you can scarcely blame them; Dubrovnik's Old Town is one of the best-preserved medieval cities in the world. For centuries it flourished as the Republic of Ragusa, maintaining independence through diplomacy and robust trade networks. This 'Pearl of the Adriatic' has withstood military bombardments and devastating earthquakes, yet the city has always rebuilt and persevered. While pop culture, history, and UNESCO World Heritage Site status are all big draws, they might be too effective: A recent report estimated that in 2019 there were 36 tourists for every resident.

bing-44238.jpg.title: American bison in Grand Teton National Park, Wyoming
bing-44238.jpg.headline: Our national mammal. American bison, Grand Teton National Park, Wyoming
bing-44238.jpg.description:
The bison is a majestic, massive creature, a true emblem of the American frontier spirit. These sturdy animals roamed North America's prairies for thousands of years in numbers estimated to be as high as 60 million. But settlement of the American West caused habitat loss, and that, combined with overhunting, nearly wiped out the species altogether by the end of the 19th century. Ranchers, conservationists, Native American tribes, and politicians worked to save the bison and today, nearly 500,000 bison can be found in North America. About 15,000 animals are in free-roaming herds that graze on US public lands, like the bison in today's image, shown at Grand Teton National Park in Wyoming.

For such large animals, bison are surprisingly agile. They're nearly 7 feet tall at their hump and weigh up to 2,000 pounds, but they can run up to 35 miles per hour, jump high fences, and are strong swimmers. In 2016, President Barack Obama paid tribute to these proud beasts by signing the Bison Legacy Act, naming bison the national mammal of the United States.

bing-44242.jpg.title: Rakhi or sacred thread of different types and colors
bing-44242.jpg.headline: Ties that never unravel. Celebrating sibling bonds
bing-44242.jpg.description: Raksha Bandhan is a popular celebration influenced by Hindu traditions, held every year to honor the bond between siblings. According to Indian custom, sisters tie a thread called Rakhi on their brothers' wrists and wish for their well-being, prosperity, and happiness. In return, the brothers promise to protect and love their sisters unconditionally. In recent times, the festival has changed and progressed, and brothers also tie Rakhis on their sisters' wrists while sisters exchange the thread as a symbol of promising to protect and love each other wholeheartedly. Additionally, siblings exchange gifts and indulge in pampering each other on this occasion. Raksha Bandhan means 'the bond of protection, obligation or care' in Sanskrit.
bing-44242.jpg.copyright: © Ritesh Shukla/Pacific Press/LightRocket via Getty Image

bing-44250.jpg.title: Whale shark, Ningaloo Reef, Western Australia
bing-44250.jpg.headline: A diver's big buddy. International Whale Shark Day
bing-44250.jpg.description: Say hello to the largest fish in the world, the whale shark. On August 30, we celebrate International Whale Shark Day to honor these magnificent marine creatures. These gentle giants are not related to whales, despite their impressive size—they can reach up to 40 feet in length. Whale sharks are calm creatures which are usually safe for divers to swim alongside. These sharks are filter feeders and consume plankton and small fish by sieving them through their gill plates. There has been a significant decline in their populations, with an estimated 63% decrease in their numbers in the last 75 years. Threats include being hit by boats or tangled in fishing gear and their habitats are being damaged by pollution, coastal development and over-fishing. Advocates work through education and community engagement to help safeguard whale sharks and preserve our oceans.

bing-44256.jpg.title: Köpfe des Heiligen Cassius und Florentius vor dem Bonner Münster, Bonn
bing-44256.jpg.headline: Köpfe der heiligen Patrone Bonns. Köpfe des Heiligen Cassius und Florentius vor dem Bonner Münster, Bonn
bing-44256.jpg.description:
Cassius und Florentius waren zwei bedeutende christliche Heilige, die als Schutzpatrone der Stadt Bonn in Nordrhein-Westfalen verehrt werden. Die zwei römischen Soldaten gehörten anscheinend der legendären Thebaischen Legion an. Es handelte sich dabei um eine christliche Legion, die angeblich viele Mitglieder durch den Märtyrertod verlor, da zu der Zeit die Christen im Römischen Reich verfolgt wurden.

Jährlich werden in Bonn Feste und Prozessionen zu Ehren der beiden Schutzpatrone gefeiert, um sie in Erinnerung und ihre Bedeutung für die Stadt lebendig zu halten. Beide sind in Bonn begraben und ihre Ruhestätte ist im Laufe der Jahrhunderte zu Wallfahrtsorten, die viele Gläubige und Geschichtsinteressierte anziehen, geworden.

Die Skulptur, die Sie auf dem heutigen Bild sehen können, befindet sich vor dem Bonner Münster, der katholischen Hauptkirche der früheren Hauptstadt Deutschlands. İskender Yediler, ein deutsch-türkischer Bildhauer hat dieses unglaubliche Meisterwerk im Jahre 2002 geschaffen. Die beiden Soldaten repräsentieren nicht nur die Stadt Bonn, sondern gelten auch als auch Vorbilder für Tapferkeit, Hingabe und Widerstandsfähigkeit.

bing-44262.jpg.title: Saguaro cacti, Ironwood National Monument, Arizona
bing-44262.jpg.headline: 'Saguaro' you today?. Saguaro cacti, Ironwood Forest National Monument, Arizona
bing-44262.jpg.description: Massive succulents against a mountainous backdrop, underneath the sun-kissed Arizona sky—it's prickly perfection. Pictured here are saguaro (pronounced 'sah-wah-roh') cacti at the Ironwood Forest National Monument in the Sonoran Desert. Even if you haven't seen one in person, when you hear the word cactus, you're probably thinking of saguaro—tall, green, cylindrical, with arms pointing upward. From tattoos to coffee cups, you'll find this iconic symbol of Arizona on almost everything. Though they are slow growers, these plants have been known to live over 200 years and reach enormous heights, with a 78-footer setting the record. Another cactus, known as 'Grandaddy,' survived in the sweltering desert for about 300 years, eventually succumbing to old age in the early 1990s. Cacti may not be for everyone, but they tend to grow on you (figuratively, of course)!

bing-44266.jpg.title: Boat at backwaters of Kerala, India
bing-44266.jpg.headline: This backwater boat beckons. Backwaters of Kerala, India
bing-44266.jpg.description: The beautiful backwaters of Kerala are made up of a network of interconnected canals, rivers, lakes, and inlets stretching across over 900 kilometres of waterways. Towns and cities were built along the intricate water system, and today they are destinations for cruises. Within the backwaters lies a distinct ecosystem where fresh river water mingles with the saltwater from the Arabian Sea, resulting in a one-of-a-kind habitat for flora and fauna. Kerala is also a famous destination for tourists who are looking for an enriching Ayurvedic escape or seeking to feast on the freshest seafood. The official and most widely spoken language of the state is Malayalam.

bing-44274.jpg.title: Turkey tail mushroom, Brevard, North Carolina
bing-44274.jpg.headline: Wanna hang with a fungi?. National Mushroom Month
bing-44274.jpg.description: When the Mushroom Council decided it was high time to 'champignon' these versatile fungi, they settled on September as the perfect time to do so. National Mushroom Month highlights their importance and encourages you to know your mushrooms. For example, poisonous jack-o'-lantern mushrooms are sometimes misidentified as edible chanterelles. Others have medicinal properties like today's homepage species, turkey tail, used to treat lung conditions in traditional Chinese medicine. Recent research showed them exhibiting anti-tumor properties and helping fortify the immune system. Other mushrooms make great meal additions, and from portobello to shiitake mushrooms, there are thousands of edible species out there. Sautéed, stuffed, sliced, on a pizza, or in soup, it is time to bring some umami fun(gi) to your plate!

bing-44283.jpg.title: Hadrian's Wall, England
bing-44283.jpg.headline: A welcome spot for wallflowers. Hadrian's Wall, Northumberland National Park
bing-44283.jpg.description:
The occasional muddy soil should not stop you from visiting the long-distance footpath of Hadrian's Wall Path. The National Trial—a classification gained in 2003—stretches for 84 miles from east to west in the north of England.

Near the footpath lie the remains of the Roman fortification, Hadrian's Wall. The wall was built under the orders of Emperor Hadrian after the Roman conquest of Britain.  Despite a common belief, it has never served as the border connecting England and Scotland. Originally, the wall covered more than 70 miles of the northern English countryside between the River Tyne and the North Sea. Recorded as a British cultural icon and a UNESCO World Heritage Site, it is the largest Roman archaeological display in Britain.

bing-44286.jpg.title: Allen's hummingbird, Santa Cruz, California
bing-44286.jpg.headline: Stopping for a blossom beverage. National Hummingbird Day
bing-44286.jpg.description: It's National Hummingbird Day, a day to celebrate these tiny wonders. Their colorful plumage and ability to hover mid-air make them particularly eye-catching. The rapid flapping of their wings—an average of 53 times a second—creates their trademark humming sound and works up quite an appetite: These little birdies can feed every 10–15 minutes! Today's homepage star is an Allen's hummingbird, which grows to about 3.5 inches in length and is found along the west coast of North America, most commonly in California. National Hummingbird Day aims to boost the preservation of these mini marvels, by protecting them and their habitat.

bing-44293.jpg.title: Regata Storica di Venezia, Venezia, Italia
bing-44293.jpg.headline: La Regata della Serenissima
bing-44293.jpg.description:
Salite a bordo e imbracciate le pagaie, è ora di vogare! La Regata Storica di Venezia è un evento annuale che si tiene nella città lagunare e che richiama spettatori da tutto il mondo. Consiste in una gara di barche a remi che si svolge lungo il Canal Grande, e che vede la partecipazione di diverse squadre provenienti dalle diverse contrade della città. La gara è preceduta da una sfilata di barche storiche e dei relativi equipaggi, rappresentanti le diverse contrade, con le rispettive bandiere e i marinai agghindati con i costumi dell’epoca.

Durante la gara, le squadre si sfidano in una corsa all'ultimo remo, cercando di raggiungere il traguardo per prime. La regata è un evento molto atteso dai veneziani, che si preparano per mesi in vista della competizione, e che si divertono a tifare per la propria contrada preferita. Se siete a Venezia durante questo evento, non dovete assolutamente perderlo! È uno spettacolo unico al mondo!

bing-44298.jpg.title: Aerial view of Manhattan, New York City
bing-44298.jpg.headline: So high they touch the sky. Skyscraper Day
bing-44298.jpg.description: Skyscraper Day pays tribute to the towering architectural wonders that dominate our city skylines. Observed on September 3, it also marks the birthday of Louis Henry Sullivan, a pioneer of modern architecture who is often called the 'father of skyscrapers.' Found in the world's biggest cities, skyscrapers serve as symbols of progress, ambition, and reaching new heights. Manhattan, the dense, vibrant heart of New York City, boasts a mesmerizing skyline with an array of iconic skyscrapers. These structures, like the Empire State Building, One World Trade Center, and the Chrysler Building, define the city's architectural and cultural legacy and captivate millions of visitors every year.

bing-44310.jpg.title: Construction workers on scaffolding
bing-44310.jpg.headline: Time to clock out. Labor Day
bing-44310.jpg.description: Labor Day is a well-earned day of rest for many workers across America. The food we eat, the shelter over our heads, and the transportation that moves us around all exist thanks to our collective labor. Organized labor movements grew in the 19th century, along with calls for a day to honor workers' contributions. The first Labor Day was celebrated with a parade in New York City in September 1882 and similar events spread throughout the country. In 1894, President Grover Cleveland signed a bill declaring the first Monday in September as Labor Day. Today, Labor Day marks the unofficial end of summer, but let's not forget to take a moment to give thanks for the work we all put in to take care of our communities, our families, and ourselves.

bing-44311.jpg.title: Marshes of Bourges, France
bing-44311.jpg.headline: Marshes of Bourges, France
bing-44311.jpg.description: At the heart of Bourges, France, you will find a natural treasure that enthrals visitors with its unique ecosystems and rich biodiversity: the Marshes of Bourges. Stretching over vast areas, these marshes include a diverse range of habitats, including wetlands, reed beds and shallow waters, and are home to numerous plant and animal species. But the area's significance extends beyond its ecological importance, as it holds historical—the marshes served as a defence until the 17th century— and cultural relevance to the local communities that organise the annual Marshes Fair in September. Over the years, various efforts have been made to preserve and protect the delicate balance of this ecosystem, promoting sustainable practices and eco-tourism to raise awareness about its conservation.

bing-44322.jpg.title: Mount Segla, Senja Island, Troms og Finnmark, Norway
bing-44322.jpg.headline: A digital creation? Nor-way!. Mount Segla, Senja Island, Norway
bing-44322.jpg.description: A beautiful island popularly known as 'Norway in miniature,' Senja's diverse landscape boasts mountainous terrain as well as lush greenery. At 600 square miles, it is Norway's second-largest island, connected to the mainland by the Gisund Bridge. The most notable spot on Senja is pictured today, Mount Segla, a magnificent peak that is visited frequently in summer, with a trail starting in Fjordgård, a fishing village in the north of Senja. It's a tough hike to the top, more than 2,000 feet above sea level. Other tourist attractions include Ånderdalen National Park and Tranøya, an island off the south coast of Senja known for its tranquility.

bing-44334.jpg.title: Old Venetian harbor, Rethymno, Crete Island, Greece
bing-44334.jpg.headline: Ready to drop anchor?. Rethymno, Crete, Greece
bing-44334.jpg.description: The Venetian harbor in the Old Town of Rethymno, on the Greek island of Crete, invites you to time travel through history. Its Egyptian lighthouse and Turkish elements are proof of different nations leaving their mark on Crete's old port. Forged in the 14th century under Venetian rule, this port has long served as a bustling hub for commerce and enterprise. For today's visitors, a replica of an old wooden sailing ship offers a full historic adventure. For a nostalgic inland experience, visit the 16th-century Fortezza, Rethymno's Venetian fortress. The citadel is visible from every corner of the town and offers a panoramic view of Rethymno.

bing-44339.jpg.title: Meandro Melero, Extremadura, España
bing-44339.jpg.headline: Una tierra que sorprende. Meandro Melero, Extremadura, España
bing-44339.jpg.description:
Este sorprendente meandro situado en Melero, Extremadura, parece sacado de un cuento de hadas. Es muy probable que, si piensas en Extremadura, se te venga a la mente sus extensas áreas de dehesas, bosques de encimas y característicos paisajes de alcornoques. Sin embargo, el meandro del Melero está ubicado en el curso del río Alagón en Cáceres.

Esta sorprendente curva que forma el río al cambiar de dirección crea una espectacular panorámica, ofreciendo una amplia variedad de fauna y vegetación autóctona.

La imagen de hoy nos sirve para recordar los preciosos paisajes que alberga la región de Extremadura, así como su diversidad y riqueza de las que se enorgullecen los habitantes de esta región en su próxima celebración.

bing-44340.jpg.title: Der Reichstag unter einem Sternenhimmel, Berlin
bing-44340.jpg.headline: Der Reichstag in all seiner Pracht. Geburtsstunde des Deutschen Bundestag
bing-44340.jpg.description:
Heute, am 7. September feiert der Deutsche Bundestag seinen 74. Geburtstag. Es handelt sich dabei um einen Meilenstein in der Geschichte der deutschen Demokratie. An jenem Tag im Jahr 1949 wurde der Bundestag erstmals in Bonn zusammengerufen, und damit begann die Ära des politischen Engagements und der repräsentativen Entscheidungsfindung in Deutschland.

Seit seiner Gründung hat der Bundestag eine zentrale Rolle im politischen Gefüge des Landes eingenommen. Es ist der Ort, an dem gewählte Vertreter aus verschiedenen politischen Parteien zusammenkommen, um Gesetze zu erlassen, Debatten zu führen und die Interessen der Bevölkerung zu vertreten. Der Reichstag in Berlin, der heutige Sitz des Deutschen Bundestags, wurde 1884 erbaut. Nach dem Brand und seiner Zerstörung 1933, wurde dieser 1995 von Sir Norman Foster renoviert. Die Kuppel symbolisiert die Transparenz und ermöglicht uns einen Blick in die Regierungsarbeit zu werfen.

Während wir diesen Tag feiern, nutzen wir die Gelegenheit, nicht nur die Errungenschaften der Vergangenheit zu würdigen, sondern auch einen Blick in die Zukunft zu werfen. Der Deutsche Bundestag bleibt eine tragende Säule der deutschen Demokratie, die kontinuierlich die Werte von Freiheit, Gerechtigkeit und Partizipation fördert.

bing-44344.jpg.title: Ipiranga, Sao Paulo, Brasil
bing-44344.jpg.headline: Ordem e Progresso
bing-44344.jpg.description: No dia 7 de setembro, o Brasil celebra com orgulho o Dia da Independência. Nessa data marcante, relembramos nossa história e celebramos a liberdade conquistada. As ruas ganham vida com desfiles vibrantes, cores verde e amarelo enfeitam cada canto e a cultura brasileira brilha em todos os cantos do país. É um momento de união, patriotismo e celebração da nossa identidade. Viva o Brasil independente e cheio de energia!

bing-44345.jpg.title: Scenic view at Toronto city waterfront skyline at sunset
bing-44345.jpg.headline: Grab your popcorn, Toronto. Toronto International Film Festival
bing-44345.jpg.description: Movie buffs eagerly anticipate the most celebrated film event in Canada, the Toronto International Film Festival (TIFF), which promises to transport audiences on an unparalleled journey through realms of storytelling and visual artistry. This annual event was established in 1976 and has since played a pivotal role in shaping the Canadian film industry. TIFF has long been revered for its display of diverse and captivating films. From gripping dramas and documentaries to heartwarming comedies, this year boasts a lineup that reflects the kaleidoscope of human emotions. Beyond the silver screen, it embraces innovation with virtual showcases and interactive experiences, redefining the boundaries of film festivals. Witness the cinematic magic unfold as the 48th TIFF hits screens from September 7 to 17.

bing-44346.jpg.title: Camels in the desert, United Arab Emirates
bing-44346.jpg.headline: Ships of the desert, ahoy!. Camels in the desert, United Arab Emirates
bing-44346.jpg.description: Desert-dwelling camels have been central to lives in the United Arab Emirates for thousands of years. A key mode of transportation for Bedouins, camels long helped them traverse the sweltering sands in search of water and supplies. These dromedaries were also used as currency to fulfill obligations such as dowries or zakat, an annual charitable fee in Muslim communities. Camel milk is a valuable and nutritious ingredient in many recipes in the region, while camel racing keeps people entertained to this day, illustrating the versatility of these hardy creatures.

bing-44354.jpg.title: Parc Olympique Lyonnais, Groupama Stadium OL Vallée, Lyon
bing-44354.jpg.headline: Allez les bleus !. Coupe du Monde de Rugby France 2023
bing-44354.jpg.description:
La Coupe du Monde de Rugby à XV, est un événement mondial de premier plan qui oppose les meilleures équipes du monde tous les quatre ans, sous l'égide de World Rugby. Les équipes s'affrontent dans des poules initiales, puis les mieux classées passent aux éliminatoires : quarts, demis et finale.

La France accueille l'édition 2023 sur 51 jours avec 48 matchs. Plusieurs villes, dont Lyon avec son stade olympique iconique en photo, accueilleront les rencontres. Une occasion pour les bleus de briller et, pour les compétiteurs, de se surpasser. Alors, souhaitons un vif succès à l'équipe de France et que la meilleure gagne !

bing-44358.jpg.title: The Circus townhouses in Bath, Somerset, England
bing-44358.jpg.headline: Jane Austen's literary circle. International Literacy Day
bing-44358.jpg.description:
Jane Austen, author of 'Pride and Prejudice,' is one of the best-known writers in English literature, so it's not a surprise that there are multiple festivals honoring her legacy. The largest is held here, in the English city of Bath, where Austen lived from 1801 to 1806. On September 8, International Literacy Day, the city begins its annual 10-day Jane Austen Festival with hundreds of Austen fans walking the streets dressed in costumes from Britain's Regency era, in the early 19th century.

International Literacy Day has been celebrated since 1967 and aims to highlight the importance of literacy to individuals and society. A global conference is held in Paris, France, including the awards ceremony of UNESCO's International Literacy Prizes.

bing-44367.jpg.title: Royal Albert Hall seen from Albert Memorial in Hyde Park, London
bing-44367.jpg.headline: Where history and harmony unite. Last Night of the Proms
bing-44367.jpg.description:
The renowned BBC Proms have been harmonising with hearts since their inception in 1895 at London's Royal Albert Hall. Running from July to September, the event offers a diverse array of contemporary and classical compositions. Today is the last night of this eight-week summer season. The second half of the evening gets properly patriotic, with anthems like 'Rule, Britannia!' and 'Land of Hope and Glory', inspiring a joyous sing-along.

Pictured here is the Royal Albert Hall in South Kensington. Built in memory of Prince Albert, Queen Victoria's consort, this iconic venue was envisioned as a tribute to his devotion to the arts and sciences. With its stunning circular design and distinctive domed roof, it has become a symbol of British culture and creativity since its opening in 1871. Beyond its architectural allure, the Royal Albert Hall boasts an impressive list of accolades, including recognition as a Grade I listed building.

bing-44370.jpg.title: Wat Chaiwatthanaram temple, Ayutthaya Historical Park, Thailand
bing-44370.jpg.headline: Ruins of a royal temple. Ayutthaya Historical Park, Thailand
bing-44370.jpg.description:
When the sun sets over Thailand, the Wat Chaiwatthanaram Buddhist temple lights up to welcome the night at the Ayutthaya Historical Park. These ruins are evidence of the area's rich history as the capital of the Ayutthaya Kingdom, which grew in power between the 14th and 18th centuries to rule Siam, or present-day Thailand. Around 1630, Wat Chaiwatthanaram was built on the orders of the dynasty's King Prasat Thong, to symbolize the center of the universe and connote his aspiration to become the future Buddha.

From the temple, the Historic City of Ayutthaya, a UNESCO World Heritage site, can be reached by boat or road. Three rivers link the once-metropolitan city to the sea. Now a historical ruin, Ayutthaya was an important point of commerce and diplomacy, with its surrounding rivers serving as a natural defense.

bing-44379.jpg.title: Bordeaux, France
bing-44379.jpg.headline: A misty Médoc morning. Médoc, France
bing-44379.jpg.description: In the Bordeaux region, the sprawling vineyards of the Médoc produce renowned wines. September marks the start of grape harvesting, with famous appellations like Margaux, Pauillac, Saint-Julien and Saint-Estèphe preserving ancient winemaking traditions. The area's history is mirrored in its architecture, with grand châteaux dotting the landscape, exemplifying past opulence. Château Margaux and Château Lafite Rothschild showcase the region's aristocratic history. These ancestral grounds also host the unique Marathon du Médoc. Established in 1985, it occurs annually in September, winding through vineyards. Known as the 'longest marathon in the world,' it merges running with wine tasting amid splendid châteaux and vineyards. Participants often wear themed costumes each year.

bing-44382.jpg.title: Walrus pair at sea in Svalbard, Norway
bing-44382.jpg.headline: Whiskery wisdom. Grandparents' Day
bing-44382.jpg.description: Have you called your nana, abuela, pop-pop or lolo lately? No matter what you call them, there's no better time to pick up the phone than Grandparents' Day, held on the Sunday after Labor Day. Grandparents play a special role in our lives, helping to raise new generations, passing down family history and sharing the wisdom of their experience. Wisdom is not always indicated by a thick Wilford-Brimley-esque mustache, but whiskers do lend a certain esteemed quality. Perhaps that's why these Atlantic walruses look like they're about to tell you why they voted for Hubert Humphrey.

bing-44387.jpg.title: Castillo de Monteagudo, Murcia, España
bing-44387.jpg.headline: Un castillo de colores. Castillo de Monteagudo, Murcia
bing-44387.jpg.description:
Los primeros días de septiembre la ciudad de Murcia toma ciertos colores especiales y música que aviva las calles gracias a las fiestas patronales que se celebran en honor a la Virgen de la Fuensanta.

La feria de Murcia cuenta con un gran recinto de casetas donde poder bailar y degustar maravillosos platos típicos, una de las mayores ferias de atracciones y actividades recreativas de España y un espectacular festival internacional de folclore. Además, podrás asistir a diversos recintos donde se celebra la feria del ganado y la feria taurina.

Sin lugar a duda, Murcia es una ciudad cargada de historia donde podrás disfrutar de su ambiente, música, gastronomía y tradición, lo que la convierten en un destino atractivo tanto para los locales como para los visitantes que desean explorar el encanto del sureste de España.

bing-44394.jpg.title: Brooklyn Bridge with the 'Tribute in Light' installation for 9/11, New York
bing-44394.jpg.headline: A 'Tribute in Light'. Patriot Day
bing-44394.jpg.description:
On September 11, Patriot Day is observed as a national day of service and remembrance to honor the 2,977 people who died in the attacks on the United States in 2001. Congress established the day in 2002 with bipartisan support, and ever since, US government buildings, both domestic and abroad, fly the American flag at half-staff. Many citizens and businesses do the same in remembrance. Patriot Day also honors the hard work and sacrifice of the first responders who bravely put themselves in harm's way in the hours and days after the attacks.

Today's image is of the Brooklyn Bridge with 'Tribute in Light' in the background, a display of 88 searchlights arranged in two columns that represent the Twin Towers that fell. Originally a temporary display, the annual installation illuminates the sky with columns of light from dusk until dawn. It is a stark reminder of the lives that were tragically lost in Manhattan, Pennsylvania, and at the Pentagon.

bing-44406.jpg.title: North Sea at sunset, Norddorf, Amrum Island, Germany
bing-44406.jpg.headline: Next stop, the horizon. North Sea at sunset, Norddorf, Germany
bing-44406.jpg.description: The small village of Norddorf is one of the oldest on the island of Amrum, off Germany's North Sea coast. Nestled amidst stunning natural beauty, Amrum is home to around 2,300 people and has a strong maritime heritage. Museums and lighthouses offer a glimpse into the island's past. Tourists can also explore the unique wildlife of the Naturschutzgebiet Amrumer Dünen (Amrum Dunes Nature Reserve), home to various bird species, like the red knot and brent goose, as well as plants like the common sundew and ragged robin.

bing-44418.jpg.title: Temples on Hemakuta Hill, Hampi, Karnataka, India
bing-44418.jpg.headline: Whispers of the past. Hemakuta Hill, Hampi, India
bing-44418.jpg.description:
Hampi is a UNESCO World Heritage Site in Karnataka, India. The group of monuments—ancient temples, majestic palaces, and intricate ruins—are remnants of the former capital city of the Vijayanagara Empire, which ruled much of South India between the 14th and 16th centuries.

The city grew during the reign of King Krishnadevaraya, from 1509 to 1529, and was famed for its art and architecture, attracting visitors from all over the world. However, Hampi lost its Midas touch in 1565, when it was destroyed after the defeat of its army at the Battle of Talikota.

Today, Hampi still houses about 1,000 ancient monuments and has become popular with modern backpackers, giving the lost city a new life. One of the most visited parts is Hemakuta Hill, with its well-preserved temples and shrines. While exploring the hill, visitors can stop by to offer prayers at the Virupaksha Temple, a pilgrimage site dedicated to Lord Shiva.

bing-44430.jpg.title: Przewalski's horses, Hustai National Park, Mongolia
bing-44430.jpg.headline: Just two pals horsin' around. Przewalski's horses, Hustai National Park, Mongolia
bing-44430.jpg.description: Hustai National Park in Mongolia is home to a very special and rare breed, the Przewalski's horse. Regarded by some as the only truly pure wild horse today, it is easily recognized by its pale yellowish-brown coat, a short, stiff mane, and short legs. The Przewalski's horse, also called the 'takhi' in Mongolia, was once extinct in the wild but has been successfully reintroduced through conservation efforts in the 1990s. An interesting fact about these horses is that they have 66 chromosomes, compared with 64 in domestic horses. Remarkably, Przewalski's horses can mate with domestic horses to produce hybrids. These hybrids have 65 chromosomes and can breed and have their own offspring.

bing-44434.jpg.title: Inside of a temple at sunrise in India Udaipur
bing-44434.jpg.headline: The jewel of Rajasthan. Udaipur, India
bing-44434.jpg.description:
The serene city of Udaipur, nestled alongside Lake Pichola and surrounded by the ridges of the Aravalli Range, offers a captivating setting that is unparalleled in Rajasthan. The city is filled with palaces, temples, and decorated homes called havelis. The bustling markets, arts scene, heritage hotels and idyllic countryside all add to its appeal.

Tourists and devotees who come to Udaipur must also visit the Jagdish Temple; an Indo-Aryan masterpiece constructed in 1651 CE. Dedicated to Lord Vishnu, this temple is celebrated for its carved pillars, ceilings and beautifully painted walls that leave spectators spellbound. Commissioned by Maharana Jagat Singh, the temple is renowned for being the biggest of its kind.

bing-44436.jpg.title: Luftaufnahme von Köln
bing-44436.jpg.headline: Da simmer dabei, dat ist prima, Viva Colonia!. Luftaufnahme von Köln
bing-44436.jpg.description:
Köln ist eine faszinierende Stadt mit einer reichen Geschichte und wurde von den Römern im Jahr 50 n. Chr. gegründet. Sie wurde mit dem Namen „Colonia Claudia Ara Agrippinensium“ getauft. Im Mittelalter blühte die westfälische Stadt auf, als sie ein bedeutendes Zentrum des Handels und der Hanse wurde. Der imposante Kölner Dom, das Wahrzeichen der Stadt, wurde im 13. Jahrhundert erbaut und erst 1880 fertiggestellt. Es handelt sich dabei um eine der größten gotischen Kirchen der Welt.

Heute repräsentiert Köln die ideale Mischung aus Antike und Moderne. Neben dem Dom thront der Kölnturm majestätisch über die Stadt, während das belebte Altstadtviertel mit seinen Fachwerkhäusern und gemütlichen Kneipen die Vergangenheit wieder zum Leben erweckt. Wie bereits erwähnt, besitzt Köln eine facettenreiche Kultur und genießt dadurch internationalen Ruf. Haben Sie schon mal das Museum Ludwig oder das Römisch-Germanische Museum besichtigt? Wenn nicht, sollten Sie dies unbedingt nachholen.

Vielleicht ist Köln den meisten jedoch aufgrund des Karnevals bekannt. Der Kölner Karneval ist eine Feier mit ausgelassenen Festlichkeiten und farbenfrohen Umzügen. Touristen aus ganz Deutschland und der Welt besuchen die westfälische Stadt, um dieses unglaubliche Fest miterleben zu können. Wo wir schon in der Zeit des Oktoberfests sind, gönnen Sie sich doch ein gutes Kölsch, ein weiteres Wahrzeichen der Stadt. Hauptsache eins, mit acht und bedacht trinken! Prost.

bing-44439.jpg.title: Sunset in Glenariff Forest Park, County Antrim, Ireland
bing-44439.jpg.headline: The Queen of the Glens. Glenariff Forest Park, County Antrim, Ireland
bing-44439.jpg.description: Glenariff Forest Park, nestled in the heart of Northern Ireland, hosts an array of wonders for nature enthusiasts. Famously known as 'the Queen of the Glens,' the park boasts a wealth of panoramic landscapes, serene riverside strolls and three magnificent waterfalls. Covering over 4 square miles, the park is under the care of the Northern Ireland Forest Service. Apart from being a recreational haven, it supports timber production and is a site of conservation for animals such as the red squirrel and Irish hare. Whether you're exploring the serene Scenic Trail or delving into the heart of the glen on the Waterfall Walk Trail, these journeys promise that you'll experience some of Northern Ireland's finest natural splendour.

bing-44442.jpg.title: Mission church ruins at Quarai, Salinas Pueblo Missions National Monument, New Mexico
bing-44442.jpg.headline: Celebrating Hispanic heritage. National Hispanic Heritage Month
bing-44442.jpg.description:
From early Spanish colonialism to modern day civil rights struggles, the timeline of Hispanic and Latino history in the US is a rich one. Hispanic Heritage Month—September 15 to October 15—is dedicated to the history, culture, and heritage grounded in Latin America. It began as Hispanic Week in 1968 and has since evolved into a 30-day celebration. Why does it start in the middle of the month? September 15 sees the first of a series of independence days in several Latin American countries—El Salvador, Honduras, Guatemala, Nicaragua, and Costa Rica. They are followed by Mexico, Chile, and Belize, which mark theirs on September 16, 18, and 21, respectively.

Pictured here are the ruins of the mission church at Quarai in New Mexico, completed in 1632 under the direction of Spanish Franciscan friars. It is one of the three Spanish mission sites that form the Salinas Pueblo Missions National Monument. Visiting the ruins is a great way to participate in Hispanic Heritage Month.

bing-44448.jpg.title: Lederhosen und Tradition, Oktoberfest auf der Theresienwiese in München
bing-44448.jpg.headline: O’zapft is!. Das Oktoberfest beginnt!
bing-44448.jpg.description:
Vielleicht wissen nicht alle, wie und wann eigentlich die Tradition des Oktoberfests begonnen hat. Kommen Sie mit auf eine kleine Geschichtsreise mit uns. Das weltberühmte Bierfest wurde zum ersten Mal am 12. Oktober 1810 zu Ehren der Hochzeit von Kronprinz Ludwig von Bayern und Prinzessin Therese von Sachsen-Hildburghausen begangen.

Doch wieso ausgerechnet im Oktober? Dafür gibt es eine einfache Erklärung: Der sogenannte Altweibersommer bietet die besten Bedingungen für Outdoor-Veranstaltungen. Unserer Meinung nach ist das Wichtigste, dass bei den ersten Oktoberfesten überhaupt kein Bier getrunken wurde. Anfangs wurden vor allem Pferderennen und Landwirtschaftsausstellungen organisiert. Erst um 1880 begann nach der Genehmigung der Stadtverwaltung der Bierverkauf.

Seit über 200 Jahren hat das Oktoberfest mit Ausnahme von Kriegszeiten und Pandemien immer stattgefunden. Das erste Oktoberfest nach dem 2. Weltkrieg wurde im Jahr 1949 abgehalten. Seitdem hat es mit Ausnahme von 2020 und 2021 jedes Jahr stattgefunden. So soll es auch sein! Ziehen wir Dirndl und Lederhosen an und auf geht's zur Theresienwiese, um diese jahrhundertealte Tradition zu feiern. Hauptsache eins: die Maß mit Maß trinken!

bing-44454.jpg.title: A beer tent at Oktoberfest in Theresienwiese, Munich, Germany
bing-44454.jpg.headline: Prost to you and yours!. Oktoberfest begins
bing-44454.jpg.description: Welcome to Oktoberfest, the world's biggest beer festival, held each year in the German city of Munich. Dating back all the way to 1810, it began with the wedding of Crown Prince Ludwig, later Ludwig I of Bavaria, and Princess Therese von Sachsen-Hildburghausen. The celebrations took place on the fields in front of the city gates, which were named Theresienwiese, or Theresa's Meadow, in honor of the bride. The festivities lasted for five days, filled with exciting activities such as parades and horse races. It was so popular that Oktoberfest became an annual event that now draws more than 6 million people. This year's festival starts today and lasts 18 days. Beyond Munich, it has become a popular celebration in multiple countries, and cities inside and outside of Germany imitate the festival and cherish its German traditions.
bing-44454.jpg.copyright: © Peter Kneffel/picture alliance via Getty Image

bing-44461.jpg.title: Parapendio che sorvola le Dolomiti, visto dal Sass Pordoi
bing-44461.jpg.headline: Volando tra le alte cime
bing-44461.jpg.description:
Le Dolomiti rappresentano l'estensione orientale delle Alpi e svettano maestose nel territorio compreso delle regioni di Veneto, Trentino-Alto Adige e Friuli-Venezia Giulia. Tra le varie vette non possiamo fare a meno di menzionare il Sass Pordoi (o anche Sasso Pordoi) situata nel gruppo del Sella, al confine tra le province di Trento e Belluno. La cima può vantare un'altezza di 2950 metri ed è raggiungibile con una funivia che parte dal Passo Pordoi, uno dei quattro passi della Strada delle Dolomiti. Sasso Pordoi è noto come la terrazza delle Dolomiti, per via della sua forma piatta e la vista panoramica che offre sulle vette circostanti, tra cui la Marmolada, la regina delle Dolomiti. Sasso Pordoi è anche una meta ambita dagli appassionati di storia, ciclismo, escursionismo, arrampicata e sci. Sul Passo Pordoi si trovano infatti il Museo della Grande Guerra e l’Ossario, che ricordano le battaglie della Prima Guerra Mondiale che si svolsero in queste zone.

I suoi 28 tornanti rendono il Passo una delle tappe più difficili, ma al tempo stesso entusiasmanti per gli appassionati di ciclismo e del Giro D'Italia. Mentre per tutti gli altri appassionati di sport e vita all'aria aperta la località offre numerosi itinerari per camminare, scalare, percorrere vie ferrate e fare tour in mountain bike, bici da strada e volare in parapendio.

bing-44463.jpg.title: Cuban tody, Alejandro de Humboldt National Park, Cuba
bing-44463.jpg.headline: Can you answer the call?. Cuban tody, Alejandro de Humboldt National Park, Cuba
bing-44463.jpg.description:
The tiny, colourful Cuban tody can only be found on Cuba and its neighbouring islands. Its vibrant outfit gives it a unique look: a sparkling green back, pale grey underparts, a red throat, pink flanks, blue ear patches and a black and red beak. Despite their colourful plumage, their size makes them hard to see; however, they are easy to hear. The soft sound of 'pprreeee-pprreeee' or a short 'tot-tot-tot-tot' will tell you there's a tody somewhere nearby.

The species are mostly found in or near evergreen forests, coastal vegetation, dry lowlands and around rivers. One of their habitats, Alejandro de Humboldt National Park, is the biggest and best-preserved zone of forested landscape in the Caribbean. The park is considered important for its endemic flora as it is one of the most biologically varied tropical island locations on Earth.

bing-44464.jpg.title: Florescimento das árvores de Piuva Rosa no Pantanal Norte, Brasil
bing-44464.jpg.headline: Beleza em Flor
bing-44464.jpg.description:
A cerejeira-do-Pantanal, também conhecida como ipê-rosa, é uma presença mágica nas vastas paisagens do Pantanal brasileiro. Suas flores rosa delicadamente vibrantes embelezam as margens dos rios e as áreas alagadas, criando um contraste marcante com o verde exuberante ao seu redor. Essa árvore simboliza a resiliência e a beleza da natureza pantaneira, que se adapta aos ciclos sazonais das águas, desabrochando em uma exibição espetacular de cores.

Além de sua estética deslumbrante, a cerejeira-do-Pantanal desempenha um papel vital no ecossistema do Pantanal. Suas flores fornecem néctar e alimento para uma variedade de insetos e pássaros, contribuindo para a complexa teia da vida na região. Em um ecossistema que pulsa com biodiversidade, a cerejeira-do-Pantanal é um símbolo de conexão entre a flora e a fauna, destacando a intrincada harmonia que define esse tesouro natural do Brasil.

bing-44478.jpg.title: Milky Way over Southwest Alentejo and Vicentine Coast Natural Park, Portugal
bing-44478.jpg.headline: A rainbow's nocturnal cousin. Fall Astronomy Week
bing-44478.jpg.description: The Milky Way has billions of stars; among them, our own sun finds its place. The galaxy's name is derived from the radiant, pale appearance of the band of stars and gas clouds that graces Earth's sky. Methodical observations of the night sky started with early civilizations but astronomy, the oldest natural science, remains a source of fascination today. It's what brings stargazers to Portugal's Southwest Alentejo and Vicentine Coast Natural Park, a site free from heavy light pollution. Now's a good time to seek out your own celestial spectacle, as it is Astronomy Week and the main event, Saturday's Fall Astronomy Day, this year coincides with the autumnal equinox.

bing-44482.jpg.title: Detail of an old Ganesh sculpture, Karnataka
bing-44482.jpg.headline: Hail the Hindu God of wisdom. Ganesh Chaturthi
bing-44482.jpg.description: Ganesh Chaturthi is a Hindu festival observed for 10 days to honour the birth of Lord Ganesha. Ganesha is an elephant-headed deity who symbolises prosperity, removes obstacles and brings wisdom and new beginnings. During the festival, people place Ganesha idols on elevated platforms in their homes and celebrate by reciting Vedic hymns along with the ceremonial anointing of the Lord Ganesha statue. On the last day of this occasion, the idols are brought to a river for their immersion, alongside a grand display of devotees playing rhythmic drums, singing devotional songs and joyfully dancing.

bing-44485.jpg.title: Festa di San Gennaro a Mulberry Street, Little Italy, New York
bing-44485.jpg.headline: Vediamo chi mangia più cannoli!
bing-44485.jpg.description:
Sei pronto per immergerti in un'esplosione di sapori e tradizioni? Allora preparati per la festa di San Gennaro di Mulberry Street, a New York! Nonostante si svolga all'estero, questo evento ti farà sentire come se fossi stato catapultato direttamente nel cuore di Napoli. Inoltre, offre a tutti l'opportunità di conoscere la vita di San Gennaro di Napoli, vescovo di Benevento e martire nel 305 d.C. e la sua importanza per la comunità italo-americana, nonché per i nostri concittadini napoletani.

Immagina di passeggiare lungo le strade di Little Italy, circondato da bancarelle che offrono deliziosi manicaretti italiani. Puoi gustare cannoli, pizza, pasta fresca e tante altre prelibatezze che ti faranno venire l'acquolina in bocca.

Ma la festa di San Gennaro non è solo cibo. Ci sono anche giochi, spettacoli, musica e divertimento per tutta la famiglia. Puoi partecipare a gare di tiro alla fune, sfidare i tuoi amici a una partita di calcio balilla o cimentarti nella famosa gara di mangiatori di cannoli, ammesso tu abbia lo stomaco adatto! Non dimenticare di provare la famosa zeppola, un dolce fritto che ti farà perdere la testa! Buon appetito!

bing-44490.jpg.title: Splügen Pass, Graubünden, Switzerland
bing-44490.jpg.headline: Fasten your seatbelts!. Splügen Pass, Switzerland
bing-44490.jpg.description: With their twists and turns, record heights, and breathtaking vistas, mountain roads are not for the faint-hearted. Pictured here is the historic Splügen Pass, which winds its way through the Lepontine Alps, on the border of Switzerland and Italy. Although its modern version was built between 1818-1823, the Splügen Pass existed in some form as far back as Roman times. At 6,936 feet high, it is one of the highest paved roads in Europe, with 51 marked hairpin bends. It is closed in winter but, if spectacular mountainside views and picturesque lakes tickle your fancy, you can enjoy this ascent between June and mid-October. Have we 'peaked' your interest yet?

bing-44495.jpg.title: Castillo de Colomares en Benalmádena, Málaga, Andalucía, España
bing-44495.jpg.headline: ¡Castillo a la vista!. Castillo de Colomares en Benalmádena, Málaga, Andalucía, España
bing-44495.jpg.description:
Este precioso “castillo” realmente es un monumento al Descubrimiento de América y en homenaje a los Reyes Católicos, el cual está repleto de simbología y compuesto por una mezcla de estilos arquitectónicos (neobizantino, neorrománico, neogótico y neomudéjar).

Un dato curioso de este monumento es que, pese a su apariencia antigua, fue construido entre el 1987 y 1994 en Benalmádena, un pueblo costero de la provincia de Málaga, al sur de la península Ibérica por un médico y la ayuda de un par de albañiles, lo cual lo hace un gran atractivo turístico de la zona.

bing-44502.jpg.title: Roman-inspired aqueduct, Arkadia Park, Poland
bing-44502.jpg.headline: Water under and over the bridge. Aqueduct, Arkadia Park, Poland
bing-44502.jpg.description: Founded in 1778 by aristocrat Helena Radziwiłłowa, Arkadia Park is an English-style landscape park in central Poland. The park displays architecture and landscapes that evoke ancient and medieval eras, like this recreation of a Roman-style aqueduct. These features are brought to life by the garden's lush greenery, tranquil water, and intricately crafted sculptures throughout the grounds, which illustrate the beauty of intermingled nature and art. Today, Arkadia Park stands as a testament to Helena Radziwiłłowa's lasting vision and creative legacy.

bing-44512.jpg.title: Copaiba - Brazil
bing-44512.jpg.headline: Honrando a Natureza e o Verde
bing-44512.jpg.description:
O Dia da Árvore, celebrado em 21 de setembro no Brasil, é uma ocasião especial que visa ressaltar a importância das árvores e da preservação ambiental. Instituída com o propósito de conscientizar a sociedade sobre a necessidade de cuidar e proteger nossas florestas e recursos naturais, essa data destaca a relevância das árvores para o equilíbrio do ecossistema e a qualidade de vida de todos os seres vivos. Nesse dia, várias atividades, como plantio de mudas, palestras educativas e ações de reflorestamento, são promovidas em todo o país, incentivando o engajamento de indivíduos, comunidades e instituições em prol da preservação ambiental e da promoção de um futuro sustentável.

No Brasil, as florestas tropicais desempenham um papel vital na regulação do clima global e na biodiversidade. O Dia da Árvore nos lembra da importância de valorizar e proteger esses ecossistemas, contribuindo para a manutenção da qualidade do ar, a conservação da fauna e flora e a mitigação dos efeitos das mudanças climáticas. A data também nos convida a refletir sobre nossas ações individuais e coletivas em relação ao meio ambiente, incentivando práticas sustentáveis e a responsabilidade ambiental como formas de garantir um planeta saudável para as gerações presentes e futuras.

bing-44514.jpg.title: Inside the Nobel Peace Center, Oslo, Norway
bing-44514.jpg.headline: Recognizing champions of peace. International Day of Peace
bing-44514.jpg.description:
Every year on September 21, the United Nations celebrates the International Day of Peace, or World Peace Day. Established in 1981 by the United Nations General Assembly, the day begins with the Peace Bell Ceremony held at the UN headquarters in New York City. The bell was a gift from the United Nations Association of Japan and is inscribed with a message of hope: 'Long live absolute world peace.'

Our homepage image was taken inside the lobby of the Nobel Peace Center, in Norway's bustling capital city Oslo. The center highlights the triumphs of Nobel Peace Prize laureates and shares the legacy of Alfred Nobel, the creator of the prize. By showcasing inspiring exhibits and insightful conversations, the center sheds light on the impact of the prize, awarded to those 'who, during the preceding year, have conferred the greatest benefit to humankind.'

bing-44523.jpg.title: Castell y Gwynt, Glyder Fach, Snowdonia National Park, North Wales, UK
bing-44523.jpg.headline: There and back again. Hobbit Day
bing-44523.jpg.description:
Bilbo Baggins, the protagonist and title character of 'The Hobbit', once famously said, 'not all those who wander are lost,' but in this realm of Castell y Gwynt, momentarily losing your sense of direction is half the fun! Though it looks like Middle-earth from the 'Lord of the Rings' trilogy, this craggy place is nestled in Snowdonia, Wales. Castell y Gwynt, which translates to 'Castle of the Wind,' is perched high on Glyder Fach, one of Snowdonia's rugged peaks.

Today is Hobbit Day—a day dedicated to celebrating the universe created by J.R.R. Tolkien. Why September 22, you wonder? It's the shared birthday of two of the most beloved hobbits in literature—Bilbo and Frodo Baggins! So, whether you're planning a grand adventure to Wales or a cosy day in, make sure to let your inner hobbit shine and remember, 'The road goes on and on.'

bing-44526.jpg.title: Southern white rhinoceros males, Shamwari Private Game Reserve, South Africa
bing-44526.jpg.headline: Sorry to crash your party. World Rhinoceros Day
bing-44526.jpg.description:
Keep the five alive! That is the mission of World Rhinoceros Day, rhino specialists, and fans around the globe. Those five species are: the Javan, Sumatran, greater one-horned, black, and white rhinoceros. It is the white rhino which can be seen on our homepage, identified by its two horns and square lip.

The wild rhino population globally is estimated to be under 27,000—less than the average capacity at a Major League Baseball stadium. While there have been conservation successes, ensuring these amazing animals survive is a continuing challenge. Habitat loss is one threat, but rhinos are particularly targeted by poachers for their horns. Parks like the Shamwari Game Reserve in South Africa, pictured above, employ anti-poaching squads to keep these rhinos safe.

bing-44527.jpg.title: Marsala salt pans, Italy
bing-44527.jpg.headline: Marsala salt pans, Italy
bing-44527.jpg.description:
Marsala salt pans are a part of the Stagnone Reserve, which has been a protected area since 1995 and occupies an area of about 1,000 hectares. In ancient times, sea salt was extracted at the reserve, but now, this beautiful place is managed by World Wildlife Fund Italy, which protects the numerous avian species that periodically migrate to the Marsala area.

This unique location offers a variety of experiences. For example, you can visit the mill or enrich your experience with a visit to a thematic museum to understand the reserve's cultural aspects. You can also take a beautiful, guided walk, which includes a visit to the mill.

bing-44531.jpg.title: Parque Nacional de Ordesa y Monte Perdido, Huesca, Aragón, España
bing-44531.jpg.headline: ¿Nos vestimos para la ocasión?. Parque Nacional de Ordesa y Monte Perdido, Huesca, Aragón, España
bing-44531.jpg.description:
El hemisferio norte del planeta se despide del verano para dar la bienvenida al otoño. El equinoccio de otoño marca este momento. Su nombre proviene del latín y significa “noche igual”, haciendo referencia al hecho de que la duración de la noche y el día se equiparan en este punto del año.

Los árboles del Parque Nacional de Ordesa y Monte Perdido (Huesca) se preparan también para este cambio de estación, cambiando la tonalidad de sus hojas a tonos más ocres, que terminarán por cubrir el suelo de un manto cobrizo cuando caigan.

El valle de Ordesa, situado en el Pirineo Aragonés, fue uno de los primeros del mundo en ser reconocido parque nacional, nada menos que en 1918. Su ampliación al territorio que cubre actualmente se llevó a cabo en 1982. Su gran estado de conservación hace de él un destino ideal para los senderistas y montañistas que quieran disfrutar de este paraje natural. Así que ponte las botas, coge tu mochila y descubre sus maravillas.

bing-44534.jpg.title: Parc ostréicole à La Faute-sur-Mer, Pointe d'Arcay France, Vendée
bing-44534.jpg.headline: Une histoire de gastronomie à la française. Fête de la Gastronomie
bing-44534.jpg.description:
La Fête de la Gastronomie, également connue sous le nom de "Fête de la Gastronomie française" ou "Goût de France", est un événement annuel qui célèbre la gastronomie française, son patrimoine culinaire et ses traditions. Cette fête a été créée en 2011 par le ministère français de l'Agriculture et de l'Alimentation.

Au cœur des eaux cristallines de la côte atlantique, La Faute-sur-Mer est un petit coin de paradis côtier. En harmonie avec la nature, cette charmante commune du département de la Vendée, s'est transformée en un lieu privilégié où les générations se transmettent l'art de l'ostréiculture.

Les bras du littoral vendéen offrent un refuge idéal pour l'élevage de ces mollusques. L'ostréiculture est bien plus qu'une simple activité, c'est un lien entre le terroir et la mer, une symphonie de saveurs et de savoir-faire.

bing-44537.jpg.title: The light installation 'Global Rainbow' by artist Yvette Mattern
bing-44537.jpg.headline: Toronto goes nocturnal. Nuit Blanche Toronto
bing-44537.jpg.description:
Nuit Blanche is the perfect night to roam the moonlit streets of Toronto in search of art installations. The event is an international celebration of contemporary art that traces its roots to Paris in 2002. Since then, this dazzling event has spread its wings and reached various cities worldwide. Tonight, the Toronto is set to transform into a nocturnal wonderland as the event returns with a theme: Breaking Ground.

This all-night experience is set to illuminate the city with numerous installations, performances, and exhibits by 250 artists from various disciplines. Get ready to explore downtown Toronto and the Etobicoke and Scarborough neighbourhoods to witness innovative projects! With its inception in 2006, Nuit Blanche 6ix has consistently enchanted both locals and visitors, offering an experience that combines art and urban landscapes.

bing-44538.jpg.title: Cottonwood trees and red sandstone in Coyote Gulch, Glen Canyon National Recreation Area, Utah
bing-44538.jpg.headline: Awash in autumn hues. Autumnal equinox
bing-44538.jpg.description:
Autumn has officially begun! In the Northern Hemisphere, the autumnal equinox falls on September 23 this year, marking the beginning of autumn. Today is one of the two moments in the year when day and night are equal in length, thanks to the sun's location exactly above the equator. In the Southern Hemisphere, today marks the vernal equinox and they are heading into spring.

Camouflaged in autumn colors, the cottonwood tree in today's image might be playing peek-a-boo among the red sandstones of Coyote Gulch in southern Utah. Here in the Glen Canyon National Recreation Area, the canyon is painted orange by oxidizing water and other fluids, as well as iron-filled minerals.

bing-44543.jpg.title: Vista de la ciudad desde el Parque Güell en Barcelona, España
bing-44543.jpg.headline: ¿Dónde está este mágico parque?. Parque Güell, Barcelona, España
bing-44543.jpg.description:
En el día de hoy, Barcelona festeja por todo lo alto la “Virgen de la Mare de Déu de la Mercè” (Virgen de la Merced), la cual lleva siendo patrona de la ciudad desde 1687 y tiene su basílica ubicada en el Barrio Gótico. Aunque su celebración oficial sea el día 24 de septiembre de cada año, lo cierto es que los barceloneses alargan los festejos durante varios días.

Durante este período, los locales y visitantes pueden disfrutar de diferentes tradiciones, como el popular “Desfile de Gegants i Capgrossos” (Gigantes y Cabezudos), los famosos “castellers” formados por torres humanas, o el “Correfoc”, en el que vecinos de la ciudad se disfrazan de diablos al atardecer y recorren las calles lanzando petardos y fuegos.

Si prefieres un plan más tranquilo, en el Parque de la Ciudadela podrás disfrutar de música y espectáculos callejeros, así como admirar las proyecciones de luz que se realizan cuando comienza a oscurecer. No lo dudes y acércate a Barcelona a conocer su rica cultura.

bing-44544.jpg.title: Berlin Marathon Skyline mit Sonnenlicht, Berlin
bing-44544.jpg.headline: Laufen zur Siegessäule, welch goldene Freude!. Berlin-Marathon
bing-44544.jpg.description:
Heute, am 24. September 2023, wird der Berlin-Marathon erneut die Straßen der deutschen Hauptstadt zum Beben bringen. Hier versammeln sich heute Tausende Leute, ob Berliner, Sportfanatiker oder Touristen. Das Motto, das uns hier alle vereint, ist: Spaß und Freude am Laufen! Der Winter nähert sich langsam, da gibt es doch nichts Besseres, als noch mal im Freien zu sprinten, bevor Kälte und Nässe wieder eintreffen.

Haben Sie schon mal dieses fantastische Event miterlebt? Wussten Sie, dass dieser Marathon zu den World Marathon Majors gehört? Keine Kleinigkeit, wenn man bedenkt, dass zu den Majors Marathonläufe das von Boston, Chicago, New York, Tokyo und London gehören. Unserer Meinung nach ist etwas an dieser Veranstaltung besonders reizvoll: Hier dürfen alle teilnehmen, auch Rollstuhlfahrer und Handbiker.

Man sagt, das Wichtigste sei, dabei zu sein und nicht zu gewinnen. Wir stimmen diesem Motto vollkommen zu. Trotzdem sollten wir auch diejenigen nennen, die Rekordler dieses Marathons sind. Die Läuferin Assefa Tigist hält den aktuellen Rekord im Berlin-Marathon, der im Jahr 2022 aufgestellt wurde. Die Zeit betrug 2 Stunden 15 Minuten und 37 Sekunden. Der Rekord bei den Männern wird von Eliud Kipchoge gehalten, ebenfalls aus dem Jahr 2022 mit einer Zeit von 2 Stunden 1 Minute und 9 Sekunden. Was meinen Sie dazu? Sind Sie bereit für diese Herausforderung?

bing-44550.jpg.title: The Fraser River near Mount Robson, British Columbia, Canada
bing-44550.jpg.headline: Trickle, babble, or roar. World Rivers Day
bing-44550.jpg.description:
If you are a nature enthusiast, or simply enjoy listening to the sound of rumbling rivers, you might like to know that today is World Rivers Day. First held in 2005 during the United Nations' 'Water for Life’ campaign, it was proposed by Canadian river conservationist Mark Angelo, who founded BC Rivers Day in western Canada in 1980. World Rivers Day is held on the fourth Sunday of September to celebrate and raise awareness of the benefits that rivers provide to people and the planet.

The star of today's image, the Fraser River, is the longest river in British Columbia and the 11th longest in Canada. The stream meanders from the Rocky Mountains, traveling more than 850 miles over slopes and flatlands before it merges with the Strait of Georgia, just south of Vancouver.

bing-44562.jpg.title: Sea otter in Bartlett Cove, Glacier Bay National Park and Preserve, Alaska
bing-44562.jpg.headline: Kick back, snack, and relax. Sea Otter Awareness Week
bing-44562.jpg.description:
It's hard not to smile when you spot a sea otter. Their whiskery faces, busy paws, and thick fur give the impression of a stuffed animal that has come to life and taken to the ocean. The heaviest members of the weasel family, sea otters aren't just cute. They also play a vital role in the underwater kelp forest ecosystem, keeping the destructive sea urchin population in check—by eating them.

Sea Otter Awareness Week aims to help protect their populations, found along the coasts of the north Pacific Ocean. They once numbered 300,000 but they dropped to fewer than 2,000 after widespread hunting. International protections were put into place in 1911 and numbers have rebounded to around 125,000, but they remain endangered. While some habitats never recovered, others have emerged in entirely new locations, such as Glacier Bay National Park and Preserve in Alaska. In 1995, five sea otters were spotted in Glacier Bay. Today, there are more than 8,000 hunting, playing, and raising pups in the kelp-abundant waters.

bing-44572.jpg.title: Estação Da Luz, São Paulo, Brasil
bing-44572.jpg.headline: O Coração de São Paulo
bing-44572.jpg.description: A Estação da Luz, situada no coração de São Paulo, é um ícone histórico que remonta ao final do século XIX, quando foi inaugurada em 1901. Projetada por arquitetos ingleses, a estação exibe uma deslumbrante arquitetura de estilo vitoriano, com sua imponente fachada e vitrais encantadores. Ao longo dos anos, a Estação da Luz testemunhou momentos cruciais da história do Brasil, desde o ciclo do café até a Revolução Constitucionalista de 1932. Hoje, além de servir como um importante centro ferroviário, abriga o Museu da Língua Portuguesa, um local que celebra a riqueza da língua e da cultura brasileira. A Estação da Luz continua a ser um marco significativo que une o passado e o presente, lembrando-nos da importância do patrimônio histórico e cultural de São Paulo e do Brasil.

bing-44574.jpg.title: Venice Skatepark at sunset, Los Angeles, California
bing-44574.jpg.headline: Waves for wheels. Venice Skatepark, Los Angeles, California
bing-44574.jpg.description:
Welcome to the concrete waves of Venice Beach, California, a skateboarder's paradise. Built next to the beach town's sun-kissed shores, Venice Skatepark stands as a testament to the history of skateboarding in the state.

Opened in 2009, the park was the result of years of efforts by residents, spearheaded by Venice skating legend Jesse Martinez. With a plethora of challenging ramps, bowls, and rails, it has something to keep skaters of all skill levels entertained. Its oceanfront setting also makes it a popular spot for spectators to stop by and watch gravity-defying tricks from backside tailslides and 360 pop shove-its, to skaters dropping into a bowl to nail an eggplant. And if you're not sure what any of those things are, there's also a great view of the beach.
