bing-45051.jpg.description: It turns out that history is not always written by the victors. Nearly four centuries ago, on November 4, 1605, a plot to kill King James I was discovered in the cellars of the Houses of Parliament. One participant, Guy Fawkes, had assembled barrels of gunpowder, and was planning to attack the state opening of Parliament the next day. Almost immediately, November 5 was set up as a day to remember the thwarting of the infamous Gunpowder Plot. Over the years, it has evolved into a celebration—though usually stripped of its political and religious connotations—with sparklers, whirling Catherine wheels, bonfires (topped by an effigy known as a Guy) and a bit of folk verse: 'Remember, remember the fifth of November, gunpowder, treason and plot. I see no reason why gunpowder treason should ever be forgot!'

bing-45052.jpg.title: GrandPrix, São Paulo, Brasil
bing-45052.jpg.headline: A vitória mais bela é sempre a próxima
bing-45052.jpg.description:
O Grande Prêmio do Brasil de Fórmula 1, celebrado em 5 de novembro, é um dos eventos automobilísticos mais emocionantes e tradicionais do mundo. A cidade de São Paulo tem sido o palco dessa corrida lendária desde 1973, e ao longo dos anos, o Autódromo José Carlos Pace, também conhecido como Interlagos, tem testemunhado inúmeras histórias memoráveis. Uma das mais icônicas é a vitória de Ayrton Senna em 1991, quando ele ultrapassou Alain Prost na última volta da corrida, tornando-se um herói nacional e conquistando o coração dos fãs de automobilismo em todo o mundo.

Além disso, a pista de Interlagos é conhecida por proporcionar corridas emocionantes e imprevisíveis devido ao seu traçado desafiador e mudanças climáticas repentinas. Grandes nomes da Fórmula 1, como Nelson Piquet, Emerson Fittipaldi e Felipe Massa, também deixaram sua marca no Grande Prêmio do Brasil. Com uma atmosfera apaixonada e uma história rica, esta corrida é um evento imperdível para os fãs de automobilismo e continua a ser uma das datas mais esperadas no calendário da Fórmula 1.

bing-45054.jpg.title: Quartzite formation, Playa del Silencio, Asturias, Spain
bing-45054.jpg.headline: A quiet place, indeed. Playa del Silencio, Spain
bing-45054.jpg.description:
Spain's Asturias region, known for its greenery, artistic legacy, and excellent food, has many hidden gems. Our homepage image shows Playa del Silencio, or Beach of Silence, a shell-shaped cove with a natural rock amphitheater. Far away from urban areas and noisy crowds, the beach enjoys a sense of isolation and solitude. Rugged cliffs surround golden sands perfect for soaking up its peaceful vibes, while nearby caves and water activities provide exciting adventures for those who crave them.

The rocky shoreline seen here is made of quartzite, formed over millions of years. This spectacular display was created when quartz grains gradually replaced the original rock while maintaining its texture. With their intricate patterns and colors, some of these rocks resemble ancient wood.

bing-45066.jpg.title: Lake Pehoé, Torres del Paine National Park, Chile
bing-45066.jpg.headline: Catching rays in Torres del Paine. Lake Pehoé, Torres del Paine National Park, Chile
bing-45066.jpg.description: Turquoise waters surrounded by jagged peaks and lush forests—that's Lake Pehoé for you. Nestled in Torres del Paine National Park, Chile, this glacial lake reflects the towering peaks of the Cuernos del Paine, pictured here bathed in the sun's rays. The lake gets its color from finely ground rock particles and minerals, known as glacial flour, suspended in the water. The word 'paine,' pronounced pie-neh, in the park’s name is believed to have its roots in a Tehuelche word meaning 'blue' while 'torres' means towers. The park is named after three striking granite peaks that reach up to 8,200 feet above sea level but boasts many other spectacular mountains. At 700 square miles, Torres del Paine is a UNESCO Biosphere Reserve with a huge amount to offer visitors, from hiking and kayaking to stargazing. So, pack your sense of adventure and head south to beat the blues.

bing-45078.jpg.title: Kirkilai lakes and lookout tower, Biržai Regional Park, Lithuania
bing-45078.jpg.headline: Lookout above!. Kirkilai lakes, Biržai Regional Park, Lithuania
bing-45078.jpg.description: Curving above the treetops of Biržai Regional Park in northern Lithuania, this unusual structure allows a bird's-eye view of a unique landscape. Built in 2015, the Kirkilai Observation Tower's shape is said to resemble a sinking boat, appropriate in an area dotted with water-filled sink holes. About 30 of these small lakes can be seen from the top of the tower, nearly 100 feet in the air. These lakes can be up to 36 feet deep and are just some of the thousands of sinkholes identified in the park. Water-soluble rocks like gypsum lie under the soil in this area, and over time they gradually erode, forming caves, which then collapse. In some cases, they fill with water, creating this mesmerizing landscape. The interconnected lakes mirror the surrounding greenery, creating a scenic haven for nature enthusiasts.

bing-45081.jpg.title: 黄山的日落，安徽省，中国
bing-45081.jpg.headline: 冬日里的壮丽美景
bing-45081.jpg.description:
立冬是中国二十四节气中的第十九个节气。 这也是冬天的开始。在南方，初冬时节一般都不是很冷。随着时间的推移，冬至后冷空气频繁南下，气温逐渐下降。入冬后，北方大部分地区将出现雨雪降温天气。华北部分地区此时常下初雪。

今天给大家带来的是冬天的黄山。雪后的黄山银装素裹，美丽极了。游客可以欣赏到“玉宇琼塔”、“水晶宫”等美景，这是其他季节难以想象的。此外，黄山的温泉也非常有名，游客可以在这里享受温暖的温泉浴，在寒冷的冬天放松身心。

bing-45087.jpg.title: Llyn Padarn, Llanberis, Snowdonia, Wales
bing-45087.jpg.headline: A place to reflect. Llyn Padarn, Snowdonia, Wales
bing-45087.jpg.description: From sparkling llyns, mountain hikes, cascading waterfalls to ruined castles, Snowdonia never ceases to amaze. Pictured here is Llyn Padarn, situated near the charming village of Llanberis. At about 2 miles in length and 95 feet in depth, this glacial lake is one of the largest natural lakes in Wales. This example of a moraine-dammed lake has been designated as both a Site of Special Scientific Interest and a bathing water. Whether you're an enthusiast of kayaking, paddleboarding or simply want to immerse your toes in the water, it has your back. In addition, its shores are dotted with remnants of slate quarries, providing a glimpse into the region's industrial past. While you're there, don't forget to explore the nearby Dolbadarn Castle, a historic gem that adds an extra layer of antiquity to your journey.

bing-45090.jpg.title: West Indian manatee mother and baby, Three Sisters Springs, Crystal River, Florida
bing-45090.jpg.headline: The life aquatic. Manatee Awareness Month
bing-45090.jpg.description:
Today we're celebrating the lovely manatee! These marvelous marine mammals have a fascinating history that spans millions of years. They are related to elephants and their ancestors can be traced back to the Eocene era (about 56 to 33.9 million years ago), making them one of the oldest mammals on Earth. These slow-moving herbivores have, over time, adapted to life in warm, coastal waters.

These sleepy creatures are friendly towards humans but boat collisions and habitat loss are among their biggest threats. Our homepage manatees are pictured in Three Sisters Springs, in Florida's Crystal River, where hundreds of manatees arrive to spend the winter months in warmer waters. If you visit the area and come across a West Indian manatee, we encourage you to take a moment to appreciate them, but from a distance.

bing-45102.jpg.title: Birch trees in autumn, Drammen, Norway
bing-45102.jpg.headline: Shades of autumn. Birch trees, Drammen, Norway
bing-45102.jpg.description: Surrounded by forests and embraced by fjords, the Norwegian port city of Drammen is a haven for outdoor enthusiasts. Birch trees flourish at high altitudes, making them a natural fit for the mountainous region. When autumn arrives, their leaves transform into a mosaic of gold and crimson, in stark contrast to their pale, slender trunks. Long associated with new beginnings and renewal, birch trees don't just look good, they provide a home and sustenance for wildlife, and can be used for firewood and in construction.

bing-45112.jpg.title: Praia de Ipanema, Rio de Janeiro, Brasil
bing-45112.jpg.headline: Ipanema: O Charme da Praia Carioca
bing-45112.jpg.description: A praia de Ipanema, localizada no coração do Rio de Janeiro, é uma joia carioca. Com um passado rico, esta praia viu muitos momentos históricos do Brasil se desenrolarem em suas areias douradas e sob o olhar atento do icônico morro Dois Irmãos. Nos anos 1960, Ipanema estava no centro da efervescente cultura bossa nova, que trouxe influências musicais inigualáveis. Hoje, Ipanema continua sendo um local de encontro para cariocas e turistas, com suas águas cintilantes, calçadão movimentado e o famoso posto 9, que é um ícone do estilo de vida descontraído e vibrante da cidade. Uma visita a Ipanema é uma jornada pelo tempo e um mergulho na história e na energia pulsante do Rio de Janeiro.

bing-45114.jpg.title: Badlands National Park, South Dakota
bing-45114.jpg.headline: Not-so-bad lands. Badlands National Park's 45th anniversary
bing-45114.jpg.description: The strange stripes in our homepage image reveal tiers of fossil beds in Badlands National Park in South Dakota. Beneath the multicolored surface lies the land's history, including the remains of ancient horses, camels, tigers, and rhinos. The barren landscape, dotted with pinnacles and prairies, was formed by two geological processes: deposition, where the layered rocks were gradually stacked up on top of each other by inland seas, winds, and rivers over millions of years, and erosion, which began about 500,000 years ago. The Red Shirt Table, at 3,340 feet, is the highest point in the park, which was established on this day in 1978. It protects 379 square miles of rocky buttes, pinnacles, and prairies. This inhospitable terrain was called 'Mako Sica,' or 'land bad' by the Oglala Lakota people, who have lived here for hundreds of years. Still thirsty for knowledge? Visit the national park's museum collection. There are over 360,000 objects that have a lot more to reveal!

bing-45118.jpg.title: Traditional chinese fishing nets in Kochi, India at sunrise.
bing-45118.jpg.headline: Tools waiting for their harvest. Chinese fishing nets in Kochi, India
bing-45118.jpg.description:
As a traditional occupation in India, fishing is woven deeply into the country's cultural and economic fabric. This is vividly exemplified in Kochi, a bustling coastal city in the southern state of Kerala. Known as the 'Queen of the Arabian Sea', its maritime heritage continues to be important for the residents.

At the heart of this tradition are the Chinese fishing nets, locally referred to as 'Cheena vala.' These are meticulously crafted nets, framed by colossal wooden beams that extend over the water, counterbalanced by large stones suspended from ropes. As visitors wander along the coastline, these Chinese fishing nets, offer a glimpse into its history and act an essential stop for anyone seeking to explore this coastal gem.

bing-45119.jpg.title: Pueblo de Sotres en los Picos de Europa, Asturias, España
bing-45119.jpg.headline: ¡Un lugar encantador!. Pueblo de Sotres en los Picos de Europa, Asturias, España
bing-45119.jpg.description:
Sotres, un paraíso en los Picos de Europa, se alza majestuosamente a 1050 metros de altitud, desafiando el cielo asturiano. Esta pequeña aldea conserva la parroquia más alta del concejo y aunque ciertamente parece un lugar bastante hostil y de vida pastoril, actualmente es una pequeña urbe de ganaderos, aventureros y empresarios.

Este paraíso asturiano ofrece unas espectaculares vistas de los Picos de Europa cuando la niebla se disipa y sin duda, una gran oferta gastronómica gracias a su materia prima y elaboración propia del queso de Cabrales, dado que es madurado en cuevas naturales de este encantador lugar.

Si tienes ganas de vivir aventuras, cruzarte con rebaños de cabras y ovejas por tu camino y recorrer senderos verdes, ¡este es tu sitio!

bing-45122.jpg.title: Drapeau français sous l’Arc de Triomphe, Paris, France
bing-45122.jpg.headline: Se souvenir et ne jamais oublier. Armistice de la Première Guerre Mondiale
bing-45122.jpg.description: Le 11 novembre est une date significative dans l'histoire de la France, car elle commémore la fin de la Première Guerre mondiale. Cette guerre a pris fin le 11 novembre 1918 à 11 heures, marquant ainsi l'armistice entre les Alliés et l'Allemagne. Ce conflit a entraîné d'énormes pertes humaines et d’importants bouleversements dans le monde. L'Arc de Triomphe à Paris, ce monument symbolique, est profondément lié à cette date historique. En effet, sous cette imposante structure, le président français allume chaque année la flamme éternelle du soldat inconnu pour honorer les soldats qui ont fait le sacrifice ultime pendant la guerre. En outre, une cérémonie officielle se déroule pour rendre hommage aux victimes de la guerre et rappeler combien la paix est précieuse.

bing-45123.jpg.title: Val di Funes, South Tyrol, Italy
bing-45123.jpg.headline: Small town life, elevated. Val di Funes, Italy
bing-45123.jpg.description: You are in luck if you are looking for a peaceful escape from everyday life in an enchanted valley. Today’s image features Val di Funes in the Dolomites, Italy. Running from the Isarco Valley to the heart of Puez-Odle Natural Park, the valley offers a spectacular view of the surrounding mountains. With a large selection of hiking paths, such as the Adolf Munkel Trail, it is also an ideal destination for hikers. In addition, Val di Funes is rich in cultural heritage. Several historic churches have been built here, including the Santa Maddalena Church, a true treasure from the 14th century. Every year, the municipality organises a peculiar festival known as the 'cattle parade.' On this occasion, cows are taken through the streets of the village, adorned with flowers and ribbons. So, if you manage to come by during this event, don't forget to take a picture with the happiest bovines in the country!

bing-45125.jpg.title: Autumnal woodland and Young Peak, British Columbia, Canada
bing-45125.jpg.headline: Forever Young. Young Peak, British Columbia
bing-45125.jpg.description: Nestled in the heart of British Columbia, Young Peak is nature's timeless masterpiece. The snowy crest glistens like diamond in the sunlight, rising to an elevation of over 2,815 metres. The Young Peak was named after Julia M. Young, the former Glacier House manager, who served in the position between 1899 and 1920. If you're as daring as Charles Ernest Fay and Redt F. Curtis—the first climbers to reach the crest— you will be rewarded with awe-inspiring panoramic views. In winter, the peak transforms, inviting skiers and snowboarders to carve their marks into the pristine, powdery slopes. So, what are you waiting for? Grab your gear and set off on an adventure to explore Young Peak.

bing-45126.jpg.title: Sunset at the Washington Monument, Washington, DC
bing-45126.jpg.headline: A salute to veterans. Veterans Day
bing-45126.jpg.description: Today we're at the Washington Monument to pay tribute to those who have served in the US Armed Forces. Over 41 million Americans have been in our military since the US Army was established in 1775, and today, on Veterans Day, we salute their service. Veterans Day started as Armistice Day, a commemoration of the end of combat in World War 1. In 1954, it was renamed Veterans Day, expanding its scope to honor all people who have served. Over 6% of Americans, more than 16 million people, are veterans. Their service will be recognised today at the Veterans Day National Ceremony at Arlington National Cemetery, and in parades and other events across the country.

bing-45138.jpg.title: Lamps on the banks of the Sarayu River for Diwali, Ayodhya, India
bing-45138.jpg.headline: A dazzling display for Diwali. Diwali
bing-45138.jpg.description: Diwali, the five-day festival of lights, holds significance in Hinduism, Jainism, and Sikhism. It is celebrated widely both in India, and in countries across the world with an Indian diaspora. The name 'Diwali' comes from the Sanskrit term 'Dipavali,' which means 'row of lights,' and the heart of the festival lies in the oil lamps, or 'diyas,' which illuminate homes and public spaces. They create a dazzling spectacle symbolizing the triumph of knowledge over ignorance and good over evil. The city of Ayodhya in Uttar Pradesh, India, pictured in today's image, hosts one of the world's largest displays of oil lamps. Hundreds of thousands of diyas are lit on the banks of the Sarayu River during Diwali.

bing-45139.jpg.title: Two mallard ducks on a pond in autumn
bing-45139.jpg.headline: Mallard ducks
bing-45139.jpg.description: The mallard, also known as the wild duck, is one of the most widespread duck species in the world. With their striking plumage, mallards are easy to recognise. Male mallard ducks, called drakes, are distinguished by their colourful wings and distinctive green head. Female ducks, on the other hand, are an inconspicuous brown. Mallards are versatile birds found in urban parks, lakes and rivers alike. They feed on plants, insects and small fish. Their adaptability and colourful appearance make them a fascinating bird species.

bing-45150.jpg.title: Old olive grove in the Serra Tramuntana range, Majorca, Spain
bing-45150.jpg.headline: From the tree to the table. Serra de Tramuntana, Majorca, Spain
bing-45150.jpg.description:
They've been growing olives on the Spanish island of Majorca in the western Mediterranean for more than 2,000 years. Early settlers, the Phoenicians and Greeks, introduced the first olive trees but the groves in the Serra de Tramuntana range expanded during Spain's Islamic era, between 709 and 1492. Olive oil became a crucial ingredient in culinary traditions on Majorca, the largest of the Balearic Islands. One ancient tree on the island, Can Det, is estimated to be more than 1,100 years old, and is still producing olives.

In 2011, the Serra de Tramuntana was established as a UNESCO World Heritage Site. Today, tourists from all over the world visit the archipelago to taste history and the 'liquid gold.'

bing-45162.jpg.title: Russell lupines along Lake Tekapo, South Island, New Zealand
bing-45162.jpg.headline: A beautiful nuisance. Russell lupines, Lake Tekapo, New Zealand
bing-45162.jpg.description: Welcome to Lake Tekapo, on New Zealand's South Island, where the colorful spikes of flowering Russell lupines transform the landscape each November and December. The plants' blooming heads, made up of clusters of pea-like flowers, can reach up to 60 inches. While photographers flock here to capture the varied hues of purple, blue, and yellow, these striking plants are controversial. Native to North America, they are considered an invasive species here, growing in dense stands and boxing out other flora. While these plants might be appealing to tourists, they can create a negative imbalance in the region's ecosystem.

bing-45174.jpg.title: Rapa Valley in Sarek National Park, Sweden
bing-45174.jpg.headline: Imagine the echo!. Rapa Valley in Sarek National Park, Sweden
bing-45174.jpg.description: Rapa Valley runs through Sarek National Park in northern Sweden, where rivers cut into lush meadows and towering peaks reach towards the sky. In this national park, covering about 760 square miles of pristine wilderness, elk roam freely, golden eagles soar overhead, and the elusive arctic fox leaves traces of its presence in the snow. From the beauty of Abisko to the rugged peaks of Sarek, Sweden's many national parks boast a range of landscapes from glaciers to lush green forests and sandy beaches. The Sámi people have called this alpine region home since ancient times, and their cultural heritage is intertwined with the landscape. They fish the coasts, and perhaps most famously, herd reindeer.

bing-45179.jpg.title: Platja des Coll Baix en Mallorca, Islas Baleares, España
bing-45179.jpg.headline: ¡Un sinfín de actividades!. Platja des Coll Baix en Mallorca, Islas Baleares, España
bing-45179.jpg.description:
Mallorca es la isla más grande de las Islas Baleares y aunque es famosa por sus espectaculares playas paradisiacas de aguas cristalinas, calas secretas y su innumerable oferta de actividades, también dispone de un interior dominado por colinas, montañas y campos verdes.

De hecho, a poco más de 30 kilómetros de esta espectacular cala que vemos en la imagen de hoy, podemos visitar el pueblo Inca, el cual celebra hoy su feria más popular de la Isla, “Dijous Bo”.

Esta feria se ha convertido en el mercado payés más grande de Mallorca, ofreciendo una variedad de actividades, como explorar las tradiciones mallorquinas y degustar delicias gastronómicas. Si estás por Mallorca, pasea por este colorido mercadillo, empápate del ambiente festivo y disfruta de los aromas de pan recién horneado, quesos caseros, sobrasadas y ensaimadas.

bing-45182.jpg.title: Moulin à vent dans les vignes, France
bing-45182.jpg.headline: Il est arrivé !. Fête du Beaujolais Nouveau
bing-45182.jpg.description: La Fête du Beaujolais Nouveau est arrivée ! Cette tradition viticole, vieille de plus de 70 ans, est un rendez-vous immanquable pour les amateurs de vin du monde entier. L'histoire derrière cette célébration remonte à 1951 lorsque les vignerons du Beaujolais, désireux de partager leurs créations plus tôt, ont obtenu l'autorisation de vendre immédiatement leur production le 13 novembre de cette année. C'est ainsi que le Beaujolais Nouveau a vu le jour, et depuis, le troisième jeudi de novembre est devenu une date incontournable pour trinquer à la joie de vivre, à la bonne cuisine et à la camaraderie. Surtout, n'oublions pas de le consommer avec modération. C'est la clé pour savourer pleinement cette journée mémorable !

bing-45185.jpg.title: Festival of Lights, VanDusen Botanical Garden, Vancouver
bing-45185.jpg.headline: The luminous spirit of nature. VanDusen Botanical Garden, Vancouver
bing-45185.jpg.description: In today's image, nature and human creativity's dazzling fusion shows the Festival of Lights—an event organized annually between November and January—in the VanDusen Botanical Garden in Vancouver. The garden is home to 55 acres of land filled with plants from all over the world, including a large collection of plants native to British Columbia. The botanical garden opened its doors in 1975 and was named after a local philanthropist and lumberjack, Whitford Julian VanDusen. In the buzzing city, the peaceful oasis charms visitors with its diverse and colorful flora, water features, sculptures and totem poles. For the bundle-of-energy type of guests, the Elizabethan Maze—created with 2,000 cedar trees—provides entertainment with its clever twists and turns.

bing-45186.jpg.title: View over Athens and the Acropolis, Greece
bing-45186.jpg.headline: The birthplace of Western philosophy. World Philosophy Day
bing-45186.jpg.description: On World Philosophy Day, we're in Athens, the capital of Greece, the birthplace of Western philosophy and democracy. The iconic Acropolis, the ancient citadel that towers over Athens, and its most famous monument, the Parthenon, remind us of the brilliant minds of Socrates, Plato, and Aristotle. Ancient Greek philosophy focused on critical thinking and questioning and started a revolution of rationale that is still shaping our society today. UNESCO recognizes the profound impact philosophy has on human thought, cultures, and individuals on World Philosophy Day. Take time today to discover the depths of the 'love of wisdom'!

bing-45192.jpg.title: Königssee im Herbst, Berchtesgaden, Bayern
bing-45192.jpg.headline: Rote Bäume, klarer See, in meinem Herbst, da sprießen Träume!. Königssee, Berchtesgaden, Bayern
bing-45192.jpg.description:
Eingebettet in die majestätischen Alpen erstrahlt der Königssee im Herbst in den schönsten Farben. Die Wälder rund um den See verwandeln sich in ein leuchtendes Mosaik aus Gold und Rot, während das klare Wasser ruhig und spiegelglatt ruht. Die Stille wird nur vom leisen Rascheln der Blätter und gelegentlichem Vogelgezwitscher unterbrochen. Der Herbst am Königssee ist eine Zeit der Ruhe und lädt ein, die Natur in ihrer ganzen Pracht zu erleben, bevor der Winter Einzug hält. Entspannen Sie sich und lauschen Sie den weisen Worten der Natur wie dem Plätschern des Wassers. Vielleicht ist diese Jahreszeit auch für Sie melancholisch, aber inspirierend?

Der Königssee hat in der Vergangenheit viele Maler*innen inspiriert, denn am Nordufer gibt es einen Aussichtspunkt, den sogenannten Malerwinkel. Berühmte Künstler wie Max Wolfinger, Johann Baptist Isenring und Fritz Richter ließen sich hier zu ihren Werken inspirieren. Ihre Bilder fangen die malerische Kulisse des Sees, die umliegenden Berge und die Farben perfekt ein und tragen zur künstlerischen Aufwertung dieses Naturschauspiels bei.

bing-45195.jpg.title: Meon Hill, Gloucestershire, England
bing-45195.jpg.headline: The rest is mystery. Meon Hill, Gloucestershire
bing-45195.jpg.description: Meon Hill, in Gloucestershire, is a lovely highlight of the Cotswolds. From boasting market gardens to having a deep-rooted connection to the Iron Age, this Area of Outstanding Natural Beauty has more to offer than just breathtaking landscapes. You can see the Cotswold hills, Stratford-upon-Avon (the birthplace and burial place of William Shakespeare) and the Vale of Evesham, all from this one spot. The hill is also said to have served as the inspiration for the location of Weathertop in J.R.R. Tolkien's 'The Lord of the Rings.' Head here to experience a taste of Middle-earth in the heart of England.

bing-45198.jpg.title: Bad River in Copper Falls State Park, Wisconsin
bing-45198.jpg.headline: Time to lace up those boots. National Take a Hike Day
bing-45198.jpg.description: Take a hike, buddy! No, not the 'get out of here' version but the 'get out there' version. It's time to lace up those boots and take advantage of our national trails, which span over 91,000 miles. Back in the 1960s, President Lyndon B. Johnson signed the National Trails System Act into law, to preserve, promote, and develop scenic and historic trails across the country. Can't decide where to start? Our homepage image offers up one option which is awash with fall colors—Copper Falls State Park in Wisconsin. With 17 miles of trails along the Bad River, past waterfalls and ancient lava flows, this park has a lot to offer. Whether it's a rugged mountain path, a serene forest walk, or an oceanside stroll, this country has a trail waiting for you. But remember to respect nature, follow 'leave no trace' principles, and take nothing but photographs. Happy hiking!

bing-45210.jpg.title: Polar bear mother and cubs, Churchill, Manitoba, Canada
bing-45210.jpg.headline: Awaiting the big freeze. Polar bear season in Manitoba
bing-45210.jpg.description: On the shore of Hudson Bay, the Canadian town of Churchill, Manitoba, is remote, but the sights are worth the journey. From beluga whales and northern lights to the shipwreck of the SS Ithaka and the Sea Walls murals, there are many surprises here. Moreover, it is also known as the 'polar bear capital of the world,' thanks to its seasonal visitors. From October to November, these white giants pass through, waiting for Hudson Bay to freeze over so they can head out to hunt seals. Tourists can safely watch polar bears from the comfort of custom-built vehicles and a so-called 'polar bear jail' helps to manage bear-human interactions. Are you ready for a wild adventure that'll send chills down your spine, but in a good way?

bing-45220.jpg.title: Bandeira brasileira voando sob o céu azul
bing-45220.jpg.headline: Amada terra do Brasil
bing-45220.jpg.description: O Dia da Bandeira, celebrado no Brasil em 19 de novembro, é uma ocasião especial que enche os corações dos brasileiros de patriotismo e orgulho nacional. Nesta data, lembramos a importância do nosso símbolo nacional, a bandeira verde e amarela, que representa a nossa história, cultura e a diversidade de nosso povo. A bandeira é um reflexo do amor e da união que temos pelo nosso país, e é uma oportunidade para reafirmarmos nosso compromisso com os valores e ideais que ela representa. Em todo o Brasil, escolas, instituições e cidadãos se reúnem para celebrar esse dia, prestando homenagem à nossa bandeira e renovando o compromisso de construir um futuro melhor para todos os brasileiros. Viva o Dia da Bandeira!

bing-45222.jpg.title: Alam-Pedja Nature Reserve, Estonia
bing-45222.jpg.headline: Tread carefully!. Alam-Pedja Nature Reserve, Estonia
bing-45222.jpg.description: Among Estonia's stunning natural sites is the Alam-Pedja Nature Reserve, covering 132 square miles of wilderness in the heart of the country. This occasionally ice-covered, vast area of wetlands, forests, and rivers is the largest natural reserve in Estonia. From the majestic white-tailed eagle to the elusive black stork, more than 200 bird species can be found here. The landscape is a tapestry of aquatic forests: still water, bog, and floodplain forests. Winding trails and boardwalks invite explorers to craft their own adventures.

bing-45234.jpg.title: Chapman Adventure Playground in the Gathering Place, Tulsa, Oklahoma
bing-45234.jpg.headline: Every day is a play day!. World Children's Day
bing-45234.jpg.description:
Children are the future and ensuring their well-being is fundamental to a thriving society. World Children's Day marks the day in 1989 that the UN General Assembly adopted the Convention on the Rights of the Child, an international treaty setting out children's rights all over the world.

To mark the day, we are at the Gathering Place in Tulsa, Oklahoma, where inventive playgrounds sit side-by-side with green spaces and scenic trails. Play is an important part of childhood and the park's adventure playground is designed to appeal to children at different stages of development, and with different physical abilities. With its creative tunnels, towering treehouses, twisted slides, play gardens, and water areas, children can explore, learn, and let their imaginations soar.

bing-45241.jpg.title: Pino Loricato sul Monte Pollino, Potenza
bing-45241.jpg.headline: Si chiama Pino... ma non è tuo cugino!
bing-45241.jpg.description:
Dall'alto dei suoi 2.248 metri si erge maestosamente al confine tra due regioni del Sud Italia, Basilicata e Calabria a ridosso delle due province adiacenti di Potenza e Cosenza. Le vette sfidano i coraggiosi escursionisti a salire sempre più in alto, ammaliando gli sguardi di turisti e naturalisti, con una lussureggiante flora fatta di una molteplicità di piante, molte delle quali tipiche solo di questi territori. Il territorio che oggi ospita l'omonimo Parco Nazionale del Pollino, in un periodo molto lontano nel tempo, tra 110.000 anni fa e terminato all'incirca 11700 anni, ospitò enormi ghiacciai che oggi lasciano il posto a questi meravigliosi esemplari di pino loricato. Il pino, così come il carattere dei calabresi e dei lucani, ha la capacità di resistere in maniera quasi stoica alle avversità di questi territori, in cui si alternano giornate soleggiate e calde che lasciano poi spazio alle freddi notti caratterizzate da temperature sotto lo zero.

Questo è possibile grazie alla loro "scorza", ovvero alla corteccia di cui sono fatti che è resistente alle intemperie così come l'animo di chi abita questo territorio: panorami mozzafiato con vallate incastonate tra i monti, che diradando verso le zone pianeggianti, lasciano intravedere le bellezze delle coste del mare calabrese.

bing-45246.jpg.title: Gray seal pup, Norfolk, England
bing-45246.jpg.headline: Welcome to the world, pup!. Gray seal pup, Norfolk, England
bing-45246.jpg.description: Here in Norfolk, on the east coast of England, a seasonal wildlife spectacle is underway. Between early November and January, thousands of gray seal pups are born on the shoreline, a little earlier than those on US coasts. The seal moms feed their pups on the beach for three weeks, during which time the pups gain about 4.5 pounds a day. They stay on the beach until they shed their pale fur to make way for a waterproof, mottled gray coat. Then it's time to head to the sea and learn to hunt for themselves.

bing-45253.jpg.title: Val di Non, Trentino-Alto Adige
bing-45253.jpg.headline: Una delizia sotto ogni aspetto!
bing-45253.jpg.description:
Indossate gli stivali da escursionista e copritevi bene, la Val di Non ci aspetta!  Attorniata dalle maestose montagne del Trentino, la valle è stata resa celebre per i suoi leggendari meli che, grazie ai loro fiori biancorosa uniti alle montagne innevate all’orizzonte, conferiscono al paesaggio uno scenario splendido da immortalare per i fotografi e I pittori dilettanti. Inoltre, l’incredibile quantità di castelli qui presenti, in parte di proprietà privata, garantiscono al Trentino il primato di regione con il maggior numero di fortezze dello Stato.

La Val di Non è una destinazione ideale per i buongustai che vogliono godere della tradizionale cucina italiana d’alta quota. La regione offre tipici piatti caserecci preparati con prodotti freschi a chilometro zero. Tra le svariate prelibatezze possiamo trovare I ravioli a base di erbe e formaggi freschi, mortadella, speck, il lardo e la famosa ciuiga. Anche gli amanti dello sport troveranno qui pane per I propri denti. I turisti possono infatti cimentarsi nel kayak attraverso gli stretti canyon, l'escursionismo e lo sci. Per poi rilassarsi a fine giornata nei centri termali.

In nuce, la Val di Non è una gemma nascosta ed una tappa obbligata nel Nord Italia ed una destinazione perfetta per chi vuole sperimentare la bellezza della campagna italiana al di fuori dalle tappe abituali.

bing-45256.jpg.title: Plantas Pepalantus  Parque Nacional da Chapada dos Veadeiros, Goias, Brasil
bing-45256.jpg.headline: Mortas, porém vivas?
bing-45256.jpg.description:
O Parque Nacional da Chapada dos Veadeiros, localizado no estado de Goiás, é um tesouro natural do Brasil. Este parque abriga paisagens deslumbrantes, incluindo cânions, cachoeiras e formações rochosas únicas, que atraem amantes da natureza e aventureiros de todo o mundo. Além de sua beleza cênica, a Chapada dos Veadeiros é conhecida por sua rica biodiversidade, abrigando várias espécies de fauna e flora. Os visitantes podem explorar trilhas que levam a locais como o Vale da Lua, as corredeiras do Rio São Miguel e a imponente Cachoeira do Segredo. Este parque oferece uma oportunidade única de conexão com a natureza e é um destino imperdível para quem deseja desfrutar da beleza intocada do Brasil.

No Parque Nacional da Chapada dos Veadeiros, os visitantes também têm a chance de conhecer as sempre-vivas, plantas nativas que se destacam por suas flores exóticas e resistência em ambientes áridos. As sempre-vivas são parte integrante do ecossistema da Chapada dos Veadeiros e representam a diversidade da flora brasileira. Ao visitar o parque, os amantes da natureza podem admirar essas plantas fascinantes e aprender sobre sua importância na preservação desse ecossistema único.

bing-45258.jpg.title: Grand Teton National Park, Wyoming
bing-45258.jpg.headline: The quiet beauty of Grand Teton. Grand Teton National Park, Wyoming
bing-45258.jpg.description: Today's image gives us a glimpse of beautiful Grand Teton National Park, in our least populous state, Wyoming. The park, established in 1929, encompasses lakes, the Snake River, and the Teton Range, famed for its series of sharp, jagged peaks. Bring your binoculars with you, and if it's summertime, be on the lookout for pronghorn, which travel about 150 miles to get there from Wyoming's Upper Green River Basin. They aren't the only creatures to visit seasonally; elk and bison are also summer visitors. These migrations play a vital role in the ecosystem of Grand Teton National Park. The animals help disperse seeds and are also food for predators.

bing-45262.jpg.title: Beautiful foggy winter sunrise at Victoria Memorial, Kolkata, India.
bing-45262.jpg.headline: Memories in the mist. Victoria Memorial, Kolkata, India
bing-45262.jpg.description: Kolkata's Victoria Memorial is a symbol of the city's rich heritage. Designed by Sir William Emerson and built in the honour of Queen Victoria, it is housed amidst many gardens on the premises of the memorial. The building is much more than just a repository of history, it is a cultural centre, with galleries housing an extensive collection of paintings, manuscripts and artefacts. A perfect example of Indo-Saracenic architecture, it hosts an elegant white marble façade, adorned with delicate sculptures and a soaring central dome. Its fusion of British, Mughal, Venetian, Egyptian and Deccan influences, constructed with white Makrana marble.

bing-45266.jpg.title: Flamants roses au lever du soleil, Saintes-Maries-de-la-Mer, Parc Naturel Régional de Camargue, France
bing-45266.jpg.headline: Les divas de la Camargue. Flamants roses de Camargue
bing-45266.jpg.description:
Découvrez la magie des flamants roses dans le Parc Naturel Régional de Camargue, le seul endroit en France où ils évoluent en liberté toute l'année. Novembre est particulièrement extraordinaire, marquant la saison des amours de ces oiseaux emblématiques. Vous assisterez à des danses nuptiales inoubliables.

Leur couleur rose vibrante provient d'un régime alimentaire unique, riche en caroténoïdes provenant des eaux des étangs et des marais camarguais. Leur plumage en bénéficie, les parant de cette teinte éclatante.

Ces oiseaux gracieux sont de véritables artistes aquatiques, glissant élégamment sur les eaux peu profondes pour se nourrir. Leurs longues pattes fines et leur cou élancé les rendent parfaits pour la pêche. Alors, ne manquez pas l'opportunité de découvrir ces divas des marais, la Camargue vous réserve une expérience mémorable au cœur de la nature !

bing-45267.jpg.title: Teide National Park, Tenerife, Canary Islands, Spain
bing-45267.jpg.headline: Summits in the sea. Teide National Park, Tenerife, Canary Islands, Spain
bing-45267.jpg.description: Unique rock formations, lunar-like terrains and spectacular skies – welcome to Teide National Park! Nestled in Tenerife, Spain, this World Heritage Site is home to Mount Teide—the third-largest volcano in the world. At 3,715 metres above sea level and 7,500 metres from the ocean floor, it is the highest peak in Spain. This diverse location has served as the backdrop for several notable films like 'Fast & Furious 6' and 'Clash of the Titans.' Moreover, it houses the Teide Observatory, one of the world's best sites for astronomical observations, owing to its high altitude and low light pollution. Whether you're into hiking, stargazing or simply photography, this park deserves a spot on your travel bucket list.

bing-45270.jpg.title: Flint corn
bing-45270.jpg.headline: Happy Thanksgiving!
bing-45270.jpg.description: While people gather across the country for feasts of turkey, mashed potatoes, and stuffing, you may wonder about the origins of Thanksgiving. Early English settlers had plenty to be thankful for, whether surviving the long voyage to America or the first harsh winters. Written records tell of an early thanksgiving shared between Plymouth Pilgrims and Wampanoag Native Americans, who provided a harvest of corn, deer, and turkey. There were many early days of thanksgiving, but an official, national celebration was proclaimed by George Washington in 1789, and has been a part of our holiday season ever since. Today, we wish you good company and plenty of things to be thankful for. Happy Thanksgiving!

bing-45275.jpg.title: Lago de Puigcerdá, Gerona, Cataluña, España
bing-45275.jpg.headline: ¡Preserva este espejo natural!. Lago de Puigcerdá, Gerona, Cataluña, España
bing-45275.jpg.description:
Ubicado en los majestuosos Pirineos, este encantador lago es en realidad un estanque artificial creado en el siglo XIII y que solo ocupa poco más de dos hectáreas. El Lago de Puigcerdá ha sido meticulosamente cuidado a lo largo de los siglos, y gracias a ello podemos admirar hoy su espectacular belleza. Por eso, queremos aprovechar la Semana Europea de la Reducción de Residuos para reconocer su valor y fomentar la concienciación sobre las conocidas 3R: reducción del consumo, reutilización de productos, y el reciclaje de residuos.

Con la llegada del "Black Friday" o “Viernes Negro”, también es crucial recordar la relevancia de preservar nuestros paisajes y prolongar la vida útil de los productos, para que no terminen afectando a estos impresionantes entornos naturales.

Si decides realizar una excursión por estos lugares de cuento, ¡te sumergirás en un mundo de maravillas naturales que te dejarán boquiabierto!

bing-45282.jpg.title: Hall of Mosses trail in the Hoh Rain Forest, Olympic National Park, Washington
bing-45282.jpg.headline: A different kind of rainforest. Hoh Rain Forest, Olympic National Park, Washington
bing-45282.jpg.description:
Imagine spending the day hiking amid these moss-covered trees instead of frantically checking items off your holiday shopping list. Welcome to Green Friday, the environmental alternative to Black Friday. The aim is to encourage people to make ethical shopping choices—or to refrain from shopping altogether and embrace nature instead.

A good place to start is the Hall of Mosses at Olympic National Park, in Washington's Hoh Rain Forest. This fantastical landscape is a temperate rainforest with an enchanting loop trail through mosses gracefully draped over majestic spruces and hemlocks. Bring a jacket though; this forest is the wettest in the contiguous United States with an annual rainfall of nearly 130 inches. No wonder it's so green!

bing-45293.jpg.title: Mount Logan in Kluane National Park and Reserve, Yukon, Canada
bing-45293.jpg.headline: Kluane's untamed beauty. Kluane National Park and Reserve, Yukon
bing-45293.jpg.description: Kluane National Park and Reserve of the Yukon beckons adventurers with its untamed beauty and plentiful peaks. Its story began millions of years ago when Mighty glaciers sculpted its landscape millions of years ago, and the federal government established Kluane National Park and Reserve in 1976. The park's most precious jewel is Canada's highest peak, Mount Logan, a towering sentinel that challenges climbers. The history of this UNESCO World Heritage Site intertwines with the culture of the Champagne and Aishihik First Nations, who have called this area home for centuries. Visitors who venture here can embark on a journey through ancient forests, navigate crystal-clear lakes, and witness the grandeur of glaciers.

bing-45294.jpg.title: Toledo, Spain
bing-45294.jpg.headline: Toledo's timeless tale. Toledo, Spain
bing-45294.jpg.description: Built on a hill and surrounded on three sides by the Tagus River, the Spanish city of Toledo is a UNESCO World Heritage Site packed with history. Its towering Alcázar fortress and impressive Gothic cathedral dominate the skyline, but the city is also home to mosques and synagogues. Toledo bears strong cultural influences from the Moors, who ruled here for centuries, following their arrival in Spain in 711. It was known as the City of the Three Cultures during the Middle Ages, when its Christian, Muslim, and Jewish communities coexisted harmoniously. Toledo has been the home of sword making since Roman times and is also famous for its marzipan. In the 16th century, the city was home to the famous painter El Greco, who was inspired to create some of his greatest masterpieces here.

bing-45306.jpg.title: Fallow deer in Bradgate Park, Leicestershire, England
bing-45306.jpg.headline: Who stepped on a twig?. Fallow deer, Bradgate Park, Leicestershire, England
bing-45306.jpg.description: This doe and fawn are fallow deer, known for their striking chestnut brown coats with white spots, which typically darken to gray in the winter. Fallow deer are native to Europe and parts of Asia and are a common sight in England, where they were introduced by the Normans in the 11th century. During the autumn rutting season, mothers stay close to their young while the males, which have broad palmate antlers, spar to establish their dominance. Our homepage doe and fawn are pictured in 850-acre Bradgate Park in Leicestershire, a medieval deer park set within woodlands and a beautiful landscape in England's East Midlands region.

bing-45312.jpg.title: Weihnachtsmarkt in Frankfurt am Main, Hessen
bing-45312.jpg.headline: Oh du gelobte Weihnachtsstimmung!. Weihnachtsmarkt in Frankfurt am Main, Hessen
bing-45312.jpg.description:
Endlich ist es wieder so weit, die Weihnachtszeit steht vor der Tür und mit ihr der Frankfurter Weihnachtsmarkt! Wussten Sie, dass er bereits 1393 urkundlich erwähnt wurde? Im Laufe der Geschichte hat sich der Markt dann etwa ab dem 19. Jahrhundert zu dem entwickelt, was er heute ist, und gehört außerdem zu den größten Weihnachtsmärkten Deutschlands.

Traditionell findet er vor dem historischen Römer, dem Frankfurter Rathaus, statt. Der Autor Heinrich Hoffmann, der den Struwwelpeter erfunden hat, schrieb auch das Weihnachtsmärchen „König Nussknacker und der arme Reinhold“. Warum erzählen wir das? Weil auf der Erstausgabe des Buches der Frankfurter Weihnachtsmarkt vom Autor gemalt wurde und der Nussknacker auf diesem Markt eine wichtige Rolle spielt.

Das vielleicht wichtigste Symbol des Marktes ist jedoch der Weihnachtsbaum. Er ist seit dem 19. Jahrhundert nicht mehr wegzudenken. Wussten Sie, dass dieser Markt lange Zeit eine reine Frankfurter Angelegenheit war? Zum Glück hat sich das geändert. Heute können wir alle diesen unglaublichen Moment zwischen einem Quetschemännche, heißem Apfelwein und den beleuchteten Ständen die magische Weihnachtsatmosphäre genießen.

bing-45318.jpg.title: Río Negro, Amazon basin, Brazil
bing-45318.jpg.headline: Mirror, mirror, on the water. Río Negro, Amazon basin, Brazil
bing-45318.jpg.description: From its source in Colombia, the Río Negro flows about 1,400 miles to become one of the largest tributaries of the Amazon River at the Meeting of Waters in Manaus, Brazil. It is also the largest blackwater river in the world, its water stained by decomposing organic matter that seeps in from swamps. These slow-moving, dark waters beautifully reflect the colors of the sky, including the rainbows which form over the Amazon basin, as seen here. The river also plays a crucial role in the ecosystem, as the home of many plants and animals, including the critically endangered Brazilian barefaced tamarin, the giant river otter, and nearly 700 species of fish.

bing-45322.jpg.title: Lush green landscape of Varandha Ghat,Bhor,Maharashtra, India.
bing-45322.jpg.headline: Over the clouds. Varandha Ghat,Bhor,Maharashtra, India
bing-45322.jpg.description: Maharashtra, a state known for its bustling cities, is also home to some of India's natural treasures. Though they can be overshadowed by the state's urban centres, these sites hold a unique charm and offer a different facet of Maharashtra's beauty. Varandha Ghat, in the Bhor region of Maharashtra, 108 kilometres from Pune, is a part of the Sahyadri mountain range and covers an expanse of 10 kilometres, and offers a mesmerising view of rolling hills, lush green valleys and cascading waterfalls. It is a serene escape that invites nature enthusiasts and adventure seekers alike.

bing-45330.jpg.title: Giant land art fresco by artist Saype in Istanbul, Türkiye
bing-45330.jpg.headline: A day to lend a hand. Giving Tuesday
bing-45330.jpg.description: As we get caught up in the hustle and bustle of gift shopping and festive decorations, it's good to remember the true spirit of times like these: generosity and kindness. That's where Giving Tuesday comes in. This annual holiday on the first Tuesday after Thanksgiving was created by the United Nations Foundation and New York's 92nd Street Y—a cultural organization and community center—in 2012. Their vision was to make a difference by providing joy to everyone through acts of charity. Generosity is something we can all practice, whether by volunteering at a non-profit organization, shelter or food bank, donating to a charity, or simply giving a voice to people in need in your community. So, let's jump on board with the millions of kind souls, shake hands, and share warm wishes far and wide!

bing-45331.jpg.title: Mount Assiniboine Provincial Park, Canada
bing-45331.jpg.headline: Mount Assiniboine Provincial Park, Canada
bing-45331.jpg.description: Nestled in the pristine wilderness of British Columbia, Mount Assiniboine and its surrounding provincial park form a captivating alpine wonderland. Also known as the 'Matterhorn of the Rockies', this majestic peak rises to 3,618 metres, commanding attention with its rugged grandeur. The name Assiniboine pays homage to the Indigenous Assiniboine people who once resided here. Mount Assiniboine Provincial Park, a protected expanse spanning over 39,000 hectares, fosters wildlife including grizzlies, cougars and mountain goats. A network of trails weaves through this terrain, providing opportunities for hiking, skiing and camping. Sheltered by the mountains, this park embodies the essence of untamed beauty in the heart of the Canadian Rockies.

bing-45342.jpg.title: Rockefeller Center Christmas tree, New York City
bing-45342.jpg.headline: Rockefeller 'round the Christmas tree. Rockefeller Center Christmas tree lighting
bing-45342.jpg.description: As December approaches, New York gears up for a sparkling spectacle. On November 29, the Rockefeller Center Tree Lighting will bring you festive vibes. The roots of this holiday tradition go back to 1931, when builders put up a balsam fir to show gratitude for their jobs amid the bleakness of the Great Depression. That tree was decorated with paper garlands and tin cans and in 1933 the first tree-lighting ceremony took place. Today, this towering Norway spruce is adorned with over 50,000 multicolored LED lights and topped with a Swarovski crystal star. The illumination of the 80-foot tree is a full-blown extravaganza with musical performances and celebrity sightings. Its mesmerizing glow marks the official arrival of the holiday season in the city that never sleeps, and you don't want to miss it!

bing-45343.jpg.title: Schwerin Castle on Lake Schwerin, Mecklenburg-Vorpommern, Germany
bing-45343.jpg.headline: Schwerin Castle on Lake Schwerin, Germany
bing-45343.jpg.description: The Schwerin Castle, standing on an island in Lake Schwerin in Germany, looks like a floating mansion from a fairy tale. But did you know that there were traces of a fortress on the lake as early as 941 CE?  The former structure was built by the West Slavic Obodrite tribe, who inhabited what is today's Mecklenburg-Western Pomerania and Poland, particularly on the southern shores of the Baltic Sea. Later, in the 16th century, Duke Johann Albrecht I expanded it into a magnificent Renaissance residence. Finally, in the 19th century, the castle was rebuilt into what we see today. The architect Georg Adolf Demmler redesigned the building in the romantic neo-Gothic style. For centuries, the castle was the residence of the Grand Dukes of Mecklenburg-Schwerin and then became a center for art and culture with an impressive art collection. Today, you can visit the Mecklenburg State Museum and admire this magnificent castle from the inside.

bing-45350.jpg.title: Cyprès chauves à l'étang de Boulieu, Isère, France
bing-45350.jpg.headline: Reflets d’automne. Cyprès chauves de l'étang de Boulieu, Isère
bing-45350.jpg.description:
L'automne à l'étang de Boulieu, c'est un festival de couleurs et de magie ! Les cyprès chauves qui entourent cet étang se parent de teintes chatoyantes, du vert à l'or, créant un tableau d'une beauté envoûtante. Quand le soleil s'y reflète, c'est une véritable œuvre d'art naturelle qui se dessine.

Ces conifères sont d'une résistance impressionnante au vent, et ils adorent les endroits humides. Ils jouent un rôle essentiel en tant que fixateurs de berges, contribuant à la stabilité de l'écosystème environnant. Leur nom "chauve" provient du fait qu'ils perdent leur feuillage en hiver. Saviez-vous qu'ils peuvent vivre jusqu'à 1.000 ans dans leur habitat naturel ? Une véritable leçon de longévité offerte par la nature elle-même !

bing-45351.jpg.title: Leadenhall Market, London
bing-45351.jpg.headline: Where the wares and goods are great. Leadenhall Market, London
bing-45351.jpg.description: With its Victorian architecture, interior details and cobbled floors, London's Leadenhall Market offers a blend of history, shopping, dining, and more. Interestingly, Leadenhall Market was the filming location for Harry Potter's Leaky Cauldron pub, but its most magical resident might have been a Victorian goose named Old Tom. According to legend, this wily bird managed to avoid the butcher shop and instead lived in the market until 1835 and the age of 38. Archaeologists have found evidence that a Roman market existed on this site well before the modern version. The market was also used as a filming location for other films like 'Hereafter,' 'Lara Croft: Tomb Raider' and 'The Imaginarium of Doctor Parnassus.' This beloved landmark is a treasure trove of culture and commerce, so be sure to explore every nook and cranny.

bing-45354.jpg.title: The Storr, a rock outcrop on the Isle of Skye, Scotland
bing-45354.jpg.headline: Happy Saint Andrew's Day. Saint Andrew's Day
bing-45354.jpg.description:
Scotland's fantastical landscapes are steeped in folklore and myths. The Old Man of Storr—a 164-foot rocky pinnacle on the Isle of Skye—is no exception. So named because it is said to resemble a craggy man when viewed from the right angle, it has long inspired tales of giants and magic. The Old Man towers over the Trotternish Ridge, a 20-mile-long landslip that is home to many stunning and strange rock formations, each with their own stories.

It is also a suitably stunning site to toast Saint Andrew, who was named as Scotland's patron saint when the country declared its independence in 1320. The celebration of St. Andrew's Day was popularized by Scottish people in the US who wanted to connect to their roots. However, Scotland is not the only country to celebrate the saint. From Romania to Barbados, many nations celebrate the historic figure, applying their own traditions. Are you celebrating today?

bing-45359.jpg.title: Pradollano, Parque Nacional de Sierra Nevada, Granada, Andalucía, España
bing-45359.jpg.headline: ¡Coge tu tabla o los esquíes, que nos vamos!. Pradollano, Parque Nacional de Sierra Nevada, Granada, Andalucía, España
bing-45359.jpg.description:
Al sur de la península ibérica se encuentra la estación de esquí de Sierra Nevada, en Granada. Esta estación de esquí es una de las más famosas de España y de Europa, ya que cuenta con una extensa área esquiable, pistas para todos los niveles, una gran altitud y una calidad de la nieve espectacular. Pradollano, es la principal área urbana donde se ubica la estación de esquí, la zona hotelera y los comercios.

La apertura de las pistas de esquí en España es el evento invernal más esperado del año, y donde muchas pistas dependen de las condiciones meteorológicas y las bajas temperaturas para su uso. En España contamos con alrededor de 34 estaciones de esquí distribuidas por todo el país, entre las que destacan, además de Sierra Nevada, las que se encuentran en los Pirineos y la Cordillera Cantábrica.

Si estás pensando en vivir una aventura en la nieve, asegúrate de que las condiciones meteorológicas sean las óptimas y no olvides llevarte un buen equipamiento de alta montaña.

bing-45366.jpg.title: Iceberg in the Ross Sea, Antarctica
bing-45366.jpg.headline: Celebrating the coolest place!. Antarctica Day
bing-45366.jpg.description:
The windiest, coldest, and driest continent on Earth—Antarctica—was officially discovered in 1820. In the following decades, several countries organized expeditions to reach and explore the Antarctic ice sheets. The southernmost continent had no indigenous population and various nations claimed ownership. But in 1959, 12 countries signed the Antarctic Treaty, banning military activities and setting Antarctica aside for scientific research. Today, we celebrate the anniversary of this treaty, which now has 56 parties.

From suspended clouds of ice crystals to a subglacial, iron oxide-rich lake that seeps into a blood-red waterfall, this polar desert is full of natural wonders. Its massive ice sheet stores about 70% of the world's fresh water, enough to raise sea levels by more than 200 feet if it were to melt entirely.

bing-45367.jpg.title: Milky Way over Athabasca Glacier in Jasper National Park, Canada
bing-45367.jpg.headline: Jasper National Park, Canada
bing-45367.jpg.description: Witness the awe-inspiring sight of the Milky Way over Athabasca Glacier, amidst the rugged terrain of the Canadian Rockies at Jasper National Park, Canada. The park boasts towering peaks, serene lakes and a diverse range of wildlife. It was established in 1907 and got its name from Jasper Haws, a fur trader. A UNESCO World Heritage Site and the largest dark-sky preserve in the world, Jasper National Park lures stargazers and nature enthusiasts alike. Over the last 100 years, due to global warming, the Athabasca Glacier has been gradually melting and has lost over half of its volume.

bing-45378.jpg.title: North Gate of Angkor Thom, Angkor Archaeological Park, Cambodia
bing-45378.jpg.headline: A city within a city. Angkor, Cambodia
bing-45378.jpg.description: Towering temples, moss-covered ruins, and enchanting forests can all be found in the ancient site of Angkor in Cambodia, once the center of the powerful Khmer Empire. Pictured on our homepage is the North Gate of Angkor Thom, the 'Great City' within Angkor, built in the 12th century. Strolling through Angkor Thom's intricate ruins, gates, and Bayon Temple, with its 216 gigantic smiling stone faces, is like stepping into an adventure movie. Angkor's star attraction, Angkor Wat, is the world's largest religious monument—spread across 402 acres—and a masterpiece of Khmer architecture. It was initially constructed as a Hindu temple before becoming a Buddhist site. So, if you're looking for a blend of history, art, and nature, this UNESCO World Heritage Site guarantees an unforgettable journey into the past.

bing-45379.jpg.title: Gwalior Fort, Madhya Pradesh, India
bing-45379.jpg.headline: Gwalior, Madhya Pradesh, India
bing-45379.jpg.description: Gwalior Fort, one of many in the country, proudly occupies the colossal rocky hill known as Gopachal. Crafted initially from a combination of sandstone and lime mortar, this fort reigns as one of Gwalior's most distinguished landmarks. Its history stretches far back, marked by sieges and conquests by a procession of rulers throughout the ages. The impregnable bastion is a symbol of military might, and harbours a multitude of temples, each bearing the unique imprint of various kings from different eras. Today, the fort's storied past shines through its splendid palaces, temples, gateways and walls. Visitors embark on a journey through time, reliving valorous battles, epic tales and the rise and fall of noble dynasties.

bing-45384.jpg.title: Die Adventszeit beginnt
bing-45384.jpg.headline: Advent, Advent, ein Lichtlein brennt.... Beginn der Adventszeit
bing-45384.jpg.description:
Die Adventszeit, die vierwöchige Vorbereitungszeit auf Weihnachten, hat in vielen Kulturen der Welt eine besondere Bedeutung. Sie beginnt in der Regel am vierten Sonntag vor dem 25. Dezember. In dieser Zeit zünden viele Menschen jeden Sonntag eine Kerze am Adventskranz an, um damit die Vorfreude auf das Weihnachtsfest zu symbolisieren.

Die Adventsbräuche und -traditionen sind von Land zu Land verschieden. Das Öffnen von Adventskalendern, das Singen von Weihnachtsliedern, das Basteln von Weihnachtsschmuck, das Spielen von Gesellschaftsspielen sowie das Genießen von Leckereien, die in dieser besonderen Zeit gebacken und gekocht werden, gehören zur Adventszeit. In manchen Regionen finden auch Adventskonzerte und Weihnachtsmärkte statt.

Besonders in dieser Zeit des Jahres, obwohl es immer so sein sollte, betonen wir die Bedeutung der Nächstenliebe und der Gemeinschaft. Es ist die Zeit der Besinnung, des Teilens und der Vorfreude auf die festliche Weihnachtszeit, wenn Familie und Freunde zusammenkommen und die Werte der Liebe und des Zusammenhalts im Mittelpunkt stehen. Wir wünschen Ihnen allen einen frohen 1. Advent!

bing-45387.jpg.title: Castleton, Derbyshire, England
bing-45387.jpg.headline: Ready, set, cheer!. Advent Sunday
bing-45387.jpg.description: Lit-up houses, the melody of festive hymns in the air and families coming together to illuminate the initial candle on the Advent wreath—Advent Sunday is here to launch the countdown to Christmas! The holiday, which gets its name from the Latin word for arrival, is usually marked with treat-filled calendars. The custom of the Advent wreath originated in 19th-century Germany and gradually spread across Europe, eventually reaching the United Kingdom. Each candle on the wreath signifies a different week of Advent, symbolising hope, peace, joy and love. So, whether your family unites for a special meal today or dedicates the day to transforming your home into a festive wonderland, remember to relish those simple moments.

bing-45390.jpg.title: Sandstone rock formations, Vermilion Cliffs National Monument, Arizona
bing-45390.jpg.headline: Sculpted by time. Vermilion Cliffs National Monument
bing-45390.jpg.description: Vermilion Cliffs National Monument in Arizona features sandstone rock formations, towering hoodoos, and surreal slot canyons. The monument, established in 2000, was named after the vibrant red hues that dominate this sandstone landscape. Once you get a permit to take part in this outdoor excursion, make sure to visit the 'Wave.' It's a stunning geological wonder, with flowing layers of rocks that look like red liquid that has been frozen in time. Other visual treats include Cobra Arch and the White Pocket rock formations, featuring swirling patterns in white, red, and orange.
bing-45390.jpg.copyright: © Yva Momatiuk and John Eastcott/Minden Picture

bing-45402.jpg.title: A mother cheetah and her cubs in the Maasai Mara National Reserve, Kenya
bing-45402.jpg.headline: Masters of agility and cuteness. International Cheetah Day
bing-45402.jpg.description: In the heart of the Maasai Mara National Reserve in Kenya, cheetahs reign as the sprinting champions of the wildlife kingdom. With speeds up to 70 miles per hour, cheetahs thrive on the open savanna, always on alert for signs of prey. While the Maasai Mara is known for its exceptional East African cheetah population, globally the species' survival is threatened by habitat loss and human influence. Today, which is both International Cheetah Day and Wildlife Conservation Day, let's raise awareness about the cheetah's plight. It's a day to appreciate the beauty and importance of not just these wild cats, but all wildlife that shares the world with us.

bing-45403.jpg.title: A mother cheetah and her cubs in the Masai Mara National Reserve, Kenya
bing-45403.jpg.headline: Cheetah and her cubs
bing-45403.jpg.description: In the heart of the Masai Mara National Reserve, where the African savanna stretches as far as the eye can see, cheetahs reign as the sprinting champions of the wildlife kingdom with measured speeds up to 129 kilometres per hour. Cheetahs, with their sleek bodies and black spots, thrive in this vast expanse, alertly watching for signs of prey. The reserve is known for its exceptional East African cheetah population. Sadly, habitat loss and human influence threaten their survival; hence, conservation efforts are crucial to protecting these incredible animals. Let's appreciate the beauty and importance of not just these wild cats, but all wildlife that shares the world with us.

bing-45409.jpg.title: Passo Pordoi, Sellaronda, vista dal Belvedere verso la Marmolada, Italia
bing-45409.jpg.headline: A tutta birra!
bing-45409.jpg.description:
Avete applicato la sciolina ai vostri sci e comperato lo skipass? È ora di scendere in pista! L'apertura della stagione sciistica nel comprensorio Arabba - Marmolada, nel cuore delle Dolomiti italiane, è un evento atteso con grande fervore dagli appassionati di sport invernali e amanti della montagna. La Marmolada, nota come la "Regina delle Dolomiti", offre una delle migliori esperienze sciistiche in Italia, grazie alle sue piste perfettamente preparate, alla copiosa neve e alle viste mozzafiato che la circondano. In particolare il Passo Pordoi di Sellaronda, sullo sfondo odierno, risulta essere una scelta appropriata per gli sciatori di tutti i livelli, dai principianti ai più esperti. L'apertura ufficiale segna l'inizio di mesi di divertimento sulla neve, con sciatori e snowboarder che affollano le piste per godere della sensazione di carving sulle discese impeccabili che caratterizzano questo paradiso invernale.

La penisola italica, con i suoi numerosi impianti sciistici, attira sciatori da tutto il mondo, offrendo un pletora di paesaggi spettacolari e un'ampia varietà di terreni sciistici. L'entusiasmo che accompagna l'apertura delle piste non solo celebra lo spirito avventuroso degli sport invernali, ma evidenzia anche il legame unico tra la cultura italiana e la montagna, un connubio che continua a ispirare appassionati di sci e snowboard di tutte le età. Ergo, attaccate gli scarponi e preparatevi al divertimento, la stagione è appena iniziata!

bing-45412.jpg.title: Museu do Amanhã, Rio de Janeiro, Brasil
bing-45412.jpg.headline: Museu maravilhoso
bing-45412.jpg.description:
O Museu do Amanhã é um museu de ciências diferente. Situado na Cidade do Rio de Janeiro, o prédio foi projeto do arquiteto espanhol Santiago Calatrava, e foi erguido ao lado da Praça Mauá, na zona portuária (mais precisamente no Píer Mauá), onde está aberto à visitação desde 2015. Esse museu abriga ambiente de ideias, explorações e perguntas sobre a época de grandes mudanças em que vivemos e os diferentes caminhos que se abrem para o futuro.

O edifício conta com espinhas solares que se movem ao longo da claraboia, projetadas para adaptar-se às mudanças das condições ambientais. A exposição principal é majoritariamente digital e foca em ideias ao invés de objetos. Com pouco menos de dez anos de existência, o Museu do Amanhã já se consolidou com um tradicional ponto turístico carioca, sendo cenário de muitas fotos com seu inconfundível espelho d’água que faz parte do museu.

bing-45414.jpg.title: Neuschwanstein and Hohenschwangau castles, Bavarian Alps, Germany
bing-45414.jpg.headline: Straight out of a fairy tale. Neuschwanstein and Hohenschwangau castles, Bavaria, Germany
bing-45414.jpg.description: The Bavarian Alps, a mountain range in southern Germany, are home to these enchanting 19th-century castles, Neuschwanstein and Hohenschwangau. Neuschwanstein Castle, on the left of our homepage image, was commissioned by King Ludwig II of Bavaria. Building work began in 1869 on this Romanesque Revival palace with its fairy-tale-like architecture and breathtaking mountain backdrop. Across the valley, gazing out over Lake Alpsee, is the equally spectacular Hohenschwangau Castle, built by Ludwig II's father, King Maximilian II of Bavaria. These two castles boast rich interiors with intricate artwork and historical artifacts. Both castles attract millions of visitors every year, offering a glimpse into the opulent past of Bavaria.

bing-45418.jpg.title: Beach with bungalow and coconut palm trees at Palolem in Goa, India.
bing-45418.jpg.headline: A sand-sational escapade. Palolem beach, Goa, India
bing-45418.jpg.description: The Indian state of Goa is renowned for its pristine coastline and serene waters. Among its many gems, Palolem Beach is a mile-long crescent-shaped beach lined with swaying palm trees and colourful houses. Busiest between November and March, the mix of foreign tourists and local fishermen in the adjacent village creates a unique blend of cultures. Palolem is also famous for the diverse activities it offers, including yoga sessions, silent discos and exciting dolphin-spotting excursions. This coastal paradise is the perfect spot for a seaside retreat, offering a range of experiences to cater to every visitor's preferences.

bing-45419.jpg.title: Congreso de los diputados, Madrid, España
bing-45419.jpg.headline: ¡Hoy es un gran día!. Aniversario de la Constitución Española
bing-45419.jpg.description:
Hoy se conmemora en España la aprobación de la Constitución Española de 1978, un hito que establece los pilares fundamentales del sistema político y social del país. Esta constitución es un faro que declara a España como un estado democrático y social de Derecho, garantizando derechos y libertades esenciales para todos los ciudadanos. Además, sienta las bases para la descentralización del poder mediante la instauración de un sistema autonómico y establece la separación de poderes (ejecutivo, legislativo y judicial), elementos clave en la organización estatal.

Durante este día, se llevan a cabo diversos actos oficiales presididos por las más altas autoridades del país, incluyendo a la familia real, el presidente del Gobierno, representantes de partidos políticos y otras figuras relevantes.

Es una jornada que nos invita a reflexionar sobre los valores democráticos, los derechos ciudadanos y la trascendencia de la ley fundamental que regula la convivencia en España.

bing-45426.jpg.title: The Globe of Science and Innovation building, Meyrin, Switzerland
bing-45426.jpg.headline: A global code for the future. Computer Science Education Week
bing-45426.jpg.description: Computer science is a dynamically developing discipline that has revolutionized our lives within a few decades. For Computer Science Education Week, we celebrate information systems and their power to connect the world, 24 hours a day. Where better to mark the occasion than the European Organization for Nuclear Research, known as CERN—birthplace of the World Wide Web? The 89-foot ball seen on today’s homepage is CERN's Globe of Science and Innovation in Switzerland, in which visitors can learn more about the organization's research work on particle physics. Quiet observers can wander around exhibitions and follow guided tours, and curious minds can take part in lab workshops and science shows for a first-hand experience.

bing-45427.jpg.title: Dardagna waterfalls, Bologna, Italy
bing-45427.jpg.headline: Dardagna waterfalls, Bologna, Italy
bing-45427.jpg.description: Among the many wonders of Emilia Romagna region, we can undoubtedly include the Dardagna waterfalls in Bologna, Italy. They were named after the stream of the same name, which originates from Monte Spigolino—a mountain in the Apennines—and seven waterfalls. The highest fall is approximately 30 metres is near the Sanctuary of the Madonna dell'Acero. After travelling for several kilometres, the Dardagna stream flows into the Leo River and subsequently into the Panaro, which in turn is a tributary of the much larger Po River. Thanks to the purity of its waters, the Dardagna stream is home to numerous species of fish, such as brown trout and blue trout.

bing-45435.jpg.title: Verdon Gorge, Provence-Alpes-Côte d'Azur, France
bing-45435.jpg.headline: Isn't it just 'gorges'?. Verdon Gorge, Alpes-de-Haute-Provence, France
bing-45435.jpg.description: Stretching nearly 100 kilometres, the Verdon Gorge is Europe's largest canyon, with majestic cliffs climbing up to 750 metres in height. The emerald hue of the Verdon River's waters, hidden far below this blanket of clouds, lends its name to this spectacular natural site, shaped by millions of years of erosion. Visitors or residents of Alpes-de-Haute-Provence hiking in the southeast of France can visit the canyon for rock climbing, kayaking, paragliding—the adventure options are endless. If you find yourself in Marseille or Nice, a day trip may be in order.

bing-45438.jpg.title: USS Arizona Memorial, Pearl Harbor, Oahu, Hawaii
bing-45438.jpg.headline: Remembering the fallen. National Pearl Harbor Remembrance Day
bing-45438.jpg.description: On the morning of December 7, 1941, American history changed forever when a surprise attack was launched on the US Naval base at Pearl Harbor, Hawaii. Japanese bombers and submarines struck the island of Oahu, taking the lives of 2,403 Americans and damaging or destroying over 300 airplanes and nearly 20% of the 100-ship Pacific Fleet. The United States entered World War II immediately after the attack, and the event hastened Hawaii's path to become the 50th state to join the union. As 82 years have passed, few veterans of Pearl Harbor are still alive today. Lou Conter, the last surviving crew member of the USS Arizona, its memorial seen here, turned 102 in September. So, thank you to Lou, and all others who served our country on that infamous day.

bing-45444.jpg.title: Souvenirverkauf auf dem Christkindlesmarkt, Nürnberg
bing-45444.jpg.headline: Weihnachtszeit, Schnee und Christkindlmärkte. Christkindlesmarkt, Nürnberg, Bayern
bing-45444.jpg.description:
Die Wurzeln der Weihnachtsmärkte reichen bis ins späte Mittelalter zurück. Damals wurden sie auch Nikolausmärkte genannt, da der Heilige Nikolaus im deutschen Raum sehr verbreitet war. Der erste urkundlich erwähnte Weihnachtsmarkt fand 1434 in Dresden statt. Er wird noch heute Striezelmarkt genannt, weil der Stollen im Mittelhochdeutschen Striezel genannt wurde. Ursprünglich dienten die Märkte der Bevölkerung dazu, sich mit Lebensmitteln für den Winter einzudecken. Im Laufe der Jahrhunderte entwickelten sie sich zu festlichen Veranstaltungen mit einem vielfältigen Angebot. Doch erst ab dem 16. Jahrhundert, im Zuge der Reformation, die den Nikolauskult langsam zurückdrängte, blühte der Begriff und Name Christkindlmarkt auf.

Hier in Nürnberg wurde der „Kindles-Marck“ erstmals 1628 urkundlich erwähnt. Später erhielt er den Namen Christkindelmarkt, wie wir ihn heute kennen. Ein beliebtes Souvenir auf diesen Märkten sind die Nussknacker, die erstmals 1870 im Erzgebirge von dem Kunsthandwerker Friedrich Wilhelm Füchtner erfunden wurden. Heute sind sie nicht nur dekorative Kunstwerke, sondern auch beliebte Sammlerstücke und in der ganzen Welt bekannt. Doch vergessen wir nicht den eigentlichen Sinn des Weihnachtsfestes und der Christkindlmärkte. Sie repräsentieren nicht nur Einkaufsstätten, sondern auch Orte der Gemeinschaft und der festlichen Tradition, die das einzigartige Erbe Deutschlands widerspiegeln.

bing-45446.jpg.title: Fête des Lumières, œuvre d'art de Daniel Knipper, nommée Regards, en hommage aux victimes de l'attentat de Paris 2015, Lyon, France
bing-45446.jpg.headline: Une féerie douce et lumineuse. Fête des Lumières de Lyon
bing-45446.jpg.description:
Plongez au cœur de la magie lumineuse de la Fête des Lumières de Lyon, une célébration envoûtante où l'art rencontre l'émotion. La photo du jour illustre l'œuvre captivante de Daniel Knipper, « Regards », qui a illuminé la colline de Fourvière en hommage aux victimes des attentats du 13 novembre 2015.

Les origines de la Fête des Lumières de Lyon remonteraient à 1852, date à laquelle une statue en hommage à la Vierge Marie devait être inaugurée. À cause du mauvais temps, les festivités étaient sur le point d'être annulées, mais le ciel s'est éclairci. Les Lyonnais ont spontanément placé des bougies aux fenêtres, illuminant ainsi toute la ville.

Aujourd'hui, la Fête des Lumières est devenue un événement populaire où des artistes du monde entier participent en créant des œuvres d'art lumineuses et des spectacles visuels pendant plusieurs jours. C'est devenu un festival artistique et culturel majeur, attirant des visiteurs du monde entier. Venez vous émerveiller, vous émouvoir et vous unir à cette célébration exceptionnelle !

bing-45450.jpg.title: La Rocque Harbour, St. Clement, Island of Jersey
bing-45450.jpg.headline: Not that Jersey Shore. La Rocque Harbour, Island of Jersey
bing-45450.jpg.description: Just off the coast of Normandy, France, lies Jersey, a British island with a Norse name. Found on the southeastern shore of the island is La Rocque Harbour, home to a white, sandy beach and an elevated walkway that stretches out into the water. The shoreline's granite and plutonic rocks, which originated more than 420 million years ago, showcase a variety of colors and textures. Visible from the harbor are the round, stubby Icho Tower and the taller Seymour Tower, built in the 18th and 19th centuries respectively as coastal defense structures. Both structures are over 1,800 feet away from the shore and can be reached on foot with a sturdy pair of shoes, but only on the days of the year where the tide is lowest.

bing-45454.jpg.title: India gate war memorial designed by Sir Edwin Lutyens in New Delhi, India.
bing-45454.jpg.headline: A majestic frame for an eternal flame. India gate, New Delhi, India
bing-45454.jpg.description: India Gate, a grand war memorial in New Delhi designed by Sir Edwin Lutyens, commemorates the Indian soldiers who lost their lives during World War I. It features the names of the more than 13,500 soldiers who fell on the Northwestern Frontier in 1919. Under the gate is the eternal flame, known as the Amar Jawan Jyoti, which honours the unknown soldiers of the 1971 Indo-Pakistan War. The India Gate was unveiled in 1931 by the Duke of Connaught. The 42-metre-high arch, reminiscent of the Parisian Arc de Triomphe, stands at the end of the Rajpath, connecting it with the Rashtrapati Bhavan. The memorial has become a symbol of national unity and a site for various commemorations, including Republic Day parades.

bing-45457.jpg.title: Luci di Natale a Torbole, Trento
bing-45457.jpg.headline: Le "calde" luci di una foto invernale
bing-45457.jpg.description: Torbole è un luogo incastonato tra le maestose montagne del Trentino sulle sponde del Lago di Garda. Affascinante borgo con stradine lastricate ed edifici colorati, è ogni anno meta apprezzata dagli amanti degli sport acquatici, offre attività come windsurf e kitesurf. Il Castello di Arco, a soli 5 km, svela la storia locale, mentre la Funivia Malcesine Monte Baldo, a 20 km, regala strabilianti viste panoramiche. Inoltre, a 10 km, si trova il Lago di Tenno che per la sua naturale bellezza e configurazione, invita al relax con acque cristalline circondate da boschi lussureggianti. Un connubio perfetto di natura, storia e attività all'aria aperta.

bing-45462.jpg.title: Guanacos in Los Glaciares National Park, Patagonia, Argentina
bing-45462.jpg.headline: Living the high life. National Llama Day
bing-45462.jpg.description:
Strap on your hiking boots because it's National Llama Day! December 9 is a designated day to appreciate these intelligent and trainable creatures. You'll need to visit the Andes Mountains to see their wild cousins, guanacos. Guanacos are believed to have originated in the central plains of North America 40 million years ago, but they gradually migrated to South America. Scientists think llamas descended from guanacos and were first domesticated around 4500 BCE.

As seen in today's image, guanacos are often spotted roaming free in Los Glaciares National Park, Argentina, sporting dark cinnamon-colored wool and cartoonish-looking faces. Cute as they are, they can be a bit rude: Both guanacos and llamas defend themselves by spitting to assert dominance within their herd or to keep intrusive peers at bay. Don't let this deter you from going on an organized llama trek though—they can make for great pack animal companions!
