bing-45939.jpg.headline: A place to think, think, think. Winnie the Pooh Day
bing-45939.jpg.description:
Fancy an excuse to reconnect with your childhood? It's Winnie the Pooh Day today! That’s right, that 'willy-nilly silly old bear' has a day to himself! It's actually the birthday of Alan Alexander Milne, the man who brought Pooh and his pals to life. Inspired by Milne's son Christopher Robin and his stuffed animals, the stories have captured the hearts of readers for nearly a century.

What better place to celebrate him than in the real Hundred Acre Wood, the Ashdown Forest in East Sussex? This conservation landscape, a mix of heathland, woodlands and grassy areas, is also a riddle of historical features from the Bronze Age, Iron Age and Romano-British era. One iconic spot here is the Poohsticks Bridge, a wooden bridge that spans a gentle stream. Inspired by the game played by Pooh and his friends, visitors can enjoy the timeless tradition of dropping sticks into the stream and watching them race to the other side. So, why not don a stout pair of boots and grab a map and take a leaf out of Pooh's book?

bing-45942.jpg.title: Pont Alexandre III at twilight, Paris, France
bing-45942.jpg.headline: Under the watch of Pegasus. Pont Alexandre III, Paris, France
bing-45942.jpg.description: The 'golden hour' just before sunset is the perfect time to take in views of Paris' most ornate bridge, the Pont Alexandre III. Arching over the Seine, the bridge was opened in 1900 and named after a Russian tsar, celebrating a new alliance between the two countries. Befitting the nobility of the event, two 56-foot columns sit on each bank of the river, crowned with gilt-bronze sculptures of the winged horse Pegasus. From the center of the bridge, standing above reliefs decorated with nymphs and beneath Art Nouveau-style lamps, you can admire some famous Parisian monuments. Views include the Esplanade des Invalides, the Grand Palais and Petit Palais museums, and the Eiffel Tower.

bing-45954.jpg.title: Frozen waterfalls in Plitvice Lakes National Park, Croatia
bing-45954.jpg.headline: Waterfalls turned waterfreeze. Plitvice Lakes National Park, Croatia
bing-45954.jpg.description:
Why visit one lake when you can visit 16? Plitvice Lakes National Park in Croatia serves up stunning terraced lakes connected to one another by more than 90 cascades and waterfalls, thanks to the unique geology of the area.

The surrounding mountains funnel water carrying calcium carbonate into the park. This accumulates and hardens over time into a type of limestone called tufa, which creates a series of barriers. These natural dams form pools, with thin, lacy waterfalls leading from one 'lake' to another. This majestic display draws more than a million visitors a year to the paths and boardwalks that wind through the lakes, a UNESCO World Heritage Site. Even in winter, the lakes retain their beauty, with once-roaring waterfalls frozen in place.

bing-45956.jpg.title: 音羽橋から見る川霧に佇むタンチョウ, 北海道 阿寒郡
bing-45956.jpg.headline: 今日は大寒
bing-45956.jpg.description:
今日 1 月 20 日は大寒。太陽が黄経 300 度の位置にあるときを指し、一年の中で最も寒い時期です。ここ北海道鶴居村の音羽橋付近で、早朝の川霧が立ち込める中、たくさんのタンチョウが佇んでいます…

音羽橋の下を流れる雪裡川は湧き水が豊富で、冬でも凍らないため、餌を探すタンチョウが集まります。橋の上からは、タンチョウを驚かすことなく観察でき、鳥愛好家とカメラマンを魅了しています。

bing-45962.jpg.title: Château de Castelnaud avant le lever du soleil, Dordogne, France
bing-45962.jpg.headline: À la recherche du diamant noir !. Fête de la truffe de Sarlat, Périgord
bing-45962.jpg.description: Bienvenue au Château de Castelnaud, perché majestueusement à 150 mètres d’altitude, il domine la vallée de la Dordogne dans le Périgord. Fondé au XIIe siècle, ce joyau médiéval offre un panorama à couper le souffle sur la région. À quelques pas de cette forteresse chargée d'histoire, la Fête de la Truffe de Sarlat bat son plein et enflamme les papilles des fins gastronomes venus savourer cette pépite incontournable. La truffe, ce champignon mystérieux, se dévoile sous des formes plus ou moins globuleuses. En Europe, six espèces de truffes gastronomiques sont récoltées, parmi lesquelles on trouve la truffe blanche et la truffe noire du Périgord. Prêt à succomber à l'arôme envoûtant de ce diamant noir qui éveillera tous vos sens ?

bing-45966.jpg.title: Macaroni penguins, Drake Passage, Chile
bing-45966.jpg.headline: Taking the plunge. Penguin Awareness Day
bing-45966.jpg.description:
Let's flap our flippers and dive into Penguin Awareness Day! Today's image features macaroni penguins swimming in the plankton-rich waters of the Drake Passage off the coast of Chile. These charming creatures, one of 18 different species of penguin in the Southern Hemisphere, can be recognized by their flashy amber crests and orange beaks. The name is said to have been coined by English sailors, derived from a term used to describe flamboyant dressers in the late 18th century.

Macaroni penguins can be a bad-tempered bunch who get into noisy fights. To avoid this, males often ease their way through crowded colonies with their heads tucked down to their chests. The main threats though, are not their fellow penguins. Reduced food availability, fishing nets, and the impact of climate change on sea ice are among challenges faced by this species, which has been classified as vulnerable due to population decline.

bing-45978.jpg.title: Eurasian red squirrel, Netherlands
bing-45978.jpg.headline: Tales from the treetops. Squirrel Appreciation Day
bing-45978.jpg.description: Have you ever been captivated by a squirrel crossing your path? January 21 is Squirrel Awareness Day, honoring these furry seed distributors. Today's homepage star is the Eurasian red squirrel, whose striking reddish-brown coat, white underbelly, and bushy tail are a familiar sight in several countries. These squirrels are not only exceptional jumpers—capable of leaping up to 6 feet in one jump—they can even swim to search for food. They gather nuts and acorns in the autumn and hide them, to see them through the winter months. If you spot fuzzy-tailed squirrels frolicking in your backyard, they might also appreciate a feeding station stocked with treats such as raspberries or crab apples.

bing-45986.jpg.title: Beatus-Rhenanus-Brücke über den Rhein, zwischen Straßburg und Kehl, Straßburg, Frankreich
bing-45986.jpg.headline: Brücke der Einheit?. Beatus-Rhenanus-Brücke, Straßburg, Frankreich
bing-45986.jpg.description:
Heute begehen wir den Deutsch-Französischen Tag. Deswegen finden wir, dass dieses Foto perfekt passt. Die Beatus-Rhenanus-Brücke ist ein perfektes Symbol für diesen besonderen Tag der nun sein 20. Jahrestag feiert. Diese elegante und moderne Architektur dient als wichtige Verkehrsverbindung für Fußgänger, Radfahrer und Straßenbahnen zwischen Kehl und Straßburg.

Vor Zwanzig Jahren wurde zum Gedenken an den Élysée-Vertrag von 1963 dieser Tag ins Leben gerufen. Zu dem Zeitpunkt waren Gerd Schröder Bundeskanzler und Jacques Chirac französischer Bundespräsident. Zu jedem Jahrestag gibt es ein verschiedenes Motto. 2016 lautete das Motto: „Franzosen und Deutsche: einmal Freunde, immer Freunde/Allemands et Français: partenaires un jour, partenaires toujours“.

Wir hoffen, dass solche besonderen Anlässe und Feiertage weltweit gefeiert werden und wir uns endlich von Konflikten und Zwietracht lösen können um gemeinsam als Menschen, Brüder und Schwestern diese wundervolle Blaue Heimat in Frieden und Freude leben und erleben können. Möge unsere Freundschaft lange dauern und ein Beispiel für die ganze Welt sein. Que notre amitié dure longtemps et soit un exemple pour le monde entier.

bing-45990.jpg.title: Winter sunrise, Walton Lighthouse, Santa Cruz, California
bing-45990.jpg.headline: A beacon from dusk till dawn. Walton Lighthouse, Santa Cruz, California
bing-45990.jpg.description:
Step to the western edge of America, where the Walton Lighthouse, also known as the Santa Cruz Breakwater Lighthouse, is a beacon for passing ships. Built in 2002, this 40-foot-tall building replaced a more modest light. The Walton Lighthouse got its name from Charles Walton, a businessman who helped fund its construction in memory of his brother Derek, a merchant seaman who died at sea during World War II.

Santa Cruz has been a busy port city since the mid-1800s, when ships would unload lime, redwood, and other agricultural products. These days, Santa Cruz Harbor is home to a commercial fishing fleet, as well as a popular place to rent kayaks, boats, and paddleboards.

bing-45991.jpg.title: Winter sunrise, Walton Lighthouse, Santa Cruz, California
bing-45991.jpg.headline: Walton Lighthouse, Santa Cruz, California, USA
bing-45991.jpg.description:
Step to the western edge of America, where Walton Lighthouse, also known as the Santa Cruz Breakwater Lighthouse, serves as a guiding beacon for passing ships. Built in 2002 in Santa Cruz, California, this 12-metre-tall modern maritime structure replaced a more modest light. The Walton Lighthouse got its name from Charles Walton, a businessman who generously contributed towards its construction costs in memory of his brother Derek Walton, a merchant seaman who tragically lost his life at sea during World War II.

Santa Cruz has been a busy port city since the mid-1800s when ships would unload lime, redwood and other agricultural products. These days, Santa Cruz Harbour is home to a commercial fishing fleet, as well as being a popular place to rent kayaks, boats and paddleboards.

bing-46002.jpg.title: Atolls in Indian Ocean, Maldives
bing-46002.jpg.headline: Eyes of the Indian Ocean. Atolls in the Maldives
bing-46002.jpg.description:
With nearly 1,200 islands spread over a chain of 26 atolls, the Maldives are popular with tourists seeking serene beaches, scuba diving, and surf in the Indian Ocean. The atolls, like those pictured on our homepage, are made up of coral reefs that formed around the top of now-sunken volcanoes. Some are single, ring-shaped islands enclosing lagoons while other atolls are a series of small, connected islets, many of which are uninhabited.

The country is also home to Baa Atoll, a UNESCO biosphere reserve whose numerous coral reefs, islands, and mangroves make it a globally important habitat for species including whale sharks, manta rays, and marine turtles. The Maldives archipelago is rich in biodiversity but faces an existential threat from climate change. As lowest-lying country in the world, much of which is less than 4 feet above sea level, it is extremely vulnerable to rising sea levels. By the end of the century, it is thought that the islands could disappear altogether.

bing-46009.jpg.title: Parco Nazionale del Gran Sasso, con il castello di Rocca Calascio
bing-46009.jpg.headline: Gran Sasso... e gran freddo!
bing-46009.jpg.description:
Il Castello di Rocca Calascio è una roccaforte medievale situata nel Parco Nazionale del Gran Sasso e Monti della Laga in Abruzzo. Con un’altitudine di circa 1.460 metri, è uno dei castelli più alti d’Europa. La sua posizione strategica sulla cima di una rocca offre una vista panoramica mozzafiato sulle montagne circostanti e sulla valle sottostante. Il castello è stato utilizzato in diversi film, tra cui il famoso “Il nome della rosa” di Jean-Jacques Annaud, conferendogli un ulteriore fascino e attirando numerosi visitatori e appassionati di cinema. Oggi, il castello è una meta turistica popolare, attirando visitatori interessati alla storia, all’architettura e alla bellezza naturale della zona.

Il massiccio del Gran Sasso, culminante con il Corno Grande, regna come il punto più alto degli Appennini, con i suoi picchi maestosi che si stagliano contro il cielo. Questa catena montuosa, immersa nel Parco Nazionale del Gran Sasso e Monti della Laga, offre una miscela unica di paesaggi, da valli selvagge a fitti boschi di faggio.

bing-46014.jpg.title: Diamond Beach, Iceland
bing-46014.jpg.headline: A real icebreaker. Diamond Beach, Iceland
bing-46014.jpg.description: From fjords and lava fields to ice caves and black sand beaches, Iceland is a treasure trove of natural wonders. The volcanic black sand of Diamond Beach, pictured in today's image, sparkles with pieces of iceberg washed ashore from the nearby Jökulsárlón glacier lagoon. The contrast between the clear ice and black sand looks particularly surreal when sunlight hits the ice, making it a must-visit destination on Iceland's south coast.

bing-46018.jpg.title: Agra Fort, Uttar Pradesh
bing-46018.jpg.headline: Regal fort in focus. Agra Fort, Agra, Uttar Pradesh
bing-46018.jpg.description: In the 16th century, when the tales of Mughal emperors were unfolding, the visionary Emperor Akbar commissioned modifications to the Agra Fort. This grand palace of the Mughal dynasty, strategically situated on the bank of the Yamuna River, was home to numerous ruling families. The architectural ensemble within the fort includes notable structures such as the Jahangir Mahal, a palace built for Akbar's son, Jahangir, the Khas Mahal, a private palace for the emperor, and the Diwan-i-Am or Hall of Public Audience. A UNESCO World Heritage Site since 1983, the Agra Fort boasts a rich historical and architectural legacy in Uttar Pradesh, making it a must-see destination near another famous monument, the Taj Mahal.

bing-46023.jpg.title: Burns National Heritage Park, Alloway, Ayrshire, Scotland
bing-46023.jpg.headline: The sun Burns like a red, red rose. Burns Night
bing-46023.jpg.description: Get ready to raise a glass to Robert Burns, as we dive into the spirit of Burns Night! Each year on January 25, Scotland lights up in celebration of its national poet, and what better place to take part in the festivities than where it all began? The Burns National Heritage Park is located in Alloway, Ayrshire–the birthplace of Rabbie himself. From his charming cottage to the museum that holds his precious works to the Brig o' Doon, a bridge made famous from his poem 'Tam o' Shanter', the park has a lot to offer. But, come Burns Night, the place transforms. We're talking about hearty plates of haggis, neeps and tatties, the unmistakable skirl of bagpipes and people coming together with a dram or two, raising a toast to the man of the hour. So, dust off your poetry books, polish your best shoes and join the belter from near or afar. Lang may yer lum reek!

bing-46024.jpg.title: Baleia metálica, Avenida Faria Lima, São Paulo, Brasil
bing-46024.jpg.headline: A cidade que nunca dorme
bing-46024.jpg.description:
A história de São Paulo é uma fascinante jornada de crescimento e diversidade cultural, desde os dias coloniais até se tornar o dinâmico centro financeiro e cultural que é hoje. O aniversário da cidade, em 25 de janeiro, não apenas celebra seu passado, mas também proporciona uma oportunidade para os paulistanos contemplarem o futuro dessa metrópole vibrante.

Nessa trajetória, três lugares icônicos se destacam. O Pátio do Colégio, localizado no centro histórico, representa o berço de São Paulo. Fundado pelos jesuítas, este espaço abriga o Museu Anchieta, preservando a história da cidade desde seus primeiros dias. Uma visita oferece uma imersão nas origens da metrópole, destacando a arquitetura colonial e conectando-se aos primeiros momentos da história paulistana.

A Avenida Paulista é o ícone contemporâneo de São Paulo, simbolizando prosperidade, cultura e diversidade. Com seus arranha-céus imponentes, museus e centros culturais, a avenida desempenha o papel crucial de ser o epicentro financeiro e cultural, refletindo a pluralidade e o dinamismo que caracterizam São Paulo. O Parque Ibirapuera, concebido por Oscar Niemeyer e Burle Marx, emerge como um oásis urbano no coração da cidade. Oferecendo espaço para atividades esportivas, piqueniques e abrigando instituições culturais notáveis, como o MAM e o Auditório Ibirapuera, o parque se torna um refúgio popular, proporcionando tranquilidade e natureza aos habitantes de São Paulo.

bing-46025.jpg.title: A snowy owl on the icy field, Quebec City, Canada
bing-46025.jpg.headline: Ready for liftoff. Snowy owl
bing-46025.jpg.description: Owls, nocturnal birds of prey characterised by their upright stance, forward-facing eyes and silent flight, encompass a diverse family of species. Among them, the snowy owl stands out as an Arctic resident known for its white plumage. The snowy owl's thick feather coat, complete with a layer of downy under plumage, provides unmatched insulation against the biting cold. With keen yellow eyes and tufted feathers, these large raptors display exceptional predatory skills. The nocturnal predators mainly consume small mammals such as lemmings, a favourite of theirs. The nomadic birds rarely breed at the same location or with the same mate. During the cold season, they leave the Arctic and migrate to southern Canada and the northern United States.

bing-46026.jpg.title: Ruins of St. Dwynwen's Church, Ynys Llanddwyn, Wales
bing-46026.jpg.headline: A haven for broken hearts. Ruins of St. Dwynwen's Church, Ynys Llanddwyn, Wales
bing-46026.jpg.description:
Ynys Llanddwyn is a tiny tidal island which, at low tide, is attached to the Isle of Anglesey in Wales. Ynys means 'island' in Welsh and Llanddwyn means 'the church of Dwynwen,' the country's patron saint of lovers.

Legend has it that Dwynwen, a 5th-century Welsh princess, sought solace on this island after a tragic love story. The young woman fell in love with a commoner, but because her royal father forbade the union—and briefly turned her beloved into a block of ice—she moved to the island and set up a convent. She dedicated her life to spirituality, living as a hermit and helping others with matters of the heart. The ruins of Dwynwen's church, a well, and a convent remain on Ynys Llanddwyn and St. Dwynwen's Day, on January 25, is the most romantic day in Wales—the country's very own Valentine's Day.
bing-46026.jpg.copyright: © Photos by R A Kearton/Getty Image

bing-46030.jpg.title: Illuminated President's Estate of India, New Delhi, India
bing-46030.jpg.headline: Lights of the capital. Republic Day
bing-46030.jpg.description:
Republic Day is observed every year on January 26 to commemorate the adoption of the Constitution of India and reaffirm of the nation's foundational ideals. In the years following independence, the foundation for the subsequent development of the Indian Constitution was laid, marking the country's transformation into a democratic republic on this day in 1950.

The Ministry of Defence is responsible for organising the Republic Day parade in New Delhi, a showcase of national pride. Beginning at Rashtrapati Bhavan, the President's residence, and moving along the Rajpath, including Raisina Hill and India Gate, this event is the highlight of the three-day-long celebrations. The parade is a vibrant display of India's defence capabilities and cultural and social heritage. Nine to twelve regiments of the Indian Army, along with the Navy and Air Force, march in regal finery and highlight the unity of India's security forces on this prestigious occasion.

bing-46035.jpg.title: Eurasian blue tit, United Kingdom
bing-46035.jpg.headline: Having a holly good time. Big Garden Birdwatch
bing-46035.jpg.description: Got a keen eye for our feathered friends? Grab your binoculars and notepad as the Big Garden Birdwatch is back for its 45th year! What started as an activity for children has now turned into the world's largest garden wildlife survey. Every year, the Royal Society for the Protection of Birds—a charitable organisation—asks volunteers to spend an hour noting down the birds that pop by their gardens over the Birdwatch weekend. No garden? No worries! A balcony or local park will do just fine. Just jot down what you see and let the RSPB know. While you're sure to see many birds, here's a peek at one of our most beloved visitors—the Eurasian blue tit. Common in woodlands, gardens and farmlands, these tiny acrobats stand out in cerulean and gold against the winter grey. Cheers and happy birdwatching!

bing-46038.jpg.title: Northern hawk-owl
bing-46038.jpg.headline: Not a night owl. Northern hawk-owl
bing-46038.jpg.description: While other owls spend their days sleeping off the night before, the northern hawk-owl is a bird of a different feather. One of the few owls active during the day, that piercing gaze scours the boreal forests of North America, Europe, and Asia for prey. Northern hawk-owls aren't picky eaters: Mice, rats, voles, lemmings, rabbits, shrews, moles, and the occasional frog are all on the menu. These vocal birds have different calls for mating, chatting with their young, and warning that danger is nearby. If you get too close to their nest, protective parents have been known to swoop at humans to keep them away.

bing-46045.jpg.title: Maschera al Carnevale di Venezia, Veneto, Italia
bing-46045.jpg.headline: A carnevale ogni scherzo vale!
bing-46045.jpg.description:
Preparate le vostre maschere migliori, oggi ha inizio il carnevale più elegante del mondo! Il Carnevale di Venezia, rinomato a livello internazionale, è un evento annuale che affonda le sue radici nella storia ricca e affascinante della città lagunare. Celebrato con sfarzo e magnificenza, esso è famoso per le sue maschere elaborate e i costumi sontuosi che trasformano la città in un palcoscenico di magia e mistero. Durante questo periodo festivo, le tradizionali maschere veneziane, come la celebre maschera di Colombina o il suggestivo volto della maschera d'Arlecchino, diventano emblemi di eleganza e sofisticatezza.

Le origini del Carnevale di Venezia risalgono al Medioevo, quando la città divenne rinomata per le sue feste in cui nobili e cittadini comuni si univano in un'atmosfera di divertimento e mascherate. Oggi, il Carnevale attira visitatori da tutto il globo che partecipano alle celebrazioni che includono sfilate di costumi elaborati, spettacoli teatrali, concerti e balli in piazza San Marco. Questa festa unica non solo celebra la tradizione veneziana, ma anche la creatività e l'arte, rendendo il Carnevale di Venezia un'esperienza straordinaria che mescola storia, cultura e intrattenimento in una cornice incomparabile.

bing-46050.jpg.title: Ice palace at the St. Paul Winter Carnival, Minnesota
bing-46050.jpg.headline: In winter's embrace. St. Paul Winter Carnival
bing-46050.jpg.description: A chilly paradise awaits at the St. Paul Winter Carnival! This annual celebration, taking place between January 25 and February 4 this year, transforms Minnesota's capital city into a winter wonderland. It all started in 1885, when a group of reporters visited and referred to Minnesota as another Siberia, unfit for human habitation. This offended city officials who devised a plan to showcase the area's winter beauty. The Winter Carnival was born, featuring seasonal activities such as bobsledding and ice horse-racing. Today, the carnival attracts visitors and strengthens community bonds through parades, markets, and winter sports. And ice sculptors carve stunning but fleeting works of art, like the frozen palace towering over today's image.

bing-46051.jpg.title: Spot-billed toucanet, Atlantic Forest, Brazil
bing-46051.jpg.headline: Spot-billed toucanet, Brazil
bing-46051.jpg.description: The spot-billed toucanet, seen today, is a species of toucan that stands out for its green plumage and a striking orange beak adorned with black spots. Females, like the one seen here, are mainly coloured in green, brown and yellow, while males add red and blue to the mix. Primarily found in in the Amazon and Pantanal regions of Brazil, these spot-billed toucanets inhabit humid tropical forests, where they feed on a variety of fruits, insects and small vertebrates. Their presence is essential for seed dispersal, an important role in the ecology of these forests. However, like many species, the spot-billed toucanet faces threats due to habitat loss and environmental degradation—an example of the need for conservation efforts to protect this fascinating species and Brazil's biodiversity.

bing-46055.jpg.title: Catedral de Burgos, Burgos, España
bing-46055.jpg.headline: ¡Un viaje en el tiempo!. Catedral de Burgos, Burgos, España
bing-46055.jpg.description:
En el corazón de Burgos, se alza majestuosa la Catedral de Santa María. Obra maestra gótica, fue consagrada en 1260 y es Patrimonio de la Humanidad desde 1984. Su belleza no reside solo en las agujas que acarician el cielo, sino en los secretos que guarda: se dice que el mismísimo El Cid Campeador descansa entre sus muros. Pero ¡hay más aún! ¿sabías que esta maravilla esconde un reloj astronómico que fascina a quienes lo contemplan?

Si las piedras hablaran, contarían cómo el rey Fernando III “el Santo” y el obispo Don Mauricio colocaron la primera piedra, iniciando una construcción que desafiaría el tiempo. Y entre sus tesoros, se encuentra la capilla del Condestable, un retablo de ensueño donde cada escultura parece cobrar vida.

Coincidiendo con la Festividad de San Lesmes, patrono de Burgos, la catedral se viste de gala, y el espíritu de fiesta inunda las calles con los colores vivos de las casas que la rodean. San Lesmes, monje benedictino de noble cuna, se convirtió en el protector de los peregrinos, y aún hoy, su legado une a los burgaleses en una celebración de fe, cultura y tradición. Ven y descubre esta maravilla, donde cada piedra y cada vitral, te cuenta una historia única.

bing-46058.jpg.title: Renard roux, Lac des Truites, Soultzeren, Alsace, France
bing-46058.jpg.headline: Tu veux ma photo ?. Le renard roux
bing-46058.jpg.description:
Le renard roux est un animal fascinant. Avec sa fourrure rousse et sa queue touffue, il est facilement reconnaissable. Mais saviez-vous qu'il est également un animal très intelligent, capable de s’adapter à différents environnements et de trouver de la nourriture dans des endroits improbables ?

Le renard roux est par ailleurs un animal très social. Il vit en famille et prend soin de ses petits. En effet, ces animaux sont connus pour leur comportement parental attentionné. Les parents enseignent à leurs petits comment chasser et se protéger des prédateurs. Ils sont également des animaux très agiles, capables de courir à une vitesse allant jusqu’à 48 km/h et de sauter jusqu’à 2 mètres de hauteur.

Malheureusement, la population de renards roux est menacée par la perte d'habitat, la fragmentation, l'exploitation et la chasse. Au début du XXe siècle, ils étaient couramment chassés et élevés pour leur fourrure. Alors, protégeons ces héros malicieux de nos contes en préservant leur habitat naturel.

bing-46062.jpg.title: Channel Country, Outback Queensland, Australia
bing-46062.jpg.headline: From parched to pastoral. Channel Country, Australia
bing-46062.jpg.description: Narrow waterways run like veins through the Australian Outback's Channel Country, a sprawling, ancient flood plain named after its crisscrossing river channels. The huge flat area is transformed from a parched desert canvas to a vibrant tapestry of wildflowers when rainfall is abundant. Indigenous Australians have lived off this land for tens of thousands of years and some offer tours and classes about how to survive in the Outback. This unspoiled region is also home to a bonanza of wildlife—kangaroos that bounce along the plains, strutting emus, and preening purple-crowned fairywrens. If you're lucky, you might even spot a bilby—a nocturnal marsupial with rabbit-like ears. So, are you ready to 'channel' your inner explorer?

bing-46074.jpg.title: Golling Waterfall, Tennengau, Salzburg, Austria
bing-46074.jpg.headline: An icy descent. Golling Waterfall, Salzburg, Austria
bing-46074.jpg.description: This chilly scene captures Austria's stunning Golling Waterfall, less than 20 miles south of the city of Salzburg. Tumbling down in two stages from the mouth of the Schwarzbachfall cave, the 249-foot fall is a sight to behold in every season—whether it's framed by the lush greenery of spring or the icy embrace of winter. This region is known for its natural wonders and is also home to the world’s biggest ice cave, Eisriesenwelt, and the narrow Salzachöfen Gorge, considered to be the birthplace of white-water kayaking. Whether you are into hiking, photography, or just looking to spend some quality time in nature, this is a great Austrian destination.

bing-46078.jpg.title: The biggest Mahatma Gandhi statue in Pondicherry
bing-46078.jpg.headline: A sculpted symbol of freedom. Martyrs’ Day
bing-46078.jpg.description:
As the nation observes Martyrs' Day on January 30th, it resonates with the echoes of sacrifice and valour. Mahatma Gandhi, a trailblazing Indian lawyer, anti-colonial nationalist and political ethicist, was assassinated on this day in 1948. He spearheaded India's successful quest for independence from British rule.

On this day, a solemn ceremony unfolds at the Raj Ghat memorial, where national leaders meet to pay homage to the samadhi of Gandhi Ji. The armed forces perform a stirring exchange of arms as a powerful symbol of respect. The nation pauses in the morning for a two-minute moment of silence to honour Indian martyrs. Across the country, people engage in all-religion prayers, singing heartfelt tributes, as the day resonates with profound reflections on sacrifice and patriotism.

bing-46086.jpg.title: Aýna, Sierra del Segura, Albacete, Spain
bing-46086.jpg.headline: Spain's little Switzerland. Aýna, Albacete, Spain
bing-46086.jpg.description: Welcome to the tiny Spanish village of Aýna, in a steep valley carved by the River Mundo in the Sierra del Segura range. This part of the Castile-La Mancha region is sometimes called Manchegan Switzerland, thanks to those snow-capped peaks during the winter months. The steep, rocky terrain here means the villagers, of whom there are less than 1,000, cultivate the land on terraces dug into the mountainside. To see Aýna from this perspective, you'll need to visit the Mirador del Diablo, or Devil's Viewpoint, one of several viewing areas dotted around this picturesque valley.

bing-46096.jpg.title: Arara-canindé voando na floresta do Pantanal, Brasil
bing-46096.jpg.headline: Um vôo colorido no céu do Pantanal!
bing-46096.jpg.description:
No coração do Brasil, um espetáculo de cor e graça toma os céus do Pantanal. O Arara-canindé (Ara ararauna), também conhecido como Arara-azul-amarela, é uma ave deslumbrante que chama a atenção por sua plumagem vibrante. Enquanto plana majestosamente pelos ares, suas asas azuis contrastam com o verde exuberante da região, criando uma pintura viva na imensidão do céu.

Esse belo pássaro não é apenas um ícone da biodiversidade brasileira, mas também um guardião do equilíbrio ecológico. Ele desempenha um papel crucial dispersando sementes, ajudando na regeneração das florestas.

Infelizmente, o Arara-canindé enfrenta a ameaça da perda de habitat e do comércio ilegal. Felizmente, esforços de conservação estão em andamento, garantindo que as futuras gerações também possam se encantar com o voo livre desse tesouro do Pantanal. Observar o Arara-canindé em seu ambiente natural é uma lembrança poderosa da riqueza natural do Brasil, e um convite para preservar a beleza que nos define.

bing-46098.jpg.title: Burchell's zebra mother and foal, Rietvlei Nature Reserve, South Africa
bing-46098.jpg.headline: Stripe a pose. International Zebra Day
bing-46098.jpg.description: It's time for some black-and-white thinking. January 31 is International Zebra Day, celebrating the stripey creatures pictured here in Rietvlei Nature Reserve, South Africa. There are three species of zebra: plains, mountain, and Grévy's, and several subspecies. The mother and foal on our homepage are Burchell's zebras, a subspecies of the plains zebra. Found across eastern and southern Africa, zebras thrive in savannas, shrublands, woodlands, and mountain regions. They spend most of their time eating grasses, leaves, and shrubs, and can travel hundreds of miles in search of food and water. Sadly, all three species are under threat due to hunting and habitat destruction. International Zebra Day aims to raise awareness of conservation efforts, to help protect these striking creatures.

bing-46107.jpg.title: Sassnitz lighthouse, Rügen, Germany
bing-46107.jpg.headline: A frozen sentinel. Sassnitz lighthouse, Rügen, Germany
bing-46107.jpg.description: This winter wonderland is Rügen, Germany's largest island. From the iconic chalk cliffs of Jasmund National Park to sandy beaches, the island provides a diverse landscape for nature enthusiasts to revel in. Many artists have come here in the past to give free rein to their creativity. The chalk cliffs inspired one of Germany's most famous painters—Caspar David Friedrich. Pictured here is Sassnitz lighthouse, a maritime beacon that has guided sailors through the Baltic Sea since its establishment in 1905. Though ice may be covering the shore, the lighthouse still stands, frozen as over, shining a light for ships to sail by.

bing-46109.jpg.title: Polar bear resting in rocky landscape, Churchill, Manitoba, Canada
bing-46109.jpg.headline: A long winter's nap. Polar bear, Churchill, Manitoba
bing-46109.jpg.description: In the rugged terrain of Churchill, Manitoba, a polar bear finds solace on a bed of stone covered with ice and snow. Every year, as Hudson Bay freezes over, polar bears congregate here, waiting to return to their icy hunting grounds. The largest land carnivores, equipped with an incredible sense of smell and powerful limbs, traverse the rocky landscapes. They primarily feed on various species of seals, walruses and beluga whale. Their thick fur is perfect for insulation, and their large paws are designed like snowshoes, making them capable of surviving in the harshest of climates. A lot of globetrotters are found here during this season, paying a visit to these marine mammals, as 64 to 80 per cent of polar bears worldwide are found in Canada.

bing-46110.jpg.title: Dizzy Gillespie in 1990 at the 32nd Monterey Jazz Festival, California
bing-46110.jpg.headline: Black History Month
bing-46110.jpg.description: Born in New Orleans around the turn of the 20th century, with a sound that came from the blues, ragtime, and call-and-response vocals, jazz music is a notable chapter in Black history. You can almost hear John 'Dizzy' Gillespie playing his signature bent trumpet, featured on our homepage today. Gillespie made his name in bebop, often called the first modern form of jazz, playing alongside other greats including Charlie Parker, Miles Davis, and Thelonious Monk. Black musicians created genres like rock and roll, funk, hip-hop, and soul, the soundtrack to American culture and Black history.

bing-46119.jpg.title: Twickenham Stadium, London, England
bing-46119.jpg.headline: Time to ruck and roll. Six Nations Championship
bing-46119.jpg.description: As February's chill sweeps across Europe, so does the anticipation of the Six Nations Championship that is back for its 25th edition. Today marks the beginning of the rugby saga where six proud nations—England, France, Ireland, Italy, Scotland and Wales—clash in a test of might, strategy and heart. While this year's opening match will be held in France, let's take you to the world's largest rugby stadium, which will host England's home Six Nations matches—Twickenham Stadium. Beyond the games, Twickenham offers an immersive experience with its World Rugby Museum and an array of sculptures that pay homage to the sport. Pictured here is artist Gerald Laing's creation, 'The Spirit of Rugby – Line-Out.' England is set to play two home fixtures here. Are you ready to don the colours, join the chants and be a part of history in the making?

bing-46122.jpg.title: Marmot peeking out of its burrow
bing-46122.jpg.headline: Will Phil see his shadow?. Groundhog Day
bing-46122.jpg.description:
How long will winter last? Much depends on whether a certain groundhog sees his shadow today in Punxsutawney, Pennsylvania. On February 2, Punxsutawney Phil emerges from his tree stump, helped by members of the Punxsutawney Groundhog Club's 'inner circle.' According to local legend, the same stocky groundhog has been predicting the weather since at least 1886 and if he sees his shadow, we can expect six more weeks of winter. If he does not, an early spring awaits.

Phil is said to make his prediction by choosing one of two scrolls, which top-hatted men then read out to the crowd, who cheer Phil on either way. Our homepage star today is a relative of Phil's, an alpine marmot, which has its own winter tradition of stocking up on food to prepare for a long hibernation. Let's hope that Phil doesn't see his shadow so we can exit our own.

bing-46124.jpg.title: 函館山から見る夜景, 北海道 函館市
bing-46124.jpg.headline: 今日は「はこだて冬花火」の開催日
bing-46124.jpg.description:
今日の画像は、日本三大夜景の一つである函館山からの夜景です。津軽海峡と函館湾に挟まれた市街には、海の暗さと対照的に、まるで無数の星々が散りばめられたような壮大な景色が広がります。また今日 2 月 3 日の夜は、函館港から打ち上げられる大輪の花火も見られます…

「はこだて冬花火」は、はこだて冬フェスティバルの一環として、2 月の毎土曜日に開催されます。同時に、歴史的な建物が並ぶ元町地区の街並みと坂道もイルミネーションで飾られ、花火とともにロマンチックな世界を演出します。

bing-46134.jpg.title: Grand Canal with Santa Maria della Salute Basilica, Venice, Italy
bing-46134.jpg.headline: It's carnival time!. Carnival of Venice
bing-46134.jpg.description: Don your tricorn hat and gilded disguise, it's time to visit the Carnival of Venice. This centuries-old festival combines revelry with anonymity, thanks to the masks traditionally worn by attendees, from the classic square-jawed Bauta mask to the Colombina eye mask, with roots in Italian theater. Costumed rowers take part in a parade of traditional boats on Venice's famous Grand Canal while thousands of people wearing elaborate costumes enjoy the carnival atmosphere. Parades, parties, concerts, and performances will fill the streets until festivities end on Shrove Tuesday, which falls on February 13 this year. Visitors might pass by the Santa Maria della Salute, seen toward the back of today's image, a baroque basilica dedicated to the Virgin Mary, who is considered to be the protector of the city.

bing-46136.jpg.title: 梅の枝に止まるメジロ
bing-46136.jpg.headline: 今日は｢立春｣
bing-46136.jpg.description:
今日 2 月 4 日は｢立春｣。春の気配が感じられるようになります。写真のように、白梅の花が咲き始め、甘く香り立つ花の蜜がメジロを引き寄せます。彼らの鳴き声が、春の訪れを予感させ、新たな季節の息吹を感じさせてくれます…

メジロは目の周りの白い縁が特徴的で、メジロ（目白）の名前の由来にもなっています。雑食性で様々なものを食べますが、特に花の蜜を好み、春にはツバキや梅の花に集まり、飛び回る姿がよく見られます。

bing-46146.jpg.title: Devetashka Cave, Devetaki, Bulgaria
bing-46146.jpg.headline: The skylights are a nice touch. Devetashka Cave, Devetaki, Bulgaria
bing-46146.jpg.description: Step through time and into the cavernous depths of Devetashka Cave in Bulgaria, a sprawling prehistoric complex which humans called home for tens of thousands of years. These days, it is home to bats, about 30,000 of them, as well as rare birds and reptiles. This karst cave was formed by erosion and is now part of a public park. Humans are thought to have sought shelter here as far back as the Early Stone Age, about 70,000 years ago, and many Neolithic artefacts from 6000-4000 BCE have been discovered. Several large openings in the cave cast natural light into the chambers, offering better illumination for photographers and nature lovers alike.

bing-46152.jpg.title: Innenansicht Münchner Nationaltheater Opernhaus, München, Bayern
bing-46152.jpg.headline: Wunder der Akustik!. Innenansicht Münchner Nationaltheater Opernhaus, München, Bayern
bing-46152.jpg.description:
Die Bayerische Staatsoper, ein kulturelles Juwel im Herzen Münchens, verbindet traditionelle Eleganz mit avantgardistischer Kunst. Seit ihrer Gründung im Jahr 1653 hat sich die Oper zu einer international renommierten Bühne entwickelt. Das majestätische Opernhaus am Max-Joseph-Platz beeindruckt seine Besucher mit seiner opulenten Architektur.

Über die Jahrhunderte hinweg wurde das Opernhaus mehrfach renoviert und erweitert. Insbesondere unter König Ludwig II. wurde es im 19. Jahrhundert grundlegend umgestaltet. Im Zweiten Weltkrieg wurde das Opernhaus beschädigt und nach mehreren Restaurierungen 1963 wiedereröffnet.

Im Laufe der Geschichte hat sich hier eine eindrucksvolle Aufführungstradition mit Werken großer Komponisten wie Wolfgang Amadeus Mozart, Richard Wagner und Richard Strauss etabliert. Mehr als 350 Aufführungen pro Jahr ziehen jedes Jahr Tausende von Besuchern aus aller Welt an, um diesen magischen Ort mit seiner spektakulären Akustik zu genießen.

bing-46158.jpg.title: Monarch butterflies, Goleta, California
bing-46158.jpg.headline: Butterfly ballet. Western Monarch Day
bing-46158.jpg.description: Western Monarch Day celebrates a stunning natural phenomenon, the annual migration of thousands of flame-colored butterflies to California. Traveling south to escape the winter weather, they use air currents to help them make journeys of hundreds of miles. They descend to gather in large numbers on eucalyptus trees, like the ones pictured on our homepage today in Goleta, Santa Barbara County. Those gathered to see clusters of butterflies in 100-foot-tall trees might confuse them for clumps of leaves at first. However, as the sun's rays gently fall upon them, their wings will begin to flutter. Bring your binoculars and take the opportunity to witness these winged wonders huddled together. It's truly a sight to behold!

bing-46165.jpg.title: Città di Sanremo di notte
bing-46165.jpg.headline: Chi vincerà il Festival di Sanremo?
bing-46165.jpg.description:
L'attesa è finita, oggi finalmente ricomincia il Festival della canzone italiana, quello che ha reso celebri numerosi artisti del panorama musicale italiano. Sul famoso palco del Teatro Ariston, si sono esibiti personaggi del calibro di Mina, Al Bano e Romina, Riccardo Cocciante, Massimo Ranieri, Vasco Rossi, Zucchero, Ramazzotti, gli Stadio, i Måneskin e tanti altri che hanno reso celebre la canzone italiana nel mondo.

Nato nel 1951, il palco dell'Ariston ha visto esibirsi leggende della musica e altre personalità che includono artisti italiani e internazionali, attori, personaggi televisivi e altri volti noti al grande pubblico. Ogni edizione è un caleidoscopio di emozioni, tra vincitori applauditi e controversie discusse. La kermesse non è solo competizione, ma anche vetrina di talenti emergenti. La sua storia è intrecciata con il tessuto culturale del Paese, e la cittadina ligure si trasforma in un palcoscenico di passioni e tensioni. Sanremo, un fenomeno intramontabile che continua a scrivere la colonna sonora dell'Italia!

bing-46170.jpg.title: Bonsai Rock, Lake Tahoe, Nevada
bing-46170.jpg.headline: Taking root on Bonsai Rock. Bonsai Rock, Lake Tahoe, Nevada
bing-46170.jpg.description: This serene scene shows Lake Tahoe, the largest alpine lake in North America and the second-deepest lake in the US. Peeking out of those misty waters is Bonsai Rock, the unlikely home of four small trees that have taken root in its cracks. Its name was inspired by the Japanese art of growing miniature trees, which are kept in small containers and pruned to control their size. The trees on Bonsai Rock are naturally restricted by the lack of space and nutrients, so no pruning is required. Part of the purpose of bonsai is to provide an opportunity for contemplation, and this tranquil spot high in the Sierra Nevada is the perfect place to relax and explore your thoughts. It is also popular with photographers, especially at sunset.

bing-46180.jpg.title: Figuras feitas pelos indígenas locais de Manaus, Brasil
bing-46180.jpg.headline: Arte indígena ganha cada vez mais espaço
bing-46180.jpg.description:
Em meio à vastidão verde e à biodiversidade sem igual, comunidades indígenas locais compartilham sua cultura com o mundo. Utilizando técnicas passadas entre gerações, esses artistas criam peças que são um mosaico de cores, texturas e simbolismos.

Feitos com materiais naturais, como sementes, madeira, e até mesmo escamas de peixe, cada item é um testemunho de uma cultura rica, histórias e sabedoria ancestral que se entrelaçam em cada trama, pintura e escultura.

Algumas peças levam dias ou até semanas para serem concluídas e muitos desses objetos têm significados simbólicos profundos, como a conexão com espíritos da natureza ou os ensinamentos dos antepassados. Em cada trançado, cada cor, há um diálogo silencioso, mas eloquente, com a natureza.

bing-46182.jpg.title: St. James Tidal Pool, Cape Town, South Africa
bing-46182.jpg.headline: Swimming with the tide. St. James Tidal Pool, Cape Town, South Africa
bing-46182.jpg.description: St. James Beach is a small, sheltered beach on Cape Town's coastline, where vibrant Victorian bathing boxes sit side by side against an azure ocean backdrop. However, it's the St. James Tidal Pool, pictured on our homepage, that steals the spotlight. This protected bathing area, built between rugged rocks, offers crystal-clear waters for a tranquil swimming experience. The pool is warm compared with the ocean, teems with small marine life, and is perfect for floating around without worrying about strong currents. For those who like to stay dry, the beach is perfect for leisurely strolls, soaking up the sun, and observing the rhythmic ebb and flow of the tides.

bing-46194.jpg.title: Mount Hood, Oregon
bing-46194.jpg.headline: A sleeping giant. Mount Hood, Oregon
bing-46194.jpg.description: Mount Hood graces Oregon's skyline with a pointed, snow-capped peak. At nearly 11,250 feet high, this dormant stratovolcano is the tallest mountain in the state, drawing adventurers and nature aficionados alike. With 12 named glaciers and numerous snow fields, Mount Hood offers a wintry playground all year round. It also nurtures ancient forests and provides a haven for wildlife, including cougars and wolves. Over the past 1,800 years, the volcano has erupted three times. While considered dormant, there is still a chance that it could erupt one day.

bing-46196.jpg.title: お城の雪像, 北海道 札幌市
bing-46196.jpg.headline: さっぽろ雪まつりが開催中
bing-46196.jpg.description:
2 月 4 日からさっぽろ雪まつりが開催されています。北海道札幌市の大通公園をはじめとする複数の会場では、さまざまな雪像や氷像が展示されており、すべり台やスノーラフトなどの雪遊びも楽しめます…

さっぽろ雪まつりは、1950 年に札幌の中・高校生が大通公園で雪像を展示したことで始まりました。その後、自衛隊、市民団体、学校などが参加することによって規模が徐々に拡大し、現在では世界三大雪まつりの一つに数えられる有名な祭典になっています。

bing-46197.jpg.title: 灯光秀点亮夜幕中的西安城墙，中国春节
bing-46197.jpg.headline: 准备好庆祝了吗？
bing-46197.jpg.description:
几乎每一年的春节，西安城墙都被装扮得光彩动人，让这座千年古都彰显着更为浓郁的传统中国春节的韵味。而西安城墙的灯会更是给人们带来了绝美的体验感。当百米长灯点亮古城，烟火气息回归，现代城市与古老城市似乎打破了时空感，在夜幕降临以后，灯光璀璨之时，同时展现在眼前。置身其间的人们，似是穿越于古今两个时代，体会着千年的沧桑与繁华。

中国的每个地方，在新春佳节这一晚皆有璀璨夜色，浓烈的年味，这是沸腾的中国年。祝大家春节快乐，新的一年，万事胜意！

bing-46199.jpg.title: Vista del faro de Ribadeo, Galicia, España
bing-46199.jpg.headline: ¡Un brillo diferente!. Faro de Ribadeo, Galicia, España
bing-46199.jpg.description:
En el corazón de la tradición gallega, la imagen majestuosa del Faro de Isla Pancha emerge como centinela del norte, guiando, desde 1859, las esperanzas de los marineros en Ribadeo, Lugo. Este custodio del Atlántico, pensado por Marcelo Sánchez Movellán, persevera entre la bruma con una luz que se proyecta hasta 39 kilómetros mar adentro, dibujando una sinfonía de destellos cada 20 segundos, orquestada para la seguridad de la navegación.

Ahora, mientras los ecos de los tambores de Cádiz aún resuenan con su carnaval, y en Canarias las murgas calientan el ambiente, Galicia se engalana con su Entroido. No hay faro que ilumine mejor el espíritu festivo gallego que el de Isla Pancha, testigo de disfraces y risas, que se mezclan con el vaivén de las olas.

El faro, que conecta con la tierra firme gracias a un puente nacido para economizar custodios, se alza como un emblema de una región donde la tradición y la modernidad conviven en armoniosa dualidad. Con sus más de 160 años de vigía, es el faro de un pueblo que sabe que después de la tempestad, siempre viene la calma... y una buena fiesta.

bing-46204.jpg.title: Praia de Copacabana, Rio de Janeiro, Brasil
bing-46204.jpg.headline: Famosa em todo o mundo
bing-46204.jpg.description:
A famosa praia de Copacabana é uma testemunha viva da história do Carnaval carioca. As celebrações carnavalescas têm uma tradição de mais de 100 anos, quando as margens da baía eram palco de festejos espontâneos.

Ao longo dos anos, Copacabana se tornou o cenário perfeito para uma mistura fascinante de tradições e modernidade. A atmosfera única à beira-mar cria uma experiência inesquecível. Uma celebração que, mais do que entreter, conta a história pulsante do Carnaval carioca.

Desde desfiles de blocos de rua até eventos culturais, o Carnaval do Rio de Janeiro se revela como uma celebração diversificada, transformando a cidade em um palco efervescente de cultura, música e tradição. Seja você um folião ávido por samba ou alguém em busca de experiências culturais únicas, o Carnaval carioca promete encantar a todos com sua energia contagiante e sua capacidade de unir as pessoas em uma festa incomparável.

bing-46206.jpg.title: Pegadung Rock, Lampung, Sumatra, Indonesia
bing-46206.jpg.headline: Rocks and rolling surf. Pegadung Rock, Lampung, Sumatra, Indonesia
bing-46206.jpg.description: An unspoiled landscape carved by nature's raw power, waves crash against Pegadung Rock on the southern coast of the Indonesian island of Sumatra. This remote beach boasts turquoise waters, but it is the striking rocks that steal the show, standing tall against the might of the Indian Ocean. The rock formations, some of which are 33 feet tall, have given rise to various nicknames, among them Gigi Hiu (shark teeth) and Batu Layar (rock screen) Beach. While this beach has no tourist accommodation, the nearby village of Kiluan presents a haven for visitors. For those ready to trade lounging for exploring, this Sumatran treasure awaits.

bing-46209.jpg.title: 中国舞狮，大年初一
bing-46209.jpg.headline: 福起新岁，万事顺意
bing-46209.jpg.description: 炮竹声中辞旧岁，烟花满天迎新春。从年初一开始便进入迎禧接福、拜祭神祖、祈求丰年主题。在春节期间，全国各地均有举行各种庆贺新春活动，带有浓郁的各地地方特色。中国民俗传统，认为舞狮可以驱邪辟鬼。故此每逢喜庆节日，都喜欢敲锣打鼓，舞狮助庆，长盛不衰，历代相传。新的一年，喜气洋洋，万事胜意！

bing-46215.jpg.title: Dunstanburgh Castle, England
bing-46215.jpg.headline: Starstruck. South Downs Dark Skies Festival
bing-46215.jpg.description: No, it's not one of Vincent van Gogh's creations or a galaxy far, far away—it's our galaxy, the Milky Way, over Dunstanburgh Castle in Northumberland. With skyglow, or light pollution, infiltrating even rural areas, faraway stars, meteor showers and other objects in the night sky are disappearing. Thankfully, the International Dark-Sky Association is promoting dark skies to do something about this loss. There are 119 Dark Sky Parks in the world, including the Northumberland National Park, as well as 21 Dark Sky Reserves, seven of which are in the UK. With its 'Bronze Level' darkness, one of the reserves—South Downs National Park—is welcoming people to their Dark Skies Festival starting today. From stargazing sessions to after-dark walks, this star-studded event ending on February 18 has a lot in store.

bing-46217.jpg.title: Chinese New Year Parade, Vancouver, British Columbia, Canada
bing-46217.jpg.headline: Welcome to the Year of the Dragon!. Happy Lunar New Year!
bing-46217.jpg.description: Let's mark the first new moon of the lunar calendar with a celebration! People gather to usher in the Lunar New Year, also known as the Spring Festival or Chinese New Year, which ends 15 days from now with the Lantern Festival. In Chinatown, Vancouver, the streets come alive with the rhythm of drums during the parade, showcasing the traditional lion and dragon dance on the second day of the festival. Visitors can also take in martial arts displays and lively floats. The Lunar New Year is a time for families to come together, and it is responsible for one of the world's largest annual human migrations. Did you know that 2024 heralds the Year of the Dragon, a mighty symbol of nobility, power and success?

bing-46218.jpg.title: Artists performing the dragon dance for Chinese New Year, Luzhou, China
bing-46218.jpg.headline: Enter the dragons. Happy Lunar New Year!
bing-46218.jpg.description: Celebrating the first new moon of the lunar calendar, an estimated 2 billion people gather worldwide to usher in the Lunar New Year with vibrant celebrations and family reunions. The festivities, also known as the Spring Festival or Chinese New Year, last for 15 days, ending with the Lantern Festival. From envelopes to lanterns, red is the dominant color, symbolizing luck and prosperity. Streets come alive with the rhythm of drums as the dragon dance takes center stage. Our homepage today shows a bird's-eye view of the dragons—elongated puppets with shimmering scales, animated by a team of dancers. Lunar New Year is a popular time for families to reunite and is said to be responsible for the world's largest annual human migration. Each year is linked to one of the 12 zodiac animals and 2024 heralds the Year of the Dragon, a symbol of nobility, power, and success.

bing-46219.jpg.title: Giant anteater in the Pantanal, Brazil
bing-46219.jpg.headline: Giant anteater
bing-46219.jpg.description: Behold the giant anteater, whose shaggy-haired appearance is a familiar sight in the Pantanal of Mato Grosso, Brazil. Giant anteaters are adapted to living in a variety of habitats. Although these mammals spend most of the time on the ground, they can climb trees. With powerful, curved claws and a tongue that can reach up to 60 centimetres, giant anteaters specialise in feeding on ants and termites, using their acute sense of smell to find their meal. Anteaters play a role as pest controllers and seed dispersers, so their survival—and the survival of many species—is crucial to keep ecosystems balanced.

bing-46230.jpg.title: Chora, Folegandros Island, Cyclades, Greece
bing-46230.jpg.headline: Elysium on the edge. Folegandros Island, Cyclades, Greece
bing-46230.jpg.description:
Welcome to Folegandros, one of the Greek Cyclades Islands in the Aegean Sea. This picturesque island has changed hands several times during its long history. It is thought it was once home to the Dorians, one of the four major ethnic groups of classical Greece, but it was also ruled for centuries by the Republic of Venice and later the Ottoman Empire. Greece reclaimed it in 1828.

Chora, the island's modern capital, can be seen on our homepage, perched on the edge of a 656-foot cliff with sweeping views of the ocean and surrounding islands. Built by the Venetians in 1212, the town is now a popular tourist destination, with its charming squares and traditional whitewashed churches.

bing-46242.jpg.title: Volcán Alcedo giant tortoises, Isabela Island, Galápagos, Ecuador
bing-46242.jpg.headline: Giants of science. Darwin Day
bing-46242.jpg.description:
When British naturalist Charles Darwin arrived in the Galápagos Islands in 1835, he was already four years into a round-the-world voyage aboard the survey ship HMS Beagle. His observations on the remote volcanic islands in the eastern Pacific Ocean would help him to develop his famous theory of evolution through natural selection. While studying the creatures here, he concluded that many South American species, mainly reptiles and birds that could cross the vast expanse of water, had migrated to the Galápagos and gradually adapted to their surroundings.

Among animals Darwin encountered were Galápagos giant tortoises, like those featured on our homepage. They grow up to 5 feet in length but have different shaped shells, depending on which island they inhabit. The islands are named after these magnificent creatures, 'galápago' meaning freshwater tortoise in Spanish. Today, on International Darwin Day, let's celebrate these gentle giants, which contributed to one of the great scientific discoveries of the 19th century.

bing-46245.jpg.title: L’arche de Port-Blanc, Saint-Pierre-Quiberon, France
bing-46245.jpg.headline: Saint-Pierre-Quiberon, France
bing-46245.jpg.description: Imagine standing on this beach, the sea air filling your nose, as you contemplate this natural arch sculpted by the whims of wind and water. L'Arche de Port-Blanc is a natural, geological feature on the wild coast of Saint-Pierre Quiberon, Brittany, France. The site is the result of marine erosion, which has carved an arch into the cliff. L'Arche de Port-Blanc is only accessible during low tide and has become a sensation among photography enthusiasts. It is not only appealing to those who prefer solitary contemplation, but it also serves as a stunning backdrop for couples seeking a romantic getaway.

bing-46251.jpg.title: Vasant Panchmi celebration in Noida, India
bing-46251.jpg.headline: Offerings for the spring. Vasant Panchmi
bing-46251.jpg.description: Vasant Panchami, also known as Saraswati Puja, is an auspicious Hindu festival that marks the onset of spring in India. The associated festivities vary across regions within religions, with each community adding its own unique flavour to the celebration. The observance of the Vasant Utsava on Panchami itself is strategically timed, aligning with the belief that any season's transition period spans 40 days. For countless individuals, this occasion is a devoted celebration of the goddess Saraswati, revered as the embodiment of knowledge, language, music and different art representations. Goddess Saraswati stands as a symbol of creative energy and power in its myriad forms, encapsulating both the essence of longing and love. The exuberant celebration extends to culinary customs, where some infuse saffron into rice, creating a golden feast as part of the elaborate rituals.
bing-46251.jpg.copyright: © Burhaan Kinu/Hindustan Times via Getty Image

bing-46258.jpg.title: Berlinale, roter Teppich am Potsdamer Platz, Berlin
bing-46258.jpg.headline: Der rote Teppich ist ausgerollt!. Berlinale 2024
bing-46258.jpg.description:
Dieses Jahr findet die 74. Berlinale statt. Wir können es kaum erwarten. Wissen Sie schon, welche Filme dieses Jahr gezeigt werden? Wenn Sie Filmfan sind, wissen Sie sicher, wie lange Martin Scorsese auf seinen Oscar warten musste. Vielleicht nicht ganz so lange wie auf den Preis der Berlinale, denn in diesem Jahr bekommt er den Goldenen Ehrenbären für sein Lebenswerk. Er hat ihn verdient. Wir gönnen ihm die deutsche Trophäe.

Die Berlinale ist in Europa neben Cannes und Venedig eines der wichtigsten Filmfestivals. Im Gegensatz zu den beiden anderen Festivals ist die Berlinale das jüngste unter ihnen. Das erste Festival fand 1951 mitten in der Nachkriegszeit statt und zeichnet sich seit je her durch Offenheit, künstlerische Vielfalt und gesellschaftliche Themen aus. Es hat vielen Filmemachern aus der ganzen Welt eine Bühne geboten, um Geschichten zu erzählen und kulturelle Brücken zu schlagen. Wir können es kaum erwarten, uns in den Sessel zu setzen und Popcorn zu knabbern. Was ist mit Ihnen?

bing-46259.jpg.title: Red-crowned crane bowing to his mate in Hokkaido, Japan
bing-46259.jpg.headline: The dance of romance. Valentine's Day
bing-46259.jpg.description: Love is in the air as Valentine's Day arrives! These red-crowned cranes, seen in the reed marshes and frozen lakes of Hokkaido Island, Japan, know how to turn on the charm. The graceful birds call in unison and bow to each other as part of their captivating mating dance. Once a mate is chosen, the pair develop a lifelong bond, a trait that has helped make them a symbol of longevity, fidelity, and good fortune in Japanese culture. These gentle creatures were also the inspiration for the traditional origami crane. According to legend, folding a thousand cranes can grant wishes.

bing-46260.jpg.title: Mardi Gras beads in the Marigny, New Orleans
bing-46260.jpg.headline: Let the good times roll!. Mardi Gras
bing-46260.jpg.description:
Get ready to revel—Mardi Gras is here! Also called Fat Tuesday or Shrove Tuesday, the holiday was originally celebrated to live life to the fullest before fasting and giving up other indulgences for Lent. For some, it's just an excuse to party.

Fat Tuesday celebrations take place around the world, particularly in areas with strong French influences. New Orleans is particularly linked with the festival and hosts a massive celebration that can last up to eight weeks, depending on when Easter falls. Mardi Gras parades are held from the official start of Mardi Gras on King's Day, January 6. Social clubs, known as krewes, hold parades on assigned schedules and routes. Crowds gather along the way, hoping to catch coins, cups, and beads thrown by float riders, a tradition that started in the 1880s. Ready to make merry and join the parade?

bing-46272.jpg.title: Sfilata dei carri di Carnevale di Viareggio, Toscana, Italia
bing-46272.jpg.headline: Passami i crostoli!
bing-46272.jpg.description:
Il Carnevale di Viareggio, in Toscana, è una festa straordinaria e colorata che attira visitatori da tutto il mondo per la sua spettacolare sfilata di carri allegorici. Ogni anno, le vie della pittoresca località marittima si trasformano in un teatro a cielo aperto dove enormi ed elaborati carri di Carnevale sfilano, estasiando gli spettatori di ogni età. Questi carri allegorici, veri e propri capolavori artistici, sono spesso satirici e critici nei confronti degli eventi sociali del momento, creando un mix unico di intrattenimento e riflessione.

La maestria artigianale e l’originalità dei costumi rendono la sfilata di Viareggio un'esperienza straordinaria, che celebra la tradizione carnevalesca italiana con una vivacità unica nel suo genere. Indossate quindi le vostre maschere di Carnevale e portate i coriandoli, è ora di sfilare a ritmo di musica!

bing-46278.jpg.title: Hippopotamus mother and calf, South Luangwa National Park, Zambia
bing-46278.jpg.headline: Happy Hippo Day!. World Hippo Day
bing-46278.jpg.description:
All eyes are on hippos today! The world's third-largest land mammals after elephants and white rhinos, hippopotamuses are found in rivers and lakes throughout sub-Saharan Africa. Despite their size—they can weigh up to 4 tons—they are vulnerable to various threats, including habitat loss.

The peeping calf in today's image is still under the watchful eye of its mother and will continue to be so until nursing ends at about 8 months. These chubby mammals might seem cute, but their strong jaws, large teeth, and aggressive behavior make them one of the world's most dangerous wild animals. So, admire them from a safe distance—despite their short legs, they are also fast runners!

bing-46286.jpg.title: Station de Saint-Jean-d'Arves, Savoie, France
bing-46286.jpg.headline: Comme un air de montagne. Station de ski de Saint-Jean-d'Arves, Savoie
bing-46286.jpg.description: Plongez dans la magie de l'hiver à la station de ski de Saint-Jean-d’Arves, nichée au cœur des Alpes françaises. Entre ses pistes variées, qui satisfont tant les mordus de descente que les novices, et son ambiance authentique avec ses chalets montagnards, cette destination offre bien plus qu'une simple expérience de ski. Après une journée pleine d'adrénaline sur les pistes, découvrez la culture savoyarde en dégustant des spécialités locales et détendez-vous en explorant les sentiers en raquettes ou en vous prélassant dans les spas. Rejoignez les sommets pour vous créer des souvenirs inoubliables !

bing-46290.jpg.title: Female pyrrhuloxia perched on cactus plant, Texas
bing-46290.jpg.headline: Make every bird count. Great Backyard Bird Count
bing-46290.jpg.description:
For the next four days, birdwatchers all over the world will be taking part in the Great Backyard Bird Count. Bird lovers will identify the feathered friends they see or hear in their area and report their findings. The data helps scientists protect birds by providing information about how populations and habitats change over time.

In today's image is a pyrrhuloxia—or desert cardinal—a songbird that lives in the deserts of northern Mexico and the American Southwest. Locals might be lucky enough to see one of these red and gray birds; they often visit backyards in search of seeds, or to eat the fruit from shrubs and cacti.

bing-46294.jpg.title: Kailasa temple in Ellora caves complex in India
bing-46294.jpg.headline: A megalithic wonder. Kailasa temple in Ellora caves
bing-46294.jpg.description: Kailasa temple in Ellora Caves near the Aurangabad district of Maharashtra, is celebrated for its colossal size, intricate stone architecture and artistic finesse evident in its sculpture. This temple stretches along a basalt cliff for over two kilometres and is intricately carved. Towering above the surrounding landscape, the sanctuary's peak reaches an impressive height of 32 metres above the court below. A legend weaves through the stones of Ellora, recounting the tale of a king from Alajapura. After being miraculously cured from a terrible illness by a sacred bath, the king and his queen pledged to construct a temple in honour of Lord Shiva.

bing-46299.jpg.title: Whitby Abbey, North Yorkshire, England
bing-46299.jpg.headline: Where the past comes to life. Jorvik Viking Festival
bing-46299.jpg.description: Grab your iron helmet, shield and axe, and travel back in time to the age of Norse sagas at the Jorvik Viking Festival! The nine-day event, which started on February 12, continues today with a Viking procession in Coppergate. Witness the ancient city of York come alive with the thunder of war drums and the clamour of market traders. Meanwhile, a short trip to the haunting beauty of Whitby Abbey, pictured here, offers a peaceful contrast. This Gothic masterpiece has withstood the North Sea's winds since the 7th century, whispering tales of monastic life and inspiring Bram Stoker's classic novel 'Dracula.' In the 9th century, it is said that the Abbey was abandoned because of raids from the Vikings. Whether you're a history buff or crave unique experiences, the Jorvik Viking Festival is sure to transport you to an era long past but never forgotten.

bing-46302.jpg.title: The Alvin Ailey American Dance Theater rehearsing 'Uptown,' 2009, New York
bing-46302.jpg.headline: Celebrating Black history. Black History Month
bing-46302.jpg.description: As we celebrate Black History Month, we're taking a moment to highlight an institution in the world of dance—the Alvin Ailey American Dance Theater in New York City. Founded by the visionary choreographer Alvin Ailey in 1958, it fuses elements of modern dance, ballet, jazz, and theater. The company's performances demonstrate the importance of artistic expression in preserving and celebrating Black culture in America. Congress described it as a 'vital American cultural ambassador to the world' in 2008.

bing-46303.jpg.title: The Pragser Wildsee in the Dolomites, South Tyrol, Italy
bing-46303.jpg.headline: The Pragser Wildsee in the Dolomites, Italy
bing-46303.jpg.description: In every season, Pragser Wildsee enchants travellers with its ever-changing allure. The lake, also known as Lago di Braies, is nestled in the Italian Dolomites in Fanes Senes Braies Nature Park, a UNESCO World Heritage Site. This enchanting lake is surrounded by mountains, with an elevation of 1,469 metres above sea level and boasting a maximum depth of 36 metres. During winter, Pragser Wildsee transforms into a mesmerising vision as ice and snow blanket its surface, while in summer, it beckons hikers to embark on adventures, with rowboats available for those who wish to get out on the water.

bing-46314.jpg.title: Sperm whale pod surfacing, Dominica
bing-46314.jpg.headline: Taking a breather. World Whale Day
bing-46314.jpg.description: Ahoy there, giants of the sea! World Whale Day is surfacing, along with these sperm whales off the coast of the Caribbean island of Dominica. Established in 1980 in Maui, the day originally aimed to celebrate the humpback whales in Hawaiian waters but has evolved into a global event for all 92 whale species.

bing-46323.jpg.title: Puerto de la Cruz, Tenerife, Spain
bing-46323.jpg.headline: Vibrant colours all year round!. Puerto de la Cruz, Tenerife, Spain
bing-46323.jpg.description: Sun-kissed beaches, colourful buildings, clear waters and rich history—there's something special going on in the city of Puerto de la Cruz. Located on Tenerife, the largest of Spain's Canary Islands, it stared out as a fishing village.  The city's centre is full of charming streets and historical buildings. For those seeking sun, sea and sand, Playa Jardín is the city's answer. This black volcanic sand beach, designed by the renowned architect César Manrique, offers lush gardens, unique sculptures and views of the world's third tallest volcano, Mount Teide. Other landmarks here include Lago Martiánez, a complex of seawater pools offering a scenic retreat, and Loro Parque, a world-famous zoo and conservation centre. So, take a moment, savour the image and let your imagination set sail to this lively port town!

bing-46326.jpg.title: Lincoln Memorial, Washington, DC
bing-46326.jpg.headline: A tribute at twilight. Presidents Day
bing-46326.jpg.description: The United States of America has had 46 commanders in chief, and today, the third Monday of February, we commemorate their legacies. Initially established to honor George Washington's birthday, Presidents Day has evolved into a celebration of all presidents. Revered among them is Abraham Lincoln, a towering figure in American history, who guided the country through the Civil War and abolished slavery in America. The Lincoln Memorial, seen in today's image, overlooks the Reflecting Pool at the west end of the National Mall in Washington, DC. Designed in a neoclassical style, the memorial is a poignant destination for those seeking to connect with American history during Presidents Day, and beyond.

bing-46338.jpg.title: Kinder Scout at sunrise, Peak District National Park, England
bing-46338.jpg.headline: A park for the people. Kinder Scout, Peak District National Park, England
bing-46338.jpg.description: Within the vast expanse of England's Peak District National Park lies Kinder Scout Nature Reserve, the site of an historic people's protest. At around 2,087 feet, Kinder Scout is the park's highest point and its rugged moorlands and windswept plateaus have drawn walkers and nature enthusiasts for generations. In 1932, it was the stage for a 'mass trespass,' in which hundreds of people on foot protested for public access to these lands. At the time, many areas of open countryside were closed to the British public. This act of civil disobedience prompted much public sympathy, which eventually led to the establishment of the UK's first national parks. The Peak District National Park was the first, designated in April 1951, ensuring that these hills and valleys would be preserved for future generations to enjoy.

bing-46350.jpg.title: Firefall at Horsetail Fall, Yosemite National Park, California
bing-46350.jpg.headline: The flaming. Yosemite National Park, California
bing-46350.jpg.description: Fancy witnessing a fiery waterfall? The seemingly impossible can be found at this time of year on the eastern side of El Capitan, Yosemite National Park's famous rock face. Horsetail Fall is a seasonal waterfall that flows only when there has been plenty of snowfall, and when temperatures have been warm enough to melt it. For a couple of weeks in February, if skies are clear, water is flowing, and the sun shines at just the right angle, the long, slender waterfall takes on a glowing, flame-hued appearance. Hundreds gather in Yosemite Valley to see this mesmerizing natural spectacle. The phenomenon has earned the moniker 'firefall,' an homage to the historic Yosemite Firefall, a manmade event from the top of the park's Glacier Point that took place between 1872 to 1968. Eventually, park rangers decided that dumping embers over a cliff onto the land below wasn't the brightest idea.

bing-46356.jpg.title: Wundervoll gefrorene Seifenblase
bing-46356.jpg.headline: Zauberhafter Baumschmuck. Wundervoll gefrorene Seifenblase
bing-46356.jpg.description: In der Stille des Wintermorgens, steht diese zarte Blase, gefroren in der Zeit auf einem Tannenzweig als perfektes Emblem des Winters. Was ist mit Ihnen? Genießen Sie den Winter oder zählen Sie schon die Tage, die bis zu dem Frühlingsanfang fehlen? Unserer Meinung nach hat jede Jahreszeit ihre Magie, man muss sie nur sehen wollen. Ein Spaziergang durch die verschneite Natur ist wie eine Reise in eine verzauberte Welt. Unter dem sanften Knirschen des Schnees betreten wir eine stille Oase der Ruhe und die Sonne, die auf den Eiskristallen glitzert, versetzt die Welt in Harmonie. Entfliehen Sie dem Alltag und entdecken Sie die Schönheit des Einfachen. Der Schnee bedeckt die Welt in einem reinen, friedlichen Weiß und die Wanderung wird zu einem poetischen Tanz im Rhythmus der Natur.

bing-46358.jpg.title: Vallée de Chamonix, Haute-Savoie, France
bing-46358.jpg.headline: Une vallée connue dans le monde entier. Chamonix, Haute-Savoie
bing-46358.jpg.description: Bienvenue à Chamonix, une ville de montagne, qui vous enchantera par sa beauté naturelle et son charme authentique. Située dans les Alpes françaises, c’est une destination de choix pour les amateurs de sports d’hiver, de randonnée, d’escalade et de parapente. Mais Chamonix est bien plus qu’une simple station de ski. C’est une ville dynamique et cosmopolite qui offre une multitude d’activités culturelles, gastronomiques et festives. Vous pourrez visiter le musée Alpin, admirer la vue panoramique depuis l’Aiguille du Midi, déguster les spécialités locales dans les restaurants et les marchés, ou encore participer aux événements annuels tels que le Marathon du Mont-Blanc ou le Festival de Jazz. Chamonix est une ville qui vous surprendra à chaque coin de rue et qui vous donnera envie de revenir encore et encore. Alors, qu’attendez-vous pour la découvrir ?

bing-46362.jpg.title: Bathing boxes at Brighton Beach, Melbourne, Victoria, Australia
bing-46362.jpg.headline: A bonanza of beach huts. Bathing boxes at Brighton Beach, Australia
bing-46362.jpg.description: The 'bathing boxes' on Brighton Beach, Melbourne, beam with a rainbow of colors against golden sands, the ocean, and the city skyline. A popular tourist attraction, they first popped up on Brighton's coastline in 1860, providing somewhere for swimmers to change into their bathing suits. They have been moved, repaired, and added to since then, and while they each have their own distinctive coat of paint, the bathing boxes are built in the same traditional style. Despite facing the threat of removal over the years, these vibrant coast guards remain, adding a splash of color to the beach, and providing their owners with somewhere to sit and enjoy the view.

bing-46364.jpg.title: 朝焼けに輝く富士山と山中湖, 山梨県
bing-46364.jpg.headline: 今日は富士山の日
bing-46364.jpg.description:
今日 2 月 23 日は天皇誕生日で祝日ですが、2 （ふ） 2 （じ） 3 （さん）で、「富士山の日」でもあります。この日を祝して、朝焼けに輝く富士山とその麓に広がる美しい湖、山中湖の風景をお届けします…

山中湖は、山梨県南都留郡山中湖村にある淡水湖で、富士五湖最大の面積を誇り、また標高が最も高い位置にあります。湖の周辺は、朝夕の富士山の風景が美しく、特に湖面に映る逆さ富士は多くの写真家や観光客を魅了しています。

bing-46374.jpg.title: Haghartsin Monastery, Dilijan National Park, Armenia
bing-46374.jpg.headline: Where eagles dance. Haghartsin Monastery, Armenia
bing-46374.jpg.description: Hidden among the forests of northern Armenia, Haghartsin Monastery is a gem of medieval Armenian architecture. Surrounded by the lush landscapes of Dilijan National Park, the monastery complex consists of several ornate structures, including the Church of the Holy Mother of God, St. Gregory's Church, and St. Stepanos' Church. The buildings date back to the 10th century and are adorned with intricately carved stone monuments, crossing arches, and other decorative details, showcasing the skilled craftsmanship of the era. Haghartsin, which translates to 'dance of the eagles,' offers a serene escape for those seeking to connect with the country's rich history. A sense of timelessness pervades as you wander through its quiet courtyards and explore the forested surroundings.

bing-46380.jpg.title: Hänsel und Gretel Haus in Oberammergau, Bayern
bing-46380.jpg.headline: Märchen oder Wirklichkeit?. Hänsel und Gretel Haus in Oberammergau, Bayern
bing-46380.jpg.description:
Heute wäre der 238. Geburtstag von Wilhelm Grimm. Obwohl zwei Jahrhunderte vergangen sind, bleiben seine Werke und Ideen zeitlos aktuell.  Zusammen mit seinem Bruder Jacob bildete er ein unvergleichliches Duo in der Welt der Literatur. Beide sind weltweit für ihre Märchensammlungen bekannt. Doch vor allem Wilhelm zeichnete sich als besonders akribischer und kreativer Geist aus. Er war nicht nur Sammler von Märchen, sondern auch ein kluger Analytiker der deutschen Sprache und Volkskunde. Er arbeitete an wichtigen deutschen Wörterbüchern mit und hinterließ sein Vermächtnis sowohl in der deutschen Literatur als auch in der Sprachwissenschaft.

Wussten Sie, dass die Brüder Jura studiert haben? Nach ihrem Studium, das nur Wilhelm abschloss, wurden beide in die Gruppe der „Heidelberger Romantiker“ aufgenommen. Zu ihnen gehörten unter anderem Brentano, von Arnim und Görres. Ob sie dort ihre Inspiration fanden? Zeitlose Märchen wie „Rapunzel“, „Hänsel und Gretel“, „Rotkäppchen“ und „Die Bremer Stadtmusikanten“ sind nur einige der Märchen, die in die Geschichte der Kinderliteratur eingegangen sind. Nun eine spontane Frage. Erkennen Sie das Häuschen auf dem heutigen Bild? Aus welchem Märchen stammt es?

bing-46381.jpg.title: Due verdoni che litigano mentre nevica, Italia
bing-46381.jpg.headline: Questo posto è mio!
bing-46381.jpg.description:
Gli uccelli Verdoni, noti anche come Carduelis chloris, sono una specie comune in Italia, particolarmente diffusi nelle zone boschive e negli ambienti aperti ricchi di alberi e arbusti. Riconoscibili per il loro piumaggio verde oliva e giallo brillante, i Verdoni sono apprezzati non solo per la loro bellezza visiva, ma anche per il loro canto melodioso, che può essere udito soprattutto durante la primavera e l'estate quando si accoppiano e reclamano il proprio territorio.

Questi uccelli sono prevalentemente granivori, alimentandosi di semi, bacche e talvolta anche di insetti, e sono spesso avvistati nei giardini, nei parchi e lungo i sentieri. Con il loro volo leggero e agile, i Verdoni sono una presenza vivace e colorata negli ecosistemi italiani, contribuendo alla biodiversità e alla ricchezza avifaunistica del paese. Tuttavia, come molte altre specie di uccelli, anche i Verdoni affrontano minacce come la perdita di habitat e il cambiamento climatico, sottolineando l'importanza della conservazione degli ambienti naturali per garantire la loro sopravvivenza.

bing-46382.jpg.title: Le Ballon d'Alsace, Territoire de Belfort, France
bing-46382.jpg.headline: La plus grande ferme de France ouvre ses portes !. Salon International de l'Agriculture
bing-46382.jpg.description: Culminant à 1424 mètres, le Grand-Ballon est une montagne située dans le massif des Vosges. Il est connu pour sa beauté naturelle et ses activités de plein air. Le Ballon d'Alsace se trouve également à proximité du Territoire de Belfort, le plus petit département de France en termes de superficie. Tout comme le reste des régions, ce territoire mythique sera présent lors du célébrissime Salon de l’Agriculture, l’un des évènements les plus attendus de l’année. Il offre aux agriculteurs l'opportunité de présenter leur travail, tandis que les visiteurs peuvent découvrir les produits locaux et les animaux de la ferme. Il sert aussi de lieu de rencontres et d'échanges entre les professionnels et le grand public.  Le salon propose diverses animations et activités pour les enfants et les adultes, telles que des dégustations, des ateliers pédagogiques, des concours et des expositions.

bing-46386.jpg.title: Almond trees in full bloom, California
bing-46386.jpg.headline: Whispers of spring. Almond trees in full bloom, California
bing-46386.jpg.description: In the sun-kissed orchards of the Golden State, almonds reign supreme, enticing the taste buds and adorning the natural surroundings. California grows about 80% of the world's almonds and 100% of those produced commercially in the United States.
