Le chevreuil d’Europe est le plus petit des cervidés européens. Reconnaissable à sa silhouette fine et élancée, il arbore une robe brun-gris en automne et rousse au printemps. Les mâles, appelés brocards, portent des bois droits pouvant atteindre 30 cm de haut. Les femelles, quant à elles, ne portent pas de bois et sont appelées chevrettes. La population de chevreuils en France a connu une forte hausse au cours des dernières décennies. Entre 1973 et 2023, elle a été multipliée par 11, atteignant plus d’1,5 million d’individus.

Malgré leur taille modeste, ils contribuent à l’équilibre de nos écosystèmes forestiers, même s’ils sont parfois confondus avec d’autres espèces comme le cerf ou la biche. En été, lorsque le soleil filtre à travers les feuillages, prenez le temps d’observer ces jeunes faons gambadés !

bing-48318.jpg.title: Three Natural Bridges, Wulong Karst National Geology Park, China
bing-48318.jpg.headline: Towering over Wulong. Three Natural Bridges, Wulong Karst, China
bing-48318.jpg.description: Carved by nature over centuries, the Three Natural Bridges tower over a deep gorge in Wulong Karst. This part of China is known for its karst landscape, which includes towering arches, extensive caves, and other rock formations. These limestone bridges are named after three dragons: Tianlong (Sky Dragon), Heilong (Black Dragon), and Qinglong (Azure Dragon), which is the tallest at 922 feet. Visitors can explore the mossy gorge beneath and the wider Wulong Karst National Geology Park, including the 9,337-foot Furong Cave with its huge limestone stalactites. Standing beneath these magnificent natural bridges, you can't help but be humbled by the sheer power of time and nature.

bing-48323.jpg.title: Romería Vikinga, Galicia
bing-48323.jpg.headline: Romería Vikinga. Romería Vikinga, Galicia
bing-48323.jpg.description:
La Romería Vikinga de Catoira, celebrada en Pontevedra, Galicia, mezcla historia, cultura y entretenimiento en un entorno pintoresco. Iniciada en 1960, conmemora las legendarias incursiones vikingas de los siglos IX y X. El festival destaca por las espectaculares recreaciones de los desembarcos vikingos en las tierras del río Ulla, sus feroces batallas y la vida medieval. Los participantes crean una atmósfera auténtica y vibrante al vestirse con elaborados atuendos de la época. Durante todo el día, se disfrutan mercados medievales, comida tradicional gallega y cautivadoras actuaciones folclóricas. Más que una fiesta, es una valiosa plataforma educativa sobre la fascinante historia vikinga y medieval de Galicia.

a celebración promueve la conservación de las majestuosas Torres del Oeste y otros elementos históricos, subrayando la importancia de la región en la historia europea. Como dice el refrán gallego, "Onde hai patrón, non manda mariñeiro", reflejando la resistencia gallega, algo que se ejemplifica en la imagen de hoy con la pintoresca ermita de Nuestra Señora de la Lanzada, rodeada por una antigua fortaleza defensiva clave frente a los temibles piratas vikingos, normandos y árabes.

bing-48324.jpg.title: Sellin Seebrücke, Sellin, Rügen
bing-48324.jpg.headline: Ein echtes Nordlicht. Sellin Seebrücke, Sellin, Rügen
bing-48324.jpg.description:
Die Seebrücke Sellin auf der Insel Rügen ist ein Wahrzeichen und ein beliebtes Touristenziel. Ursprünglich 1906 erbaut, wurde sie nach mehreren Sturmschäden in den 1920er Jahren restauriert. Von 1950 bis 1970 beherbergte die Brücke ein beliebtes Tanzlokal, bevor sie 1978 komplett abgerissen wurde. Erst in den 1990er Jahren wurde die Seebrücke nach dem ursprünglichen Vorbild wieder aufgebaut. Mit einer Länge von 394 Metern ragt sie weit in die Ostsee hinein und bietet atemberaubende Ausblicke auf die Küste und das Meer. Die Brücke ist bekannt für ihre prächtige Architektur, insbesondere den markanten Pavillon, der im Stil der Bäderarchitektur gestaltet ist. Im Kaiserpavillon erwartet Sie ein exklusives Restaurant mit kulinarischen Genüssen und einem fantastischen Blick auf die Ostsee.  Unterhalb der Brücke befindet sich eine Tauchgondel, die es Besuchern ermöglicht, die Unterwasserwelt der Ostsee zu erkunden.

Die Seebrücke ist zudem der Ausgangspunkt eines beliebten Wanderweges, der zu den nahegelegenen Klippen und Stränden führt. Jährlich zieht sie Tausende von Besuchern an, die die Kombination aus Geschichte, Architektur und Natur genießen. Die nächtliche Beleuchtung der Brücke, wie auf unserem heutigen Bild zu sehen, verleiht ihr einen ganz besonderen Charme und macht sie zu einem romantischen Ort für abendliche Spaziergänge.
bing-48324.jpg.copyright: © SW Travel Imagery/Alamy Foto de stoc

bing-48328.jpg.title: Diversos Preguiças-de-três-dedos, Amazônia, Brasil
bing-48328.jpg.headline: Dia de descanso
bing-48328.jpg.description: Descubra o sereno mundo do bicho-preguiça de três dedos, um verdadeiro mestre da paciência na exuberante tapeçaria das florestas tropicais. Navegando pelos ramos com uma calma inabalável, esse curioso animal vive uma vida invejável, pendurado de cabeça para baixo com a ajuda de suas garras curvas e robustas. Capaz de girar a cabeça em 270°, ele observa o mundo com um olhar suave e despretensioso. Curiosamente, apesar de seu ritmo lento, o bicho-preguiça é um excelente nadador, capaz de atravessar rios com habilidade. Sua dieta vegetariana, rica em folhas, não é suficiente para grande energia, por isso ele economiza seus movimentos - inclusive fazendo suas necessidades apenas uma vez por semana!

bing-48330.jpg.title: Impala and red-billed oxpecker, South Africa
bing-48330.jpg.headline: You've got a friend in me. Friendship Day
bing-48330.jpg.description: Friendship comes in all shapes and sizes. This impala and the red-billed oxpecker, pictured in South Africa, both get something out of buddying up. The oxpecker gets food by eating ticks from the impala's skin, while the impala gets to stay clean.

bing-48342.jpg.title: Lavender field, Hertfordshire, England
bing-48342.jpg.headline: A sea of purple. Lavender field, Hertfordshire, England
bing-48342.jpg.description: This lavender landscape stretching over fields in the English county of Hertfordshire is the quintessential summer scene. A member of the mint family, lavender has been popular through various civilizations. It was used by the Egyptians for mummification; traces of lavender were discovered in the tomb of Tutankhamun. It was also treasured by the Romans for its healing and cleansing properties.

bing-48344.jpg.title: 巨大な吹き流し, 宮城県 仙台市
bing-48344.jpg.headline: 今日から仙台七夕まつり
bing-48344.jpg.description:
今日 8 月 6 日から 8 日の 3 日間、宮城県仙台市で「仙台七夕まつり」が行われます。その歴史は古く、仙台藩祖伊達政宗公の時代から続く行事ともいわれています。また、東北三大祭りの一つに数えられ、その規模と華やかさで多くの人々を魅了しています…

期間中、仙台市内各地で商売繁盛や健康長寿などの願いを込めた色とりどりの笹飾りなどが飾られます。特に、一番町や中央通などのアーケード、仙台駅周辺では、竹竿に吊るされた非常に豪華絢爛な「吹き流し」が見られます。

bing-48354.jpg.title: Molokini Crater, Maui, Hawaii
bing-48354.jpg.headline: A very pleasant crescent. Molokini Crater, Maui, Hawaii
bing-48354.jpg.description: Today we're at Molokini Crater. This pleasant crescent in the Pacific Ocean lies in the 'Alalākeiki Channel between the Hawaiian islands of Maui and Kaho'olawe. The islet is all that remains of a volcano that erupted about 230,000 years ago. According to Hawaiian mythology, Pele the fire goddess was in love with a man named Mo'o. The trouble was that Mo'o was in love with another woman. Pele's revenge was typically violent: She cut her rival in two, her body becoming Molokini, while her head became Pu'u Olai, a cinder cone on Maui.

bing-48366.jpg.title: St. Joseph North Pier Inner and Outer Lights, Michigan
bing-48366.jpg.headline: More than nautical necessity. St. Joseph North Pier Inner and Outer Lights, Michigan
bing-48366.jpg.description: Amid dusky hues, lighthouses mark where a Great Lake meets a river. Two piers were built on Lake Michigan, one either side of the mouth of the St. Joseph River to help protect ships sailing upstream. In the early 20th century, a lighthouse was built at the end of each pier; the St. Joseph North Pier Inner and Outer Lights, pictured here.

bing-48378.jpg.title: Spotted owlet, Bangkok, Thailand
bing-48378.jpg.headline: Big stare for a little owl. Spotted owlet, Bangkok, Thailand
bing-48378.jpg.description: Could you win a staring contest with this spotted owlet? These primarily nocturnal owls are sometimes mobbed during the day by birds trying to defend their territory from predators. With their piercing yellow eyes, the small owls will stare down intruders, bob their heads, and emit a loud 'chirurrr-chirurrr-chirurrr' screech, sometimes likened to laughter or chuckling.

bing-48387.jpg.title: Clifton Suspension Bridge during the Bristol Balloon Fiesta, Bristol
bing-48387.jpg.headline: Up, up and away. Bristol International Balloon Fiesta
bing-48387.jpg.description:
Ever dreamt of seeing the sky filled with colourful hot air balloons? Well, the Bristol International Balloon Fiesta is here to lift your spirits—quite literally. This annual gala, which is one of Europe's largest hot air balloon events, will feature multiple balloon ascents from today until August 11 at Ashton Court estate in Bristol. The Bristol International Balloon Fiesta began in 1979, thanks to a Scottish balloon enthusiast, Don Cameron. From its humble beginnings, it has grown into a massive event attracting hundreds of thousands of spectators. During the festival there are multiple 'mass ascents,' where up to 100 balloons take to the skies simultaneously.

The 'night glow' events are another crowd favourite. Balloons are tethered to the ground and illuminated after dark to music, creating a magical display of light and sound. There's also live music, food stalls and even an arts and crafts market. For the adrenaline junkies, there are air displays featuring planes and motorbike stunts. Feeling competitive? There are balloon races and even the British National Hot Air Balloon Championships. So, ready for lift-off?

bing-48390.jpg.title: Inca ruin of Sacsayhuamán near Cusco, Peru
bing-48390.jpg.headline: Celebrating Indigenous culture. International Day of the World's Indigenous Peoples
bing-48390.jpg.description: Today we are celebrating the heritage and culture of native populations worldwide. There are some 5,000 Indigenous cultures in 90 countries around the world, from Samoa and Greenland to New Zealand and Nepal. One of the major challenges they face is the loss of their languages: It's estimated that of the 4,000 Indigenous languages in the world, around 2,600 are in danger of becoming extinct.

bing-48396.jpg.title: Luftaufnahme der Elbphilharmonie in Hamburg
bing-48396.jpg.headline: Eine kulturelle Wiedergeburt. Elbphilharmonie
bing-48396.jpg.description:
Die Elbphilharmonie in Hamburg, oft liebevoll „Elphi“ genannt, ist ein Meisterwerk moderner Architektur und ein Symbol für die kulturelle Wiedergeburt der Stadt. Das beeindruckende Bauwerk, entworfen von den Schweizer Architekten Herzog & de Meuron, erhebt sich majestätisch über dem Hafen und kombiniert historische und moderne Elemente. Errichtet auf dem ehemaligen Kaispeicher A, einem Lagerhaus aus den 1960er Jahren, bewahrt das Fundament aus rotem Backstein die Vergangenheit und wird von einer markanten, wellenförmigen Glasfassade gekrönt, die an die Wellen der Elbe erinnert.

Das Herzstück der Elbphilharmonie ist der Große Saal mit Platz für 2.100 Zuhörer. Die außergewöhnliche Akustik, konzipiert von Yasuhisa Toyota, einem weltweit anerkannten Akustikexperten, macht jedes Konzert zu einem unvergesslichen Klangerlebnis. Neben dem Großen Saal gibt es zwei weitere Säle, ein Hotel, Restaurants und eine öffentlich zugängliche Plaza mit atemberaubendem Blick auf die Stadt und den Hafen. Seit ihrer Eröffnung im Januar 2017 hat die Elbphilharmonie zahlreiche Besucher aus aller Welt angezogen und die kulturelle Identität Hamburgs gestärkt.

bing-48397.jpg.title: Monte Argentario, Toscana, Italia
bing-48397.jpg.headline: Notti magiche
bing-48397.jpg.description:
Siete pronti per la notte magica di San Lorenzo? Avete già trovato lo spot ideale per poter osservare le stelle cadenti? Noi vi consigliamo luoghi lontani dalla città e da centri densamente abitati dove l’inquinamento luminoso può influire negativamente su questa esperienza. Un posto ideale potrebbe essere quello che potete ammirare nella immagine di oggi, il Monte Argentario in Toscana, che si affaccia sul Mar Tirreno. Da qui potrete godere di una vista mozzafiato ed ammirare le Perseidi, lo sciame meteorico, rendendo questa notte davvero indimenticabile.

Sapete per quale motivo si chiama Notte di San Lorenzo? La tradizione popolare associa questo fenomeno al martirio di San Lorenzo, un diacono romano vissuto nel III secolo d.C., i cui “fuochi” si dice, illuminino il cielo in questa notte speciale. Tuttavia, l’evento ha una forte componente scientifica: le Perseidi sono frammenti della cometa Swift-Tuttle, che entrando nell’atmosfera terreste, si incendiano creando scie luminose. Che sia per scienza o che sia per mito, questa notte invita a connettersi e riflettere con la natura sotto a un cielo stellato. E voi, avete già espresso un desiderio?

bing-48402.jpg.title: Joshua Tree National Park, California
bing-48402.jpg.headline: Joshua under a starry blanket. Joshua Tree National Park, California
bing-48402.jpg.description: California's Joshua Tree National Park has a history that began way before it was made a national monument on August 10, 1936. Located where the Mojave and Colorado Deserts meet, it has been home to various cultures for thousands of years. Its earliest known residents were people from the Pinto Culture, who lived here from 8000 to 4000 BCE. Centuries later, this land was inhabited by the native Cahuilla, Serrano, and Chemehuevi peoples. The park's namesake, the Joshua tree, grows in a landscape covering 1,242 square miles. Despite their name, they are not really trees, but rather a kind of succulent. Native to southwest US and northern Mexico, they can grow up to 40 feet tall.
bing-48402.jpg.copyright: © Chris Moore - Exploring Light Photography/Tandem Stills + Motio

bing-48404.jpg.title: 草津白根山, 群馬県 吾妻郡
bing-48404.jpg.headline: 今日は山の日
bing-48404.jpg.description:
今日 8 月 11 日は山の日。「山に親しむ機会を得て、山の恩恵に感謝する」ことを趣旨として、2016 年に新設された国民の祝日です。ご存じのように、日本は山が多い国であり、富士山をはじめとする美しい山々は多くの人々に愛されています…

そして画像は草津白根山。群馬県吾妻郡草津町にある活火山で、標高は 2160m です。山頂付近には白い山肌が広がり、複数の火口湖が存在します。中でも湯釜と呼ばれる火口湖は、世界でも有数の酸性度が高い湖といわれています。

bing-48412.jpg.title: Garça-tigre-ruiva (Tigrisoma lineatum) adulta e filhote no ninho, Mato Grosso, Pantanal
bing-48412.jpg.headline: Um momento de pai e filho
bing-48412.jpg.description:
Observe a concentração dessa garça-tigre-ruiva com o seu filhote, aninhados no coração do pantanal mato-grossense. Essa espécie é conhecida por sua postura ereta e pela capacidade de ficar imóvel por longos períodos, esperando pacientemente para capturar presas. Tanto o macho quanto a fêmea participam da incubação dos ovos, que geralmente são de 2 a 4 por ninhada; o casal se reveza para manter os ovos aquecidos e protegidos. No entanto, após o nascimento dos filhotes, é o pai o responsável por alimentá-los, assim como garantir a proteção do ninho.

Dessa forma podemos ver a natureza mostrando que a figura paterna também é sinônimo de cuidado no reino animal. Que tal nos inspirarmos na dedicação inabalável dessas aves? Reflitamos sobre as lições de paciência e colaboração que a natureza nos ensina através dessas aves fascinantes e vamos celebrar os cuidados paternos em todas as suas formas. Feliz Dia dos Pais!

bing-48414.jpg.title: Wooden path to Kennedy Lake, Vancouver Island, BC, Canada
bing-48414.jpg.headline: The path less taken. Wooden path to Kennedy Lake, Vancouver Island, Canada
bing-48414.jpg.description: Discover the beauty of Vancouver Island, Canada. The wooden pathway in today's image, surrounded by ancient pine and cedar trees, leads to Kennedy Lake, the largest freshwater body on the island. The lake covers a surface area of 16,000 acres. It is part of the ancestral lands of the Tla-o-qui-aht First Nation where the Clayoquot and Kennedy Rivers meet. Tofino, over 24 miles away, has a real surf vibe. This small coastal town is a sanctuary for hikers, bird watchers, artists, and dreamers. Famous for its mild winters and pleasant summers, it has been a filming location for movies like 'The Twilight Saga: New Moon' and 'One Week.'

bing-48422.jpg.title: Éléphants d'Afrique, parc national d'Amboseli, Kenya
bing-48422.jpg.headline: Un engagement planétaire pour sauver ces géants. Journée mondiale de l'éléphant
bing-48422.jpg.description:
Célébrons les éléphants, ces majestueux géants terrestres parmi les plus imposants ! Connaissez-vous les trois espèces encore présentes sur notre planète ? Les éléphants des savanes africaines, leurs cousins des forêts et les éléphants d'Asie. La Journée mondiale de l'éléphant, célébrée aujourd’hui, sensibilise aux défis urgents qu'ils affrontent : le commerce de l'ivoire et la perte de leur habitat. Cette dernière les rapproche des zones habitées, entraînant des conflits préjudiciables des deux côtés.

L'image du jour nous montre une famille d'éléphants d'Afrique se déplaçant à travers l'immensité du parc national d'Amboseli, au Kenya. Ils vivent en groupes dirigés par une femelle âgée, appelée matriarche, tandis que les mâles se séparent pour vivre seuls ou en troupeaux de célibataires, se joignant aux femelles uniquement lors de la reproduction. Malheureusement, toutes les espèces d'éléphants sont menacées.

En France, de nombreuses initiatives voient le jour pour soutenir la conservation des éléphants. Des expositions, des documentaires et des conférences sont régulièrement organisés pour sensibiliser le public et encourager les dons pour les programmes de protection. Protéger les éléphants, c'est préserver un patrimoine mondial précieux.

bing-48426.jpg.title: African elephants, Amboseli National Park, Kenya
bing-48426.jpg.headline: Herd you loud and clear. World Elephant Day
bing-48426.jpg.description: Get ready to celebrate elephants, the largest living land animals. There are three elephant species alive today: African bush, African forest, and Asian. All three species are endangered, and World Elephant Day is dedicated to highlighting the challenges they face, like the ivory trade and habitat loss.

bing-48434.jpg.title: Citadelle de Port Louis, Lorient, Morbihan, France
bing-48434.jpg.headline: À vos binious !. Festival interceltique de Lorient
bing-48434.jpg.description:
Découvrez la richesse culturelle de Lorient en visitant la Citadelle de Port-Louis ! Construite au XVIe siècle par les Espagnols, sous les ordres de Cristobal de Rojas, cette merveille est située sur une pointe rocheuse à l’entrée de la rade de Lorient. Elle abrite aujourd'hui le musée de la Compagnie des Indes, unique en France, qui retrace l'histoire fascinante du commerce maritime entre la France et l'Orient, avec des collections d'objets d'art, des maquettes de navires et des expositions interactives.

Chaque été, Lorient s'anime avec le Festival Interceltique, un événement incontournable célébrant les cultures celtiques du monde entier. Pendant dix jours, la ville résonne au son des cornemuses, des harpes et des danses traditionnelles. Des artistes venus de Bretagne, d'Irlande, d'Écosse, d'Espagne et d'autres régions celtiques se produisent sur diverses scènes, offrant un spectacle vibrant et coloré. Le festival propose également des ateliers, des expositions et des dégustations de cuisine celtique, créant une atmosphère conviviale et festive.

Que vous soyez passionné d'histoire ou amateur de musique, Lorient vous promet une expérience inoubliable entre patrimoine et festivités !

bing-48438.jpg.title: Cliffs of Telašćica Nature Park, Dugi Otok Island, Croatia
bing-48438.jpg.headline: Adriatic heights. Telašćica Nature Park, Dugi Otok, Croatia
bing-48438.jpg.description: Welcome to the slice of paradise that is Telašćica Nature Park, on the Croatian island of Dugi Otok. Pictured behind cliffs separating it from the Adriatic Sea is the park's Telašćica Bay, which stretches inland over 6 miles and is the largest natural harbor in the Adriatic. Dotted with islets and surrounded by small islands, its dramatic cliffs tower more than 520 feet above sea level and are known locally as the 'stene.' Other features of the park include 25 secluded beaches, as well as the therapeutic Mir salt lake known for its healing properties. So, the next time you're in the mood for island-hopping, come to Telašćica, where the land and sea play an endless game of tag.

bing-48450.jpg.title: Thorny devil, Watarrka National Park, Australia
bing-48450.jpg.headline: Feeling sharp today. World Lizard Day
bing-48450.jpg.description: From mythology to movies, lizards have often been portrayed as scary reptiles. But they're not as dangerous as stories might lead you to believe. World Lizard Day is the perfect time to learn about these cold-blooded creatures. With more than 7,000 species, lizards have adapted to a wide range of environments—from deserts to rainforests. Take geckos—these little climbers have toe pads that let them scale walls and walk on ceilings. Then there are chameleons with their color-changing skin. While many think it's all about blending in, this ability is also used to communicate and regulate temperature.
bing-48450.jpg.copyright: © Yva Momatiuk and John Eastcott/Minden Picture

bing-48454.jpg.title: Red Fort Delhi front view with Indian National Flag
bing-48454.jpg.headline: The triumphant tricolour. Independence Day
bing-48454.jpg.description: It's Independence Day, the day our nation threw off the yoke of British rule. This day commemorates the transfer of legislative sovereignty from the British crown to the Indian Constituent Assembly. Our first prime minister, Jawaharlal Nehru, hoisted the national flag at the Lahori Gate of the Red Fort in Delhi on August 15, 1947. Since then, it has become a tradition for the sitting prime minister to raise the flag and deliver a national address on Independence Day. Over time, the focus of the celebration has shifted from solely nationalism to a broader appreciation of Indian culture and heritage. The Indian diaspora also celebrates this day worldwide, with parades and events, especially in areas with significant Indian populations. In New York and other US cities, it has come to be recognised as 'India Day.' Independence Day is not just a reminder of our country's journey towards independence but also the ongoing commitment to build a brighter future for all.

bing-48457.jpg.title: Capo Vaticano, Calabria, Italia
bing-48457.jpg.headline: “Sotto questo sole...”
bing-48457.jpg.description:
Buon Ferragosto! State festeggiando in spiaggia? Da dove ci leggete? Magari per casualità vi trovate proprio qui, a Capo Vaticano in Calabria. Questo gioiello, situato sulla costa tirrenica della Calabria, è un vero e proprio paradiso. La spiaggia di Grotticelle, con la sua sabbia fine e le acque turchesi, è l’ideale per nuotare, fare snorkeling e, in un giorno di festa come oggi, per godersi il dolce far niente. Da qui avete numerosi punti panoramici da dove potrete ammirare spettacolari tramonti sul mare.

Sicuramente siete al corrente che la festa di Ferragosto ha radici che risalgono all’epoca romana. Fu istituito dall’imperatore Augusto nel 18. a. C. come periodo di riposo e festeggiamenti dopo le fatiche dei raccolti. Dopo la caduta dell’Impero Romano, la festa assunse una connotazione cristiana, collegandosi alla celebrazione dell’Assunzione di Maria. Oggi, il Ferragosto è una festa celebrata in tutta Italia, spesso trascorsa in compagnia di amici e familiari tra pranzi all’aperto, feste in spiaggia, gite e spettacolari fuochi d’artificio. E voi, come lo celebrate questo 15 di agosto?

bing-48462.jpg.title: Hang Sơn Đoòng cave, Phong Nha-Kẻ Bàng National Park, Vietnam
bing-48462.jpg.headline: A 'hole' new world. Hang Sơn Đoòng Cave, Vietnam
bing-48462.jpg.description: In 1991, logger Hồ Khanh stumbled upon something big in what is now Vietnam's Phong Nha-Kẻ Bàng National Park. During a jungle expedition, he found the entrance to a cave with a roaring underground river. It was later named Hang Sơn Đoòng, or 'cave of the mountain river' and in 2009, the British Cave Research Association led an expedition to explore it. They realized something incredible: It was the world's largest cave. Hang Sơn Đoòng's main passage is 3.1 miles long, 490 feet wide, and 660 feet high. That's tall enough to fit a 40-story skyscraper.

bing-48464.jpg.title: 大文字山の大文字, 京都
bing-48464.jpg.headline: 今日は五山送り火
bing-48464.jpg.description:
今日 8 月 16 日は、京都で五山送り火が行われます。東山の大文字山で「大文字」が点火され、その後、松ヶ崎の「妙法」、西賀茂の「船形」、大北山の「左大文字」、嵯峨の「鳥居形」の順に炎が上がり、お盆の精霊をあの世へと送り届けます…

五山送り火の起源には公式な記録が存在せず、平安時代とも江戸時代とも様々な説がありますが、京都の文化と歴史に深く根ざしていることは間違いありません。現在、京都市登録無形民俗文化財にも指定されており、日本の夏の風物詩として人気が高く、国内外から多くの観光客が訪れます。

bing-48470.jpg.title: Papillon et fleur de lavande au lever du soleil, France
bing-48470.jpg.headline: Un tableau idyllique. Les papillons et l’équilibre écologique
bing-48470.jpg.description:
Saviez-vous que les papillons jouent un rôle crucial dans les écosystèmes ? En tant que pollinisateurs, ils contribuent à la reproduction de nombreuses plantes, favorisant ainsi la biodiversité végétale. Leur capacité à transporter le pollen d’une fleur à l’autre est essentielle pour la survie de nombreuses espèces végétales, assurant la production de fruits et de graines.

En France métropolitaine et en Corse, on compte 253 espèces de papillons de jour, dont 16 sont menacées. Parmi eux, le Machaon, présent dans la plupart des régions tempérées de l'hémisphère nord, est particulièrement connu en Europe où il est relativement commun. En outre, les papillons sont des indicateurs écologiques précieux. Les scientifiques utilisent les populations de papillons pour évaluer l’impact des changements environnementaux, tels que le réchauffement climatique et la pollution.

Malheureusement, les papillons sont menacés par la perte d’habitat, l’usage intensif de pesticides et le changement climatique. Il est donc crucial de protéger leurs habitats naturels et de promouvoir des pratiques agricoles durables pour préserver ces précieux insectes. Ensemble, nous pouvons contribuer à leur conservation et à la protection de notre biodiversité.

bing-48473.jpg.title: Canadian International Air Show at the Canadian National Exhibition, in Toronto, Ontario
bing-48473.jpg.headline: Look up, Toronto!. Canadian National Exhibition 2024
bing-48473.jpg.description:
Come one, come all, to the Canadian National Exhibition (CNE)—a time-honoured tradition held from August 16 to September 2 in Toronto. As the sun sets, the grounds of the CNE will come alive with live performances from artists and bands like Doriann Forrester, James Naro and Kyle Layton, Sloan, and MacKenzie Porter. A lineup that spans all musical tastes, from toe-tapping country beats to electric pop rhythms—there's a song for every taste. As well as music, there's plenty more to do; go for a ride on the Century Wheel or the Berry Go Round, or take part in games like the Peewee Baseball Tournament and Girls Fastball Tournament.

As thrilling rides and decadent treats fill the grounds, the sky above will be filled with the manoeuvres of the Canadian International Air Show from August 31 to September 2. The Snowbirds, seen in today's image, are officially known as the '431 Air Demonstration Squadron' and have been wowing audiences since 1971. This year, the Royal Air Force's Red Arrows, Canadian Force's Snowbirds and the United States Air Force's F-22 Raptor will transform the sky above Toronto into a canvas with daredevil loops and electrifying fly-bys.

bing-48474.jpg.title: Roller coaster in Nagashima Spa Land, Mie prefecture, Japan
bing-48474.jpg.headline: Buckle up!. International Roller Coaster Day
bing-48474.jpg.description: From single rails to virtual reality, roller coasters have been thrilling people for centuries. Their origins can be traced back to 17th-century Russia, where wooden slides—'Russian Mountains'—provided seasonal entertainment. The first roller coaster was built in early 19th-century Paris, France. Called 'Les Montagnes Russes à Belleville,' it featured wheeled carts securely attached to tracks. By the 1900s, coasters were looping the loop for the first time.

bing-48479.jpg.title: Anochecer en el Museo Guggenheim, Bilbao, País Vasco
bing-48479.jpg.headline: Creación contemporánea. Semana Grande de Bilbao
bing-48479.jpg.description:
Esta semana, Bilbao se viste de gala para celebrar su icónica Semana Grande, una celebración emocionante que combina eventos populares, folclóricos y culturales, transformando la ciudad en un hervidero de actividades. Desde el famoso “txupinazo”, que marca el inicio de las festividades, hasta los conciertos electrizantes, las divertidas atracciones de feria, el teatro cautivador y los deslumbrantes fuegos artificiales, hay algo para todos los gustos.

Además, es una oportunidad para disfrutar de la gastronomía vasca con sus famosos y exquisitos pintxos y platos tradicionales, y sumergirse en la cultura local con danzas encantadoras, desfiles de gigantes y cabezudos impresionantes, y la presencia del Gargantúa.

En la imagen de hoy se muestra el majestuoso Museo Guggenheim Bilbao, una joya arquitectónica que ha transformado la ciudad en un epicentro cultural. Este evento no solo es una fiesta, sino también una oportunidad para sumergirse en la rica historia y tradiciones de Bilbao. No te pierdas la oportunidad de ser parte de esta celebración única. ¡Ven y descubre su magia!

bing-48486.jpg.title: Alfanzina Lighthouse, Algarve, Portugal
bing-48486.jpg.headline: Light the way. International Lighthouse and Lightship Weekend
bing-48486.jpg.description: The lighthouse featured in today's image stands in southern Portugal's popular Algarve region. Built in 1919, Alfanzina Lighthouse helps ships navigate dangerous waters near the town of Carvoeiro. A popular tourist destination, the lighthouse also has become a symbol of the region's deep links to the sea. If you're lucky enough to live near a lighthouse, this weekend is the perfect time to pay it a visit.

bing-48492.jpg.title: Externsteine im Teutoburger Wald, Nordrhein-Westfalen
bing-48492.jpg.headline: Magische Steinzeitfelsen. Externsteine im Teutoburger Wald
bing-48492.jpg.description:
Auf unserem heutigen Bild sehen Sie die imposanten Externsteine, ein bemerkenswertes Natur- und Kulturdenkmal im Teutoburger Wald in Nordrhein-Westfalen. Die markanten Sandsteinfelsen, die seit Jahrhunderten Besucher faszinieren, entstanden vor rund 70 Millionen Jahren durch geologische Prozesse und wurden durch Erosion geformt. Die höchsten Felsen ragen bis zu 35 Meter in die Höhe.

Archäologische Funde deuten darauf hin, dass die Felsen seit der Steinzeit als Kultstätte genutzt wurden. Besonders beeindruckend sind die in den Felsen gehauenen Reliefs und Kammern, darunter das berühmte "Kreuzabnahmerelief" aus dem 12. Jahrhundert, das die Kreuzabnahme Christi zeigt. Diese Reliefs und Kammern lassen vermuten, dass die Externsteine auch im Mittelalter eine wichtige religiöse Rolle spielten. Heute sind die Externsteine ein beliebtes Ausflugsziel und Naturdenkmal. Erklimmen Sie die Felsen über Treppen und Plattformen und genießen Sie den atemberaubenden Blick über den Teutoburger Wald.

bing-48495.jpg.title: Fresh garlic bulbs for sale at the garlic farm on the Isle of Wight, England
bing-48495.jpg.headline: The root of all deliciousness. The Isle of Wight Garlic Festival
bing-48495.jpg.description: Every year, since 1983, garlic lovers and culinary adventurers from around the globe flock to the Isle of Wight for a festival that's as aromatic as it is appetising—The Isle of Wight Garlic Festival. This quirky celebration of all things garlic is taking place near Newchurch village on the Isle of Wight, from August 17-18. From traditional garlic bread to more adventurous offerings like garlic fudge, garlic ice cream and garlic beer, there's something to satisfy every palate. The festival is also a hub of entertainment and activities for all ages, with live music filling the air. Kids can enjoy face painting, garlic-themed games, and even garlic bulb planting workshops. For those who can't get enough garlic in their lives, the event offers ample opportunities to stock up.

bing-48498.jpg.title: Huntington Beach Pier, California, at sunset
bing-48498.jpg.headline: Pier today .... Huntington Beach Pier, California, at sunset
bing-48498.jpg.description: In today's image, we see the sun disappearing below the pier at Huntington Beach, California. First built in 1902, the pier was damaged by a storm and had to be rebuilt just nine years later. During World War II, a submarine lookout post was installed on the pier to help with the war effort. These days, it's a popular spot for fishing and watching surfers ride the waves out in the Pacific Ocean.

bing-48502.jpg.title: Festival of Raksha Bandhan
bing-48502.jpg.headline: Twists, turns and ties. Raksha Bandhan
bing-48502.jpg.description:
Raksha Bandhan's here. Are you ready with your rakhis? This is an annual Hindu ritual celebrated by sisters of all ages as they tie a sacred thread called a rakhi around their brothers' wrists to symbolise protection. In return, brothers traditionally promise to safeguard their sisters and often give them gifts as a token of appreciation. The celebration is observed on the last day of the Hindu lunar month of Shravana, usually in August.

The term 'Raksha Bandhan' means the bond of protection, obligation or care in Sanskrit. Historically, the term referred to a different ritual where priests would tie amulets or threads on their patrons' wrists and receive gifts in return, a practice still followed in some areas. Over time, the sister-brother version of the festival, with roots in folk traditions, became more popular. The festival had different names in folk culture, depending on the region, like 'saluno,' 'silono' and 'rakri.' While it is typically a North Indian tradition, Raksha Bandhan is also celebrated in Central and Western India, Nepal, and among Hindu communities overseas, like in Fiji, as well as Pakistan and Mauritius. Today, the festival is all about celebrating the unique bond between siblings with lots of love, laughter and, of course, gifts!

bing-48507.jpg.title: Huntington Beach Pier at sunset, California, USA
bing-48507.jpg.headline: A peerless pier. Huntington Beach Pier, California, USA
bing-48507.jpg.description:
In today's image, we see the sun beginning to disappear below the pier at Huntington Beach, California. First built in 1902, Huntington Beach Pier was damaged by a storm, leading it to be rebuilt just nine years later. During the Second World War, a submarine lookout post was installed on the pier to help with the war effort. These days, it's a popular tourist spot, with visitors heading there to fish and to watch surfers ride the waves out in the Pacific Ocean.

And there will be plenty of surfers to watch. Huntington Beach has been nicknamed Surf City, and it's not hard to see why. Its 9.5-mile-long sandy beach gets great waves all year round, making it a surfer's paradise. In fact, the city is home to the International Surf Museum, where visitors can learn about the history of the sport and see historic surfboards. Whether you're hitting the waves yourself or watching from the pier, Huntington Beach is a peerless destination.

bing-48509.jpg.title: Two Atlantic puffins, Elliston, Newfoundland, Canada
bing-48509.jpg.headline: Puffins with a plan. Two Atlantic puffins in Elliston
bing-48509.jpg.description:
In Elliston, Newfoundland and Labrador, Atlantic puffins, like the ones in today's image, draw onlookers with their black and white plumage and orange beaks. As well as in Newfoundland and Labrador in Canada, these seabirds breed in several countries, including Russia, Iceland, Norway, and Greenland. These 'sea parrots' have a wingspan of 47 to 63 centimetres and travel vast distances to mate. Surprisingly, the colour of their beaks changes seasonally; during the breeding season, it is brighter with a hint of yellow and orange. However, in the nonbreeding season, the beak sheds its yellow highlight.

During spring, Elliston's cliffs transform into bustling communities as puffins pair and construct burrows in the soft soil of the coastal slope to welcome their single egg. The puffin parents search for food and return with beaks brimming with fish to feed their puffling. Puffins face challenges, enduring threats from human activity like hunting, climate change and pollution. Fortunately, a growing awareness has led to steadfast conservation efforts.

bing-48510.jpg.title: Museum of Flight, Seattle, Washington
bing-48510.jpg.headline: An old dream takes flight. National Aviation Day
bing-48510.jpg.description: Established in 1939 to honor Orville Wright's birthday, National Aviation Day kicks off a week-long celebration of America's long history of flight. Pioneers Orville and Wilbur Wright designed, built, and flew the world's first engine-powered airplane near Kitty Hawk, North Carolina, in 1903. America's love of flight, however, goes all the way back to 1793, when President George Washington watched a hot air balloon launch in Philadelphia.

bing-48511.jpg.title: Bufadero de la Garita, Gran Canaria, Spain
bing-48511.jpg.headline: Bufadero de la Garita, Gran Canaria, Spain
bing-48511.jpg.description:
Have you ever heard of the Bufadero de la Garita? It's on the Spanish island of Gran Canaria, off the Atlantic coast of Northwest Africa. This natural phenomenon is a wonder you can't miss. Found on the picturesque eastern coast of the island, the 'Bufadero' is a fascinating sea-based blowhole in the rocks where seawater enters and exits with force, creating an impressive spectacle, as we can see in today’s image.

The waves hit with such intensity that the water can rise several metres into the air, forming a kind of majestic marine geyser. It's a perfect spot for nature lovers and avid photographers. Don't forget to bring your camera and capture this unique moment. In addition, this month, Gran Canaria hosts the exciting San Ginés International Regatta, a fun-filled sailing event that will make your trip even more unforgettable.

bing-48522.jpg.title: Sunrise at Grand Teton National Park, Wyoming
bing-48522.jpg.headline: A grand view. Sunrise at Grand Teton National Park, Wyoming
bing-48522.jpg.description: Mind-blowing beauty is one reason people keep coming back to Wyoming and the Grand Teton National Park. Named 'les trois tétons' by early French trappers, the park was created in 1929 by conservationists including John D. Rockefeller Jr. It is home to a virtually untouched ecosystem of plants and animals, such as grizzly bears, wolves, bison, moose, and bald eagles.

bing-48534.jpg.title: Nazca boobies, Wolf Island, Galápagos Islands, Ecuador
bing-48534.jpg.headline: Waiting to 'Galápa-go'. Nazca boobies, Wolf Island, Galápagos Islands, Ecuador
bing-48534.jpg.description: The Galápagos Islands in the eastern Pacific are a paradise for wildlife. Habitats range from arid regions to tropical rainforests. Because these islands are so isolated, many of the species that live here are not found anywhere else in the world. One species found in abundance is the Nazca booby, pictured here on Wolf Island. The name might raise a few eyebrows, but it actually comes from the Spanish word 'bobo,' meaning clown, because of the birds' clumsy demeanor when they're walking.

bing-48538.jpg.title: Aerial view of Ocean City, Maryland, at sunrise
bing-48538.jpg.headline: The morning glow. Aerial view of Ocean City, Maryland, USA
bing-48538.jpg.description: Here is a beautiful coastal getaway offering endless fun and adventure—welcome to Ocean City, Maryland. Ocean City remained a quiet fishing village until 1875, when the Atlantic Hotel opened its doors, marking the town's transformation into a burgeoning resort destination. Today, it is one of the most popular vacation spots in the country, offering a plethora of activities for people of all ages. The town's iconic four-kilometre-long boardwalk is lined with restaurants, shops and amusement parks. Pristine sandy beaches that stretch for 16 kilometres are perfect for sunbathing, beach volleyball or building sandcastles, and the ocean waters beckon for a refreshing swim. With plenty of adventure and a heritage deeply rooted in history, Ocean City is a charming retreat that draws visitors back time and again.

bing-48544.jpg.title: Artesanato indígena brasileiro exposto para venda em feira ao ar livre
bing-48544.jpg.headline: As cores do nosso folclore
bing-48544.jpg.description:
Descubra as tradições que moldam nossa identidade no Dia do Folclore! Nas feiras a céu aberto do Brasil, tesouros artesanais expressam a alma indígena da nossa terra. Em cada peça de artesanato indígena, há uma história, um legado que transborda em cores e formas. Grupos indígenas como os Yanomami, Ashaninka e Yawanawá mostram suas habilidades nessas peças feitas a partir de sementes e miçangas coloridas, unidas por técnicas ancestrais como encaixe, amarração e bordado, que dão vida a colares, pulseiras, brincos, cintos e adornos de cabeça.

O nosso folclore é o conjunto de tradições, lendas e crenças do nosso povo, sendo um elemento vital para entender a identidade nacional. Aqui no Brasil, medimos essa riqueza em elementos tão variados como são os nossos quilômetros de costa ou os hectares de floresta amazônica. Permita-se mergulhar nessa jornada cultural rica e multifacetada, onde cada mito e lenda é um fio do tecido chamado Brasil.

bing-48546.jpg.title: Ocean City, Maryland, at sunrise
bing-48546.jpg.headline: The morning glow. Ocean City, Maryland, at sunrise
bing-48546.jpg.description: Here is a beautiful coastal getaway offering endless fun and adventure—welcome to Ocean City, Maryland. Ocean City was a quiet fishing village until 1875, when the Atlantic Hotel opened its doors, marking the town's transformation into a burgeoning resort destination. Today, it is a popular vacation spot, with an iconic 3-mile-long boardwalk lined with restaurants, shops, and amusement parks. Pristine sandy beaches stretching over 10 miles are perfect for sunbathing, beach volleyball, or building sandcastles, and the ocean waters beckon for a refreshing swim. Ocean City is a charming retreat that draws visitors back time and again.

bing-48548.jpg.title: 厳島神社, 広島県 廿日市市
bing-48548.jpg.headline: もう一度見たい宮島水中花火大会
bing-48548.jpg.description:
一瞬の夢のように、美しくも儚い花火は、夜空を彩る日本の夏の風物詩として多くの人々に愛されています。そして写真は、もう二度と見られない「宮島水中花火大会」。かつて広島県廿日市市宮島町の厳島界隈で毎年 8 月に行われていた花火大会で、大型の水中花火が目玉となっていました…

1973 年に初めて開催され、花火も 1000 発程度と小規模でしたが、年々その規模は大きくなり、「日本の花火大会百選」のひとつにも選ばれました。しかし、2020 年に安全確保の難しさなどの理由で、無期限での開催打ち切りが発表されました。花火が打ち上がるたびに大鳥居が浮かびあがる光景は、今も人々の心に深く刻まれています。

bing-48558.jpg.title: Prasat Phanom Rung temple ruins, Buriram province, Thailand
bing-48558.jpg.headline: Doorway to the past. Prasat Phanom Rung temple ruins, Thailand
bing-48558.jpg.description: Today, let us step into the Phanom Rung Historical Park in Buriram province, Thailand. Here, Khmer architecture and history come to life. Built between the 10th and 13th centuries, this remarkable site served as a Hindu temple dedicated to the god Shiva. It is on the rim of an extinct volcano, offering views of the surrounding paddy fields and the towering Dongrek Mountains of Cambodia in the distance.

bing-48560.jpg.title: 三千院のわらべ地蔵, 京都
bing-48560.jpg.headline: 今日は地蔵盆
bing-48560.jpg.description:
今日 8 月 24 日は地蔵盆。子どもの守り神である地蔵菩薩の縁日で、関西地方を中心に行われる行事です。お地蔵様の像を清め、化粧をするなどして飾り付けたり、地蔵尊と子どもの名前を書き入れた提灯を奉納したりします。また、「数珠まわし」などの伝統行事も行われます…

ここ、京都の大原三千院の苔むした庭園の中に、「わらべ地蔵」と呼ばれるたくさんのお地蔵様たちがひっそりと佇んでいます。彫刻家の杉村孝氏によって平成の初め頃に奉納されたもので、その可愛らしくユニークな姿は、訪れる人々を楽しませてくれます。

bing-48564.jpg.title: Museumsinsel auf der Spree und Fernsehturm, Berlin
bing-48564.jpg.headline: Nachts im Museum. Lange Nacht der Museen
bing-48564.jpg.description:
Heute feiern wir die Lange Nacht der Museen in Berlin! Dieses jährliche Ereignis, das Kunst- und Kulturbegeisterte aus der ganzen Welt anzieht, bietet eine einzigartige Gelegenheit, zahlreiche Museen der Stadt in einer besonderen nächtlichen Atmosphäre zu erleben. Mit einem einzigen Ticket erhalten Besucher Zugang zu über 70 Museen, Galerien und historischen Stätten, die bis in die frühen Morgenstunden geöffnet sind.

Unser heutiges Bild zeigt die berühmte Museumsinsel an der Spree, die zum UNESCO-Weltkulturerbe gehört. Diese Museumsinsel beherbergt fünf der bedeutendsten Museen Deutschlands: das Pergamonmuseum, das Bode-Museum, das Alte Museum, die Alte Nationalgalerie und das Neue Museum. Die gezeigten Sammlungen spannen einen Bogen von der Prähistorie über die Antike bis hin zur Kunst des 19. Jahrhunderts. Das Pergamonmuseum ist bekannt für seine archäologischen Schätze wie das Ischtar-Tor und den Pergamonaltar. Im Neuen Museum können Besucher die weltberühmte Büste der Nofretete bewundern. Die Alte Nationalgalerie bietet eine umfassende Sammlung von Kunstwerken des 19. Jahrhunderts, während das Bode-Museum mit seiner Skulpturensammlung und byzantinischen Kunst beeindruckt. Lassen Sie sich die Lange Nacht der Museen nicht entgehen und entdecken Sie die kulturelle Vielfalt Berlins!

bing-48567.jpg.title: Notting Hill Carnival on August 15, 2009, in London, England
bing-48567.jpg.headline: 'Notting' but colours, sounds and flavours. Notting Hill Carnival
bing-48567.jpg.description: Music, glitter, flavours, masquerade dancers and colourful feathers—Notting Hill Carnival is back in London. This annual carnival, now in its 58th year, began in 1966 as a small community event to ease racial tensions and celebrate Caribbean heritage. Fast forward to 2024, and it has grown into one of the largest street festivals in the world, drawing around a million visitors eager to soak up the carnival atmosphere. This year, the main action happens on August 25 and 26 when the parade takes place. However, there's an extra event, the Panorama Steel Band Competition, today. So, dust off your dancing shoes, ready your taste buds and prepare to paint the town red.

bing-48570.jpg.title: Katahdin Woods and Waters National Monument, Penobscot County, Maine
bing-48570.jpg.headline: All about the woods and waters. Katahdin Woods and Waters National Monument anniversary
bing-48570.jpg.description: Welcome to Katahdin, where dense woodlands and pristine waterways stretch out as far as the eye can see. Covering nearly 87,500 acres, this new national monument was established eight years ago today. Maine's logging industry was a big part of this region for over a hundred years but declined toward the end of the 19th century. Efforts to preserve its landscape were spearheaded by philanthropist Roxanne Quimby. She started buying land near Baxter State Park in 2001 and donated it to the federal government in 2016, ensuring its preservation for future generations.

bing-48574.jpg.title: Arched parapets of the Golconda Fort in Hyderabad, Telangana
bing-48574.jpg.headline: More than just walls. Golconda Fort in Hyderabad, Telangana
bing-48574.jpg.description:
Today, let us step into Golconda Fort in the bustling city of Hyderabad. This fort once housed a vault that safeguarded some of the world's most famous gems, including the legendary Koh-i-Noor and Hope diamonds. The origins of the fort date back to the 11th century when it was first established as a modest mud fort by Pratāparudra of the Kakatiya Empire. It's also believed that the Kakatiya ruler Ganapatideva, who reigned from 1199 to 1262, constructed a stone outpost on the hilltop to protect the empire's western frontier.

This outpost would later evolve into the iconic Golconda Fort. In 1518, Sultan Quli of the Qutb Shahi dynasty expanded and transformed the fort into a formidable citadel, eventually designating the surrounding city as the capital of the Golconda Sultanate. In 2014, UNESCO added the Golconda Fort complex to its tentative list of World Heritage Sites in the region under the collective title 'Monuments and Forts of the Deccan Sultanate.' Although the fort is now abandoned, its historical importance still resonates strongly.

bing-48575.jpg.title: Sitges, Barcelona, Cataluña, España
bing-48575.jpg.headline: La regata sin segundo puesto. America's Cup Barcelona
bing-48575.jpg.description:
¿Listo para zarpar? La America’s Cup es el trofeo internacional más antiguo, con origen en 1851, y uno de los desafíos deportivos más exigentes. El New York Yacht Club mantuvo el primer puesto durante 132 años, hasta que Australia ganó en 1983. Desde entonces, solo equipos de EE. UU., Suiza y Nueva Zelanda han logrado la codiciada victoria.

En la imagen de hoy, se aprecia la pintoresca costa de Sitges, en Barcelona, donde se celebra la 37ª edición. Las bases de los equipos están en el vibrante Port Vell, rodeadas por el “Race Village”, donde miles de espectadores disfrutan de estas emocionantes regatas. Entre los equipos más destacados se encuentran Emirates Team New Zealand, INEOS Britannia, Alinghi Red Bull Racing, Luna Rossa Prada Pirelli, NYYC American Magic y Orient Express Racing Team. Los barcos utilizados son los AC75, monocascos con hidroalas, y los AC40, usados para pruebas y entrenamientos. ¡Siente la adrenalina y la pasión de la America’s Cup, un evento que promete ser tan vibrante y emocionante como la propia ciudad de Barcelona!

bing-48576.jpg.title: Drohnenansicht der Weinberge im Remstal, Baden-Württemberg
bing-48576.jpg.headline: Ein Paradies für Weinliebhaber. Weinberge im Remstal, Baden-Württemberg
bing-48576.jpg.description:
Der Weinanbau im Remstal, östlich von Stuttgart gelegen, hat eine lange Tradition, die bis ins Mittelalter zurückreicht. Heute erstrecken sich die Weinberge auf rund 640 Hektar und produzieren einige der besten Weine Deutschlands. Ein besonderes Highlight des Remstals sind die zahlreichen Weinfeste und Weinwanderwege, die Besucher einladen, die Vielfalt der regionalen Weine zu entdecken. Besonders beliebt ist der „Wein-Lese-Weg”, ein 11 Kilometer langer Wanderweg, der durch die Weinberge führt und atemberaubende Ausblicke auf das Tal bietet. Entlang des Weges gibt es zahlreiche Weinstände, an denen die örtlichen Winzer ihre Erzeugnisse präsentieren.

Im Remstal gedeihen vor allem Riesling, Trollinger und Lemberger Rebsorten. Die Region ist Teil des Weinbaugebiets Württemberg, das für seine hochwertigen Rotweine bekannt ist. Das milde Klima und die fruchtbaren Böden des Remstals bieten ideale Bedingungen für den Weinanbau. Ein Besuch lohnt sich jedoch nicht nur für Weinliebhaber, denn historische Städte wie Waiblingen und Schwäbisch Gmünd verzaubern Sie mit ihren charmanten Altstädten und zahlreichen Sehenswürdigkeiten.

bing-48578.jpg.title: Reflet du ciel sur le lac Blanc, Alpes françaises, Monte Bianco en arrière-plan, Chamonix
bing-48578.jpg.headline: L’émeraude des Alpes. L'Ultra-Trail du Mont-Blanc
bing-48578.jpg.description:
L'Ultra-Trail du Mont-Blanc (UTMB) est l'un des événements de course à pied les plus emblématiques au monde. Chaque année, fin août, les passionnés de trail se réunissent à Chamonix pour vivre une expérience sportive exceptionnelle. Ce défi colossal, long de 170 km avec un dénivelé positif de 10 000 mètres, traverse trois pays : la France, l'Italie et la Suisse.

L'UTMB attire les meilleurs athlètes de la discipline, mais aussi des amateurs avides de repousser leurs limites. Les coureurs affrontent des sentiers techniques, des conditions météorologiques imprévisibles et des paysages à couper le souffle, tout en bénéficiant du soutien inébranlable des bénévoles et des spectateurs.

Pour Chamonix, l'événement est aussi une grande fête qui met en valeur les richesses naturelles et culturelles de la région. L'UTMB, c'est l'occasion de vivre une épopée unique, de se dépasser et de se reconnecter avec la nature dans un cadre majestueux. Un rendez-vous incontournable pour tous les amoureux de la montagne et du sport !

bing-48582.jpg.title: Sunrise over Swiftcurrent Lake, Glacier National Park, Montana
bing-48582.jpg.headline: Preserving paradise. National Park Service Founders Day
bing-48582.jpg.description: Join us as we celebrate the American wilderness on National Park Service Founders Day. Today we honor the foresight of visionaries who spearheaded the creation of the NPS. This organization was established by President Woodrow Wilson to conserve wildlife, maintain natural landscapes, preserve historical artifacts, and offer educational programs. You can enjoy this day by visiting one of 429 national parks in the country and diving into ranger-led programs, volunteer efforts, and celebratory events to learn more about the history.

bing-48594.jpg.title: Palmyra Atoll National Wildlife Refuge, Central Pacific Ocean
bing-48594.jpg.headline: Idyllic island escape. Palmyra Atoll National Wildlife Refuge
bing-48594.jpg.description: Welcome to this eco-travelers' paradise in the middle of the Pacific. Situated halfway between Hawaii and American Samoa, the Palmyra Atoll National Wildlife Refuge was established in 2001 to conserve, manage, and restore the nation's fish, wildlife, plants, and habitats.

bing-48601.jpg.title: Lago Misurina, Auronzo di Cadore, Belluno, Veneto
bing-48601.jpg.headline: Acqua, Aria, Aetherius
bing-48601.jpg.description:
Nel cuore delle Dolomiti bellunesi sorge uno specchio d'acqua che incanta al primo sguardo: il lago di Misurina. Ci troviamo in Veneto, in provincia di Belluno. Un gioiello incastonato nel cuore delle Dolomiti, dove risplende l’acqua cristallina e dal quale si può osservare il famoso gruppo delle Tre Cime di Lavaredo. A 1.754 metri di altitudine, offre un panorama mozzafiato, trasmettendo una sensazione di tranquillità unica. Passeggiare lungo i sentieri, respirare l’aria pulita delle montagne e il solo ascolto del mormorio delle acque, sono una cura per anima e corpo.

Non solo il fascino naturale, anche quello folcloristico e magico avvolge questo luogo. Una delle tante leggende vuole che, Misurina, una bambina capricciosa e viziata, figlia del re Sorapiss, desiderava a tutti costi uno specchio magico. Il re, per amore della figlia, accettò di trasformarsi in una montagna per soddisfare il suo desiderio. Le lacrime della bambina, pentita del suo capriccio, dopo aver visto le conseguenze del suo desiderio, formarono il lago che oggi porta il suo nome. I miti e bellezza del lago si intrecciano, invitando ogni visitatore a scoprire la magia unica di questo luogo.

bing-48606.jpg.title: Young black caiman, Tambopata National Reserve, Peru
bing-48606.jpg.headline: Life's good in the swamp!. Young black caiman, Tambopata National Reserve, Peru
bing-48606.jpg.description: Today's image features a black caiman, South America's stealthy river giant, in the Tambopata National Reserve of Peru. These caimans are the largest species in the alligator family, growing up to 20 feet and weighing as much as 1,000 pounds. Their dark color helps them blend into the murky depths. These carnivorous creatures thrive in freshwater environments such as slow-moving rivers, lakes, and seasonally flooded savannas. From these waters, they hunt for birds, fish, turtles, and occasionally big mammals. Black caimans play an important role in making sure ecosystems stay balanced by keeping the populations of their prey under control. More caimans mean fewer piranhas, which attack cattle, and fewer capybaras, which can cause crop damage.

bing-48616.jpg.title: Montmartre e a Basílica de Sacré-Cœur, Paris, França
bing-48616.jpg.headline: Chegou o dia!
bing-48616.jpg.description:
Ainda não acabou! Começam hoje os Jogos Paralímpicos de Verão, reunindo mais de 4.000 atletas de todo o mundo para competir em 22 esportes e 549 eventos. Em sua estreia como anfitriã, a cidade irá realizar a Cerimônia de Abertura na icônica Champs-Élysées, com as delegações de 184 países desfilando até a Praça da Concórdia. Desde os primeiros jogos em Roma, em 1960, com 23 países e apenas 8 esportes, essa competição de superação e talento cresceu e se tornou gigante!

Na imagem de hoje, vemos outro importante cartão postal da capital francesa. A Basílica de Sacré-Cœur ergue-se imponente no bairro de Montmartre, um dos pontos mais altos de Paris, completada em 1914. Deste ponto é possível admirar o panorama espetacular da cidade-luz, com a Torre Eiffel, Notre Dame e o Panthéon. E para quem está na cidade aproveitando os Jogos Paralímpicos, essa parada é imperdível para sentir o pulso parisino!

bing-48618.jpg.title: Montmartre and Sacre Cœur, Paris, France
bing-48618.jpg.headline: Games on. Paralympic Games begin in Paris
bing-48618.jpg.description: The Summer Paralympic Games get underway in Paris today. Over 4,000 athletes with a range of disabilities from all around the world will meet in the French capital to compete across 549 different events. For its first time hosting the Summer Paralympics, the city has got something special in store for the opening ceremony. Delegations from 184 nations will parade down the iconic Champs-Élysées to the Place de la Concorde, rather than entering a stadium. The first official Paralympic Games were held in Rome in 1960. Twenty-three nations took part, competing in eight sports, including wheelchair basketball and Para athletics.

bing-48630.jpg.title: Castellfollit de la Roca, Catalonia, Spain
bing-48630.jpg.headline: A Catalan cliffhanger. Castellfollit de la Roca, Catalonia, Spain
bing-48630.jpg.description: Perched on the edge of a basalt cliff above two rivers, today's image takes us to Castellfollit de la Roca, in the Spanish region of Catalonia. This town is not for the faint-hearted: There's a 160-foot drop down to the Toronell and Fluvia Rivers, which converge at the base of the cliff. Many of the buildings, which are made of the same basalt that the town stands on, seem to teeter on the edge of the precipice. Pictured at the end of the crag is the 13th-century church of Sant Salvador.

bing-48642.jpg.title: A whale shark in Cenderawasih Bay, West Papua, Indonesia
bing-48642.jpg.headline: Being gentle to the giants. International Whale Shark Day
bing-48642.jpg.description: Today we’re celebrating the world's largest fish, the whale shark. These gentle giants can grow up to 40 feet long, with one reaching a record 61.7 feet. Found in tropical oceans, these filter feeders glide through the water, mouths wide open, straining plankton and small fish. The patterns on their dotted, starry skin are as unique as a human fingerprint. Sadly, the International Union for Conservation of Nature lists whale sharks as endangered due to overfishing, habitat loss, and climate change.

bing-48654.jpg.title: Rock formations and sand dunes in the Sahara, Tassili n’Ajjer, Algeria
bing-48654.jpg.headline: Dune days and desert haze. Tassili n’Ajjer, Sahara, Algeria
bing-48654.jpg.description: From the Mediterranean coast to the vast Sahara, Algeria in North Africa has a wide variety of landscapes. Today, we're exploring the area around the Tassili n'Ajjer plateau. This UNESCO World Heritage Site is famed for its rock formations and cave art. More than 15,000 ancient engravings, some dating back 12,000 years, depict scenes of daily life, hunting, and mystical beings.

bing-48661.jpg.title: Regata Storica, Venezia, Veneto, Italia
bing-48661.jpg.headline: Regata, remi e risonanze
bing-48661.jpg.description:
Immergetevi nella tradizione e nel colore della Regata Storica di Venezia 2025, uno spettacolo fluviale che incanta e coinvolge ogni anno cittadini e visitatori. La Serenissima veste i suoi migliori ornamenti: gondole splendidamente decorate, gondolieri in abiti storici e una parata che rievoca il fasto della Venezia antica, creando un mosaico vivente di storia e cultura. L’evento si divide in due parti: la sfilata storica e le competizioni. La sfilata, che apre la giornata, vede un corteo di imbarcazioni storiche, con figuranti in costumi d’epoca che rappresentano il Doge e la sua corte, rievocando l’accoglienza riservata alla regina di Cipro nel 1489.

Cominciano poi le regate vere e proprie, che includono diverse categorie: Il pupparino, piccola imbarcazione veneziana, con la poppa elevata, usata storicamente per spostamenti privati e il gondolino, una versione più leggera della gondola, progettata per le competizioni. La gara più attesa è proprio quella dei gondolini, dove i migliori vogatori della laguna si sfidano in un appassionante testa a testa. Venezia, con il suo fascino senza tempo e la sua ricca storia, è sempre un gioiello, ma la Regata Storica è la ciliegina sulla torta che rende questa città ancor più straordinaria.

bing-48666.jpg.title: River Thames, London, England
bing-48666.jpg.headline: Row your boat gently down the Thames. Totally Thames Festival, London
bing-48666.jpg.description: Welcome to the Totally Thames Festival in London, England. Each year, it brings together communities, artists, and nature enthusiasts in a month-long tribute to the river. Highlights for 2024 include the annual boat marathon, Great River Race, and the Clean Thames Challenge.

bing-48670.jpg.title: Rhino mother and calf, Kaziranga National Park, Assam
bing-48670.jpg.headline: Bonding in the bush. Rhino mother and calf, Kaziranga National Park, Assam
bing-48670.jpg.description:
What's grey and grumpy looking? Of course, a rhino. Today's image features a rhino mother with her calf in Kaziranga National Park's expanse. The Indian rhinoceros, also known as the greater one-horned rhinoceros, is native to the Indian subcontinent. It's the second-largest living rhinoceros species, with adult males weighing between 2.07 and 2.2 tonnes and adult females around 1.6 tonnes. These rhinos are mostly solitary, coming together only during the breeding season or when raising their young.

They have sharp hearing and a keen sense of smell, but their eyesight isn't the best. Kaziranga National Park in Golaghat and Nagaon districts of Assam hosts two-thirds of the world's Indian rhinoceroses, so it's no wonder this place is a UNESCO World Heritage Site. Local communities surrounding the park have played a crucial role in preventing rhino poaching and supporting conservation efforts for rhinos and other wildlife. Although the park has faced significant animal losses, including rhinos, due to annual floods, the latest census offers a hopeful outlook for these endangered species.

bing-48674.jpg.title: Les Pénitents des Mées, Alpes-de-Haute-Provence
bing-48674.jpg.headline: Les Géants de la Haute-Provence. Les Pénitents des Mées, Alpes-de-Haute-Provence
bing-48674.jpg.description:
Avez-vous déjà eu l'occasion d'admirer les Pénitents des Mées ? Situés dans les Alpes-de-Haute-Provence, cet ensemble de formations rocheuses spectaculaires surplombent la vallée de la Durance. Ces colonnes de pierre, façonnées par l’érosion au fil des millénaires, évoquent des moines en prière, d’où leur nom évocateur.

L'origine de ces formations remonte à des millions d'années, lorsque des couches de sédiments se sont accumulées, avant d'être sculptées par l'érosion au fil du temps. La légende raconte que ces pierres représentent des moines pétrifiés par la colère divine pour avoir succombé à la tentation.

Ce site naturel, accessible via des sentiers balisés, offre une expérience de randonnée unique, mêlant histoire géologique et beauté paysagère. Les visiteurs peuvent admirer la vue imprenable depuis les sommets des Pénitents, tout en découvrant la riche biodiversité locale, incluant des espèces protégées comme la Molinie Tardive et le Grand-Duc d’Europe. Que vous soyez amateur de randonnée ou simplement curieux de nature, ne ratez pas cette étape incontournable lors de votre passage en Haute-Provence !

bing-48678.jpg.title: 'Power of the Titans' mural by Andrei Krautsou, North Kansas City, Missouri
bing-48678.jpg.headline: Workers of the world, relax. Celebrating Labor Day
bing-48678.jpg.description: Take a load off this Labor Day weekend. One of 11 federal holidays, Labor Day honors America's workers and is celebrated on the first Monday of September. Its origins are rooted in late 1800s efforts to recognize the contributions the country's workers, and labor activists ultimately helped establish the 40-hour work week and weekends. President Grover Cleveland made the US holiday official in 1894. Today, many Americans celebrate the long weekend, which is often considered the unofficial end of summer, by grilling, hanging out with friends and family, and going to parades.

bing-48679.jpg.title: Red-and-green macaws, Mato Grosso do Sul, Brazil
bing-48679.jpg.headline: Red-and-green macaws, Brazil
bing-48679.jpg.description: Today's image features red-and-green macaws at Buraco das Araras, in the state of Mato Grosso do Sul in Brazil. In this sanctuary, their vibrant red and green plumage with wings can reach over 90 centimetres. Their wings shine brightly against the expansive blue Brazilian sky and its impressive backdrop of towering red sandstone walls. Being one of the largest macaw species, they play a crucial role in dispersing seeds in their habitat, helping the regeneration of vegetation. Embark on a journey to Buraco das Araras and witness the graceful flight of these birds, a testament to the mesmerising beauty that our world so generously bestows. Spread your imaginary wings, and let us peek at these feathered creatures, shall we?

bing-48690.jpg.title: Crystal Lake in the Enchantments, Alpine Lakes Wilderness, Washington
bing-48690.jpg.headline: Unspoiled beauty for all. Wilderness Act anniversary
bing-48690.jpg.description: Sometimes it's nice to get away. Thanks to environmentalist Howard Zahniser, Americans can do that in one of the country's many wildernesses—areas sheltered from human activities. While conservation efforts like the creation of national forests and parks began in the late 1800s, untamed wilderness had dwindled to only 2.5% of the nation's land by the 1960s. To reverse this trend, Zahniser wrote most of what became the Wilderness Act. Signed into law by President Lyndon Johnson on September 3, 1964, it today protects more than 109 million acres—5% of the land in the US.

bing-48695.jpg.title: La Vuelta en Peñas Blancas, Estepona, Málaga
bing-48695.jpg.headline: ¡Pedalea hasta la meta!. La Vuelta
bing-48695.jpg.description:
¿Estás preparado para una ruta inolvidable por la Península Ibérica? La Vuelta 2024 ya ha comenzado y culminará el 8 de septiembre en Madrid. Esta edición cuenta con 21 etapas y abarcará un total de 3.265 kilómetros, en los que los ciclistas atravesarán 9 comunidades autónomas y dos países, España y Portugal, ofreciendo un espectáculo único.

El recorrido está diseñado para ser tanto exigente como diverso: habrá 5 etapas onduladas (dos de ellas con final en alto), 2 contrarrelojes individuales, 5 de media montaña, 8 de alta montaña y una llana. Entre las cumbres más destacadas se encuentran el imponente Cuitu Negro y el majestuoso Alto de Hazallanas, así como los desafiantes puertos de Leitariegos y El Purche.

La combinación de paisajes impresionantes, desafíos técnicos y la pasión de los ciclistas hacen de este evento una cita imperdible. Ya seas un aficionado del ciclismo o simplemente alguien que disfruta de los deportes, esta edición promete emociones intensas y momentos de pura adrenalina.

bing-48702.jpg.title: Dusky eagle-owls, Pakistan
bing-48702.jpg.headline: Birds of a feather hoot together. Dusky eagle-owls, Pakistan
bing-48702.jpg.description: As daylight fades, dusky eagle-owls, the silent hunters seen in today's image, emerge from their nests. These primarily nocturnal raptors were snapped in Pakistan and can be found in the forests and scrublands across South and Southeast Asia. An impressive wingspan of 15–17 inches, piercing yellow eyes, and exceptional hearing help them to catch small mammals and birds with precision in dim light. Measuring up to 2 feet tall, these feathered predators can also be spotted hunting in the daytime when the weather is cloudy. They often live in the abandoned nests of other birds or in natural crevices. Dusky eagle-owls breed in December and January, usually rearing their young in the safety of tall trees or cliff ledges. Nature lovers and bird watchers are captivated by their solemn gaze and elegant stature.

bing-48712.jpg.title: Confluência do Rio Negro e do Amazonas, Manaus, estado do Amazonas
bing-48712.jpg.headline: O Encontro das Águas
bing-48712.jpg.description:
Imagine um espetáculo da natureza onde dois rios dançam lado a lado, sem jamais se misturar. E é nesse Encontro das Águas que celebramos o Dia da Amazônia, onde o Rio Negro, de águas escuras e ácidas, e o Rio Solimões, barrento e alcalino, se abraçam numa extensão de mais de 6 quilômetros. Eles correm lado a lado devido às diferenças de temperatura, densidade e velocidade, embora acabem se juntando depois para formar parte do majestoso Rio Amazonas.

O vasto e vital bioma amazônico, com seus incríveis 5,5 milhões de quilômetros quadrados, precisa do nosso compromisso inabalável. No Brasil, reconhecemos a urgência de preservar essa maravilha natural, onde cada hectare é crucial para o equilíbrio climático global. Participe das iniciativas locais de conservação, porque quando se trata da Amazônia, cada ação conta. Juntos, podemos garantir que as futuras gerações também celebrarão esta data!

bing-48714.jpg.title: Toronto city skyline seen from Lake Ontario, Canada
bing-48714.jpg.headline: Lights, camera, TIFF '24!. 2024 Toronto International Film Festival
bing-48714.jpg.description: Cinema aficionados, assemble. The Toronto International Film Festival (TIFF) gears up to dazzle with its 49th edition in Canada's largest city, seen in today's image. Since it began in 1976, the TIFF has become one of the largest publicly attended film festivals in the world. Attendees range from seasoned directors to rising stars and eager cinephiles and the festival has hosted premieres of many critically acclaimed films, including 'The Fabelmans' and 'Black Swan.'

bing-48722.jpg.title: Cabines de plage à Deauville, France
bing-48722.jpg.headline: Moteur… action !. Festival du cinéma américain de Deauville
bing-48722.jpg.description:
À vos caméras ! Le Festival du film américain de Deauville attire chaque année des milliers de passionnés et de professionnels du septième art. Situé sur la côte normande, ce festival célèbre depuis 1975 les productions américaines, offrant une vitrine prestigieuse aux talents émergents et confirmés. Les projections, souvent en avant-première européenne, se déroulent dans des salles de renom telles que le Centre international de Deauville et sont accompagnées de discussions enrichissantes et de rencontres avec les réalisateurs et les acteurs.

Parallèlement aux festivités cinématographiques, les festivaliers peuvent profiter des célèbres plages de Deauville. Les Planches, en photo aujourd’hui, offrent une vue imprenable sur la mer et permettent d’admirer les cabines de bain portant les noms des stars hollywoodiennes ayant visité la ville. Alliant culture et détente, Deauville offre une expérience unique et mémorable pour tous les amoureux du cinéma et de la mer !

bing-48726.jpg.title: Ancient beech tree, Glenariff Forest Park, County Antrim, Northern Ireland
bing-48726.jpg.headline: 'Wood' you believe this view?. Glenariff Forest Park, Northern Ireland, UK
bing-48726.jpg.description: Ever wondered what it's like to stroll through a storybook? Welcome to Glenariff Forest Park in County Antrim, Northern Ireland. This park spans nearly 3,000 acres of woodland, waterfalls, and wonder, and it boasts several walking trails, each offering its own unique perspective of the landscape. The most popular is the Waterfall Walkway, a 3-mile trail that passes through a National Nature Reserve and features the Ess-na-Crub and Ess-na-Larach waterfalls. Glenariff is home to a rich diversity of wildlife including red squirrels, pine martens, and badgers. Birdwatchers will be delighted by willow warblers, chiffchaffs, and kingfishers. The flora is just as impressive, with trees such as the ancient beech, pictured here, oak, birch, and rowan creating a lush canopy. So, whenever you choose to visit, Glenariff is sure to leave you feeling 're-leafed' and rejuvenated.

bing-48730.jpg.title: Idols of Lord Ganesha for sale in Gulbai tekra, Ahmedabad
bing-48730.jpg.headline: Crafted blessings. Ganesh Chaturthi
bing-48730.jpg.description:
Get ready to dance and paint the town red; it's Ganesh Chaturthi. The festival honours Ganesha, revered as the Hindu deity of fresh starts and the dispeller of challenges, along with being the embodiment of wisdom and intellect. Celebrated across the Indian subcontinent, it brings together people in a joyous observance. The exact origins of the festival are not clear, but it has been a prominent public celebration in Pune since the time of King Shivaji, who ruled from 1630 to 1680. Later freedom fighter Bal Gangadhar popularised it in Maharashtra in 1893. This move aimed to foster a 'Hindu nationalist identity' and resist British colonial rule.

Ganesh Chaturthi is observed with the installation of clay Ganesha idols both in homes and in grand public displays set up on temporary stages called pandals. The festivities conclude with a grand public procession, featuring music and collective chanting. On Ananta Chaturdashi, or the tenth day, the idol is carried to a nearby river or sea for immersion, known as 'visarjana'. After this, the clay idol dissolves, symbolising Ganesha's return to his heavenly abode.

bing-48733.jpg.title: Vista di Firenze dal Duomo, Toscana, Italia
bing-48733.jpg.headline: Scivoli rinascimentali?
bing-48733.jpg.description:
Firenze, culla del Rinascimento e gioiello incastonato nel cuore della Toscana, è un museo a cielo aperto che incanta ogni visitatore con la sua bellezza senza tempo. Passeggiare tra i suoi vicoli significa viaggiare indietro nella storia, scoprendo tesori architettonici come il Duomo di Santa Maria del Fiore con la sua imponente cupola di Brunelleschi, o la maestosa Galleria degli Uffizi che custodisce alcuni dei più famosi capolavori dell'arte mondiale. Oggi però, invece che portarvi alla scoperta di basiliche e musei, vi racconteremo di un evento tipico del capoluogo toscano.

Il 7 settembre è un evento speciale e si celebra la Festa della Rificolona, giorno della vigilia della natività di Maria. Questo evento, databile tra il XVI e il XVII secolo, è caratterizzato da una suggestiva sfilata di lanterne colorate, portate dai bambini in corteo per le strade della città, simboleggiando il percorso dei pellegrini verso la Basilica della Santissima Annunziata. Le rificolone, originariamente semplici lanterne di carta, si sono evolute in creazioni sempre più elaborate e ingegnose, illuminando la notte fiorentina con una magia che lascia gli spettatori a bocca aperta.

bing-48736.jpg.title: Parque da Independência, São Paulo
bing-48736.jpg.headline: Uma viagem no tempo
bing-48736.jpg.description:
Hoje comemoramos o Dia da Independência do Brasil, um marco que reverbera pelas paredes do imponente Museu do Ipiranga. Imagine-se passeando pelos jardins que parecem pinturas e se maravilhando com relíquias que contam nosso percurso como nação... Localizado em São Paulo, o museu foi construído no lugar onde Dom Pedro I declarou a independência em 7 de setembro de 1822. Marcado pelo estilo neoclássico, sua arquitetura foi inspirada no esplendor de Versalhes e reflete a grandiosidade da cidade de São Paulo no século XIX.

Este ícone paulista detém mais de 450 mil peças artísticas e históricas, incluindo a épica pintura de "Independência ou Morte" (1888) de autoria de Pedro Américo. Após uma monumental restauração, o museu agora permite que qualquer um explore séculos de história com um toque moderno de realidade aumentada.  Um legado cultural no coração de São Paulo com destaque especial para o período do Império e a vida cotidiana no século XIX - uma viagem pela nossa soberania e progresso!

bing-48738.jpg.title: Anna's hummingbird, Santa Cruz, California
bing-48738.jpg.headline: Humming along. National Hummingbird Day
bing-48738.jpg.description: Every first Saturday in September, bird enthusiasts and nature lovers gather to celebrate National Hummingbird Day. This day is dedicated to appreciating these tiny, agile birds and their role as a pollinator in our ecosystem. Hummingbirds are known for their incredible speed; they can flap their wings up to 80 times per second, allowing them to hover in place and even fly backward. Emily Dickinson aptly describes their swift movement: 'A Route of Evanescence / With a revolving Wheel—.' Their high metabolism requires them to eat constantly, so they spend their days flitting from flower to flower, sipping nectar and catching insects. Fun fact: these birds can remember every flower they've visited and how long it will take a flower to refill with nectar.

bing-48747.jpg.title: Tyne Bridge, England
bing-48747.jpg.headline: 'Tyne' to shine. Great North Run
bing-48747.jpg.description:
Today, the streets of Newcastle will transform into a sea of runners, joggers and walkers all headed in one direction—south. The Great North Run, the world's largest half marathon, is back. Founded in 1981 by former Olympic 10,000-metre bronze medallist Brendan Foster, this annual event started with humble beginnings. Just over 12,000 runners took part in the inaugural race, but it quickly grew into a phenomenon. Today, the race attracts around 60,000 participants each year, from elite athletes to charity fundraisers dressed as giant bananas.

The 13.1-mile course is a scenic tour of the northeast, beginning in the heart of Newcastle and crossing the iconic Tyne Bridge, featured in today's image. Along the course, you'll find locals offering everything from cheers to jelly sweets, and let's not forget the famous 'Oggy, Oggy, Oggy' chant echoing through the streets. The finish line at South Shields is where the real celebration begins. And if you've made it this far, you deserve a medal—and maybe a pint or two.

bing-48750.jpg.title: Interior of the Stockholm Public Library, Sweden
bing-48750.jpg.headline: A global chapter. International Literacy Day
bing-48750.jpg.description: 'Literacy is a bridge from misery to hope.' These words by former secretary-general of the United Nations Kofi Annan capture the essence of International Literacy Day, celebrated every September 8. Established by UNESCO in 1966, this observance not only celebrates those who can read but also highlights the ongoing battle against illiteracy. With approximately 775 million people worldwide still lacking basic literacy, this day resonates powerfully within the hallowed walls of the Stockholm Public Library in Sweden, or 'Stadsbiblioteket' as it is known to locals, featured in today's image.

bing-48751.jpg.title: Abbey of Saint-Martin-du-Canigou, Northern Catalonia, France
bing-48751.jpg.headline: Abbey of Saint-Martin-du-Canigou
bing-48751.jpg.description: Looking for a timeless getaway? The Abbey of Saint-Martin du Canigou opens its doors to you! Nestled in the western foothills of the Canigou massif in the Pyrénées-Orientales, this is an eleventh-century Romanesque marvel. The abbey has two churches built in the first Romanesque style: the lower church, dedicated to St. Mary, and the upper church, dedicated to St. Martin. This historic structure is catalogued in the Base Mérimée, an architectural heritage database managed by the French Ministry of Culture. The original appearance of the cloister is now hard to envision due to extensive restorations carried out between 1900 and 1920.
