Ese mismo día, en 1492, el Descubrimiento de América marcó el inicio de un contacto trascendental entre los continentes, uniendo a Europa y América en un evento histórico de inmensa relevancia.

Desde 1892, esta festividad se distingue por sus majestuosos desfiles militares y vibrantes exhibiciones aéreas en el Paseo de la Castellana de Madrid, como se puede ver en la imagen de hoy. El evento, que comienza en la Plaza de Neptuno, es presenciado por la familia real y altos representantes del Estado, incluidos los de las comunidades autónomas. Además, hoy se honra a la Virgen del Pilar, patrona de Zaragoza y de España.

Conocida también como el Día de la Hispanidad, esta festividad celebra la conexión histórica y cultural entre España y América.
bing-49153.jpg.copyright: © Carlos Alvarez/Fotógrafo autónomo/Getty Images Entertainment/Getty Image

bing-49158.jpg.title: Brinquedos tradicionais feitos com a fibra da palmeira Miriti, Belém
bing-49158.jpg.headline: Navegando pela imaginação
bing-49158.jpg.description:
Hoje, o Brasil celebra com muito carinho o Dia das Crianças! Esta data tão especial destaca-se por ser um símbolo do compromisso da nossa nação com os pequenos. Você sabia que o Brasil foi um dos primeiros países em oficializar um dia dedicado a celebrar a infância? Hoje é um dia para lembrar da necessidade de garantir educação de qualidade, saúde, segurança e proteção contra qualquer tipo de exploração. Está intimamente entrelaçado ao Estatuto da Criança e do Adolescente (ECA), que defende esses direitos essenciais.

E nesse espírito festivo, convidamos você a mergulhar nos mares da imaginação com esses tesouros coloridos: os brinquedos feitos da fibra da palmeira miriti que apreciamos na imagem de hoje. Nas mãos hábeis dos artesãos paraenses, a fibra da palmeira se transforma em brinquedos que carregam em si a magia das lendas amazônicas. Mais do que brinquedos, cada criação é um manifesto ecológico, uma celebração de uma matéria-prima sustentável e um convite à responsabilidade ambiental, mostrando que é possível sim, brincar e ao mesmo tempo preservar.

bing-49160.jpg.title: Wood duck, Quebec, Canada
bing-49160.jpg.headline: It's time to wing it!. World Migratory Bird Day
bing-49160.jpg.description:
Celebrate our traveling feathered friends on World Migratory Bird Day! Some migrations are truly astounding. The bar-tailed godwit embarks on a nearly 7,000-mile nonstop flight across the Pacific from Alaska to New Zealand. The tiny ruby-throated hummingbird, weighing less than a nickel, makes the trip all the way across the Gulf of Mexico. Migratory birds navigate the globe, instinctively knowing when and where to move to exploit seasonal abundance. The Arctic tern outshines them all with its intercontinental journey from pole to pole, covering roughly 25,000 miles in its annual round trip.

Let's take a moment to admire the vibrant plumage of the wood duck, photographed in Quebec, Canada. Wood ducks nest in tree cavities close to water and sometimes take advantage of human-made boxes. During the breeding season, from February to April, you'll find the females laying 7–15 eggs. From the eastern and western United States and southern Canada, these ducks migrate southward in the fall to avoid harsh winter conditions. By October and November, they move towards milder climates in the southeastern US and occasionally into Mexico.

bing-49172.jpg.title: Courtyard of the Maidens, Alcázar of Seville, Spain
bing-49172.jpg.headline: The splendor of Seville. Royal Alcázar of Seville, Spain
bing-49172.jpg.description:
Today we're stepping into the heart of the historic empire of Islamic Spain. The Royal Alcázar of Seville, in the southern region of Andalusia, stands on the site of a 10th-century citadel, which was expanded over the following 200 years. When Christian forces captured the city in 1248, this historic palace was almost totally rebuilt in the Mudejar style, which takes inspiration from the intricate patterns and decorative motifs found in Islamic architecture. Within the Alcázar, there are several courtyards lined with delicately carved columns. One of these is the Patio de las Doncellas, or Courtyard of the Maidens, pictured here today.

In the center of this beautiful space is a pool, whose still waters provide reflections of not only the blue Andalucian sky above, but of the intricate latticework of the courtyard's arches. Look a little closer at these arches, and you'll see carved shells, Hands of Fatima—a symbol said to bring protection—plants, and Arabic script. Behind the columns, the walls are decorated with colorful ceramic tiles decorated with geometric patterns. These tiles, known as azulejos, are a hallmark of Andalusian decoration. Outside, there is a large garden full of fountains and tree-lined paths—a perfect spot to cool off from the hot Spanish sun.

bing-49174.jpg.title: 東京駅, 東京都
bing-49174.jpg.headline: 今日は鉄道の日
bing-49174.jpg.description:
今日 10 月 14 日は鉄道の日。1872 年に新橋と横浜の間に日本初の鉄道が開業した日であり、1921 年に鉄道開業 50 周年を記念して東京駅の丸の内北口に初代の鉄道博物館が開館した日でもあります。この日を記念して、日本全国の駅や鉄道関連の博物館などでは様々なイベントが行われます…

そして、画像は東京駅。新幹線や在来線、地下鉄など、1 日当たりの列車発着本数は約 3000 本以上というターミナル駅です。建築家辰野金吾らが設計し、ヨーロッパの建築様式を取り入れた赤レンガ造りの壮麗な丸の内駅舎は、東京のシンボルとも言える存在で、2003 年に国の重要文化財にも指定されました。

bing-49180.jpg.title: Bateaux dans la baie de Marigot, Terre-de-Haut, archipel des Saintes, Guadeloupe
bing-49180.jpg.headline: Un cadre idylique. Baie de Marigot, Guadeloupe
bing-49180.jpg.description:
Plongez dans la magie de la plage de Marigot à Terre-de-Haut, l'une des plus belles baies du monde. Cette perle des Saintes vous séduira avec ses ruelles colorées, ses charmantes cases en bois et ses barques multicolores. Imaginez-vous déambuler dans cette ville pittoresque, où chaque coin de rue cache un trésor.

Ne ratez pas le Fort Napoléon, une forteresse majestueuse offrant une vue à couper le souffle sur la Guadeloupe. Pour les gourmands, laissez-vous tenter par le Tourment d'Amour, une tartelette exquise à la banane, à la noix de coco ou à la goyave.

La plage de Marigot est un véritable havre de paix pour les amoureux de la nature et de la culture. Ses eaux turquoise et son ambiance sereine en font l'endroit parfait pour se détendre et savourer la beauté naturelle de l'île. Laissez-vous envoûter par la magie de Terre-de-Haut, une expérience inoubliable vous attend !

bing-49181.jpg.title: Coco Beach, Goa, India
bing-49181.jpg.headline: Sandy secrets and sunsets. Coco Beach, Goa, India
bing-49181.jpg.description:
Welcome to every beach lover's dream: Goa. This Indian state is known for its golden shores that draw visitors from all over the world. Tourism is at the heart of its economy, and it's no surprise that most of the buzz happens along its coastline, 78 miles of which is covered by beaches. Today's image features Coco Beach, a gem tucked away in Nerul, a village in the northern part of the state. Despite its calm vibes, there's plenty to do here. You can soak up the sun and dive into adventures like fishing, boating, dolphin spotting and swimming, all while immersing yourself in the local culture. But there's something that makes this beach even more special: its historical significance.

It played an important role in the Goa Liberation Movement during the 1950s and 60s. It was one of the places where locals fought to end Portuguese rule and unite Goa with India. So, Coco isn't just another beach; it's a place with stories to tell, where history meets the sea.

bing-49184.jpg.title: Ancestral Pueblo granaries at Nankoweap, Grand Canyon National Park, Arizona
bing-49184.jpg.headline: Honoring Indigenous Peoples. Celebrating Indigenous Peoples' Day
bing-49184.jpg.description:
The second Monday of October is used by many to celebrate Indigenous Peoples' Day as an alternative to Columbus Day, held on the same date. It highlights the customs and heritage of the Indigenous Peoples who lived in North America before the arrival of European settlers, and the devastating impact colonization had upon them.

Today's image takes us to one of the places that Indigenous Peoples' legacy can still be seen. In the rocks of the Grand Canyon, the Nankoweap Granaries were carved by the Ancestral Pueblo culture around 1100 CE. Used to keep the crops that were grown safe from the elements, these granaries could be fully sealed when needed. The Ancestral Pueblo people lived in the Four Corners region, building houses and other structures out of stone and adobe, or carving them into canyon walls.

bing-49196.jpg.title: Great wildebeest migration at Mara River, Kenya
bing-49196.jpg.headline: The race for life. Great wildebeest migration at Mara River, Kenya
bing-49196.jpg.description:
They say the grass is always greener on the other side, and no one takes that more literally than the wildebeests of the Serengeti in Tanzania. Every July, roughly 2 million of these determined grazers, along with zebras and other herbivores, set off on a journey north to the Masai Mara in Kenya in search of lush pastures and fresh water. The great migration, considered one of the seven wonders of the natural world, is a safari spectacle where survival is the prize.

One of the most dramatic moments of the migration is the crossing of the Mara River at the border between Tanzania and Kenya. Thousands of wildebeests gather at the riverbank, aware that danger lurks beneath the surface—crocodiles—not to mention the lions and leopards that patrol the banks. When the first wildebeest takes the plunge, it's a wild rush as the rest of the herd follows, creating a chaotic scene. Some make it across, while others become part of the food chain. As October rolls around and the rains return to the Serengeti, the herds begin their journey back south, completing the cycle once again.

bing-49203.jpg.title: Vista su Piazza Venezia e il centro di Roma, Roma, Italia
bing-49203.jpg.headline: Ciak, comincia la Festa
bing-49203.jpg.description:
La Festa del Cinema di Roma 2024, che si svolgerà all’Auditorium Parco della Musica Ennio Morricone, celebra il centenario della nascita di Marcello Mastroianni con un omaggio speciale: l’immagine del manifesto del Festival ritrae Guido Anselmi, il celebre personaggio interpretato dall’attore nel film “8 ½” (1963) di Federico Fellini e vincitore di due premi Oscar. Si tratta di una delle icone più luminose del cinema italiano, e la scelta di questo personaggio rappresenta un tributo alla carriera leggendaria e al suo immenso contributo al mondo del cinema.

Dal 16 al 27 ottobre, la capitale ospiterà una selezione di film di altissimo livello. Il Festival offrirà anche eventi speciali e retrospettive, mantenendo viva la tradizione di celebrare il meglio della cinematografia contemporanea e di esplorare nuovi talenti. Con il centenario di Mastroianni come punto di riferimento, la Festa del Cinema di Roma 2024 si preannuncia come un’edizione imperdibile per tutti gli appassionati di cinema. Venite a Roma e immergetevi in proiezioni cinematografiche, documentari, retrospettive e nelle strade della città eterna, proprio come se foste protagonisti di un viaggio onirico nell’universo felliniano.

bing-49208.jpg.title: Fossils of belemnites and ammonites, Jurassic Coast, Dorset, England
bing-49208.jpg.headline: Unearthing the past. National Fossil Day
bing-49208.jpg.description:
If you're a fan of dinosaurs, trilobites, or fossilized shells, then National Fossil Day is the perfect excuse to get your hands dirty. Celebrated on the second Wednesday of October, this day is dedicated to promoting the scientific and educational value of fossils. From towering T. rexes to tiny ammonites, these ancient remains help scientists piece together the puzzle of our planet's history.

Let's visit the Jurassic Coast, a UNESCO World Heritage Site in Dorset, England, pictured here today. It's like a giant natural history museum, with rocks and cliffs that reveal 185 million years of Earth's history. But what really steals the show are the fossils, especially those of belemnites and ammonites—extinct marine creatures—that are pictured here. Mary Anning, a pioneering fossil hunter who combed these shores two centuries ago, paved the way for our current understanding of fossils. Now, it's your turn. Embrace National Fossil Day by embarking on your own journey through time.

bing-49216.jpg.title: Volcan Formica Leo, Piton de la Fournaise, île de La Réunion
bing-49216.jpg.headline: Connaissez-vous la Diagonale des Fous ?. Grand Raid La Réunion 2024
bing-49216.jpg.description:
Chaque année, en octobre, l'île de La Réunion devient le théâtre d'une aventure épique : le Grand Raid, également connu sous le nom de Diagonale des Fous. Cette course mythique de 48h, longue de 165 km avec 10 000 mètres de dénivelé positif, attire des coureurs du monde entier. Le parcours traverse des paysages à couper le souffle, dont le majestueux Piton de la Fournaise, l'un des volcans les plus actifs de la planète, en photo aujourd’hui.

Ce volcan, avec ses éruptions effusives régulières, offre un spectacle naturel impressionnant. Les coureurs, en passant à proximité de ce géant de feu, ressentent la puissance brute de la nature. Le volcan, qui a contribué à la formation de l'île il y a des millions d'années, est un symbole de la force et de la résilience, des qualités essentielles pour les participants du Grand Raid.

Participer à cette course, c'est non seulement un défi sportif, mais aussi une immersion dans un environnement unique où la nature règne en maître. La Diagonale des Fous est bien plus qu'une simple course, c'est une expérience inoubliable qui marie sport et découverte de la beauté sauvage de La Réunion.
bing-49216.jpg.copyright: © Stefan Kiefer/imageBROKER.com GmbH & Co. KG/Alamy Stock Phot

bing-49220.jpg.title: Frost-covered dunes on the surface of Mars
bing-49220.jpg.headline: Astronauts, grab your skis!. Frost-covered dunes on Mars
bing-49220.jpg.description:
Mars, the fourth planet from the sun, is often referred to as the 'Red Planet' due to its rusty hue from the iron oxide-rich soil dust. The planet is dotted with frosty dunes, largely located in the high latitudes of the northern plains. Mars' atmosphere is composed of nearly 96% carbon dioxide, which is why carbon ice forms on the surface. These dunes showcase the dynamic interaction between Mars' thin atmosphere, its surface, and seasonal temperature changes.

As the Martian seasons change, the frost layer transforms directly from solid to gas as temperatures rise. The dunes then gradually lose their frosty appearance, and the cycle repeats with each cold season. Data collected from spacecraft and orbiters, like NASA's Phoenix spacecraft and the Mars Reconnaissance Orbiter, has helped us to better understand these intriguing frost-covered formations.

bing-49231.jpg.title: The Milky Way above Pyramid Lake, Jasper National Park, Alberta, Canada
bing-49231.jpg.headline: Stars above, stillness below. Jasper Dark Sky Festival, Alberta
bing-49231.jpg.description:
As dusk settles over Jasper National Park, Alberta, the stars begin to dot the sky, glittering like diamonds. This panorama is no accident—as a designated Dark Sky Preserve since 2011, Jasper has made strides to protect its nocturnal environment, minimising light pollution and allowing stargazers to witness the galaxy's splendour unhindered. Jasper National Park is the largest national park within Alberta's Rocky Mountains, spanning 11,000 square kilometres.

If looking at the stars brings a smile to your face, then this reserve is the place to be, as the Jasper Dark Sky Festival begins today. Attendees can expect a schedule filled with engaging activities, from expert-led workshops and keynote speeches to night sky photography sessions. The 16-day festival offers an educational experience where you and your friends can learn about constellations, planet spotting and the importance of dark sky conservation. So, join the Jasper Dark Sky Festival, where the stars are the luminous storytellers.

bing-49232.jpg.title: Autumn in Central Park, Manhattan, New York
bing-49232.jpg.headline: Falling for Central Park. Autumn in Central Park, New York
bing-49232.jpg.description:
Every autumn, many of the 18,000 trees in Central Park, New York, are painted in shades of yellow, red, and orange. It's one of Central Park's most photographed seasons, and fall in the park has provided iconic backdrops for movies like 'When Harry Met Sally…' and 'Hair.' Trees sense the coming of winter not only by temperature, but by the angle at which sunlight hits their leaves. Because of New York's buildings, the unique interaction of light, shadows, and temperatures often results in fall foliage occurring later in the park than the rest of the city.

Today's image features fall in the Mall, a pedestrian walkway designed and built in the mid-1800s. Flanked by benches and American elm trees, the Mall's canopy was meant to evoke an architectural space like a cathedral. The quarter-mile promenade is the park's only straight path, and it was intended to be a place for New Yorkers of all classes and backgrounds to gather, stroll, sit, and perhaps ponder the passing seasons.

bing-49244.jpg.title: Temple of Hathor, Dendera Temple Complex, Qena, Egypt
bing-49244.jpg.headline: Uncovering the past. International Archaeology Day
bing-49244.jpg.description:
Today, dig deep and unearth your inner Indiana Jones or Lara Croft on International Archaeology Day. The event celebrates archaeology's benefits for society, and includes exhibits and hands-on excavations, some of which run throughout the month. Many US national and state parks, historic landmarks, and local museums also hold events.

Egypt is steeped in ancient history and home to many internationally renowned archaeological sites, including the Temple of Hathor, the ceiling of which can be seen in today's image. Part of the Dendera Temple Complex in Qena, Hathor is one of the best-preserved ancient Egyptian temples. While the current temple dates to Ptolemy XII and Cleopatra VII (around 50 BCE), evidence suggests that previous temples dedicated to Hathor, an Egyptian goddess of love and fertility, go back thousands of years earlier.

bing-49249.jpg.title: Puesta de sol en Almuñécar, Granada
bing-49249.jpg.headline: Sobre ruedas hacia el horizonte. Campeonato de España de BMX Racing 2024
bing-49249.jpg.description:
Hoy, la localidad granadina de Almuñécar acoge con entusiasmo la edición 2024 del Campeonato de España de BMX Racing. Tras haber sido sede en 2020 y 2021, y consolidarse como una de las citas clásicas de la Copa de España, Almuñécar se transforma nuevamente en el escenario ideal para este evento, que promete emociones y adrenalina con la llegada de los mejores ciclistas del país, listos para competir al más alto nivel.

Este campeonato forma parte de un circuito de seis pruebas puntuables, que comenzó en Mazarrón y culminará en El Campello. En esta jornada decisiva, los pilotos se juegan puntos cruciales en un entorno inigualable, famoso por sus paisajes costeros, su historia milenaria y su envidiable clima.

En la imagen de hoy, Almuñécar se presenta en todo su esplendor, con sus playas bañadas por el sol y las montañas que enmarcan este enclave privilegiado, ofreciendo el escenario perfecto para esta vibrante competición. Sin duda, es una experiencia única para quienes desean combinar la emoción del BMX con la belleza de la costa tropical.

bing-49252.jpg.title: Vignobles de Champagne, parc naturel régional de la Montagne de Reims, Verzenay
bing-49252.jpg.headline: Mélodies au cœur des vignes. Les Nuits de Champagne
bing-49252.jpg.description:
Au cœur de la région Champagne, le parc naturel régional de la Montagne de Reims se dévoile comme un trésor inestimable, où la nature et la culture s’entrelacent harmonieusement. Imaginez des forêts denses, des collines verdoyantes et des vignobles en terrasses, offrant un panorama à couper le souffle. Chaque année, le festival des Nuits de Champagne, qui se déroule à Troyes depuis 1988, attire des milliers d’amateurs de musique. Cette célébration de la chanson francophone est une invitation à l’évasion.

Avant une journée rythmée par des concerts envoûtants, offrez-vous une balade dans les sentiers boisés de la montagne de Reims. Un verre de champagne local à la main, laissez-vous bercer par le murmure des arbres et le chant des oiseaux. Les Nuits de Champagne transcendent le simple festival ; elles sont une véritable immersion dans l’art, la nature et le terroir. Plongez dans cette atmosphère unique, où chaque note musicale résonne avec la beauté des paysages environnants. Explorez la magie de la montagne de Reims et savourez cette expérience inoubliable !

bing-49256.jpg.title: Three-toed sloth in Costa Rica
bing-49256.jpg.headline: Hanging in there. International Sloth Day
bing-49256.jpg.description:
The world's slowest mammal takes the spotlight today on International Sloth Day. Celebrated on October 20, it highlights their lives, conservation efforts, and the threats they face, including shrinking habitats. There are six living sloth species, divided into two types: three-toed sloths and two-toed sloths.

Today's image features the laid-back, tree-loving, three-toed sloth, found in the tropical regions of South and Central America. With three clawed toes on each limb, they cling onto branches with ease. Sloths are mainly leaf eaters, and to help them break down tough, fibrous leaves, they have a special multi-chambered stomach. With their super slow metabolism, digestion takes its sweet time, and they don't need much food each day to get by. They're so slow-moving that algae often develop on their fur, giving a greenish tint that provides them camouflage.

bing-49262.jpg.title: Herbstbäume am Baldeneysee, NRW
bing-49262.jpg.headline: Goldene Momente. Baldeneysee, NRW
bing-49262.jpg.description:
Der Baldeneysee, der größte der sechs Ruhrstauseen, liegt idyllisch im Süden von Essen und ist ein beliebtes Ausflugsziel für Naturliebhaber und Wassersportbegeisterte. Der künstlich angelegte See, der auf unserem heutigen Bild abgelichtet wurde, entstand 1933 durch die Aufstauung der Ruhr und erstreckt sich über eine Fläche von etwa 2,7 Quadratkilometern. Hier finden Sie nicht nur Ruhe und Entspannung, sondern auch vielfältige Freizeitmöglichkeiten.

Wassersportler kommen voll auf ihre Kosten: Segeln, Rudern und Stand-Up-Paddling sind nur einige der Aktivitäten, die am Baldeneysee angeboten werden. Für Radfahrer und Wanderer gibt es einen 14 Kilometer langen Rundweg um den See, der durch grüne Landschaften und Naturschutzgebiete führt. Ein besonderes Highlight ist die Villa Hügel, das ehemalige Wohnhaus der Industriellenfamilie Krupp, das in unmittelbarer Nähe liegt. Heute ist die Villa ein Museum und kultureller Veranstaltungsort, der einen Einblick in die Geschichte der Familie Krupp und die Industrialisierung Deutschlands bietet.

bing-49268.jpg.title: Cypress trees in George L. Smith State Park, Georgia
bing-49268.jpg.headline: Standing tall in fall. Cypress trees in George L. Smith State Park, Georgia
bing-49268.jpg.description: The sturdy, swamp-loving, cypress trees pictured in the mist on our homepage can grow over 100 feet tall. These towering specimens are found in George L. Smith State Park, which spans 1,634 acres in Emanuel County, Georgia. The park's centerpiece is a 412-acre mill pond, a favorite spot for fishing and canoeing. Out of its waters grow pond cypress and bald cypress trees, two varieties that are native to the southeastern US. Winding through the park are over 7 miles of nature trails, leading visitors through sandy landscapes past a bird sanctuary and tortoise habitat. The hardwood trees here are a haven for woodpeckers and other birds, while the soft soil provides ideal burrowing ground for tortoises. No matter the season, this park promises a peaceful retreat for all.

bing-49270.jpg.title: 平安神宮, 京都府 京都市
bing-49270.jpg.headline: 今日は平安遷都の日
bing-49270.jpg.description:
今日 10 月 22 日は平安遷都の日。西暦 785 年の藤原種継暗殺事件で首謀者の一人とされた早良親王は、身の潔白を信じてもらえず、怨みを抱いて亡くなりました。その後、親王の怨霊によるものとされる飢饉や疫病など様々な不吉な出来事に悩まされた桓武天皇は、西暦 794 年 10 月 22 日、長岡京から平安京に遷都しました…

平安遷都を記念して、本日京都で平安神宮の例大祭「時代祭」が開催されます。祭りの最大の見どころは都の 1000 年を振り返る「時代風俗行列」です。約 2000 人の市民が歴史的な衣装を着て京都の街を練り歩き、平安時代から明治時代までの各時代の文化や風俗を再現します。

bing-49280.jpg.title: Palazzo Zuccari, Rome, Italy
bing-49280.jpg.headline: Fearsome façade. Palazzo Zuccari, Rome
bing-49280.jpg.description:
At the top of the Spanish Steps in Rome, take a left underneath the imposing Catholic church. Down an unassuming side street, there's a surprise waiting for you: a house of monsters. Welcome to the Palazzo Zuccari, a 16th-century palace where myths seem to come to life on its façade—grotesque faces swallow up its doors and windows. Federico Zuccari, who built the palace, was well-versed in monsters. His painting of the Last Judgment in Florence Cathedral and his illustrations of Dante's Inferno are replete with mythical beings. The monster door originally led to the palazzo's garden because Zuccari enjoyed making his guests experience the contrast between the scary entrance and the beautiful serenity of the garden. These days, the door leads to the Bibliotheca Hertziana, a library specializing in Italian art history, from the Middle Ages to the modern day, which has occupied the site of the garden since 1912.

If you're looking for more monstrous mouths in Rome, not far from the Palazzo Zuccari is the Bocca della Verità, an ancient Roman mask. According to legend, it will bite off any liar's hand that's placed in its mouth.

bing-49282.jpg.title: 紅葉に包まれた法体の滝, 秋田県 由利本荘市
bing-49282.jpg.headline: 今日は霜降
bing-49282.jpg.description:
今日 10 月 23 日は二十四節気の「霜降」。朝晩の冷え込みが一層厳しくなり、地面や草木に霜が降りる時期です。木々の紅葉が進み、秋田県由利本荘市の「法体の滝」を取り囲む木々も、鮮やかな赤や黄色に染まり、滝の白い水しぶきとコントラストを描きます…

「法体の滝」は子吉川の上流である赤沢川にかかる美しい滝で、一の滝、二の滝、三の滝といった三段の滝から成っています。滝の周辺には 10 万年前の溶岩流で削られた多くの甌穴（おうけつ）があり、これらの甌穴は滝とともに、秋田県の名勝および天然記念物に指定されています。

bing-49292.jpg.title: Madame Sherri Forest and the ruins of an old castle, New Hampshire
bing-49292.jpg.headline: Stairway to nowhere. Madame Sherri Forest, New Hampshire
bing-49292.jpg.description:
Madame Sherri Forest in Chesterfield, New Hampshire, is a captivating destination steeped in history and natural beauty. It was once the site of an extravagant house built in the 1930s by Madame Antoinette Sherri, a flamboyant 1920s costume designer known for her lavish parties. Madame Sherri's dramatic arrivals in town, often in a chauffeur-driven Packard, draped in furs, became the talk of the locals. As her fortune declined, her 'castle' fell into disrepair and was vandalized. In 1959, she returned to find her property in ruins and never came back. A fire destroyed the house in 1963, leaving behind only the stone foundation, an iconic staircase, and a large fireplace leading to a lone chimney.

Today, the forest where her house once stood spans over 500 acres and offers scenic hiking trails through woodlands, hemlock groves, and around peaceful brooks, a picturesque setting for outdoor enthusiasts. Managed by the Society for the Protection of New Hampshire Forests, this area was named in honor of Madame Sherri, and it also includes trails that lead to the ruins of her former estate. So, while the house was originally separate from the forest, the two are now intricately entwined.

bing-49298.jpg.title: Die Bibliothek der Humboldt-Universität in Berlin
bing-49298.jpg.headline: Geometrie der Weisheit. Tag der Bibliotheken
bing-49298.jpg.description:
Willkommen zum Tag der Bibliotheken, der jedes Jahr am 24. Oktober gefeiert wird! Dieser besondere Tag würdigt die Bedeutung von Bibliotheken als Orte des Wissens, der Bildung und des kulturellen Austauschs. Bibliotheken bieten nicht nur Zugang zu einer Fülle von Büchern und digitalen Medien, sondern sind auch Treffpunkte für Menschen, die ihre Liebe zum Lernen teilen.

Auf dem heutigen Bild ist die Universitätsbibliothek der Humboldt-Universität in Berlin abgelichtet, eine der ältesten und renommiertesten Universitätsbibliotheken Deutschlands. Im Jahr 1831 gegründet, verfügt sie heute über mehr als 6,5 Millionen Medien und hat eine lange Tradition in der Förderung von Forschung und Bildung. Ein interessantes Detail: Die Bibliothek ist nicht nur für Studierende und Forschende zugänglich, sondern auch für die breite Öffentlichkeit, was sie zu einem zentralen Wissenszentrum in Berlin macht.

bing-49304.jpg.title: Bodie State Historic Park, Mono County, California
bing-49304.jpg.headline: Ghosts of the gold rush. Bodie State Historic Park, California
bing-49304.jpg.description:
In the ghostly silence of Bodie, California, it feels like time stands still. This mining camp became a booming gold rush town in the 1870s, after a cave-in revealed a rich vein of gold. Bodie was named after W.S. Bodey, a prospector who died in a blizzard before seeing the town's rise. When large deposits were found there, it grew to nearly 10,000 residents, with saloons, dance halls, and breweries lining its streets. But as the gold ran dry, so did the town's fortunes. The mines closed, the population dwindled, and by 1915, the place was abandoned. Bodie's streets are now empty, its wooden buildings frozen in decay.

Today, Bodie is one of America's best-preserved ghost towns. Wandering through the streets, you can peer into dusty homes and storefronts, and even find small artifacts like shards of china and square nails from the glory days. Legend has it that Bodie's ghosts fiercely guard the town, and those who take souvenirs risk being cursed with bad luck. Taking items home is also strictly against the park's rules. So, be sure to leave with nothing but memories—lest the town's spirits follow you home.
bing-49304.jpg.copyright: © Julien McRoberts/Tetra Images, LLC/Alamy Stock Phot

bing-49308.jpg.title: Golden Temple at dusk, Amritsar
bing-49308.jpg.headline: A timeless glow. Golden Temple, Amritsar
bing-49308.jpg.description:
Glistening like a jewel under the sun, the Golden Temple is not just a place of worship—it's an experience for the soul. A gurudwara in Amritsar, Punjab, it is also known as Sri Darbar Sahib or Sri Harmandir Sahib. The site's journey began in 1577, when Guru Ram Das, the fourth Sikh Guru, completed the man-made pool surrounding the temple. Fast forward to 1604, and it was the fifth Guru, Guru Arjan, who placed the sacred Adi Granth within the temple, shaping its spiritual significance. Despite facing destruction multiple times at the hands of Mughal and Afghan invaders, the Sikhs showed resilience, rebuilding the temple each time.

In 1809, Maharaja Ranjit Singh stepped in, giving the temple its present look by reconstructing it with marble and copper, and later, covering its sanctum with gold leaf in 1830—hence the name, Golden Temple. What makes this gurudwara truly special is its unique design. Built lower than the land around, it represents humility and equality. The Golden Temple, with its four entrances on all sides, symbolises its open doors to people of all backgrounds, warmly welcoming everyone regardless of caste, creed or religion.
bing-49308.jpg.copyright: © Vincent Boisvert, all right reserved/Getty Image

bing-49311.jpg.title: Isola di Procida, Golfo di Napoli, Campania, Italia
bing-49311.jpg.headline: Pasta e felicità
bing-49311.jpg.description:
La pasta è molto più di un semplice alimento; è un simbolo di tradizione, cultura e convivialità. In occasione del “Giorno Internazionale della Pasta”, celebriamo questo piatto iconico che unisce persone di tutto il mondo. Ammirate l’isola di Procida, una delle gemme del Golfo di Napoli, dove il profumo del mare si mescola con quello della pasta appena cucinata. In Campania, come in tutta Italia, la pasta è un'arte. Dai classici spaghetti alle vongole, con il loro sapore di mare e un tocco di prezzemolo fresco, al ragù napoletano, una salsa ricca e corposa che cuoce e “pippia” per ore, dalla romana Carbonara alla Norma siciliana, ogni piatto racconta una storia di passione e maestria culinaria.

Quel che conta, non è solo il piacere gustativo che questa leccornia ci dà, ma anche il valore culturale che apporta. La pasta è uno degli alimenti più consumati al mondo, e la nostra maestria nel creare capolavori culinari, a partire da ingredienti semplici, è invidiata ovunque. La domanda è una: quale meraviglioso piatto, tra mille delizie, porterete in tavola?

bing-49316.jpg.title: The Mont Blanc massif, near Chamonix, France
bing-49316.jpg.headline: The heights of horror. Frankenstein Friday
bing-49316.jpg.description:
Picture yourself at the highest peak in the Alps, where the air is crisp and the views are breathtaking. The towering presence of Mont Blanc has left an indelible mark on literature, most notably on Mary Shelley's 'Frankenstein.' The last Friday of October is Frankenstein Friday, honoring Shelley's literary genius and the fascinating creature born from her imagination. 'Frankenstein' was conceived during a ghost story challenge. In 1816, an 18-year-old Shelley, along with fellow writers Percy Bysshe Shelley, John Polidori, and Lord Byron, spent a stormy summer in Switzerland. Forced inside by incessant rain, she penned the tale of Victor Frankenstein and the Creature. A pivotal scene in the novel takes place on a glacier near Mont Blanc, where Victor is confronted by his monstrous creation. This setting, with its surreal beauty and treacherous terrain, perfectly captures a sense of awe and terror.

'Frankenstein,' also known as 'Frankenstein; or, The Modern Prometheus,' was first published anonymously in 1818. Shelley's use of the epistolary form—a novel told through letters—and her blend of Gothic and early science fiction made 'Frankenstein' a timeless classic.

bing-49323.jpg.title: Parco delle Chiese Rupestri, Matera, Basilicata, Italia
bing-49323.jpg.headline: Tradizione e folklore, m’immergo di colore
bing-49323.jpg.description:
Oggi, per la “Giornata del Folklore” ci rechiamo a Matera, in Basilicata, una città ricca di storia e tradizioni. Il folklore italiano è un patrimonio culturale che riflette le radici profonde e le diversità regionali del nostro paese. Un esempio emblematico è la Festa della Bruna, celebrata ogni anno il 2 luglio a Matera, che combina elementi cristiani e pagani in un'esplosione di colori e suoni. L'antropologo Ernesto De Martino ha studiato a fondo le tradizioni popolari del Sud Italia, evidenziando come il folklore sia un mezzo per comprendere le dinamiche sociali e culturali delle comunità.

Le sue ricerche hanno mostrato come riti e leggende siano strumenti per affrontare le difficoltà della vita quotidiana e per mantenere viva l'identità collettiva. Un fatto sociale interessante è la tradizione dei "cunti", racconti orali tramandati di generazione in generazione, che spesso mescolano realtà e fantasia. Questi racconti non solo intrattengono, ma educano e rafforzano i legami comunitari. Il folklore italiano è un tesoro di storie e tradizioni che continua a vivere e a evolversi, offrendo uno sguardo affascinante sulla nostra cultura e sulle nostre radici.

bing-49324.jpg.title: Vue de Paris à travers l'horloge géante du Musée d'Orsay, Paris
bing-49324.jpg.headline: Il est l’heure du changement d’heure !. Passage à l’heure d’hiver
bing-49324.jpg.description:
Alors que les aiguilles de l'horloge géante du musée d'Orsay dominent la vue imprenable sur Paris, elles nous rappellent que le temps est en perpétuel mouvement. Cette horloge emblématique, vestige de l'ancienne gare d'Orsay, est aujourd'hui un symbole du passage du temps. Et quel moment plus propice pour réfléchir à ce flux inéluctable que le passage à l’heure d’hiver ?

À chaque automne, lorsque nous reculons d’une heure, nous gagnons un peu plus de lumière matinale, mais les soirées tombent plus rapidement. Le mécanisme de l'horloge de l’Orsay, avec sa précision sans faille, devient une métaphore visuelle parfaite pour ce changement d'heure. Ce passage marque la fin de l'heure d'été, où les jours paraissent plus longs, pour céder place à l’hiver, synonyme de soirées cocooning et de crépuscules hâtifs.

Au cœur de Paris, l'horloge du musée d'Orsay ne change jamais son rythme, mais pour nous, elle nous invite à prendre conscience du temps qui passe et à vivre pleinement chaque instant, même en cette saison plus sombre.

bing-49328.jpg.title: Gespensterwald, Nienhagen, Mecklenburg-West Pomerania, Germany
bing-49328.jpg.headline: Into the woods. Gespensterwald, Nienhagen, Germany
bing-49328.jpg.description: On Germany's Baltic coast lies the Gespensterwald, which means 'Ghost Forest,' seen in today's image. This spine-tingling forest covers about 445 acres, with its gnarled beech, hornbeam, ash, and oak trees twisting toward the sky. The salty sea air, wind, and the moist climate helped mold the trees' distorted shapes, which look particularly haunting at night. Visitors to this forest in the Mecklenburg-West Pomerania region, can brave the trails alone or sign up for a storytelling session where actors dressed as ghosts bring local legends and folktales to life. Photographers and nature enthusiasts alike find inspiration in the eerie silhouettes etched against the sky, immortalized in countless pictures.

bing-49336.jpg.title: The Balmoral Clocktower, Edinburgh
bing-49336.jpg.headline: Time to set your clocks right. British Summer Time ends
bing-49336.jpg.description:
Time is of the essence today: the last Sunday of October marks the end of British Summer Time. At 2 AM this morning, the clocks fell back one hour, meaning there was an extra hour of sleep. While the idea of summer time was mentioned in 1784 by American inventor Benjamin Franklin, the first serious proposal for changing the clocks in the United Kingdom came from British builder William Willett in 1907. He valued having more daylight and felt so strongly about this that he published a pamphlet called 'The Waste of Daylight. Over time, many countries adopted the practice to give people more daylight in the evenings during the summer months.

The clock in today's image is of the Balmoral Hotel in Edinburgh, Scotland. This famous clock hasn't been on time since 1902, by three minutes, to be exact. The move was made to lessen the likelihood that the people would miss their trains. However, it does align with Greenwich Mean Time once a year, on December 31.

bing-49340.jpg.title: Polar bear mom and cub, Churchill, Manitoba, Canada
bing-49340.jpg.headline: A mother's warmth in the cold. Polar Bear Week
bing-49340.jpg.description:
Polar Bear Week champions the Arctic's majestic predator, one of nature's greatest hunters. Established by Polar Bears International, it highlights the challenges they face due to climate change, particularly the rapid loss of Arctic Sea ice. At this time of year, polar bears gather in Churchill, Canada—known as the 'polar bear capital of the world.' Here, bears wait for Hudson Bay to freeze so they can start hunting for seals, their primary food source.

Despite their huge size, these marine mammals are remarkably good swimmers, often covering more than 90 miles at a time. With their thick fur and a generous layer of fat, polar bears perfectly adapt to cold environments. Yet they now navigate a fragile line between survival and decline. As the ice melts, their hunting grounds disappear. Polar Bear Week aims to make sure these noble giants of the North have a secure future.

bing-49347.jpg.title: Gernika-Lumo, País Vasco
bing-49347.jpg.headline: Celebrando la cosecha. Feria agrícola de Gernika
bing-49347.jpg.description:
Hoy se celebra la emblemática Feria Agrícola de Gernika, un evento esencial en el País Vasco que resalta la riqueza agrícola de la región. En el corazón del centro histórico de esta localidad, los baserritarras exhiben sus productos en cerca de 900 puestos, donde los visitantes pueden deleitarse con una variada oferta de hortalizas, frutas, flores, quesos, txakolí y miel.

Uno de los momentos más esperados de la jornada es la ceremonia de entrega de premios, que tiene lugar al mediodía frente a la icónica fuente de Mercurio. Además de la posibilidad de realizar compras, los asistentes pueden disfrutar de animados pasacalles y emocionantes actuaciones de bertsolarism, figuras que evocan la rica tradición de los trovadores vascos. Aunque el mercado concluye a las 14:00 h, el ambiente festivo perdura a lo largo de la tarde, convirtiendo este evento en una experiencia inolvidable en un lugar impregnado de historia y tradición.

bing-49352.jpg.title: Pumpkin field, Victoria, British Columbia, Canada
bing-49352.jpg.headline: It's carving time. Pumpkin field, Victoria, British Columbia, Canada
bing-49352.jpg.description:
As fall covers the landscape with amber hues and the chill of Halloween approaches, it's time to start carving some spooky jack-o'-lanterns. Originally from Ireland and Scotland, this craft was brought to America by immigrants who initially made lanterns from turnips and potatoes but later found pumpkins more plentiful and easier to carve. Once hollowed out and lit with candles, the gourds were transformed into flickering defenses against evil spirits.

Today's image shows a pumpkin field outside of Victoria, British Columbia, Canada, full of blank canvases awaiting their ghoulish and whimsical creations. As people gather to scoop, carve, and light their pumpkins, they take part in a ritual passed down through generations. As well as gracing porches to welcome trick-or-treaters, pumpkins fill pies and spice up lattes, adding a tasty element to the season that many anticipate all year long. Once merely a fruit, the pumpkin now enjoys a revered place in Halloween celebrations.

bing-49362.jpg.title: Gabinete Real de Leitura, Rio de Janeiro Real Gabinete Português de Leitura
bing-49362.jpg.headline: Entre no mundo dos livros
bing-49362.jpg.description:
Feliz Dia Nacional do Livro! Para celebrar essa data especial, vamos embarcar em uma aventura até o Rio de Janeiro, no Gabinete Real de Leitura. Um exemplo impressionante de arquitetura inspirada no estilo manuelino, característico de Portugal no século XVI, este estilo combina elementos góticos, renascentistas e mouriscos, conferindo ao edifício uma aparência majestosa e única. O salão principal é especialmente deslumbrante, com estantes de madeira esculpidas que se estendem do chão ao teto e vitrais coloridos que permitem a entrada de luz natural, criando um ambiente mágico para os visitantes. Consegue sentir o cheiro da madeira e dos livros que estão aí?

O dia 29 de outubro foi escolhido como a data para celebrar o livro porque corresponde a fundação da Biblioteca Nacional (também no Rio de Janeiro) em 1810, após a chegada da Família Real Portuguesa ao Brasil. A criação da Biblioteca Nacional trouxe consigo um vasto acervo de livros, consolidando-se como um marco significativo na história literária brasileira. Aproveite o dia para revisitar seu livro favorito e homenagear a importância da leitura na formação cultural do nosso país.

bing-49364.jpg.title: Great horned owl
bing-49364.jpg.headline: Hoots and haunts. Great horned owl
bing-49364.jpg.description:
The Halloween season is upon us, so let's meet one of the holiday's icons: the great horned owl. With its keen vision, eerie vocalizations, and silent flight, this owl has historically been revered and feared. In folklore and mythology, owls were considered symbols of wisdom and omens of death. On Samhain, the Celtic precursor to Halloween, the owl was believed to be the kin of roaming spirits.

The owl in today's image is far more than a character in ghostly tales. Often called the 'tiger of the air,' the great horned owl, named for its signature feathers that look like horns, is one of the most fearsome and adaptable predators in the ornithological world. Primarily active at night, the owl has large, powerful talons that exert around 300 pounds of pressure, which it uses to grab prey like small rodents and skunks. It has incredible night vision, but its eyes are fixed, so it must turn its head a whopping 270 degrees to see everything. So, whether you hear it hooting from treetops or see it flying in the night, this owl proves that not all scary apparitions are supernatural.

bing-49376.jpg.title: View of Edinburgh Castle from a churchyard in Scotland
bing-49376.jpg.headline: A haunting history. Edinburgh Castle, Scotland
bing-49376.jpg.description:
If you're looking for a Halloween destination that combines history with a hefty dose of hauntings, Edinburgh Castle is the place to be. Positioned high on an extinct volcano, the castle's royal connections go back nearly 1,000 years, and its walls have witnessed wars, royal births, executions, and other dramas. But what really sets it apart is its reputation as one of Scotland's most haunted spots.

Legend has it that the Grey Lady, Janet Douglas, roams the castle's corridors. Also known as Lady Glamis, a noblewoman accused of witchcraft by King James V, she is believed to still lament her fiery execution in 1537. Others say the Grey Lady might be the ghost of Marie de Guise—mother of Mary, Queen of Scots—mourning her lost power amid the turmoil of religious reform. Then there's the Dung Man, a prisoner who attempted to escape in a wheelbarrow full of excrement. He died from the fall when the cart was emptied from the castle wall. The lost piper, who vanished into underground tunnels, continues to play a haunting melody beneath the city. And in 2001, the shadowy figure of a man in a leather apron emerged during a paranormal research project, leaving volunteers with a chilling memory. Spooked yet?

bing-49377.jpg.title: Gran Paradiso National Park, Italy
bing-49377.jpg.headline: Gran Paradiso National Park, Italy
bing-49377.jpg.description: Established in 1922 to protect the dwindling population of ibex—any of several species of wild goat—Gran Paradiso National Park in northern Italy, spans 70,300 hectares of breathtaking alpine terrain, a sight captured in today's image. As the country's first national park, it represents a conservation success story, where the once-endangered ibex now thrives alongside chamois, marmots and eagles. The landscape changes with elevation, featuring rolling meadows adorned with wildflowers and moss-covered rocks that give way to rugged peaks, the ideal challenge for climbers. Skirting the borders of Piedmont and the Aosta Valley, the park attracts those eager for wildlife photography, hiking and the serenity of alpine air. It is not only a refuge for animals but also a living museum of alpine culture.

bing-49378.jpg.title: 草間彌生の「南瓜」, 香川県 香川郡
bing-49378.jpg.headline: 今日はハロウィン
bing-49378.jpg.description:
今日 10 月 31 日はハロウィン。欧米では子供たちが仮装をして「トリック・オア・トリート」と言いながら家々を回り、お菓子をもらいます。日本でも形を変えながら人気のイベントとして広がっており、特に若者を中心に仮装パーティーやイベントが盛んに行われています…

ハロウィンのシンボルと言えばカボチャ。特に「ジャック・オー・ランタン」と呼ばれるカボチャのランタンは、ハロウィンの象徴的なアイテムです。そして、画像のカボチャは、芸術家の草間彌生さんの作品。香川県直島町にあり、黄色いカボチャに黒いドット模様が施された野外彫刻です。

bing-49380.jpg.title: Diwali celebrations
bing-49380.jpg.headline: Celebrating shades of light. Happy Diwali!
bing-49380.jpg.description: Homes sparkle with decorations, and the night sky bursts with colour as Diwali celebrations begin. Also known as 'Deepavali,' the name translates to 'rows (avali) of lights (deepa)' in Sanskrit, capturing the essence of this festival. Widely celebrated across various religions and regions, each has its own origin story. Regardless of the countless narratives and reasons behind the festivities, the central theme remains the triumph of good over evil. For many, Diwali is a homage to Lakshmi, the Hindu goddess of wealth, who is thought to be guided into the homes of devotees by the glow of lights and lamps. The day isn't just about lights and legends—it's also a time for enjoying moments with loved ones, exchanging gifts and sweets, indulging in delicious feasts and dressing up in new outfits. Observed worldwide, its largest celebrations outside of India occur in Leicester, United Kingdom.

bing-49386.jpg.title: Pinheiros de araucária em um amanhecer enevoado, paisagem próxima a Gramado, Rio Grande do Sul
bing-49386.jpg.headline: Uma neblina misteriosa
bing-49386.jpg.description:
Está sentindo um clima de mistério? Hoje vamos explorar o folclore brasileiro por meio da figura icônica do Saci-Pererê! Comemorado em 31 de outubro, o Dia do Saci foi criado como uma alternativa ao Dia das Bruxas (ou Halloween), incentivando a valorização das lendas e mitos nacionais. Conta a lenda que o Saci-Pererê é frequentemente avistado em regiões do Sudeste, Sul e Centro-Oeste do Brasil, especialmente em áreas rurais e florestas densas. Imagine encontrá-lo em um amanhecer enevoado entre os pinheiros de araucária, como na imagem de hoje... A névoa e a tranquilidade da paisagem criam o cenário perfeito para as travessuras do Saci, que se esconde entre as árvores e prega peças nos desavisados.

A data foi oficializada em 2005 para resgatar e promover as figuras do folclore brasileiro, com o Saci como símbolo central. Além do Saci, a celebração também destaca outros personagens folclóricos, como a Iara, o Curupira, o Boitatá e o Boto, valorizando a rica tradição oral e mítica do Brasil. Aproveite o dia para conhecer mais sobre essas lendas e mergulhar no fascinante mundo do folclore brasileiro!

bing-49388.jpg.title: Chimera of Notre-Dame de Paris, France
bing-49388.jpg.headline: Stone-cold stares on Halloween. Happy Halloween!
bing-49388.jpg.description:
Do you sometimes get spooked? If you do, that means you have a healthy sense of fun and fear. And what better day of the year than Halloween to indulge in all things scary? The holiday we know today traces its roots to ancient traditions, including the Celts' Samhain, the Romans' Feralia, and medieval Christian observances. Today, costumed people mingle in the streets, not unlike their ancestors who donned animal skins to divine the future or celebrate saints and martyrs.

Amid modern festivities like trick-or-treating, pumpkin carving, and parties, you might spot a few spooky decorations that look like the one pictured here—a chimera of Notre-Dame Cathedral in Paris. Perched high above the city, this mythical creature is often mistaken for a gargoyle, but unlike its waterspout cousins, the chimera is purely decorative. So today, let's remember the shadows and stories that dance around the edges of our brightly lit celebrations. Happy Halloween!

bing-49397.jpg.title: Aerial view of vineyards in autumn, Varnhalt, Black Forest, Germany
bing-49397.jpg.headline: A proud heritage. Vineyards in Varnhalt, Black Forest, Germany
bing-49397.jpg.description:
The Badische Weinstraße is a picturesque route that stretches over 300 miles along the Black Forest, leading you through some of Germany's most beautiful wine-growing regions. In today's image, we find ourselves in Varnhalt, a charming wine village that is part of Baden-Baden. One of the region's highlights is the Nägelsförsterhof winery, which has been in operation since 1588. This vineyard is well-known for producing Riesling wines, renowned for their exceptional quality.

Varnhalt shares a unique and fascinating tradition with Steinbach and Neuweier: since the 18th century, these villages have had the rare privilege of bottling their wine in Bocksbeutel, a type of flattened round wine bottle. This right, granted by the Bishop of Würzburg, makes the region truly special, as it is one of the few places in Germany outside of Franconia permitted to use this bottle shape. With special EU trademark protection since 1989, the Bocksbeutel emphasises the exclusive character and high quality of the wine. Whether you're a wine lover or a history enthusiast, Varnhalt offers a captivating glimpse into the world of winemaking.

bing-49400.jpg.title: Pueblo ruins, Hovenweep National Monument, Utah
bing-49400.jpg.headline: Celebrating America's Native heritage. Native American Heritage Month
bing-49400.jpg.description:
Today marks the start of Native American Heritage Month. Throughout November, we honor the history, traditions, stories, and languages of Native Peoples. The Indigenous Peoples of North America have played a significant role in shaping our country, including developing the food we eat and the medicines that heal us. November is also a time to reflect on the issues that Native Peoples face, including civil and voting rights, land access, and education.

An important part of Native American heritage is the legacy that Indigenous Peoples have left on the landscape. One such place is Hovenweep National Monument on the Utah-Colorado border. Ancestral Pueblo people built the structures seen in today's image between 1200 and 1300 CE. All across Hovenweep are dwellings and circular and square towers. Although the purpose of these towers remains uncertain, they could have been used for defense, observing the stars, storing grain, or a combination of all of these. Here, the enduring legacy of America's Indigenous Peoples can still be felt.

bing-49412.jpg.title: American bison in Yellowstone National Park, Wyoming
bing-49412.jpg.headline: From near extinction to national icon. National Bison Day
bing-49412.jpg.description:
Once upon a time, in the boundless grasslands of North America, there roamed creatures of great strength and majesty—the American bison. These animals were a key part of life for many Native American tribes, providing food, clothing, and tools. Their population dwindled perilously low in the late 1800s, falling from as many as 60 million to fewer than 1,000 due to excessive hunting and disease. Enter a group of conservationists, ranchers, and Native Americans who stepped in to save the species. Now, over 500,000 bison roam again, many in protected areas like Yellowstone National Park, featured in today's image. Today, on National Bison Day, observed every first Saturday in November, we honor these noble creatures—a testament to the American spirit and the monumental conservation efforts to save them.

It's no wonder the bison was officially named the national mammal in 2016. From the buffalo nickel to state flags, they are a deeply embedded symbol in American culture. Bison are North America's largest mammals, and they have been introduced as far away as Russia. While the bison has made a heroic recovery, the story isn't over. These animals still face challenges, including habitat loss and hunting.

bing-49424.jpg.title: Caribbean flamingo nests, Ría Lagartos Biosphere Reserve, Yucatán, Mexico
bing-49424.jpg.headline: Nurturing nature. International Day for Biosphere Reserves
bing-49424.jpg.description:
Today is the International Day for Biosphere Reserves. Biosphere reserves may sound like a mouthful, but they're essentially nature's sweet spots— biodiverse places that are home to a huge variety of life. These reserves, recognized by UNESCO, keep ecosystems healthy, protect endangered species, and help regulate climate through forests, wetlands, and other crucial habitats. There are 759 biosphere reserves across 136 countries. From the lush greenery of the Sundarbans in India to the vast expanses of the Great Sandy Biosphere Reserve in Australia, each reserve is unique.

Let's visit another—the Ría Lagartos Biosphere Reserve in Yucatán, Mexico, a UNESCO-protected sanctuary since 2004. Its forests and savannas cradle over 550 vertebrate species, including 142 species found only here. There are over 400 bird species in this reserve, including a large population of flamingos whose nests are seen in today's image. Biosphere reserves are all about balance, and Ría Lagartos is a prime example. Fishing, ecotourism, and even salt production are done in ways that respect the environment.

bing-49431.jpg.title: Altare della Patria, Monumento nazionale a Vittorio Emanuele II, Lazio, Roma, Italia
bing-49431.jpg.headline: La vittoria italiana
bing-49431.jpg.description: Il “Giorno dell'Unità Nazionale Italiana”, celebrato il 4 novembre, commemora la vittoria del nostro paese nella Prima Guerra Mondiale. Questo giorno segna l'unione delle diverse regioni italiane sotto un'unica bandiera, un evento che ha trasformato il panorama politico e culturale del paese. Durante questa giornata, si ricordano le lotte e i sacrifici dei patrioti italiani, come gli eroi del Piave, che hanno combattuto per l'indipendenza e l'unità. Le celebrazioni includono parate, eventi culturali e cerimonie ufficiali in tutto il paese, con un particolare focus sulle città storiche come Firenze, Milano, Roma e Torino. È un'occasione per riflettere sul passato e guardare al futuro con speranza e determinazione. Uniti nella diversità, celebriamo il nostro passato per costruire un domani migliore!

bing-49436.jpg.title: Grasmere, Lake District, Cumbria, England
bing-49436.jpg.headline: Worth a thousand words. Grasmere, Lake District, Cumbria, England
bing-49436.jpg.description: A place where poetry, history, and nature blend—welcome to Grasmere in England's Lake District. The village was once the cherished residence of the celebrated poet William Wordsworth, who described Grasmere, with its valley and lake of the same name, as 'the loveliest spot that man hath found.' Here, visitors are greeted by old cottages and homes built from local bluish-green slate. Dove Cottage, Wordsworth's humble abode from 1799 to 1808, and the adjacent museum offer a dive into the poet's life. His later residence, Rydal Mount, continues the story just a short journey away. The heart of the village is St. Oswald's Church, which dates to the 13th century and is Wordsworth's final resting place. Not far from the church, the aroma of the renowned Grasmere Gingerbread, made from a secret recipe, will set visitors' mouths watering.

bing-49438.jpg.title: 酉の市で販売される縁起熊手, 東京
bing-49438.jpg.headline: 今日は一の酉
bing-49438.jpg.description:
今日 11 月 5 日は一の酉。一度目の酉の市が行われる日です。酉の市は、江戸時代から続く行事で、主に関東地方の鷲神社、大鳥神社、酉の寺など、鷲や鳥にゆかりがある寺社で開催されます。商売繁盛や家内安全を祈願するために多くの人々が集まります…

酉の市の名物は縁起熊手。熊手には、七福神、松竹梅、大判小判などの様々な縁起物が飾られています。伝統的な技法を守りつつ、現代のニーズに合わせたデザインも取り入れられており、画像のような犬やネコなどの動物をモチーフにしたものも人気があります。

bing-49440.jpg.title: Ranakpur Jain temple, Ranakpur, Rajasthan
bing-49440.jpg.headline: Sanctuary of serenity. Ranakpur Jain temple, Ranakpur, Rajasthan
bing-49440.jpg.description:
Step into the world of intricate artistry at the sacred site of Ranakpur Jain temple, Rajasthan. Also known as Chaturmukha Dharana Vihara, because of the four faces temple design, this stunning Śvētāmbara Jain temple is dedicated to Tirthankara Rishabhanatha, also known as Ādinātha. This architectural marvel was commissioned by Darna Shah, a local Jain businessman, in the 15th century after he experienced a divine vision. The temple is crafted in the form of the Nalini-Gulma Vimana—a heavenly vehicle that he envisioned in his dreams. Built in the Māru-Gurjara architectural style, the temple houses a garbhagriha, the innermost sanctuary, where the main Chaumukha Adinatha idol is enshrined.

The temple's Shikhara symbolises Mount Meru, the sacred mountain that serves as the axis of Jambudvipa, a term used in ancient texts to describe Greater India. The preaching hall within the temple represents the Samavasarana, the divine hall where the Tirthankara delivered teachings. Along with these, the premises also feature several temples, including the Suparshvanatha Temple and Amba Temple.

bing-49441.jpg.title: Amanecer en Barcelona, España
bing-49441.jpg.headline: Tecnología que conecta. Smart City Expo World Congress, Barcelona
bing-49441.jpg.description:
Hoy, la Smart City Expo se erige como un evento clave en el avance hacia un futuro urbano más sostenible e innovador. Celebrada en la cosmopolita ciudad de Barcelona, este encuentro reúne a líderes de la industria, autoridades gubernamentales, visionarios tecnológicos e investigadores, todos comprometidos con la transformación de nuestras ciudades. Durante varios días, se presentarán soluciones revolucionarias para mejorar la vida urbana, abarcando desde tecnologías inteligentes hasta proyectos de movilidad y sostenibilidad.

Barcelona, con su rica historia y arquitectura vanguardista, se convierte en el escenario ideal para este intercambio de ideas y la creación de alianzas estratégicas. Además de ser un referente cultural, su espíritu de innovación se alinea perfectamente con la misión de la Expo: construir ciudades más eficientes y humanas. ¡Únete a nosotros en este emocionante evento y sé parte del cambio hacia un futuro urbano más prometedor!

bing-49445.jpg.title: Fireworks at Bolton Priory, North Yorkshire on Guy Fawkes Night 2015
bing-49445.jpg.headline: A tale of treason and tradition. Guy Fawkes Night
bing-49445.jpg.description: 'Remember, remember the fifth of November, gunpowder, treason and plot. I see no reason why gunpowder treason should ever be forgot!' The tale begins in 1605, when a man named Guy Fawkes became part of a conspiracy to blow up the Houses of Parliament on November 5. Alongside a group of disillusioned Catholics, Fawkes had hatched a bold and dangerous plan to kill King James I and end Protestant rule in England. Their secret weapon? Thirty-six barrels of gunpowder hidden in the cellars of Parliament, enough to blow the entire place sky-high. However, the plan was discovered a day before and the plot foiled. And so, 5 November became a day of celebration—not of the plotters, but of their failure. Today, communities gather to burn effigies of Fawkes, light fireworks and enjoy treats like bonfire toffee, remembering the night the plot went up in smoke—literally!

bing-49446.jpg.title: Vista de livros antigos na Biblioteca Nacional Brasileira no Rio de Janeiro
bing-49446.jpg.headline: Riqueza e diversidade linguística
bing-49446.jpg.description:
Hoje é o Dia Nacional da Língua Portuguesa! Vamos mergulhar nas páginas da riqueza e a diversidade do português brasileiro, conhecido por ter termos praticamente intraduzíveis, como “saudade”, que expressa um profundo sentimento de nostalgia ou falta de algo ou alguém. Com um vocabulário estimado em cerca de 400.000 palavras, o português é uma das línguas mais ricas do mundo.

A imagem do dia nos leva à Biblioteca Nacional do Brasil, localizada no Rio de Janeiro. Considerada pela UNESCO uma das dez maiores bibliotecas nacionais do mundo e a maior da América Latina, a biblioteca foi fundada em 1810, após a chegada da Família Real Portuguesa, que trouxe a Real Biblioteca de Lisboa. Com um acervo inicial de cerca de 60 mil itens, a biblioteca se tornou um patrimônio histórico do Brasil, com sua construção em estilo neoclássico concluída em 1910. Além do acervo físico, a Biblioteca Nacional também disponibiliza um acervo digital acessível online, incluindo documentos históricos, jornais e revistas antigas, que podem ser consultados por todos. Aproveite este dia para explorar a língua que molda nossa identidade cultural!

bing-49448.jpg.title: Autumn sunrise over the National Mall, Washington, DC
bing-49448.jpg.headline: Out of many, one. US Election Day
bing-49448.jpg.description:
It's time to get out and vote! In 1845, Congress designated the first Tuesday after the first Monday in November as the day Americans vote for most federal offices. Prior to this, states held elections on a date of their choosing within about a month of early December, which created issues with early and late elections. For convenience and to save money, many elections for state and local offices are also held on Election Day.

At the heart of this process is Washington DC, seat of the US federal government. Pictured here today is the National Mall, a landscaped park in the capital that is affectionately known as America's Front Yard. Within the National Mall lie some of the country's most famous museums and monuments, including the Washington Monument, the Lincoln Memorial, and the Smithsonian Institution. It also serves as a symbolic link between two of the branches of government, connecting the Capitol building—home of the legislature—to the White House, headquarters of the executive branch.

bing-49449.jpg.title: Sunset in Lençóis Maranhenses National Park, Maranhão, Brazil
bing-49449.jpg.headline: Lençóis Maranhenses National Park, Brazil
bing-49449.jpg.description:
Let's explore the breathtaking beauty of the Lençóis Maranhenses National Park! Located in the north-eastern region of the state of Maranhão, Brazil, this park is a conservation unit that covers an impressive area of more than 150,000 hectares. Created with the aim of protecting the region's flora, fauna and natural beauty, the park is a true ecological treasure, part of the coastal marine and cerrado biomes. Here we find unique ecosystems such as mangroves, sandbanks and dunes, moulded by strong winds and regular rainfall.

In addition to its environmental importance, the Lençóis Maranhenses Park is known for its scenic beauty, having been chosen as the setting for the films 'Avengers: Infinity War' and 'Avengers: Endgame.' Visitors can enjoy ecotourism trips through the dune fields, bathe in the crystal-clear lagoons and observe the star-filled night sky. The park attracts tourists from all over the world all year round, and in July 2024, it was declared a UNESCO World Heritage Site, recognised for its exceptional beauty and for being a unique natural phenomenon in the world.

bing-49460.jpg.title: Shi Shi Beach in Olympic National Park, Washington
bing-49460.jpg.headline: Shades of sunset. Shi Shi Beach, Olympic National Park, Washington
bing-49460.jpg.description:
Olympic National Park, established in 1938, offers an escape into unspoiled wilderness. It covers nearly 1,440 square miles on Washington's Olympic Peninsula. With a labyrinth of ecosystems that range from glacier-capped mountains to temperate rainforests, the park is a home for wildlife and an International Biosphere Reserve. Within it lies Shi Shi Beach, a serene stretch where the Pacific laps against sea stacks and sandy shores, as seen in today's image.

From here, you can follow one of the park's many trails and trek along the coast to see the beach's sea arch at Point of the Arches, an outcrop that has over 30 sea stacks, columns of rock rising from the beach. Within the park, visitors can get a closer look at Mount Olympus, spot over 300 bird species like red-breasted nuthatches, winter wrens, and spotted owls. They can also take a refreshing swim in Lake Crescent. The coastal wilderness area north of Cape Alava, including Shi Shi Beach, has been home to the Makah Tribe of the Pacific Northwest Coast for over 2,000 years. Visitors can gain an insight into their culture at the nearby Makah Reservation.

bing-49462.jpg.title: マガンの群れ
bing-49462.jpg.headline: 今日は立冬
bing-49462.jpg.description:
今日 11 月 7 日は立冬。暦の上では、冬が本格的に始まる時期とされ、空気も一段と冷たくなります。人々が冬を過ごすための寝具や暖房器具などを準備するのと同様に、ハクチョウやツル、そして画像のマガンなど、多くの渡り鳥は越冬のためシベリアや北極圏から日本へ飛来します…

マガンは日本に最も多く飛来するガンの一種で、北米大陸北部やユーラシア大陸北部で繁殖し、日本では、湖沼や湿原などに生息しています。非常に警戒心が強く、環境に対して敏感な鳥です。宮城県の伊豆沼や蕪栗沼は、彼らの重要な越冬地として知られています。1971 年には日本の天然記念物に指定され、狩猟を禁止し、保護に転じました。

bing-49463.jpg.title: 金色的松树，坝上草原，中国
bing-49463.jpg.headline: 初冬之美
bing-49463.jpg.description:
今天是二十四节气之一的立冬，也是冬季的开始。今天图片中地方是位于中国坝上草原地区的松林美景。坝上草原位于内蒙古高原的东南端，大兴安岭的南麓，是内蒙古高原的重要组成部分。

坝上草原地区值得游览的景点颇多，其中的塞罕坝国家森林公园是十分值得一去的地方。塞罕坝国家森林公园总经营面积约940平方千米，其中以落叶松人工林和天然白桦林为主的风景林面积约710平方千米，草原面积约150平方千米，森林覆盖率75.2%。这里不仅有浩瀚的林海、广袤的草原，还有清澈的高原湖泊和清代历史遗迹。是一处集人文景观和自然景观相融合的绝美森林公园。

bing-49472.jpg.title: Vancouver Coastal Sea wolves in Great Bear Rainforest, British Columbia, Canada
bing-49472.jpg.headline: Wolves in the wild. Vancouver Coastal Sea wolves, Great Bear Rainforest, Canada
bing-49472.jpg.description: Amidst the mist-covered cedars and Sitka spruces of Canada's Great Bear Rainforest, the Vancouver Coastal Sea wolf roams free. These canines thrive in this ecosystem in British Columbia, which stretches from the north of Vancouver Island to the Alaskan border. This unique subspecies of the gray wolf is specific to the region and leads a semi-aquatic lifestyle, swimming between islands in search of food. Unlike other wolf species, they have a marine-based diet, consisting of fish, clams, mussels, crabs, otters, and seals. These animals live in packs, communicating with each other through growls, barks, and whines, so they're often heard before they are seen.

bing-49479.jpg.title: LUMEN - Museo della fotografia di montagna, Brunico, Trentino-Alto Adige, Italia
bing-49479.jpg.headline: Si scorge una festa in lontananza
bing-49479.jpg.description:
Ci troviamo a Brunico, un angolo incantato dove le montagne abbracciano il cielo, e in lontananza, come un miraggio, si scorge Merano. Oggi ha inizio il Wine Festival di Merano, uno degli eventi enogastronomici più prestigiosi d'Italia, che attira appassionati di vino da tutto il mondo. Situato nella pittoresca Merano, in Trentino-Alto Adige, il festival offre una selezione di vini pregiati, degustazioni guidate e incontri con produttori di fama internazionale. Merano, con il suo clima mite e i suoi paesaggi incantevoli, è il luogo ideale per un evento di tale portata. Merano è famosa per i suoi giardini, le terme e l'architettura in stile liberty, che contribuiscono a creare un'atmosfera unica e affascinante.

Il panorama mozzafiato aggiunge un tocco di magia all'esperienza del Wine Festival, rendendo ogni sorso di vino indimenticabile. Circondate dalle maestose Alpi, le colline della regione offrono un contrasto spettacolare con i vigneti e le cime innevate, creando un quadro perfetto per gli amanti della natura e del buon vino. Ricordate, godetevi ogni sorso con moderazione, per rendere l’esperienza ancor più piacevole.

bing-49484.jpg.title: Aerial view of glacial rivers in Iceland
bing-49484.jpg.headline: From the land of fire and ice. Glacial rivers in Iceland
bing-49484.jpg.description: Iceland's glacial rivers have shaped the landscape here in the land of fire and ice over thousands of years. The rivers seen in today's image are formed from the meltwater of vast glaciers like Vatnajökull, Langjökull, and Hofsjökull. Vatnajökull, the largest ice cap in Iceland, covers over 3,000 square miles—approximately 10% of the country's landmass. As the glaciers melt, the water carries fine sediments, creating a braided river system with a milky appearance that contrasts with the earthy tones of the volcanic terrain. Every spring and summer, the rivers swell with seasonal meltwater, continually shaping and reshaping the land. Aerial views reveal their intricate patterns, interwoven across the terrain toward the North Atlantic Ocean. The water also powers hydroelectric power stations, reinforcing Iceland's status as a leader in sustainable energy.

bing-49489.jpg.title: Catedral de la Almudena, Madrid, España
bing-49489.jpg.headline: Cultura y devoción. Día de la Almudena
bing-49489.jpg.description:
Hoy, Madrid se engalana para honrar a su patrona en el Día de Nuestra Señora de la Almudena, una festividad que conmemora un antiguo relato en el que, en el año 712, los madrileños ocultaron la imagen de la Virgen en los muros de la ciudad para protegerla de los invasores árabes. Siglos más tarde, en 1085, la imagen fue milagrosamente redescubierta, intacta y acompañada de dos velas encendidas.

Este día se celebra con gran fervor a través de procesiones solemnes y actos religiosos que recorren el corazón de la ciudad. La imagen actual de la Virgen, venerada en la majestuosa Catedral de la Almudena, es una réplica del siglo XV, tras la pérdida de la original en un incendio. Esta festividad no solo une a los madrileños en su fe, sino que también es una ocasión especial para celebrar la historia y el patrimonio cultural de Madrid, atrayendo tanto a fieles como a curiosos visitantes.

bing-49496.jpg.title: Milky Way, Aït Benhaddou, Morocco
bing-49496.jpg.headline: Cosmic views over earthly hues. Aït Benhaddou, Morocco
bing-49496.jpg.description:
Get ready for a starry Moroccan night! Stargazing here is truly magical, as the vast skies and minimal light pollution transform each evening into a dazzling display. Every star you see is part of our galaxy, the Milky Way, which appears as a creamy band of light in the darkest skies. In today's image, you can see this cosmic beauty glowing over Aït Benhaddou, a historic fortified village known as a ksar, in the Ouarzazate province of Morocco. This site was first fortified in the 11th century. It was a key stop on the ancient caravan trade route connecting the Sahara and the city of Marrakesh. Perched on a hillside by the Ounila River, this village is a cluster of buildings encircled by a protective wall, complete with towers and a gate.

The earthen clay architecture here, built from rammed earth, adobe, and wood, showcases traditional craftsmanship. This UNESCO World Heritage Site is celebrated for its authenticity and is known for preserving conventional building techniques and avoiding modern concrete.

bing-49504.jpg.title: Les Sables-d'Olonne, la Tour d'Arundel, le casino, le fort Saint-Nicolas et le chenal menant au port
bing-49504.jpg.headline: La flamboyance en vol. Vendée Globe 2024
bing-49504.jpg.description:
Le port des Sables-d’Olonne, emblème du Vendée Globe, se prépare à vivre une nouvelle édition de cette course mythique. Depuis 1989, cette ville côtière est le point de départ des skippers les plus intrépides du monde, prêts à défier des océans parfois hostiles.

Les quais, autrefois le théâtre de jeux d’enfants et de cris de goélands, se transforment en une scène de passion et de défis. Les Sables-d’Olonne, avec ses charmantes ruelles et son port de plaisance animé, se transforment en véritable centre du monde nautique. Chaque édition du Vendée Globe écrit une nouvelle page de l’histoire de la voile, mêlant exploits, drames et innovations.

Cette année, la ville se prépare à accueillir une flotte record, promettant un spectacle inoubliable pour les milliers de spectateurs venus des quatre coins du monde. L’événement est également l'occasion de découvrir la richesse culturelle de la région, avec ses spécialités culinaires et ses traditions maritimes.

bing-49505.jpg.title: Aberystwyth war memorial, Wales
bing-49505.jpg.headline: Honouring the fallen. Remembrance Sunday
bing-49505.jpg.description:
Every November, Remembrance Sunday offers a chance to hit the pause button and think about those who gave everything during times of conflict. Held on the second Sunday of November, this day coincides with Armistice Day and is dedicated to honouring the armed forces and civilians who sacrificed their lives in World War I, World War II and subsequent conflicts. At 11 a.m. on the day, a two-minute silence is observed. This moment serves as a national pause to reflect and remember. The end of the silence is signalled by playing 'The Rouse,' a poignant bugle call.

Pictured here is Aberystwyth's iconic war memorial in Wales. The memorial—Aberystwyth Allegory—erected in 1923, stands proudly overlooking Cardigan Bay. At the top there's a figure of Victory (sometimes interpreted as Peace), and at the base of the obelisk stands another figure, representing humanity entangled in the chaos of war. It's a fitting reminder that the light of those lost in war still burns bright in the memory of the town.

bing-49508.jpg.title: Caribbean flamingos, Yucatán Peninsula, Mexico
bing-49508.jpg.headline: Flamboyance in flight. Caribbean flamingos, Yucatán Peninsula, Mexico
bing-49508.jpg.description:
Ever seen a group of flamingos take to the skies? If you have, there's a good chance they were Caribbean flamingos, also known as American flamingos, as seen in Yucatán Peninsula, Mexico, in today's image. Flamingos are referred to as a flamboyance when in a group, but they can also be called a stand, colony, or pat. The Caribbean flamingo is the largest flamingo species in the Americas and the only one native to North America. These vibrant pink birds are typically found around brackish and saltwater areas, like marshes, estuaries, and along coastlines.

Found across regions like the southeastern United States, northern South America, the Galápagos Islands, and Mexico's Yucatán Peninsula, Caribbean flamingos are well adapted for short migrations in search of food. Using long legs and webbed feet, they hunt shallow waters for shrimp, crustaceans, mollusks, fish, and algae. Their habitats are increasingly threatened by coastal development, pollution, and rising sea levels, putting their population at risk. Yet, Caribbean flamingos still amaze us when they soar gracefully through the skies.

bing-49517.jpg.title: Banff National Park, Alberta, Canada
bing-49517.jpg.headline: First flakes in the wilderness. Banff National Park, Alberta, Canada
bing-49517.jpg.description:
Featured in today's image is a winter wonderland in Alberta, Canada. Banff National Park is the perfect place for those seeking a refreshing escape. Established in 1885, it became the first national park in the country following the discovery of hot springs near Sulphur Mountain. Over time, Banff's boundaries expanded, and it became part of the Canadian Rocky Mountain Parks UNESCO World Heritage Site. Spanning over 2,500 square miles, this national park transforms into a snowy playground during the winter, attracting visitors eager for skiing, snowshoeing, curling, skijoring and wildlife tours that offer plenty to explore.

Despite the cold, life thrives in the park: it's home to a variety of wildlife, including elk, grizzly bears, mountain goats and wolves. Lodgepole pines and spruces also stand resilient against the harsh weather. Banff's flora and fauna are closely monitored, ensuring that this balance remains intact.

bing-49520.jpg.title: Mural Wall, Korean War Veterans Memorial, Washington, DC
bing-49520.jpg.headline: Heroes among us. Veterans Day
bing-49520.jpg.description:
Freedom is not free, and nobody understands that better than veterans. Today, America honors its military men and women for their service. The holiday originally celebrated the end of fighting on the Western Front during World War I on November 11, 1918—the official end of the war came the following year. Armistice Day, as it was later named, became a federal holiday in 1938. Following World War II and the Korean War, Congress amended the holiday in 1954, exchanging the word 'Armistice' with 'Veterans' to include veterans of all the country's wars.

Today's image depicts the Mural Wall, one of five parts of the Korean War Veterans Memorial in Washington, DC. Also known as 'The Forgotten War,' the three-year conflict began in 1950 and was one of America's most hard-fought wars. Near the National Mall, the Korean War Veterans Memorial honors the tens of thousands of US service personnel who died or went missing and more than 100,000 soldiers who were wounded.

bing-49526.jpg.title: Kirchturm von Bremm an der Moselschleife, Rheinland-Pfalz
bing-49526.jpg.headline: Magische Schleife der Natur. Bremm an der Moselschleife, Rheinland-Pfalz
bing-49526.jpg.description:
Die Moselschleife bei Bremm ist eine der spektakulärsten Natursehenswürdigkeiten Deutschlands und ein wahres Paradies für Naturliebhaber und Weinfreunde. Diese beeindruckende Flussschleife, die sich über 180 Grad erstreckt, bietet Ihnen atemberaubende Ausblicke auf die Mosel und die umliegenden Weinberge. Der Kirchturm von Bremm, der auf unserem heutigen Bild abgelichtet wurde, ist ein faszinierendes Wahrzeichen der Region. Der Ort war bereits in keltischer und römischer Zeit besiedelt, und die älteste urkundliche Erwähnung stammt aus dem Jahr 1051.

Bekannt ist Bremm auch für seine hervorragenden Rieslinge, die in den umliegenden Weinbergen unter optimalen Bedingungen gedeihen. Der steilste Weinberg Europas, der Calmont, lädt zum Wandern und Entdecken ein. Im Herbst locken die Weinlesefeste Besucher aus nah und fern an, um die regionalen Weine in gemütlicher Atmosphäre zu genießen.
