This consists of telling friends and family the ways they've disappointed you over the year. This can provide some much-needed catharsis at what can be a stressful time of year. The day traditionally concludes with feats of strength. Once the head of the household has been pinned, Festivus is officially over. Those who embrace this farcical holiday welcome the opportunity to let off some steam amid the Christmas build-up chaos—much like these red-crowned cranes in Hokkaido, Japan.

bing-50031.jpg.title: Galleria Vittorio Emanuele II, Milano, Lombardia
bing-50031.jpg.headline: Vigilia di Natale
bing-50031.jpg.description:
Benvenuti alla Galleria Vittorio Emanuele II, uno dei simboli di Milano. Sotto l’iconica cupola di vetro e ferro, ogni dicembre si accendono migliaia di luci che trasformano questo gioiello architettonico ottocentesco in un vero spettacolo natalizio. Un tempo ritrovo preferito dei futuristi, che qui discutevano di arte e progresso, oggi la Galleria continua ad essere un crocevia di cultura e bellezza. Tra boutique eleganti e caffè storici, i visitatori entrano in un’atmosfera calda e raffinata. L’albero di Natale, spesso sponsorizzato da grandi marchi è una delle attrazioni più fotografate, con decorazioni scintillanti che riflettono sulle pareti.

Le luci, i profumi delle pasticcerie e il suono delle risate creano una colonna sonora perfetta per la magia natalizia. Anche se non siete a caccia di shopping, potete godere un momento veramente speciale: il rito di calpestare il toro sul pavimento a mosaico come gesto apotropaico per invocare la fortuna nell’anno che sta per venire. Che siate milanesi o turisti, la Galleria a Natale è un luogo dove lo spirito delle feste si respira a pieni polmoni. Buona Vigilia di Natale a tutti voi, con l’augurio di trascorrere giorni sereni e pieni di gioia!
bing-50031.jpg.copyright: © Stefan Huwiler/imageBROKER.com GmbH & Co. KG/Alamy Stock Phot

bing-50036.jpg.title: Christmas market scene in Germany
bing-50036.jpg.headline: Have yourself a very merry Christmas!. Silent night, sparkling lights, and hearts full of joy
bing-50036.jpg.description: Christmas markets in Germany are a cherished holiday tradition that welcome visitors into a magical world of twinkling lights, festive music, and delicious seasonal treats. These markets date back to the Middle Ages and are held in town squares throughout Germany, with iconic examples in cities such as Nuremberg, Munich, and Dresden. Each market displays unique regional crafts and festive customs. Here, guests can discover handcrafted ornaments, wooden toys, and cozy winter accessories, along with specialties like Glühwein (mulled wine), Lebkuchen (gingerbread), and roasted nuts—ideal for enjoying while immersing themselves in the enchanting atmosphere.

bing-50037.jpg.title: Half-timbered Houses of Freudenberg, North Rhine-Westphalia, Germany
bing-50037.jpg.headline: Half-timbered Houses of Freudenberg, Germany
bing-50037.jpg.description:
Freudenberg is a charming little town nestled in the Siegen-Wittgenstein district of North Rhine-Westphalia, Germany. The town lies in the beautiful hilly uplands, ranging from 243 to 505 metres above sea level. The town is made up of 17 communities spread across about 55 square kilometres, two-thirds of which is lush forest, mainly broadleaf and spruce trees. The heart of Freudenberg is the 'Alter Flecken,' the historic old town centre, entirely made up of half-timbered houses that give it the feel of a 17th-century town.

So picturesque, in fact, that it's been included in the Cultural Atlas of North Rhine-Westphalia as a 'Building monument of international importance.' The town's Evangelical church was designed as a 'fortress church,' with its architecture reminiscent of military fortifications. The church in Oberholzklau, which dates back to the early 13th century, is a stunning example of Romanesque architecture with noticeable transitions to Gothic style. Right next door, you'll find the rectory, built in 1608 in the traditional half-timbered style.

bing-50047.jpg.title: Christmas trees with the Three Sisters mountain in the background, Canmore, Alberta
bing-50047.jpg.headline: Merry Christmas!
bing-50047.jpg.description:
Deck the halls—it's Christmas time! Christmas Day is a holiday filled with joy, warmth and cherished traditions. For many, it's a celebration of the birth of Jesus Christ, bringing family and friends together to exchange gifts, share meals and enjoy festive decor. Beyond its spiritual roots, Christmas also illuminates the season with beloved customs—decorating trees, carolling and eagerly awaiting Santa's arrival. These traditions, blending both old and new, make the holiday a magical experience filled with connection and cheer.

Picture this: Christmas trees adorned with sparkling lights and snowflakes, framed by the mighty Three Sisters mountains, as seen in today's image. These peaks in Canmore, Alberta—Big Sister (Faith), Middle Sister (Charity) and Little Sister (Hope)—aren't just another mountain range. Rising to heights of 3,000 metres approximately, these peaks were originally named the 'Three Nuns' by Albert Rogers, as they resembled nuns in white veils after a winter storm. However, in 1886, Canadian geologist George Dawson renamed them the 'Three Sisters.' While their rugged faces attract hikers and climbers during warmer months, in the Christmas season, they inspire awe from below. So, whether you're here for the scenery, the stories or just that festive holiday energy, the Three Sisters never disappoint. Christmas spirit? Checked, wrapped and ready under these mountains!

bing-50048.jpg.title: Svalbard reindeer in Van Mijenfjorden NP, Norway
bing-50048.jpg.headline: Merry Christmas!
bing-50048.jpg.description: Deck the halls, it's Christmas time! Christmas Day is a holiday packed with joy, warmth, and cherished traditions. For many, it's a celebration of the birth of Jesus Christ, bringing family and friends together to exchange gifts, share meals, and enjoy festive décor. Beyond its spiritual roots, Christmas also lights up the season with beloved customs—decorating trees, caroling, and eagerly awaiting Santa's arrival. These traditions, blending both old and new, make the holiday a magical experience filled with connection and cheer.
bing-50048.jpg.copyright: © Martin Zwick/REDA&CO/Universal Images Group via Getty Image

bing-50049.jpg.title: Lakes of Covadonga, Asturias, Spain
bing-50049.jpg.headline: Lakes of Covadonga, Asturias, Spain
bing-50049.jpg.description:
The dazzling Lakes of Covadonga, nestled in the heart of the towering Picos de Europa mountain range in Asturias, northern Spain, is an iconic tourist destination, particularly captivating in winter. The sight of these lakes draped in a blanket of snow and surrounded by majestic mountains creates a breathtaking natural spectacle that fascinates and attracts visitors from all over. In addition to their stunning beauty, the lakes hold deep historical significance. Nearby lies the emblematic Cave of Covadonga, the site of the renowned Battle of 722, a milestone in the Reconquista. This corner of Asturias is the perfect place to immerse yourself in both nature and history.

Adding a charming touch to the landscape are the sturdy Asturian cows that graze peacefully in the lush green meadows during the warmer months. These cows, well-adapted to the mountainous climate, embody the essence of rural Asturian life. It's undoubtedly a place where nature and history come together in perfect harmony. Come and discover this tranquil corner of Asturias, where every view whispers an unforgettable story.

bing-50053.jpg.title: Cala Comte al atardecer, Ibiza, Islas Baleares, España
bing-50053.jpg.headline: Arcoíris abrazando la cala desde el horizonte. San Esteban
bing-50053.jpg.description:
Hoy celebramos San Esteban, una festividad que evoca la serenidad de los momentos compartidos en familia, rodeados de profundas tradiciones y costumbres llenas de amor. La jornada comienza con solemnes misas y continúa con festines que combinan lo mejor de la gastronomía local, como el tradicional "canelón". Es un día en el que el bullicio navideño se suaviza, dando paso a una atmósfera más tranquila, donde los hogares se llenan de risas y alegría.

Es como si la celebración de San Esteban fuera un reflejo de un paisaje en calma, tal como el que ofrece la imagen de hoy: Cala Comte, en las Islas Baleares, donde, tras un día soleado, el cielo se ilumina con un arcoíris. La escena, serena y llena de colores vibrantes, nos recuerda la profunda conexión entre la naturaleza y las tradiciones, que, al igual que ese arcoíris, se extienden sobre el día con su belleza única.
bing-50053.jpg.copyright: © Vicente Soler Marmaneu Vicenfoto/Alamy Stock Phot

bing-50055.jpg.title: Albero di Natale, Portofino, Liguria
bing-50055.jpg.headline: La vacanza continua
bing-50055.jpg.description:
Il 26 dicembre in Italia, come in molti altri paesi di tradizione cattolica, si celebra Santo Stefano, il primo martire cristiano. La sua figura incarna il valore della fede e del sacrificio, ma in Italia questa giornata è anche un'opportunità per festeggiare con la famiglia e gli amici, magari facendo una gita fuori porta. Se state pensando a un luogo da sogno, Portofino è la scelta perfetta. Questo gioiello della Riviera Ligure è incantevole in ogni stagione, ma a Natale si trasforma in un quadro magico.

L’albero di Natale sulla celebre piazzetta è illuminato da luci che si riflettono sulle acque calme, creando un'atmosfera incantata. Tra i vicoli pittoreschi e le case color pastello, si respira un'atmosfera di festa intima e raffinata, perfetta per una passeggiata natalizia. Santo Stefano è il giorno ideale per rallentare e ammirare luoghi come Portofino, dove la bellezza del paesaggio si fonde con la serenità delle tradizioni natalizie. Auguri di un felice Santo Stefano e che possiate continuare a godervi la magia delle feste.

bing-50059.jpg.title: Gastown steam clock in Vancouver, British Columbia, Canada
bing-50059.jpg.headline: The holidays continue. Boxing Day
bing-50059.jpg.description:
As the last notes of Christmas carols linger in the air, Boxing Day arrives. This day is celebrated in Canada, the United Kingdom and several Commonwealth countries. In the past, it was customary for the wealthy to give boxes filled with gifts to their servants on the day after Christmas. The tradition evolved into a day for charitable giving to the less fortunate. Today, while the spirit of giving remains, it has transformed into a holiday centred around enjoying bustling sales and a lineup of football matches.

What's got steam, whistles and tourists pointing cameras? Yep, it's Vancouver's Gastown steam clock! Featured in today's image, this clock—built in 1977—is a clever blend of old-school vibe and modern steam power, imagined by horologist Raymond Saunders and metalwork specialist Doug Smith. It's a creative fix for an underground steam vent turned into a local legend. The clock uses steam power to drive its mechanisms, chugging out a puff of steam and a melodic whistle every quarter hour. Gastown itself is Vancouver's oldest neighbourhood, and the clock fits right into its cobblestone charm. Boxing Day crowds often pause to marvel at the steam clock's festive cheer, with its plumes of steam cutting through the winter chill.

bing-50060.jpg.title: Christmas lights at Mousehole Harbour, Cornwall, England
bing-50060.jpg.headline: The holidays continue. Boxing Day
bing-50060.jpg.description: As the last notes of Christmas carols linger in the air, Boxing Day arrives. This day is celebrated in the United Kingdom, Canada, and several Commonwealth countries. In the past, it was customary for the wealthy to give boxes filled with gifts to their servants on the day after Christmas. The tradition evolved into a day for charitable giving to the less fortunate. Today, while the spirit of giving remains, it has transformed into a holiday about enjoying bustling sales and a lineup of soccer matches.

bing-50072.jpg.title: Lake Bled, Slovenia
bing-50072.jpg.headline: Icy reflections and snow-dusted peaks. Lake Bled, Slovenia
bing-50072.jpg.description: Lake Bled in Slovenia gets plenty of attention in summer, but winter? That's when things slow down in the best way. The lake's emerald waters take on a softer tone, and Bled Island, with its quaint church, looks straight out of a winter fairytale, as seen in today's image. The 1.3-mile lake, surrounded by the snow-dusted Julian Alps, was formed over 14,000 years ago through glacial and tectonic activity. The first signs of settlement on Bled Island date back to the New Stone Age (10,000 BCE to 3,000 BCE). Additionally, archaeologists uncovered an Early Medieval graveyard here from the 9th century CE. Today, it houses the Church of the Assumption—built in its current form near the end of the 17th century—where visitors ring the 'wishing bell' for good luck.

bing-50076.jpg.title: Dudhsagar Falls, Goa
bing-50076.jpg.headline: Pouring wonders. Dudhsagar Falls, Goa
bing-50076.jpg.description: Today, let's explore the magic of Dudhsagar Falls in Goa. Towering at an impressive 310 metres with a 30-metre width, it is among India's tallest waterfalls. Translating to 'Sea of Milk,' it is a spectacular four-tiered waterfall on the Mandovi River. Legend has it, a beautiful princess would take a bath here and then drink sweetened milk from a golden jug. One day she saw a handsome prince watching her. To protect her modesty, she poured the milk, forming a white curtain as a shield. According to the tale, the milk continues to flow down the mountains as a tribute to her grace and virtue. This gem in the Western Ghats marks the journey of the Mandovi River as it falls toward Panaji and finally meets the Arabian Sea. During the dry season, the falls might seem unassuming, but with the arrival of the monsoon, they transform into a magnificent cascade of thundering water.

bing-50084.jpg.title: A green sea turtle swims in the Pacific Ocean near the French special collectivity of New Caledonia
bing-50084.jpg.headline: Shell-abrating a life. Endangered Species Act
bing-50084.jpg.description: Today is a big day for conservation—it's the anniversary of the Endangered Species Act. Passed in the US in 1973, this law was a game-changer, ensuring that economic growth wouldn't steamroll over species at risk of disappearing forever. For the first time, plants were given protection too, and the focus shifted from merely avoiding extinction to actively helping species recover to the point where they could thrive without protection.

bing-50096.jpg.title: Borobudur Temple, Java, Indonesia
bing-50096.jpg.headline: On the sacred mountain. Borobudur Temple, Java, Indonesia
bing-50096.jpg.description: Imagine a colossal puzzle made from over 2 million stone blocks—that's Borobudur, seen in today's image. Built during the 9th century in the reign of the Shailendra dynasty—an influential ruling family in Southeast Asia—it's the world's largest Buddhist temple, standing tall on the island of Java, Indonesia. This ancient sanctum has withstood centuries of natural challenges, including volcanic eruptions and earthquakes, thanks to its advanced interlocking stone system. Historically, Borobudur was an important pilgrimage site. After being abandoned for centuries, it was rediscovered in the 19th century by the English lieutenant governor Thomas Stamford Raffles.

bing-50106.jpg.title: Vista aérea da Avenida Paulista na cidade de São Paulo
bing-50106.jpg.headline: Dia de entrar em ação!
bing-50106.jpg.description:
A Corrida de São Silvestre é um evento histórico no Brasil, com sua primeira edição realizada em 31 de dezembro de 1925. Idealizada pelo jornalista Cásper Líbero, a corrida se tornou um marco esportivo e cultural, celebrando o fim de ano com energia e determinação. Até 1988, a corrida era realizada à noite, iluminando as ruas de São Paulo na virada do ano. Hoje em dia, com um percurso de 15 km, a prova passa por pontos icônicos da cidade, como a Avenida Paulista (vista na imagem de hoje) e o Vale do Anhangabaú, atraindo corredores de todo o mundo.

Conhecida por seu espírito festivo, a corrida conta tanto atletas de elite quanto amadores, muitos dos quais participam fantasiados, adicionando um toque de alegria e descontração ao evento. O nome da corrida é uma homenagem a São Silvestre, cuja festa litúrgica é celebrada na mesma data pela Igreja Católica. Com uma história rica, a São Silvestre é a corrida de rua mais antiga da América Latina e uma das mais antigas do mundo ainda em atividade. Se você é um entusiasta da corrida ou simplesmente quer começar o ano de uma maneira diferente, a São Silvestre é o evento perfeito. Tudo pronto para fazer parte dessa tradição?

bing-50108.jpg.title: Tasmanian snow gum and pandani plants near Lake Dobson, Mount Field National Park, Tasmania, Australia
bing-50108.jpg.headline: A park for all seasons. Mount Field National Park, Tasmania, Australia
bing-50108.jpg.description: At the heart of Tasmania, an island state off the southeastern coast of Australia, lies Mount Field National Park. Covering more than 60 square miles, it's one of the state's oldest national parks. As you follow the winding road up through the park, you'll see a whole range of landscapes, from temperate rainforests full of some of the world's tallest eucalyptus trees to alpine moorland. These ever-changing views are what give the park its nickname, 'the park for all seasons.' One of the park's must-visit sites is Russell Falls, a three-tiered waterfall that plunges 190 feet.

bing-50110.jpg.title: 平等院の梵鐘, 京都
bing-50110.jpg.headline: 今日は大晦日
bing-50110.jpg.description:
今日 12 月 31 日は大晦日。大晦日といえば除夜の鐘ですね。京都府宇治市の平等院では、午後 11 時 30 分から 1 月 1 日午前 1 時ごろまで、5 ～ 6 名ずつ 1 回の鐘つきができます。また、先着 1000 名には多幸を祈願した特製絵馬が配られます…

平等院の梵鐘は、鳳凰堂と同じく 11 世紀頃に作られたと推定されており、全面には天人や獅子、唐草文様などの精巧な浮き彫りが施されています。日本三名鐘のひとつとして数えられ、「音の三井寺、銘の神護寺、姿の平等院」と称されており、国宝に指定されています。
bing-50110.jpg.copyright: © Asia Images Group LLC/Alamy Stock Phot

bing-50113.jpg.title: Nochevieja en la Puerta del Sol, Madrid, España
bing-50113.jpg.headline: ¡Suenan las campanadas!. Nochevieja en la Puerta del Sol, Madrid, España
bing-50113.jpg.description:
¡Vive la magia de la Nochevieja! Si alguna vez has soñado con recibir el Año Nuevo en un lugar lleno de historia y tradición, la Puerta del Sol en Madrid es tu destino ideal. Cada 31 de diciembre, miles de personas se reúnen bajo el emblemático reloj de la Real Casa de Correos para despedir el año al son de las campanadas. ¿Sabías que esta tradición de tomar 12 uvas comenzó en España en 1909? Se dice que, si comes una uva con cada campanada, tendrás un año lleno de suerte y prosperidad.

Antes de las 12 campanadas, escucharás los "cuartos", que marcan el inicio del ritual. Suenan cuatro toques rápidos que te preparan para coordinarte con las campanadas principales.

Con luces, música y una energía única, la Puerta del Sol te invita a vivir una Nochevieja inolvidable. ¿Estás preparado para celebrar con tus uvas y dar la bienvenida al nuevo año? No olvides brindar por tus sueños y, al amanecer, deleitarte con un delicioso chocolate con churros, una tradición para empezar el año con buen sabor. ¡Te deseamos un Feliz Año Nuevo!

bing-50114.jpg.title: Silvesterfeuerwerk über der Stadt Garmisch-Partenkirchen mit Blick auf die Zugspitzgruppe, Bayern
bing-50114.jpg.headline: Prosit Neujahr!. Silvester
bing-50114.jpg.description:
Der Countdown läuft – bald begrüßen wir das neue Jahr! Das heutige Bild zeigt ein Feuerwerk über Garmisch-Partenkirchen und fängt die Magie dieses besonderen Moments ein. Die bunten Lichter erhellen den Himmel und die majestätischen Alpen im Hintergrund verleihen der Szene eine besondere Atmosphäre. Das Feuerwerk symbolisiert nicht nur den Beginn eines neuen Jahres, sondern auch die Hoffnung auf eine strahlende Zukunft.

Wie wird in anderen Ländern das neue Jahr eingeläutet? In Österreich tanzt man traditionell um Mitternacht den Donauwalzer. In Spanien isst man um Mitternacht zwölf Weintrauben, eine für jeden Glockenschlag, und in Italien tragen viele rote Unterwäsche. All diese Bräuche sollen Glück und Erfolg für das neue Jahr bringen. Ob es darum geht, mehr Zeit mit der Familie zu verbringen, gesünder zu leben oder neue Hobbys zu entdecken – der Jahreswechsel ist eine Zeit des Aufbruchs und der Chancen. Begrüßen wir also das neue Jahr mit offenen Herzen und großen Erwartungen!

bing-50115.jpg.title: Fuochi d'artificio di Capodanno a Firenze, Toscana
bing-50115.jpg.headline: Notti magiche?
bing-50115.jpg.description:
Ci siamo, il 31 di dicembre è arrivato e si sa, l’ultimo giorno dell’anno porta con sé un'atmosfera unica: è il momento di salutare ciò che è stato e accogliere con entusiasmo ciò che sarà. Sullo sfondo di questa notte speciale, il Duomo di Firenze, maestoso e senza tempo, si illumina di luci e fuochi d’artificio, offrendo uno spettacolo mozzafiato. Tra storia e festa, Firenze si trasforma in un palcoscenico magico, dove i vostri desideri per l’anno nuovo possono diventare realtà.

E voi, come trascorrerete questa serata? In compagnia degli amici più cari, con la famiglia o da soli a pensare a ciò che vorreste per il futuro? Qualunque sia il luogo o l’occasione, che sia un momento per brindare a ciò che avete conquistato e sognare in grande per ciò che verrà. Lasciatevi ispirare dalla bellezza e dalla luce della notte, che si tratti di Firenze, Roma, Venezia o di qualsiasi altro luogo sulla terra: ogni scintilla nel cielo è un augurio che il futuro risplenda per tutti voi. Buon anno, che sia straordinario e pieno di emozioni.

bing-50116.jpg.title: Arc de Triomphe sous les feux d’artifice, Paris
bing-50116.jpg.headline: Le compte à rebours est lancé !. Réveillon du Nouvel An sur les Champs-Élysées
bing-50116.jpg.description:
Le réveillon du Nouvel An sur les Champs-Élysées est bien plus qu'un simple événement, c'est une tradition emblématique qui attire chaque année des milliers de spectateurs. Cette avenue, l'une des plus célèbres au monde, se métamorphose en un véritable écrin de fête, débordant de lumière et de musique.

La soirée débute souvent dès la fin d'après-midi, avec des animations musicales, des artistes de rue et des stands de restauration. Les Parisiens et les visiteurs se rassemblent dans une ambiance festive et animée, unissant leurs voix pour accueillir ensemble la nouvelle année.

Au moment précis où les horloges sonnent minuit, une explosion de lumière marque l'arrivée de la nouvelle année, un spectacle magique et inoubliable pour toutes les personnes qui ont la chance de vivre cette tradition. Bon réveillon !

bing-50117.jpg.title: Fireworks in Edinburgh, Scotland
bing-50117.jpg.headline: Midnight in Edinburgh. Hogmanay
bing-50117.jpg.description:
When it comes to ringing in the New Year, Scotland takes the cake—or perhaps the haggis, its national dish. From torchlight processions to street ceilidhs, Hogmanay is the New Year's Eve celebration that says, 'Why settle for one night of celebration when you can have three?' The term 'Hogmanay' has murky origins—some link it to the French 'hoguinané,' which means 'gala day,' others to Norse or Gaelic roots. But what it means today is clear: an unmissable celebration filled with fireworks, folk songs and feasting. This year, the festivities kicked off on December 29 with a dramatic torchlight procession.

On December 31, as the clock nears midnight, cities like Edinburgh and Glasgow gear up for their iconic countdowns. Fireworks illuminate the skies as seen in today's image, but the real magic happens when the crowd bursts into 'Auld Lang Syne'. No Hogmanay is complete without 'first-footing,' a tradition where the first person to step into your home after midnight brings good luck for the year ahead. Bonus points if the first-footer carries coal, shortbread or whisky—symbols of warmth, sustenance and cheer. In true Scottish fashion, the party doesn't end when the clock strikes twelve. January 1 sees loony dooks—brave souls plunging into icy waters to shake off the cobwebs—or perhaps last night's whisky. And while January 2 is a public holiday in Scotland, it's probably less about recovering and more about preparing for another year of unforgettable celebrations. Cheers—or as the Scots say, Slàinte!
bing-50117.jpg.copyright: © Jane Barlow/PA Images via Getty Image

bing-50120.jpg.title: New Year's Eve fireworks over Copacabana Beach, Rio de Janeiro, Brazil
bing-50120.jpg.headline: Midnight in Rio. New Year's Eve in Rio de Janeiro, Brazil
bing-50120.jpg.description: New Year's Eve, also known as Old Year's Day, is celebrated around the world with revelry, fireworks, and for some, religious and cultural observances. Many countries celebrate with foods symbolic of prosperity, long life, and good fortune for the coming year, and many people sing the Scottish folk song 'Auld Lang Syne' at the stroke of midnight in remembrance of old friends and past experiences. The new year is often personified as a baby in a tradition that dates back to ancient Greeks, and paired with an old man who represents the year that is ending.

bing-50121.jpg.title: Fireworks over Parliament Hill, Ottawa, Canada
bing-50121.jpg.headline: Fireworks over Parliament Hill, Ottawa, Canada
bing-50121.jpg.description:
New Year's Eve, also known as Old Year's Day, is celebrated around the world with revelry, fireworks and for some, religious and cultural observances. Many countries celebrate with foods symbolic of prosperity, long life and good fortune for the coming year, and many people sing Scottish folk song 'Auld Lang Syne' at the stroke of midnight to remember old friends and past experiences. The new year is often personified as a baby, a tradition that dates back to ancient Greeks, often paired with an old man who represents the previous year.

Featured here is the dazzling canvas of light and colour as fireworks burst over the Parliament Hill in Ottawa, Canada. Often called the 'The Hill,' it is a significant landmark in downtown Ottawa, Ontario, resting along the southern bank of the Ottawa River. This Crown land is home to Canada's Parliament, housed within a striking collection of Gothic Revival buildings designed to reflect the heritage of parliamentary democracy. Welcoming around three million visitors annually, Parliament Hill is both a hub of political activity and a cultural attraction.

bing-50122.jpg.title: 朝日と白髭神社の鳥居, 滋賀県 高島市
bing-50122.jpg.headline: 今日は元日
bing-50122.jpg.description:
明けましておめでとうございます。今年も Bing をよろしくお願いします。今年最初の Bing は滋賀県高島市の琵琶湖から、白鬚神社の鳥居の向こう側から昇る日の出をお届けします。朝の静けさの中、鳥居のシルエットが徐々に明るくなり、やがて太陽が顔を出す瞬間は、まさに神聖なひとときです…

この鳥居は、室町時代の「近江名所図」や白鬚神社の「縁起絵巻」にも描かれており、古来より波打ち際に鳥居が見え隠れしていたなどともいわれる伝説の鳥居です。この神秘的な鳥居が実際に建てられたのは 1937 年。現在の鳥居は 1981 年に建て替えたものです。

bing-50132.jpg.title: Polar bears at play in the Arctic
bing-50132.jpg.headline: Have an ice New Year's Day. Happy New Year!
bing-50132.jpg.description: Happy New Year's Day! Humans have celebrated the new year since at least 2000 BCE, but various cultures have chosen different days coinciding with equinoxes or lunar cycles. The Romans established January 1 as the beginning of the year in 153 BCE, but this fell out of favor throughout Europe during the medieval era. Since 1582 and the widespread adoption of the Gregorian calendar, however, much of the world now celebrates the new year today. In addition to watching fireworks, drinking champagne, and making resolutions in the wee hours of the morning, other global traditions include making noise, eating lucky foods, and giving gifts.

bing-50140.jpg.title: Montagne enneigée au coucher du soleil, Alpes françaises
bing-50140.jpg.headline: Le trésor de l’Europe. Les Alpes françaises
bing-50140.jpg.description:
Saviez-vous que les Alpes françaises abritent non seulement le Mont-Blanc, point culminant de l'Europe à 4 807 mètres, mais aussi des trésors cachés sous la glace ? Les glaciers alpins recèlent des fossiles marins témoignant de l’époque où ces montagnes étaient enfouies sous un océan, il y a des millions d’années.

Les Alpes ne sont pas qu’un paradis pour les skieurs : elles renferment également une biodiversité fascinante. Le gypaète barbu, un rapace rare surnommé le « nettoyeur des montagnes », y survole majestueusement les cimes. En été, certaines fleurs comme la gentiane jaune ou l’edelweiss ne poussent qu’à des altitudes vertigineuses.

Côté humain, les Alpes sont le théâtre de records insolites. En 1955, le téléphérique de l’Aiguille du Midi, près de Chamonix, devenait le plus haut du monde, grimpant à 3 842 mètres. Aujourd’hui encore, il offre une vue à couper le souffle. Que ce soit pour leur histoire géologique, leur faune unique ou leurs exploits techniques, les Alpes françaises fascinent et invitent à l’exploration. Un voyage dans ces montagnes, c’est toucher l’infini tout en découvrant l’inattendu.

bing-50144.jpg.title: Star trails over Ardez, Graubunden, Switzerland
bing-50144.jpg.headline: The glistening village. Ardez, Graubunden, Switzerland
bing-50144.jpg.description: Perched on a terrace above the Inn Valley at 4,790 feet, Ardez is a hidden gem in eastern Switzerland renowned for its deep cultural roots and stunning preservation of history. This picturesque village, starring in today's image, showcases the rich traditions and unique language of Switzerland's Romansh-speaking communities. Its homes are adorned with sgraffiti—decorative designs etched into plaster—and colorful murals, both iconic art styles of the Engadin region. Dating back to 840 when it was first referred to as Ardezis, the village's history includes Steinsberg Castle, originally owned by the Bishop of Chur. Though destroyed during the Swabian War in 1499, the castle's tower has been restored multiple times and stands today as a proud reminder of its past. In 1975, Ardez was chosen as a Swiss model village for its exceptional preservation efforts, which have kept its historic charm intact.

bing-50156.jpg.title: The Radcliffe Camera and All Souls College, University of Oxford, England
bing-50156.jpg.headline: Ring in the fun. Happy Birthday, J.R.R. Tolkien!
bing-50156.jpg.description: 'Don't adventures ever have an end? I suppose not. Someone else always has to carry on the story.' Today, on Tolkien Day, fans around the world honor the master storyteller who crafted the epic adventures of Middle-earth: J.R.R. Tolkien. While Tolkien may have started the tale, it's his readers who carry it forward, generation after generation, diving into the pages of 'The Hobbit,' 'The Lord of the Rings,' and beyond. Tolkienists are encouraged to celebrate the author's birthday with a toast at 9 PM local time—to participate, all you must do is stand and raise a glass of your choice, say 'The Professor,' and take a sip.

bing-50168.jpg.title: Bản Giốc–Detian Falls on the Quây Sơn River, Vietnam
bing-50168.jpg.headline: A borderline paradise. Bản Giốc–Detian Falls, Vietnam
bing-50168.jpg.description: Welcome to a spot where rivers meet borders in the most stunning way: Bản Giốc–Detian Falls, featured in today's image. Tucked between the karst hills of Daxin County in China and Trùng Khánh district in Vietnam, these falls tumble along the Quây Sơn River. Over 95 feet tall and 980 feet wide, it holds the distinction of being the widest waterfall in Vietnam. Located just 169 miles north of Hanoi, this waterfall have gradually worn away their crest over the years, inching upstream. For most of the year, they flow as two distinct cascades, but come summer, when the rains swell the river, they merge into one big fall.

bing-50172.jpg.title: Pushkarani, Sri Krishna Temple, Hampi, Karnataka
bing-50172.jpg.headline: Steps to serenity. Pushkarni, Sri Krishna Temple, Hampi, Karnataka
bing-50172.jpg.description:
The ancient city of Hampi's architectural brilliance is displayed in the Pushkarani water tanks. These beautifully designed tanks, with their perfectly laid stone steps, were crafted to make access to the water easy. These tanks have deep cultural significance and are highly revered. Historically, Pushkaranis were built for ritualistic temple practices or as royal amenities during the Vijayanagara Empire. In Hampi, almost every grand temple has one tank, serving both spiritual and functional purposes. The Pushkarani in front of the Sri Krishna Temple, seen in today's image, is one of the most elegant and accessible tanks here.

The structure's symmetry showcases the skilled craftsmanship of its time. Beyond the ceremonial significance, it served as a vital resource for the community, providing water for public use. Dedicated to Bala Krishna, the infant form of Lord Krishna, this temple is a treasure trove of history and architecture. With intricately carved pillars and a grand sanctum, it continues to attract travellers and history buffs alike.

bing-50173.jpg.title: Árboles escarchados en la Sierra de Aralar, Navarra, España
bing-50173.jpg.headline: ¡Vamos a tomar la fresca!. Sierra de Aralar, Navarra, España
bing-50173.jpg.description:
Hoy, 5 de enero, la víspera del Día de Reyes, es una noche llena de ilusión en toda España. Los niños esperan con ansias la llegada de los Reyes Magos, que recorren las calles en la famosa Cabalgata, lanzando caramelos y llenando las ciudades de magia.

Esta noche, los más pequeños colocarán sus zapatos en un lugar especial de la casa y dejarán un vaso de agua, leche y turrón, para que los Reyes puedan descansar y coger fuerzas para seguir su camino. Mañana, en el Día de Reyes, es tradición que las familias se reúnan para disfrutar de un buen festín y, sobre todo, del tradicional Roscón de Reyes. Ya sea con o sin relleno, la elección es tuya, pero ¡esperemos que no te toque la famosa haba!

Y mientras tanto, en lugares como la Sierra de Aralar, en Navarra, que vemos en la imagen de hoy, los Reyes Magos podrían estar cruzando los montes cubiertos de escarcha, rumbo a sus hogares. ¡Que la magia de este día nos llene de alegría y sorpresas! ¡Feliz víspera de Reyes!

bing-50174.jpg.title: Winterlandschaft in Bayern, Deutschland
bing-50174.jpg.headline: Wo die Stille den Nebel umarmt. Winterlandschaft in Bayern
bing-50174.jpg.description:
Wenn der Winter Einzug hält, verwandelt sich diese bayerische Landschaft in ein Märchen aus Schnee und Eis. Wälder sind in ein weißes Kleid gehüllt, und die Berge glitzern im Sonnenlicht wie Diamanten. Die Kälte beißt sanft in die Wangen, während der Atem in kleinen Wolken vor einem schwebt. Schnee knirscht unter den Füßen, und die Welt scheint still zu stehen, eingehüllt in eine Decke aus Stille und Frieden.

Haben Sie auch Lust, es sich drinnen in einer gemütlichen Stube bei einer dampfenden Tasse Tee bequem zu machen? Stellen Sie sich vor, wie der Duft von Zimt und Nelken die Luft erfüllt und die Wärme des knisternden Kamins sich wohlig ausbreitet. Sie sitzen am Fenster, schauen hinaus auf die verschneite Landschaft und fühlen sich geborgen. So schön ist der Winter, eine Zeit der Ruhe und Besinnlichkeit, eine Zeit, um innezuhalten und die Schönheit der Natur zu erleben.

bing-50180.jpg.title: Plum-headed parakeet at Shimoga, Karnataka, India
bing-50180.jpg.headline: Head-turner in the treetops. National Bird Day
bing-50180.jpg.description: Look up at the skies and experience the magic of birds—it's National Bird Day. Birds come in many shapes and colors, but few are as striking as the plum-headed parakeet, seen in today's image. Native to the Indian subcontinent, these birds are known for their swift, acrobatic flight and distinctive calls that echo through the air. There have been reports of plum-headed parakeets making their way to places like New York, Florida, and even parts of the Middle East.

bing-50192.jpg.title: Flooded crypt, Basilica of San Francesco, Ravenna, Italy
bing-50192.jpg.headline: Divine depths. Flooded crypt, Basilica of San Francesco, Ravenna, Italy
bing-50192.jpg.description: In the Italian province of Ravenna lies the Basilica of San Francesco, recognized for its beauty and historical significance. This Romanesque church, originally built in 450, features a sturdy square bell tower added in the 9th century, enhancing the basilica's exterior. Its design features three naves, divided by two rows of 12 columns each. Featured in today's image is the basilica's real showstopper: The basement crypt, or burial chamber, is a stunning model of early religious design. Complete with vaulted ceilings that slope down into rows of stone columns, its floor is a work of art itself. It's inlaid with beautifully intricate mosaic tiles that have withstood the test of time.

bing-50199.jpg.title: Frecce Tricolori in formazione acrobatica sulle dolomiti italiane, Cortina d'Ampezzo, Veneto
bing-50199.jpg.headline: Vola, il Tricolore vola...
bing-50199.jpg.description:
Oggi festeggiamo la Festa del Tricolore, dedicata alla bandiera italiana, simbolo di unità e di orgoglio nazionale. Istituita ufficialmente nel 1997, questa ricorrenza ricorda l’adozione della bandiera tricolore nel 1797 a Reggio Emilia, dove la Repubblica Cispadana scelse il verde, il bianco e il rosso come emblemi di libertà e unità. È interessante notare che il tricolore nacque ben prima della stessa Italia unita, diventando fin da subito un simbolo di aspirazione all'indipendenza e alla coesione nazionale.

Uno dei momenti più magici di questa giornata è il volo delle Frecce Tricolori, che con precisione ed eleganza disegnano nel cielo delle scie verdi, bianche e rosse. Quando sorvolano le maestose Alpi, il contrasto tra le vette innevate e i colori vibranti del Tricolore regala un'emozione unica, capace di evocare un legame profondo con la storia e le radici del nostro Paese. È uno spettacolo che celebra l’identità collettiva e che ci ricorda la bellezza e la forza che nascono dall’unità. In ogni tricolore che sventola, si può leggere una storia di coraggio e speranza. E in ogni scia lasciata nel cielo, l’Italia spicca il volo verso il futuro!

bing-50204.jpg.title: Moeraki Boulders at sunset, South Island, New Zealand
bing-50204.jpg.headline: Rocks and rollers. Moeraki Boulders, South Island, New Zealand
bing-50204.jpg.description: Are you ready to rock the new year? Today is Old Rock Day, a day for celebrating and learning about old rocks and fossils. Rocks are common and few of us take the time to consider how amazing they are. But forged in volcanoes or molded by millennia of pressure, these solid masses of minerals hold the key to understanding how our planet formed. Rocks can also contain fossils, the remnants of long-extinct organisms, which give scientists clues about what creatures and plants have lived on Earth during its 4.5-billion-year history.

bing-50214.jpg.title: Jacaré (Caiman yacare) bebê visto de baixo
bing-50214.jpg.headline: Lentes para um mergulho especial
bing-50214.jpg.description:
Hoje é um dia especial para quem ama fotografia! No dia 8 de janeiro, comemoramos o Dia Nacional do Fotógrafo, uma data que homenageia o nascimento de Afonso Gonçalves, um dos primeiros fotógrafos a atuar no Brasil. Este dia é uma celebração da arte e da técnica fotográfica, reconhecendo a importância dos profissionais que capturam momentos e contam histórias através das lentes. Para celebrar, que tal admirar a imagem desse bebê jacaré visto de baixo? Uma perspectiva diferente que nos mostra a beleza da natureza!

No cenário internacional, fotógrafos brasileiros têm se destacado, como Sebastião Salgado, cujas obras são reconhecidas mundialmente por sua profundidade e impacto social. E se você é um entusiasta da natureza captada pelas lentes das câmeras fotográficas, vai gostar de conhecer o trabalho de Adriano Gambarini, conhecido por suas imagens que documentam a beleza e a diversidade do Brasil. Neste dia especial, parabenizamos todos os fotógrafos que, com sensibilidade e talento, nos presenteiam com suas visões únicas do mundo. Feliz Dia do Fotógrafo!

bing-50216.jpg.title: Snow on the Great Wall of China
bing-50216.jpg.headline: Step up your game. National Take the Stairs Day
bing-50216.jpg.description: New year, new goals—so why not start by taking a step toward better health? On this National Take the Stairs Day, let's climb into the past. The Great Wall of China, one of the longest humanmade structures in the world, offers the perfect inspiration. Stretching more than 13,000 miles and dating back thousands of years, the ancient marvel in today's picture is a series of fortifications spanning rugged mountains, valleys, and deserts. Featuring steep trenches and watchtowers, parts of it were designed to keep invaders at bay. Hiking the Great Wall offers a unique glimpse into this historical landmark. The experience varies from well-preserved sections like Mutianyu to wild, unrestored parts such as Jiankou. Some steps are so high, they're more like steps on a ladder! Talk about a workout—taking these stairs could rival any modern fitness challenge.

bing-50225.jpg.title: Sossusvlei sand dunes, Namib desert, Namibia
bing-50225.jpg.headline: Shifting horizons. Sossusvlei sand dunes, Namib desert, Namibia
bing-50225.jpg.description:
Picture a sea of shifting sand dunes glowing orange in the sunrise, stretching as far as the eye can see. Welcome to the Namib desert, spanning thousands of miles across Namibia. Estimated to be 55 million years old, it is believed to be the oldest desert in the world. It also boasts some of the tallest sand dunes on Earth, including the famous 'Big Daddy,' which towers roughly 325 metres; Dune 7, the highest dune in Namibia at 383 metres; and Dune 45, which, at roughly 170 metres, is a favourite among photographers.

At the heart of this vast, arid expanse is Sossusvlei, seen in today's image. A salt and clay pan surrounded by towering dunes, Sossusvlei tells a story of contrasts. Every 10 years or so, an extraordinary event occurs when the Tsauchab River floods the pan, transforming it into a stunning turquoise lake. Nearby is the eerie Dead Vlei, with its ancient, desiccated camelthorn trees, which remain frozen in time as the extremely dry climate keeps them from decaying. Visitors to this landscape also witness an ecosystem full of surprising life. From the adaptable gemsboks to the ingenious Namib desert beetle that drinks fog droplets that collect on its back, the Namib is brimming with stories of survival and resilience.

bing-50228.jpg.title: The US Capitol dome with flags flying at half-staff in honor of former President Jimmy Carter, Washington, DC
bing-50228.jpg.headline: Honoring Jimmy Carter. Remembering Jimmy Carter
bing-50228.jpg.description: Thursday, January 9 is a national day of mourning in the United States in honor of former President Jimmy Carter, who died on December 29 at 100 years old. After his lying in state at the Capitol, a funeral for the 39th president will be held today at Washington National Cathedral. The federal government will be closed today, as will other institutions, including the New York Stock Exchange. Our photo shows the Capitol dome on December 30, 2024, with flags flying at half-staff in honor of the longest-lived US president.

bing-50236.jpg.title: Route de la bande dessinée, peinture murale de Tintin de Hergé à Bruxelles
bing-50236.jpg.headline: Le plus célèbre des journalistes. Journée mondiale de Tintin
bing-50236.jpg.description: Le 10 janvier est une date à ne pas manquer pour tous les passionnés de bande dessinée : c’est la Journée mondiale de Tintin ! Cette journée est l'occasion idéale de découvrir ou de redécouvrir l’œuvre magistrale d’Hergé. Tintin, ce reporter audacieux, a voyagé à travers le monde, d’Égypte à l’Asie, et a participé à des aventures palpitantes avec ses compagnons inoubliables comme Milou ou le capitaine Haddock. Mais Tintin, c’est aussi un regard précis sur les événements historiques et sociaux de son époque. Que vous soyez à la recherche d’une aventure captivante ou d’une lecture qui vous en apprend plus sur le monde, Tintin saura vous séduire. Profitez de cette journée pour vous plonger dans ses albums et découvrir les nombreuses facettes de ce personnage iconique.

bing-50240.jpg.title: Abraham Lake, Alberta, Canada
bing-50240.jpg.headline: Bubbles, bubbles everywhere. Abraham Lake, Alberta, Canada
bing-50240.jpg.description: Ever heard of frozen bubbles? Abraham Lake in Alberta, Canada, has them during the winter, and they're not just beautiful—they're science in action. Created in 1972, Abraham Lake is a human-made reservoir that spans more than 20 square miles along the North Saskatchewan River. Thanks to glacier-fed waters from the Rocky Mountains, the lake stays transparent even in the coldest months. Glacial meltwater carries fine sediment that scatters sunlight, while natural filtration through rocks keeps pollutants to a minimum.

bing-50246.jpg.title: Apfel hängt an einem verschneiten Baum, Deutschland
bing-50246.jpg.headline: Ein Hauch von Rot im Winter. Tag des deutschen Apfels
bing-50246.jpg.description:
Wussten Sie, dass der 11. Januar der Tag des deutschen Apfels ist? Seit 2010 verteilen Freiwillige in Städten wie Köln, München, Berlin und Stuttgart kostenlos Äpfel, um für die Vielfalt und Qualität unserer heimischen Apfelsorten zu werben. Beliebte Sorten sind der Pinova, der für sein fruchtiges, saftiges und knackiges Fruchtfleisch bekannt ist, und der Holsteiner Cox, der für seine großen Früchte und sein fruchtiges Aroma geschätzt wird. Erwähnenswert ist auch der Altländer Pfannkuchenapfel. Diese alte Sorte stammt aus dem Alten Land bei Hamburg wurde bereits im 19. Jahrhundert als Zufallssämling entdeckt. Der Apfel ist groß, süß-säuerlich und sehr gut lagerfähig, was ihn ideal für die Wintermonate macht.

Diese Aktion hat sich zu einem festen Bestandteil des deutschen Kalenders entwickelt und bringt Menschen zusammen, um die Vorzüge des Apfels zu feiern. Der Apfel ist nicht nur lecker, sondern auch gesund – er enthält viele Vitamine und Ballaststoffe. Feiern Sie die Widerstandsfähigkeit und Schönheit des Apfels, wie es unser heutiges Bild symbolisch darstellt. Genießen Sie einen frischen Apfel und lassen Sie sich von seiner Geschichte und Vielfalt inspirieren!

bing-50252.jpg.title: Heri es-Swani in Meknes, Morocco
bing-50252.jpg.headline: Arches of a bygone era. Heri es-Swani in Meknes, Morocco
bing-50252.jpg.description: An imperial city in northern central Morocco, Meknes is steeped in history. Once the capital of Morocco under Sultan Ismail Ibn Sharif of the Alawi dynasty in the 17th century, it's known for its massive walls, grand gates, and structures built to last centuries. Meknes reflects the Moroccan style of architecture, with one of its most impressive landmarks being Heri es-Swani, seen in today's image.

bing-50262.jpg.title: Cidade de Belém, capital do estado do Pará
bing-50262.jpg.headline: Terra da tarde molhada de chuva
bing-50262.jpg.description:
Hoje celebramos o aniversário de Belém, conhecida carinhosamente como a "Cidade das Mangueiras". Esta cidade encantadora é famosa por suas ruas arborizadas, especialmente na Avenida Nazaré, onde as mangueiras são abundantes. Durante a época de frutificação, é comum ver mangas caindo pelas calçadas, adicionando um charme especial à cidade. Famosa por seu clima quente e úmido, Belém oferece aos seus moradores e visitantes o "banho de cheiro", uma chuva rápida e refrescante que ocorre quase todos os dias no início da tarde.

Além do "banho de cheiro" e das mangueiras, Belém é rica em história e cultura. Fundada em 1616, a cidade abriga importantes marcos históricos e culturais, como o Círio de Nazaré, uma das maiores procissões religiosas do mundo. A culinária local, com pratos como o tacacá e o pato no tucupi, é outro destaque que encanta moradores e visitantes. Vamos celebrar esse tesouro nacional, com sua gastronomia única, celebrações vibrantes e uma cultura cheia de história. Parabéns, Belém!

bing-50264.jpg.title: Crescent-tail bigeye fish in the Great Barrier Reef, Australia
bing-50264.jpg.headline: Sharp vision in the depths. Crescent-tail bigeye fish, Great Barrier Reef, Australia
bing-50264.jpg.description: Say hello to the crescent-tail bigeye, a fish as eye-catching as its name suggests. With large, wide eyes and a distinctive tail shaped like a crescent moon, it's hard to miss. Measuring about 20 inches long, it has a sleek body and a protruding lower jaw with small conical teeth. Its eyes are adapted to the low-light conditions of deep waters, helping it spot prey and avoid predators. This fish mainly feeds on smaller fish, crustaceans, and invertebrates, fueling its active lifestyle as it patrols the reefs and hunts for food.

bing-50276.jpg.title: Cottage with Tŵr Mawr Lighthouse in the background, Ynys Llanddwyn, Wales
bing-50276.jpg.headline: 'Welsh' you a Happy Hen Galan!. Happy Welsh New Year!
bing-50276.jpg.description: Who says New Year's Day has to be on January 1? In Wales, the clocks turn back—figuratively—to celebrate Hen Galan, or the 'Old New Year,' on January 13. As part of this tradition, Calennig, meaning 'New Year's gift' in Welsh, plays a central role, linking the celebration to customs from the Julian calendar era. Even after most of the world switched to the Gregorian calendar in 1582, some Welsh communities clung to their old ways. Traditionally, the day involves children going door-to-door, singing songs, and offering good wishes in exchange for gifts like coins, food, or sweets. A unique feature is its clove-decorated apples. These aren't for snacking, though; they're miniature symbols of luck and prosperity.

bing-50280.jpg.title: Sky full of kites
bing-50280.jpg.headline: Stringing traditions in the sky. Makar Sankranti
bing-50280.jpg.description:
Get ready to string up those kites and dive into the sweetness of Makar Sankranti. A significant Hindu festival observed every year, its roots trace back to the Vedic texts, including the sacred Gayatri Mantra from the Rigveda. This occasion is celebrated across India with various multi-day festivities. It includes a burst of social festivities, from colourful decorations and joyful kite flying to lively fairs, bonfires and sumptuous feasts. In some regions, children go door-to-door singing songs and collecting treats, adding to the festive spirit.

A key ritual is taking a holy dip in rivers like the Ganga, Yamuna, Godavari, Krishna and Kaveri, believed to cleanse sins and bring blessings. People pray to Surya, the sun deity, expressing gratitude for their prosperity. A shared tradition in various parts of India is preparing sweets made with sesame (til) and jaggery (gud), symbolising unity, joy and harmony amidst diversity. Falling during the early stages of the Rabi crop cycle, Makar Sankranti also represents a time of relaxation, socialising and family bonding after months of hard work in the fields.

bing-50288.jpg.title: Village of Zahara de la Sierra overlooking Zahara-El Gastor Reservoir, Cádiz province, Spain
bing-50288.jpg.headline: Calmness overload. Village of Zahara de la Sierra, Cadiz, Spain
bing-50288.jpg.description: Zahara de la Sierra, a stunning whitewashed village in the hills of Cádiz province in Spain, offers a blend of history and nature in the south of the Iberian Peninsula. Perched on a rocky hilltop, the village seen in today's image overlooks the Zahara-El Gastor Reservoir and the Sierra de Grazalema Natural Park, a UNESCO Biosphere Reserve since 1977. Its Moorish castle ruins and 15th-century tower reflect its history as a medieval fortress. Stroll through streets lined with flower-filled balconies, visit the church of Santa María de la Mesa, or simply relax and take in the views. Zahara is also a gateway to adventure—activities like hiking, cycling, and kayaking are only a little of what the village has to offer.

bing-50290.jpg.title: カラフルな餅花, 愛知県 豊田市
bing-50290.jpg.headline: 今日は小正月
bing-50290.jpg.description:
今日は 1 月 15 日、小正月。年神様を迎える行事の多い大正月に対して、豊作祈願や家庭的行事が中心となります。この日は小豆粥を食べたり、門松やしめ飾りなどを左義長で燃やしたりします。また、一部地域では餅花を飾る風習もあり、小さく切った餅や団子を木の枝につけて五穀豊穣を願います…

写真の撮影地である愛知県豊田市足助地区は、尾張・三河から信州を結ぶ中馬街道の重要な中継地にあたり、江戸時代から続く伝統的な町並みが残っています。毎年 2 月上旬から 3 月上旬に「中馬のおひなさん」というイベントが行われ、約 100 軒の商家や民家が、お雛様や餅花などを店先や玄関先に飾り、訪れた人々に町並みの散策を楽しんでもらいます。
bing-50290.jpg.copyright: © Photo taken by Bong Grit/Getty Image

bing-50292.jpg.title: Chital, Bandhavgarh National Park, Madhya Pradesh
bing-50292.jpg.headline: High deer life. Chital, Bandhavgarh National Park, Madhya Pradesh
bing-50292.jpg.description:
Today's image features a chital in Bandhavgarh National Park, Madhya Pradesh. Also known as the spotted deer or axis deer, this species is native to the Indian subcontinent. From the forests of eastern Rajasthan and Gujarat in the west to the Terai, Sikkim and Bhutan's valleys, the chital thrives in diverse habitats, favouring elevations below 1,100 metres. The males, larger than the females and adorned with striking three-pronged antlers that can grow nearly a metre long, are a sight to behold in the wild.

Bandhavgarh, with its lush landscapes and rich biodiversity, is the perfect home for these deer. This sanctuary spans 716 square kilometres and supports a dynamic ecosystem. The chital, abundant here, plays a vital role in the food chain as the primary prey for the majestic tigers and Indian leopards. Alongside the chital, Bandhavgarh is also home to elusive species like the Indian wolf, striped hyena and the rare caracal.

bing-50298.jpg.title: Praia dos Nativos vista de Quadrado, Trancoso, Porto Seguro, Bahia
bing-50298.jpg.headline: Refresco para os olhos
bing-50298.jpg.description:
Hoje nos transportamos a esse destino que é um refresco para o corpo e também para os olhos! Trancoso, localizada no sul da Bahia, é um destino encantador que combina beleza natural e história. Fundada pelos jesuítas no século XVI, a vila preserva seu charme rústico com o famoso Quadrado, uma praça cercada por casas coloridas e a igreja de São João Batista. As praias de Trancoso, como a Praia dos Nativos vista na imagem de hoje, são conhecidas por suas águas cristalinas e paisagens deslumbrantes.

Além de suas belezas naturais, Trancoso é um polo cultural, atraindo artistas e celebridades de todo o mundo. Durante o verão, a vila se transforma em um ponto de encontro para eventos e festivais que celebram a cultura local. Essa combinação de refúgio paradisíaco com um toque de história e cultura parece irresistível, não é mesmo? Mergulhe na imagem do dia e aprecie as maravilhas da Bahia!

bing-50299.jpg.title: Lake Superior during winters, Thunder Bay, Ontario
bing-50299.jpg.headline: Freeze the day. Lake Superior, Thunder Bay, Ontario
bing-50299.jpg.description:
Lake Superior in Ontario isn't just a massive freshwater lake—it's a natural wonder with a backstory. Spanning 82,100 square kilometres, this is the world's largest freshwater lake by surface area. Its shoreline extends across Ontario, Minnesota, Wisconsin and Michigan, making it a part of both Canadian and American landscapes. Historically, the lake has been an essential waterway for the fur trade, used by Indigenous peoples and later, European settlers. Its hydrography is equally impressive. It holds about 10% of the world's freshwater and reaches depths of 406 metres, fed by over 200 rivers. While the waters might seem endless, this lake takes on an entirely different personality during the winter months, as seen in today's image.

Situated along the shoreline is Lake Superior Provincial Park. A protected area since 1944, it encompasses the site of an Ojibwe fishing village known as Nanabozhung. The park is also home to ancient pictographs at Agawa Rocks, estimated to be between 150 and 400 years old, which offer insights into Indigenous history. These century-old Ojibwe artworks, painted with ochre, provide a glimpse into the beliefs and the connection between the people and the lake.

bing-50300.jpg.title: The Great Court of the British Museum, London, England
bing-50300.jpg.headline: Where the past is always present. Anniversary of the British Museum
bing-50300.jpg.description: January 15, 1759, marked the opening of a place that would become the pride of London, a hub of global history, and a keeper of countless stories: the British Museum. For the first time, a national museum flung its doors wide open, offering free access to knowledge and culture for all. The story begins with Sir Hans Sloane, an Anglo-Irish physician and avid collector. His collection of more than 71,000 items, ranging from books and manuscripts to botanical samples and antiquities, formed the museum's foundation. Fast-forward nearly 266 years, and the museum houses more than 8 million objects, the largest collection of artifacts in the world, although only about 1% of the collection is currently on display. Its treasures span continents and millennia, from the Rosetta Stone—key to deciphering ancient Egyptian hieroglyphs—to the Parthenon Marbles, the Benin Bronzes, and samurai armor.

bing-50301.jpg.title: Pointe du Diable, Saint-Pierre, Réunion Island
bing-50301.jpg.headline: Pointe du Diable, Saint-Pierre, Réunion Island
bing-50301.jpg.description:
The Pointe du Diable, on the island of Réunion, is a striking intersection of nature's power and mystery. Formed 200,000 years ago by lava flows from the Piton des Neiges, this basaltic peninsula juts majestically into the Indian Ocean. On one side lies Petite Baie, once a haven for surfers, its shores still echoing tales of a time when humans and the ocean coexisted in harmony—until shark attacks imposed a solemn stillness. On the other side is a pebble beach, where the unrelenting waves sculpt the landscape. Here, the salty spray carried by the wind and the thunder of waves crashing against cliffs serve as constant reminders of nature's raw force.

For fishermen, it's a rich refuge teeming with rockfish. For hikers, coastal trails offer breathtaking views. Straddling fascination and peril, the Pointe du Diable is a living testament to the geological and human history of La Réunion—a place where awe inspires deep respect for untamed nature.

bing-50305.jpg.title: Jaén al anochecer, Andalucía, España
bing-50305.jpg.headline: ¡Una fiesta inesperada!. Jaén, Andalucía, España
bing-50305.jpg.description:
Las Fiestas de San Antón y la Carrera Urbana Internacional Noche de San Antón son eventos que no te puedes perder en Jaén, Andalucía. Cada año, la noche del 16 al 17 de enero, la ciudad se llena de vida y tradición para celebrar la víspera de San Antón, una festividad declarada de Interés Turístico Nacional desde 2019. Desde el siglo XIII, Jaén honra a San Antonio Abad con devoción, una tradición que llegó desde Europa central durante la Reconquista. En el siglo XV, Miguel Lucas de Iranzo, alcaide de la ciudad, impulsó esta fiesta religiosa, que se consolidó en el siglo XIX gracias a los agricultores y ganaderos.

Las Lumbres de San Antón son un espectáculo único. Decenas de hogueras iluminan la ciudad, mientras los vecinos cantan, comen rosetas, calabaza asada, morcilla, chorizo y disfrutan del vino local. Las hogueras, hechas con restos de poda de olivo, tienen un origen mágico y se usaban para ahuyentar enfermedades y plagas.

Otro de los grandes eventos del día es la Carrera Urbana Internacional Noche de San Antón, celebrada desde 1984, es otro gran atractivo. Atletas de todo el mundo corren por las calles decoradas con luces, animados por el público con antorchas. ¿Te atreves a vivir esta experiencia inolvidable?

bing-50306.jpg.title: Bartmeisen (Panurus biarmicus) Männchen und Weibchen auf Nahrungssuche in verschneiten Schilfrohren, Baden-Wuerttemberg
bing-50306.jpg.headline: Flügel der Treue. Bartmeisen, Baden-Württemberg, Deutschland
bing-50306.jpg.description: Mit seinem hellblaugrauen Kopf und dem markanten schwarzen Bartstreif ist die Bartmeise ein stolzer Wächter des Schilfs. Sein Gefieder schimmert in warmen Gelbtönen, während seine gelborange Iris in der Sonne leuchtet. Das zierliche und elegante Weibchen trägt ein beigebraunes Kleid ohne den auffälligen Bartstreif. Ihre schmutzigweiße Kehle und die hellbraunen Unterschwanzdecken verleihen ihr eine sanfte Anmut. Gemeinsam durchstreifen sie die dichten Schilfwälder, immer auf der Suche nach Nahrung und einem sicheren Nistplatz. Ihr harmonisches Zusammenspiel und ihre liebevolle Fürsorge füreinander sind ein Zeugnis der Natur, wie sie in perfekter Symbiose lebt. Die Bartmeise ist nicht nur ein Symbol für Treue und Partnerschaft, sondern auch ein Beweis dafür, dass wahre Schönheit oft in den kleinen, unscheinbaren Dingen des Lebens zu finden ist. Ihre zarten Rufe und das leise Rascheln ihrer Flügel im Schilf sind eine Melodie, die das Herz eines jeden Naturliebhabers höher schlagen lässt.

bing-50312.jpg.title: High Peaks Trail in Pinnacles National Park, San Benito County, California
bing-50312.jpg.headline: Born from fire, built to last. Anniversary of Pinnacles National Park, California
bing-50312.jpg.description: Jagged pinnacles and spires, monoliths, and unusual caves—welcome to Pinnacles National Park in central California. President Theodore Roosevelt designated the area as a national monument in 1908, and Pinnacles would earn its status as a national park in 2013. As we celebrate the park's anniversary today, let's take a moment to appreciate this landscape. Pinnacles owes its formations to an ancient volcanic eruption that occurred 23 million years ago. The fiery beginnings made towering spires, cliffs, and talus caves, which are created by falling boulders wedged into narrow canyons. Over millennia, tectonic forces shifted the landmass northward, leaving the park far from its volcanic birthplace. Talk about a journey!

bing-50324.jpg.title: Brown pelican, San Diego, California
bing-50324.jpg.headline: Pouch perfect. Brown pelican, San Diego, California
bing-50324.jpg.description: Today's image features the brown pelican, a bird that doesn't just fly but soars, spots, and dives with unmatched precision. Although it's the smallest of the eight pelican species worldwide, it's still a large bird, measuring about 4 feet in length and having a wingspan of 6.5 feet. It's a marine-dwelling species and can be spotted along the Atlantic coast of the Americas, from New Jersey to the mouth of the Amazon River. On the Pacific coast, it can be spotted from British Columbia all the way to Peru, including a stop at the Galápagos Islands.

bing-50333.jpg.title: Ashdown Forest, East Sussex, England
bing-50333.jpg.headline: Home of Winnie-the-Pooh. National Winnie-the-Pooh Day
bing-50333.jpg.description:
If you find yourself in a sticky situation, surrounded by honey pots and daydreams, you might just be celebrating National Winnie-the-Pooh Day! Today marks the birthday of AA Milne, the creator of the lovable, honey-obsessed bear who taught us that sometimes the best adventures happen when you're not looking for them. The writer introduced the world to Pooh in 1926, and he quickly became a household name. Milne's writing was inspired by his own son, Christopher Robin, and his toy bear—a story that began in a small nursery and turned into a global phenomenon.

Ever wondered where Winnie-the-Pooh and his friends truly roam? Well, today's image features Ashdown Forest in East Sussex, England, which is the real-life Hundred Acre Wood. The forest covers over 6,500 acres (2,500 hectares), giving you plenty of space to picture Pooh off on another adventure. Moreover, you can visit Pooh Bridge and play Poohsticks in the exact spot where Pooh and his friends did. It's a fantastic way to connect with the characters and bring a bit of that childhood magic into your day.

bing-50336.jpg.title: Sunset at White Sands National Park, New Mexico
bing-50336.jpg.headline: 1,001 New Mexican dunes. Dunes at White Sands National Park, New Mexico
bing-50336.jpg.description: Today's image features the dazzling beauty of White Sands National Park, New Mexico—a surreal expanse of glistening white gypsum dunes, the largest of its kind on Earth. Spanning more than 145,000 acres, these ever-shifting dunes rise up to 60 feet tall, creating a landscape not seen in many places. This park isn't only a natural wonder but a historical treasure, with fossilized human footprints dating back as far as 23,000 years, some of the oldest in North America.

bing-50343.jpg.title: Agordino, Colle Santa Lucia, Belluno, Veneto
bing-50343.jpg.headline: Alpi da sogno
bing-50343.jpg.description:
Agordino, nella provincia di Belluno, è una perla delle Dolomiti che d’inverno si veste di magia. Le montagne, imponenti e silenziose, si coprono di un manto candido che brilla sotto il sole invernale, mentre i boschi di abeti, custodi di antiche storie e leggende, si stagliano in miscele cromatiche vivaci. I piccoli borghi, con le loro case in legno e pietra, sono oasi di calore in un paesaggio immacolato. Ogni angolo regala scorci da cartolina, un invito irresistibile per chi cerca pace e meraviglia, avvolti dall’atmosfera ovattata della neve.

Se siete amanti della neve e degli sport alpini, a pochi chilometri di distanza, Cortina d’Ampezzo sta offrendo in questi giorni il cuore pulsante dello sci alpino internazionale: l’Audi FIS Ski World Cup. La “Regina delle Dolomiti” accoglie i campioni di tutto il mondo sulle sue iconiche piste, come la Olympia delle Tofane, dove velocità e precisione si sfidano in un contesto straordinario. Oltre a celebrare l’adrenalina dello sport, l’evento offre agli spettatori l’opportunità di immergersi nell'unicità di Cortina, tra l’eleganza delle sue vie, la tradizione alpina e il fascino senza tempo delle Dolomiti, patrimonio dell’UNESCO.
bing-50343.jpg.copyright: © Moreno Geremetta/Mauritius Images GmbH/Alamy Stock Phot

bing-50348.jpg.title: Neptune's Grotto, Sardinia, Italy
bing-50348.jpg.headline: A grotto fit for a god. Neptune's Grotto, Sardinia, Italy
bing-50348.jpg.description: Down 654 steps, perched perilously over the sea in Sardinia, Italy, you'll find a surprise waiting for you. Neptune's Grotto is a stunning stalactite cave that sits just over 3 feet above sea level. First discovered by local fishermen in the 18th century, the grotto was named after the Roman god of the sea. The entire cave complex stretches on for around 2.5 miles, although visitors can only access about 1,000 feet of the total. Inside, there's a labyrinth of lit pathways winding past stalactite and stalagmite formations, leading to a 390-foot-long saltwater lake.

bing-50350.jpg.title: コタンの湯, 北海道 川上郡
bing-50350.jpg.headline: 今日は「大寒」
bing-50350.jpg.description:
今日 1 月 20 日は二十四節気の「大寒」。1 年のうちで最も寒くなる時期とされています。そして画像は、北海道川上郡弟子屈町、屈斜路湖のほとりにある野湯・コタンの湯。冬の澄んだ空気の中、雪景色を眺めながら暖かい温泉に浸かるのは、まさに至福のひとときです…

屈斜路湖は冬になると湖全体が氷結しますが、温泉が湧いている部分は凍結しないため、白鳥の飛来地になっています。そのため、目の前で優雅に泳ぐ白鳥たちを眺めながら温泉に入れば、まるで白鳥と混浴しているかのよう。コタンの湯は、無料で利用できるにもかかわらず、とても綺麗に管理されており、更衣室もあるため、野湯のなかでは比較的入りやすいです。

bing-50353.jpg.title: Real Monasterio de Santa María de Guadalupe, Cáceres, Extremadura, España
bing-50353.jpg.headline: ¡El guardián de historias!. Real Monasterio de Santa María de Guadalupe, Cáceres, Extremadura, España
bing-50353.jpg.description:
Sumérgete en la majestuosidad del Real Monasterio de Santa María de Guadalupe en Cáceres, Extremadura. Este impresionante monasterio franciscano, declarado Patrimonio de la Humanidad por la UNESCO, custodia la imagen de la Virgen de Guadalupe, patrona de Extremadura y Reina de la Hispanidad. Un lugar donde el arte y la espiritualidad convergen en estilos gótico, mudéjar, renacentista, barroco y neoclásico, y cuya rica historia nos conecta con los siglos XIV al XXI.

A tan solo 180 kilómetros, pasando por el maravilloso Parque Nacional Monfragüe, se encuentra Acehúche, un pequeño municipio de 800 habitantes que celebra Las Carantoñas, una fiesta de Interés Turístico Nacional que rinde homenaje a San Sebastián. El día comienza con la Alborá, donde el tamborilero despierta al pueblo para iniciar la celebración. Los hombres, conocidos como Carantoñas, se visten con pieles de animales y máscaras, representando a las bestias que veneraron al Santo. Las mujeres, las regaoras, lucen el traje típico regional y acompañan con cánticos y confeti.

Extremadura es el lugar indicado para dejarse sorprender, con su fauna, vegetación, cultura y tradición. Y si lo tuyo son las rutas gastronómicas, no pueden faltar unas migas extremeñas, cordero al horno y la torta del Casar.

bing-50360.jpg.title: Martin Luther King Jr. Memorial in Washington, DC
bing-50360.jpg.headline: Honoring the dream. Martin Luther King Jr. Day
bing-50360.jpg.description:
Today we honor the life and legacy of Rev. Martin Luther King Jr. Prominent in the 1950s and 1960s, King was a Baptist minister who promoted nonviolent protest to effectuate social change. In 1963, he helped organize the March on Washington, DC, which 250,000 people attended to protest discrimination and support pending civil rights legislation. During this event, King delivered his famous "I Have a Dream" speech, imagining America free of racism and segregation. His speech is regarded as one of America's greatest, and his leadership was instrumental in ending racial segregation of African Americans throughout many parts of the United States. He received the Nobel Peace Prize in 1964, but his life was cut short by an assassin in 1968.

Seen in today's image near the Washington Monument, his 30-foot statue is the centerpiece of the Martin Luther King Jr. Memorial in Washington, DC. Emerging from between the Stone of Hope and Mountain of Despair, the figure of Dr. King resolutely looks to the horizon, and his memorial is a place for visitors to ponder a future where all are free at last.

bing-50361.jpg.title: Looking over the Gulf of Naples towards Mount Vesuvius, Italy
bing-50361.jpg.headline: Gulf of Naples and Mount Vesuvius, Italy
bing-50361.jpg.description:
Today we celebrate World Pizza Day, an important anniversary for pizza lovers around the world. That's why we are in Naples, the home of pizza. Although similar dishes existed in ancient times, the modern pizza has its roots in the heart of the capital of Campania, the city that gave birth to this dish in the 18th century, when tomatoes imported from America were combined with bread. Created in 1889 in honour of Queen Margherita of Savoy, the Pizza Margherita, with its ingredients reminiscent of the Italian flag—red tomatoes, white mozzarella and green basil—became a symbol of Italian conviviality, culture and tradition.

Already at the beginning of the 20th century, Neapolitan pizza makers celebrated this day in honour of Saint Anthony Abbot, protector of animals, firemen and bakers. More than a hundred years later, the art of the Neapolitan pizza maker was recognised by UNESCO as part of the Intangible Cultural Heritage of Humanity. Today we celebrate by eating pizza, a symbol of Italy, and rediscovering its history and culture. Which is your favourite? Margherita, Marinara or something else? Let's enjoy a pizza and let ourselves be carried away by the taste and the joy of a shared moment.

bing-50368.jpg.title: Cabanes aux toits colorés recouvertes de neige à Gouville-sur-Mer, Normandie
bing-50368.jpg.headline: Dites non au Blue Monday !. Blue Monday
bing-50368.jpg.description:
Pas facile de garder le moral un lundi d’hiver, surtout quand il s’agit du fameux Blue Monday, ce jour censé être le plus déprimant de l’année. Ce concept trouve son origine dans un calcul mêlant météo, dettes post-fêtes et baisse de motivation. Mais saviez-vous que les couleurs peuvent avoir un effet magique sur notre humeur ?

À Gouville-sur-Mer, en Normandie, les cabanes aux toits colorés recouvertes de neige semblent défier la monotonie de l’hiver. Le rouge éclatant, le bleu profond et le jaune ensoleillé tranchent avec le paysage blanc, rappelant que même en pleine saison froide, il est possible de trouver des éclats de vie et de joie.

Alors, pourquoi ne pas s’inspirer de ces cabanes pour égayer votre journée ? Une touche de couleur dans votre environnement, que ce soit un pull vif ou une plante fleurie, peut suffire à chasser la grisaille du Blue Monday.

bing-50372.jpg.title: Eurasian red squirrel
bing-50372.jpg.headline: Feeling squirrely?. Squirrel Appreciation Day
bing-50372.jpg.description:
What's that long, bushy tail scurrying across the branches? Chances are, it's a squirrel. These little rodents are found across most of the globe, and today is their special day: Squirrel Appreciation Day. This unofficial holiday was started by a North Carolina wildlife rehabilitator to encourage people to leave out seeds and nuts for these critters. From the tiny least pygmy squirrel—just 5.5 inches long—to the Bhutan giant flying squirrel at more than 4 feet, these mammals come in all shapes and sizes.

Today's image features a Eurasian red squirrel, photographed in the Netherlands. The red squirrel can be found across Europe and Russia, from western Spain and Portugal all the way to eastern Siberia. Their diet mainly consists of nuts, fungi, seeds, and berries, but they will occasionally eat birds' eggs. In addition to being the national mammal of Denmark, they also play a part in old Norse mythology. Ratatoskr is a red squirrel who scurries up and down Yggdrasil, the sacred tree, carrying messages and spreading gossip. So, next time you spot a red squirrel, it could just be a furry little messenger!

bing-50384.jpg.title: Ad-Deir, Petra, Jordan
bing-50384.jpg.headline: Finding beauty in the Lost City. Ad-Deir, Petra, Jordan
bing-50384.jpg.description:
Carved into rose-red cliffs, Petra and its crown jewel, Ad-Deir (The Monastery) feel like stepping into a real-life Indiana Jones adventure. Tucked in the heart of Jordan's arid desert landscapes, this ancient city once thrived as the capital of the Nabataean Kingdom in the 2nd century BCE. It was also a hub of the spice trade, connecting distant regions like China, Egypt, Greece, and India. The city was abandoned for around 500 years before being rediscovered in 1812, earning it the Lost City moniker.

Ad-Deir, seen in today's image, dates to the 1st century CE. Its design is characterized by a combination of Hellenistic and Mesopotamian influences. Although the exact purpose of the structure is debated, it's believed to have been used as a church during the Byzantine period. Standing nearly 150 feet tall and 160 feet wide, its massive facade is carved directly into the sandstone cliffs, showcasing the Nabataeans' ingenious craftsmanship and architecture. The journey to this landmark involves a steep hike up 800 stone steps, winding through rocky terrain. At the top, you're rewarded with panoramic views of the rugged Petra valley that make the climb more than worth it.

bing-50396.jpg.title: Deer Valley at dusk, Park City, Utah
bing-50396.jpg.headline: Movies, mountains, and magic. Sundance Film Festival
bing-50396.jpg.description:
Today, the Sundance Film Festival kicks off, celebrating the magic of movies against the backdrop of Utah's mountains. As a launchpad for groundbreaking films and emerging talent, Sundance has come a long way since its humble beginnings in 1978. Now one of the film industry's most influential events, it has introduced the world to talents like Quentin Tarantino and Steven Soderbergh, whose early works premiered here before shaping their iconic careers. With competitive sections for dramatic and documentary movies, from features to shorts, the festival offers an inspiring array of storytelling.

At its heart is Park City, pictured here, one of Sundance's vibrant host cities—the event takes place across several Utah locations. Every January, this quaint destination transforms into a buzzing hub of creativity, drawing filmmakers and cinephiles from across the globe. Beyond the silver screen, Park City is worth exploring. It boasts stunning landscapes, top-tier ski resorts like Deer Valley and Park City Mountain, and endless outdoor adventures, from hiking and biking to soaking in nearby hot springs. Whether you're here for the films or the thrills, Sundance in Park City promises an unforgettable experience.

bing-50408.jpg.title: Strokkur geyser in Iceland
bing-50408.jpg.headline: Bubbling with power. Thorrablot: The Icelandic midwinter festival
bing-50408.jpg.description: What could be better than warming up winter with a feast that's a little wild and a lot of fun? Thorrablot, Iceland's midwinter festival, invites you to dive headfirst into tradition. This celebration of survival, culture, and community, which dates to the Viking Age, was once a way for Icelanders to honor Thor, the Norse god of thunder. Today, people celebrate by gathering to feast on an array of local delicacies, including fermented shark, smoked lamb, rye bread, and shots of Brennivín—often called 'black death' schnapps.

bing-50417.jpg.title: Devorgilla Bridge in Dumfries Galloway Scotland, UK
bing-50417.jpg.headline: Ode over the bridge. Celebrating Robert Burns OR Burns Night
bing-50417.jpg.description:
It's Burns Night—time to toast to poetry and passion. This celebration honours Scotland's famous poet, Robert Burns, on his birthday. Born on this day in 1759, his work blends sharp insight, emotion and cultural pride. Although much of his writing was in Scots, he also used English, ensuring his voice reached far beyond the country. Burns Night isn't just a party—it's a celebration of Scotland's cultural heritage, recognised by the Scottish Parliament, and highlights the richness of the Scots language.

Burns' connection to Dumfries, a market town, is an important part of his legacy. He moved to Dumfriesshire in 1788 and settled in Dumfries in 1791, where he lived until his death in 1796. The town is home to the historic Devorgilla Bridge, pictured here, also known as Dumfries Old Bridge. Once a road bridge, it now serves pedestrians and stands as a reminder of the time Burns spent there. The bridge we see today contains remnants dating back to the early 1430s, with its stone structure likely completed by 1432.

bing-50418.jpg.title: Amanhecer no Rio de Janeiro
bing-50418.jpg.headline: Olha que coisa mais linda
bing-50418.jpg.description:
Hoje celebramos o Dia da Bossa Nova, um gênero musical que nasceu nos anos 1950, em Copacabana, Rio de Janeiro. Com claras e diretas influências do samba tradicional e do jazz americano, a bossa nova criou seu próprio caminho a partir desses outros gêneros musicais herdeiros da cultura afro-brasileira e afro-americana. A expressão "bossa nova" significa "novo jeito" ou "nova onda", uma gíria popular durante essa época. Nos anos 1960, a Bossa Nova ganhou reconhecimento mundial, especialmente com a canção "Garota de Ipanema" de Tom Jobim e Vinicius de Moraes.

A maneira de tocar violão na Bossa Nova, desenvolvida por João Gilberto, é única e se tornou a marca registrada do gênero, conquistando o mundo com sua sofisticação e charme. Inclusive artistas de outros gêneros, como Billie Eilish e C. Tangana já usaram influências do gênero musical brasileiro em suas canções. Que tal aproveitar o dia para aprender mais sobre esse estilo musical e apreciar suas melodias? Vamos juntos celebrar a Bossa Nova e sua rica história!
bing-50418.jpg.copyright: © Stanley Chen Xi, landscape and architecture photographer/Getty Image

bing-50420.jpg.title: Porto, Portugal
bing-50420.jpg.headline: Golden hour in Porto. Porto, Portugal
bing-50420.jpg.description: Today's image takes us to a city that is bold, unpolished in the best way, and brimming with personality. While it's famous for its port wine (cheers to that!), there's so much more to discover in the Portuguese city of Porto.
